They were to learn for certain what his intention was: whether he would stubbornly maintain the articles that the witnesses brought against him, or change his opinion and, by renouncing his teaching in accordance with the council's decree, write and teach things entirely different.

units.la: Postquam Husiũ e carcere coram legatis adductus esset: primus D. Ioannes Chlumensis hoc pacto eum est allocutus. Optime magister, nos homines illiterati tibi in hac re consulere haud possumus. Proinde ipse videris an criminum, quorum te concilium hoc accusat, tibi ipse sis conscius. Quod si reus es, ne pudeat te sententiae meliori cedere, atque tuam retractare: Sin autem conscientia tuae innocentiae testis est, caue quicquam committas contra eam, neue in conspectu Dei mentiaris, neque patiare tibi prius veritatem diuinam, nisi simul cum anima cripi.
units.tr: After Hus had been brought from prison before the envoys, Sir John of Chlum was the first to address him in this way: "Most excellent master, we are unlearned men and cannot advise you in this matter. So you yourself must see whether you are conscious of the crimes of which this council accuses you. If you are guilty, let it not shame you to yield to a better opinion and retract your errors. But if your conscience bears witness to your innocence, take care not to do anything against it, nor to lie in the sight of God, nor allow the divine truth to be torn from you, unless your soul is torn away with it."

units.la: Ibi ille constitit & lachrymas fundens modeste ita respondit: Spectabilis vir, Deum meum testor, si quid vnquam erroneum scripsi, aut si quid a Lege diuina alienum, quod cum sancta Ecclesia minus cō-sentiat, sentiat, docui, supplex retractabo, ac cedam lubens: imò summopere desidero rectiori & firmiori scriptura instrui. Quod si ipsi fecerit, revocare ex animo singula paratus sum. Sermonem hunc excepit vnus episcoporum qui astabant: Hui, inquiens, vis tu plus sapere vniuerso concilio? Cui Huffius: Ego vero, inquit, per Deum omnipotentem vos obtestor, vel vnum ex eo concilio, etiam infimae sortis hominem docite, qui me rectiora doceat de veritate, equidem libenter ei cedam: tantum abest vt me plus vniuerso concilio sapere existimem. Ad haec verba Episcopi alij: Heu, inquiunt, quam est ille pertinax in sua haeresi. Hoc dicto eum in carcerem reduci mandantes, ipsi abiere.
units.tr: At this Hus stopped, and weeping, answered modestly: "Honourable sir, I call God to witness: if I have ever written anything erroneous, or taught anything that is foreign to the divine Law, or that does not agree with holy Church, I will humbly retract it and gladly give way. Indeed I greatly desire to be instructed by a more correct and firmer Scripture. If anyone does this for me, I am ready to recall each point from my heart." One of the bishops standing by took up this speech: "Hus," he said, "do you wish to be wiser than the whole council?" Hus replied: "Indeed, I beseech you by almighty God: if even one man from that council, a man of the lowliest rank, will teach me a more correct account of the truth, I will gladly yield to him. So far am I from thinking that I am wiser than the whole council." At these words the other bishops said, "Alas, how obstinate he is in his heresy!" With this remark they ordered him led back to prison, and they themselves departed.

units.la: Postero die, qui mensis Iunij erat dies sextus, ductus est Husius ab Archiepiscopo Rigentino ex factione [illegible, ~10 letters], ad magnum illud Constantiense templum, quo Episcopi & alij sacerdotum principes, ad eum condemnandum confluxerant: porrò postquam ad valvas templi ventum erat, restiterunt ibi cum eo, dum sacra in templo finirentur: veriti enim sunt hominem introducere sub missae tempus, ne rem diuinam sua praesentia polluceret.
units.tr: On the next day, which was the sixth day of June, Hus was led by the Archbishop of Riga from the faction [illegible, ~10 letters] to that great church at Constance, where the bishops and other chief priests had gathered to condemn him. But when they came to the doors of the church, they stopped there with him while the sacred rites were finished inside. For they were afraid to bring the man in at the time of the Mass, lest his presence defile the holy service.

units.la: Tandem peractis sacris pertraxerunt eum in consessum sacerdotum, vbi pro more in excelsis sedilibus consedere, pro dignitate videlicet illius ordinis constructis, asseribus in sublime eos ambientibus. Imperator verò celsiori loco in suo solio sedebat, cui alterum latus claudebat filius Clementis tenens pomum imagine crucis insigne: alterum autem, dux quidam fulgentem gladium manu gerens. Erat praeterea mensa in hoc ambitu paululum supra terram elevata, cui impositus erat truncus, atque in eo vestes & stolae appositae, quibus sacerdotes ad missandum vtuntur, ad exaugurandum seu degradandum Husium, quem ante eam mensam consistere iusserunt: vbi ille procumbens diu preces fundebat. Interea episcopus Londensis, cui Monacho erat cognomen, suggestum ascendit: vnde fere edicta sua promulgare solebant, concionaturus arripuit locum Pauli Rom. 6. Vetus homo noster simul crucifixus est, vt destruatur corpus peccati: in hac concione vehementissimè docebat quàtae [?] pestes sint, & quam graves in sancta Ecclesia haereses: deinde quod regum & cuiusuis magistratus interfit, eas & praesertim simoniaca è medio Ecclesiae tollere: tales namque haereses vnitate Ecclesiæ qualibet vi aperta & tyrannide scindere longè nocentius. Ac sermonem ad Imperatorem conuertens sic est locutus, Æquum est igitur, Imperator inuictissime, vt hæreticum hunc in sua malitia rigidum extinguas (in manibus etenim nostris est). hoc si quidem pulcherrimo facinore, immortale nomen apud posteros iuuenes iuxta ac senes, tibi parabis. Hactenus fuit summa concionis. Successit autem huic Henricus quidam concilij illius orator:is acriter instare, & vniuersum cœtum stimulare, vt cœptam causam contra Hussium persequerentur, vrgerent, nec prius desisteret, quàm homo morti addiceretur.
units.tr: When the rites were at last completed, they dragged him into the assembly of priests, where, as is customary, they sat on high seats, built to suit the dignity of that order, with boards rising around them. The Emperor sat on his throne in a higher place; on one side of him stood the son of Clement holding an orb marked with the image of the cross, and on the other a certain duke carrying a gleaming sword in his hand. Moreover, within this enclosure there was a table raised a little above the ground, on which a block was set, and on it were laid the vestments and stoles that priests use for saying Mass, for stripping and degrading Hus. They ordered him to stand before this table, and there he knelt for a long time, pouring out prayers. Meanwhile the bishop of London, whose surname was Monk, went up into the pulpit, from which they were accustomed to proclaim their decrees, and taking up as the text for his sermon the words of Paul in Romans 6, "Our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed," he preached very vehemently how great the plagues are, and how grave the heresies in holy Church; then that it concerns kings and every magistrate to remove them from the midst of the Church, especially the heresy of simony; for such heresies tear the unity of the Church apart far more harmfully than any open force or tyranny. Turning his speech to the Emperor, he spoke thus: "It is right, therefore, most unconquered Emperor, that you extinguish this heretic, stiff in his malice (for he is in our hands). By this most splendid deed you will win for yourself an immortal name among posterity, both young and old." So far was the substance of the sermon. After him came a certain Henry, an orator of that council, who urged the whole assembly sharply and spurred them on to pursue and press the cause begun against Hus, and not to stop until the man was given over to death.

units.la: Deinde Episcopus quidam iussu concilij processit ad pulpitum, ex quo formulam Hussij causæ habitā cum Archiepiscopo Pragensi, & cæteris sacerdotū principibus recitat: mox etiam quam ipsi aduersus Husium agebat causam, cum formula condemnationis proferūt ij quibus id à concilio mandatum erat.
units.tr: Then a certain bishop, by order of the council, came forward to the pulpit, and from it read out the record of Hus's case held with the Archbishop of Prague and the other chief priests. Soon afterwards those who had been commissioned by the council brought forward the charge they were bringing against Hus, together with the form of condemnation.

units.la: Legebantur insuper in hoc consessu crimina quæ contra pium virum testes tam Pragæ quàm Constantiæ intendebant, & plura alia (quæ quidem ipse in carcere sua manu perscripsit, ac suis fratribus misit, quo & ipsis Iudicum fraus perspecta foret, & habebant quod mendacijs & commentis respondere possint:) Ac principio cum hoc inter alia, illorum quidem iudicio, crimen legeretur, Quòd vna sit Ecclesia sancta catholica, quæ est cœtus omnium credentium, ad salutem prædestinatorum (id quidem execranda Synodus pro hæresi habebat) Hussius sublata voce in hæc verba prorupit: Nõ dubito profecto, quin vna sit Ecclesia catholica, quæ est congregatio omnium electorum, tam eorum qui adhuc viuunt, quàm mortuorum & cœlestium. Cumque ite & ad alia responderet, tum Cardinalis Cameracensis ad eum: Agedum, inquit: tace modò, ad omnia simul postmodò respondebis. Cui ille: Prohibeßne inquit, quo minus singula refellam, cum vniuersum calumniarum cumulum meminisse non queam? Rursus ad cætera dicere volenti, impositum fuit silentium per Cardinalé Florentinum, qui surgens, Tacc, inquit, obtundis: atque eum coerceri iussit à præconibus. Tum ille alta voce ac manibus ad sydera tensis, exclamauit: Precor omnipotentis Dei nomine, ne vos pigeat me æquis animis audire, vt saltem apud istos qui circumstant, me purgem, atque suspicionem errorum quàm quam de me habet ex eorum cordibus dimovea: id si modo dederitis tum iure vestro sino[?] de me quod libuerit faciatis: sed cum nihil prosiceret, atque omnem purgandi se de criminibus falso obiectis ereptam videret potestatem: supplex in genua procidens, sublatis in cælum & manibus & oculis, orabat, causam suam Deo iudici æquissimo magna voce commendans. atque sæpius hac appellatione ad Deum usus est, dum accusaretur.
units.tr: Moreover, in this assembly were read the charges that the witnesses, both at Prague and at Constance, had brought against that godly man, and many others as well (which he himself had written out by hand in prison and sent to his brothers, so that the trickery of the judges might be seen clearly and they might have something to answer lies and fabrications with). First, among other things, this charge was read, as they judged it: that there is one holy catholic Church, which is the assembly of all believers, predestined to salvation (which the accursed Synod regarded as heresy). Hus, raising his voice, burst out with these words: "I have no doubt at all that there is one catholic Church, which is the congregation of all the elect, both those who are still living and those who are dead and in heaven." And when he went on to answer the other points, the Cardinal of Cambrai said to him, "Come now, be quiet. You will answer everything together afterwards." He replied: "Are you forbidding me to refute each point one by one, when I cannot remember the whole heap of slanders?" As he was about to speak again to the rest, silence was imposed by the Cardinal of Florence, who rose and said, "Be quiet, you are wearying us!" and ordered the heralds to restrain him. Then he, with a loud voice and his hands stretched up to heaven, cried out: "I beg you in the name of almighty God, do not be displeased to hear me with an even mind, so that at least before these who stand around I may clear myself, and remove from their hearts the suspicion of errors which they hold against me. If you grant this, then by your right you may do with me whatever you please." But when he gained nothing, and saw that the power of clearing himself of the falsely alleged crimes had been snatched from him, he fell on his knees, and with both hands and eyes lifted to heaven, he commended his cause in a loud voice to God, the most just Judge, and he often used this form of address to God while he was being accused.

units.la: Tandem illi omnibus articulis, quos ex libris ipsius decerpserat, expositis, subiiciebant quoque eos qui testibus confirmati erant: callide quidem singulis capitibus nomina testium ambigua, nempe officiorum aut dignitatum subiungebant: germana vero reticebat artificiose admodum. exempli gratia: Singulis capitibus recitatis, ita nomina testium addebant: Huius criminis testes sunt, duo Canonici Pragenses & totidem Parrochi, altarii tres, & unus doctor: atque hoc artificio usi sunt in citandis testimonijs.
units.tr: At last, after all the articles he had drawn from his books had been set out, they also presented the witnesses who had been brought to support them. They cleverly attached to each article a name of a witness that was vague, namely by giving only his office or rank, while carefully leaving out the actual name. For example, after each article was read, they added the witnesses' names in this way: "The witnesses to this charge are two canons of Prague, as many parish priests, three chaplains, and one doctor." They used this trick in citing the testimonies.

units.la: Omnibus itaque criminum capitibus finitis & perlectis, Pontificius Iudex mox surrexit: Erat autem senex quidam, caluicio insignis, Italus genere, Italus.is condemnationis sententiam in Hussium legebat, quam ad verbum describere hic, supervacaneum visum est, potiora saltem declarare satis sit, ad quæ obiter, quanquam illis sedulo inhibentibus, ipse respondebat. Ac in primis cum legeretur, quod multos annos pertinaciter hæsisset in erroribus, Ego vero inquit Hussius, id pernego. semper enim desideravi, & etiamnum desidero firmiore Scriptura doceri: ac utinam vel unum sacræ scripturæ verbulum mihi hodie daretur, quod omnes hos errores tollere & convincere posset. Et cum in ea sententia, libros quoque eius condemnassent, quos de Ecclesia inscripsit, denique quicquid ædidit Latinè, Bohemicè, & si quæ in alias linguas transfusa erant, ut Constantiæ & passim alibi, per Episcopos in regionibus omnia exurerentur ac abolerentur. Ad ea Hussius ita respondit, Quo iure mea scripta damnare potestis, quæ nec ullis firmioribus argumentis, quod sæpe cupivi & iam cupio, refutastis, nec ullius erroris convicistis? Deinde qua re impulsi libros nostros in Bohemicam vel aliam quampiam linguam versos abrogare decrevistis? nimirum quos nunquam vidistis: & ut maxime videritis, non intellexistis, quippe Bohemicè prorsus ignari. Hæc conquestus tandè alias criminum partes in ea condemnatione cötra se lectorum auscultando, cælum suspiciens, supplex ac genibus flexis, orabat.
units.tr: So when all the heads of the charges had been finished and read through, the Papist judge stood up. He was an old man, notable for his bald head, an Italian by birth, and he read out the sentence of condemnation against Hus. It seems superfluous to write it out word for word here; it is enough to set out the main points, to which Hus responded in passing, although the judges sternly tried to stop him. First, when it was read that he had obstinately clung to errors for many years, Hus replied: "I flatly deny that. For I have always desired, and still desire, to be taught by firmer Scripture. Would that someone might give me today even one little word of Holy Scripture that could remove and refute all these errors!" Then they condemned his books, namely those he had written on the Church, and in short whatever he had published in Latin and Bohemian, and whatever had been translated into other languages, ordering that all of them be burned and destroyed by the bishops at Constance and everywhere else in their regions. To this Hus answered: "By what right can you condemn my writings, which you have refuted by no firmer arguments (as I have often wished and still wish you would), and whose errors you have not proved? Further, on what grounds have you decided to abolish our books, translated into Bohemian or any other language? You have never seen them, and even if you had, you would not have understood them, since you are wholly ignorant of Bohemian." Having complained of this, and listening as the other charges against him were read out in that condemnation, he looked up to heaven and, kneeling, prayed earnestly.

units.la: Porrò condemnatione hac finita, Hußius pro omnibus inimicis suis voce clara ita deprecatus est: Domine Deus, per tuam misericordiam precor, omnibus hostibus meis digneris ignoscere. Nam tu scis me ab his iniustè esse accusatum, falsis testibus circunuentum, effectis criminibus oppressum, denique iniquè condemnatum. Propter misericordiam igitur tuam, culpam eis remitte.
units.tr: Then, when this condemnation was finished, Hus, praying aloud for all his enemies, said: "Lord God, through your mercy I beg you to forgive all my enemies. For you know that I have been unjustly accused by them, surrounded by false witnesses, overwhelmed by fabricated charges, and at last wickedly condemned. Therefore, for the sake of your mercy, remit their guilt."

units.la: His dictis plerique sacerdotum seniores, ac præsertim Episcopi torno[?] vultu inspicientes, cum irridebant. Deinde septem Episcoporum iussu, qui illi sacerdotium adimebant, vestibus sacrificorum induebatur, ac si ci missa celebranda esset. Ac principio albam vestem induens, dixit: Dominus meus Iesus Christus cum ab Herode mitteretur ad Pilatum, in veste candida illusus est.
units.tr: After he had said this, many of the senior priests, and especially the bishops, looked at him with scornful faces and laughed at him. Then, by the order of seven bishops, who were taking away his priesthood, he was dressed in the vestments of the priests, as if Mass were about to be celebrated for him. Putting on first the white alb, he said: "When my Lord Jesus Christ was sent by Herod to Pilate, he was mocked in a white robe."

units.la: Postea illis indutus vestibus, admonebatur ab Episcopis, ut errores illos, dum liceret, retractaret iuramento etiam adiecto. Ipse verò coram his in ea mensa, ubi induebatur stans, ad vulgus se conuertit, ac voce querula & lachrymans, ad turbas inquit: En isti Episcopi persuadent ac hortantur me ad errores illos retractandum. Ast ego hoc facere metuo, ne mendacij arguar olim in conspectu Dei, si errorum me reum esse faterer, quorum nunquam essem conscius, quos nunquam docuerim, atque adeo ne cum conscientiam, tum veritatem diuinam offenderem, quandoquidem nunquam eos asseruerim, sed per falsa testimonia mihi obtruduntur iniquè, quibus ego contraria & scripsi & docui. Ad hæc ne animi tantæ multitudinis, cui hactenus concionatus sum, offensi à veritate auellerentur, ac aliorum quoque, qui verbi diuini fideles sunt ministri. Hoc dicto, Episcopi cum reliquo cœtu in hæc verba prorumpunt: Iam tandem perspeximus, quàm peruicax sit in malicia, atque tenax in sua hæresi.
units.tr: Afterwards, when he had been dressed in these vestments, the bishops urged him to retract those errors while there was still time, adding an oath. But he, standing there before them at the table where he was being dressed, turned to the people and, with a plaintive voice and in tears, said to the crowds: "Look, these bishops are persuading and urging me to retract those errors. But I fear to do this, lest I be convicted of lying before God in time to come, if I confessed to errors of which I was never aware, which I never taught, and so offend both my conscience and divine truth, since I have never asserted them, but they are unjustly imposed on me through false testimonies, while I have both written and taught the opposite. Moreover, I fear that the minds of this great multitude, to whom I have preached until now, would be torn away from the truth, and those of others too who are faithful ministers of the divine Word." At these words the bishops and the rest of the assembly burst out: "At last we have seen how stubborn he is in his wickedness, and how tenacious in his heresy!"

units.la: Ac mox ijdem Episcopi Hußio mandarunt, de mensa descenderet, ibi adimentes ci sacerdotium. Principio auferunt ab eo calicem, dicentes: O Iuda maledicte, qui deserens consilium pacis, iniisti consilium cum Iudæis, En auferam[?] à te calice hunc, in quo sanguis Iesu Christi offertur in redemptionem mūdi. Tū ille alta uoce exclamauit vicissim: Ego vero spē omnē & fiduciā in Deo meo & saluatore meo fixam habeo, quòd ille calicem salutaris à me nunquā auferet, & confido constanter, quòd ipsius præsidio adiutus, hodie in regno eius hūc bibiturus sū. Illi vero reliquo habitu cum exuere perrexerunt. Subinde more suo singulis vestibus turpem execrationem adiicientes. Hußio interea respondente: Illusiones has æquissimo animo pro nomine & veritate Iesu Christi se ferre.
units.tr: Immediately these same bishops ordered Hus to come down from the table, taking away his priesthood there. First they took away the chalice, saying: "O cursed Judas, who, abandoning the counsel of peace, have entered into a plot with the Jews! Behold, I shall take from you this chalice, in which the blood of Jesus Christ is offered for the redemption of the world." Then he cried out in a loud voice in reply: "But I have all my hope and trust fixed in my God and my Saviour, that he will never take from me the chalice of salvation, and I am confident that, aided by his protection, I shall today drink it in his kingdom." They then went on stripping him of the rest of his garments, each time adding a foul curse as they did so, in their usual manner. Meanwhile Hus, answering them, said that he bore these mockeries with the most tranquil mind for the name and truth of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Tandem Episcopi multiplici illa sacrificantium veste ab eo abstracta, ad rasum etiam verticem corrumpendū accingunt sese, sed de hac re magnum inter cos [?] dissidium ortum est, quibusdam nouacula eum tondere volentibus, contrà nonnullis satis esse censentibus, ut forsice duntaxat rasura turbaretur.
units.tr: At last, when the bishops had stripped him of the many vestments of the priesthood, they set about shaving the crown of his head to make a tonsure. But a great dispute arose among them over this matter: some wanted to shave him with a razor, while others thought it enough that his hair be disturbed by scissors alone.

units.la: Hæc dum agitantur, Hußius ad Imperatorem in solio sedentem conuersus, ait: Eia inter Episcopos istos non bene cōuenit, mirum sanè cum omnes æque crudeles sint, in ipsa tamen crudelitate non consentire. Viat [?] tandem factio ea, quae pro forsicibus contendebat, ac capillis eius in quatuor partibus ad speciem crucis scissis, orbem illum rasum abolcuerunt [?], his verbis adiectis: Iam hoc sacrū Constantiense concilium, Ioannem Hußium ordine sacerdotij ac munere præclaro quo exornatus fuit, amouet, ea re declarans, quòd hominem hunc templū atque Ecclesia Dei ab sese abdicauerit, ac destitutum suo præsidio, potestati seculari tradiderit.
units.tr: While these things were going on, Hus turned to the Emperor, who was sitting on his throne, and said: "Ah, these bishops do not agree well among themselves. It is surely remarkable that, though they are all equally cruel, they cannot agree even in their cruelty." At last the faction that insisted on scissors prevailed. They cut his hair in four parts, in the form of a cross, and then shaved off the circle that remained, adding these words: "Now this holy Council of Constance removes John Hus from the priestly order and the distinguished office with which he was adorned, declaring thereby that this man has disowned the temple and Church of God, and, being deprived of its protection, has handed him over to the secular power."

units.la: Priusquàm autem coronam in ludibrium ex papyro facta impo-suerunt capiti eius, inter cætera conuitia dixerunt: Animam tuam devouemus Diabolis inferni. Ille vero manibus complicatis, cælū suspiciens, inquit: Ast ego cā commēdo benignissimo Domino Iesu Christo. Postquam autem coronam eam vidit, dixit: Dominus meus Iesus Christus pro me misero longè asperiorem atque graviorem spineam coronam innocēs ad infame genus mortis gestare dignatus est, quapropter ego miser peccator hanc multo leviorem coronam, quanquam meū ludibrium, libens nominis ipsius ac veritatis causa in capite ferā. Porrò corona hæc erat ex papyro facta, & ad speciem pyramidis fastigiata, cubitali ferme longitudine, in ea tres horrendi cacodæmones erant depositi, cum hac inscriptione criminis: Iste est Hæresiarcha.
units.tr: Before they placed on his head a crown made of paper in mockery, they said among other insults: "We devote your soul to the devils of hell." But he, folding his hands and looking up to heaven, said: "But I commend it to the most gracious Lord Jesus Christ." When he saw the crown, he said: "My Lord Jesus Christ, innocent, deigned to bear a far harsher and heavier crown of thorns for me, a wretched sinner, to a shameful kind of death. Therefore I, a wretched sinner, will gladly wear on my head this much lighter crown, though it is meant as a mockery, for the sake of his name and the truth." The crown was made of paper and shaped to a point like a pyramid, about a cubit in length, and on it were depicted three horrible evil demons, with this inscription of his crime: "This man is the arch-heretic."

units.la: Tum Imperator ad Clemetis filium Lodouicū, de quo paulo ante meminimus, Germanicè inquit: Abi, & accepto homine trade lictoribus.
units.tr: Then the Emperor said in German to Clement's son Lodovicus, whom we mentioned a little earlier: "Go, and when you have the man, hand him over to the lictors."

units.la: Ille mox veste sua depositā, qua, ut solent duces exornatus erat, imperium exequitur, ac correptum Hussium carnificibus in manus dat & lictoribus, ipseque ad supplicium comitatus est eum. Igitur ea corona ex templo ad supplicium ductus est, ante cuius conspectum sub eandem horam libros ipsius tradiderunt incendio, quo condemnatione eorum testarentur. Porrò Hussius eo facinore, prædaro scilicet, viso, subrisit, ac ad rogum profectus, turbam commonebat, ne crederent propter errores se exustum iri, falsò enim accusatum esse, ac testibus iniquis oppressum, hostibus sibi infestissimis: Quid, quod hactenus rectius non docuerunt, inquit, atque ego sensi, ex sacra scriptura, id quod vnice semper cupiebam? Turba autem quæ comitabatur eum fere armata erat.
units.tr: He at once laid aside his own garment, with which, as commanders are accustomed to be adorned, he carried out the command. He seized Hus and handed him over to the executioners and lictors, and himself accompanied him to the execution. So Hus was led from the church to his death, and before his face, at the same hour, his books were given to the flames, so that they might bear witness to their condemnation. Then Hus, having seen this outrage, smiled, and as he went to the stake he warned the crowd not to believe that he was being burned for errors, for he had been falsely accused and oppressed by unjust witnesses, his most bitter enemies. "What, then," he said, "have they not taught more rightly up to now, and have I not perceived from Holy Scripture that which I have always, above all, desired?" The crowd that accompanied him was almost entirely armed.

units.la: Postquam autem peruenit ad eum locum, in quo passurus erat, flexo poplite, ac manibus oculisque cælum versus sublatis, supplex precabatur, recitando quosdam Dauidis Psalmos, ac præsertim quinquagesimum & tricesimum, Versum quoque huc: In manus tuas Domine, commendo spiritum meum: voce clara & vultu hilari subinde repetens, ita vt facile circumstantes audirent eum. Porrò locus, in quo vrēdus [?] erat, est instar prati situs inter hortos suburbij Constatiensis, quo itur ad arcem nomine Gotleben, in qua Hussius antea vinculis detentus fuerat.
units.tr: When he came to the place where he was to suffer, he knelt, and with hands and eyes raised toward heaven he prayed as a suppliant, reciting some Psalms of David, especially the fiftieth and the thirty-first, and this verse: "Into your hands, Lord, I commend my spirit," repeating it from time to time in a clear voice and with a cheerful face, so that those standing around could easily hear him. The place where he was to be burned lies like a meadow among the gardens of the suburb of Constance, on the way to the citadel called Gottleben, where Hus had previously been held in chains.

units.la: Ac cum ita, vt iam dictum est, orasset, interea quidam ex plebe homines illiterati dixerunt: Nobis non est compertum, quid hic Hussius antea docuerit vel concionatus sit, cæterum nunc audimus ex eo sacra eloquia, ac pias preces. Alij verò optabant illi dari confessorem. Quidā verò sacerdos equo insidens, conspicua tunica indutus, quæ intus rubra, ac tenuissima tela suffulta erat, respondit: Indignus est vt audiatur, nec adhibendus est ei confessor. hæreticus enim est.
units.tr: When he had prayed in this way, as has been said, some of the common people, unlearned men, said: "We do not know what this Hus taught or preached before, but now we hear holy words and pious prayers from him." Others wished that a confessor be given to him. But a certain priest, sitting on a horse and dressed in a conspicuous tunic, red inside and made of very fine cloth, replied: "He is not worthy to be heard, nor is a confessor to be provided for him, for he is a heretic."

units.la: Cæterum dubium non est, quin hæc opprobria animum Hussij grauius pertentassent, nisi in hac tota causæ actione id alte animo infixū fuisset, se pro Christo pati: vt ipse testatur in epistolis quas in carcere scripsit. Porrò inter orandum, contumeliosa corona illa cecidit de capite ipsius, quam Husius conspicatus subrisit. Quidam verò satellites, quibus cinctus erat, inquiunt: Restituatur rursum corona capiti eius, ut unà cum Diabolis dominis suis, quos hic coluit, exuratur.
units.tr: Yet there is no doubt that these insults would have weighed more heavily on Hus's mind, had he not held deeply fixed in his heart throughout this whole affair that he was suffering for Christ, as he himself testifies in the letters he wrote in prison. Meanwhile, as he prayed, that mocking crown fell from his head, and Hus, noticing it, smiled. Some of the guards with whom he was surrounded said: "Let the crown be put back on his head, so that he may be burned together with his masters the devils, whom he worshipped here."

units.la: Tum ille iussu carnificis, & lictorum erectus, clara voce, ita ut ab circunstante turba facilè, & audiretur & intelligeretur, sic orabat: Domine Iesu Christe, crudelissimum hoc atque horrendum supplicium, propter sanctum Evangelium tuum, ac sacri verbi praedicationè, libens & humiliter pati volo, tu autem omnibus inimicis meis ignosce precor. A lictoribus circunductus, omnes hortabatur, ne crederent se ulli errorum esse obnoxium, quos vel docueret, vel adsereret, sed falso sibi adscriptos esse, ac falsis testibus firmatos.
units.tr: Then he, raised up at the command of the executioner and the lictors, prayed in a clear voice, so that the crowd standing around could easily hear and understand him: "Lord Jesus Christ, I am willing and humbly ready to suffer this most cruel and horrible death for the sake of your holy Gospel and the preaching of your sacred Word. But I pray you, forgive all my enemies." Led around by the lictors, he urged everyone not to believe that he was guilty of any errors that he had taught or asserted, but that these had been falsely attributed to him and confirmed by false witnesses.

units.la: Tandem petijt ab eis, ut liceret sibi carceris sui custodes alloqui. Quibus ubi ad eum accessere, inquit: Gratias vobis ago fratres mei dilectissimi, de omnibus beneficijs, quae contulistis in me. nam fratres mihi charissimi fuistis, nedum custodes mei.Ac scitote, quod constàter[?] credo Salvatori meo, cuius nomine hoc genus mortis aequo animo volo perferre, certò confisus me hodie cum ipso fore in paradiso. Id verò Germanicè ad eos locutus est.
units.tr: At last he asked that he be allowed to speak to his prison guards. When they came up to him, he said: "I give you thanks, my dearest brothers, for all the kindnesses you have shown me. For you have been most dear brothers to me, not merely my guards. And know that I firmly believe in my Saviour, in whose name I am willing to endure this kind of death with a calm mind, confidently trusting that today I shall be with him in paradise." He said this in German, speaking to them.

units.la: Mox ipsum ad quendam crassum ac perforatum asserem manibus obuersis, sex aut septem funibus durissimè alligarunt. Ac primus proximè talos, deinde sub genibus, mox supra genua, praeterea iuxta inguina, sextus medium corpus vinciebat, postremus sub brachijs. Porrò asser ille terrae intrusus ac infixus stabat.
units.tr: Soon they tied him, with his hands behind him, to a thick plank full of holes, binding him very tightly with six or seven ropes. The first bound his ankles, the second below the knees, the third above the knees, the fourth near the groin, the fifth the middle of his body, and the last under his arms. The plank was driven into the ground and fixed upright.

units.la: Sed quosdam ibi astantes male habebat, quòd constitutus esset facie ad orientem versa. iubent igitur, ut occasum versus vultu obverteretur, esse enim haereticum. id quod statim factum est. Ad haec ipsius cervix alligata erat huic asseri atra quadam catena, ac fuligine obducta, quippe ex qua forte quispiam antea ahenum appenderat. quum ubi Husius capite paulùm reflexo vidit in haec verprorupit, Dominus Iesus Christus ille redemptor meus ac saluator charissimus, longè crudeliore ac duriore catena propter me vinctus erat, cur igitur ego miser erubescam, propter ipsius nomen sacrosanctum hac fuliginosa constringi ? Porrò ipsius pedibus (ocreatis etiamnum, & vno copede cinctis) duos lignorum fasces supposuerunt. Hic cum quendam rusticum conspiceret ligna adferentem, blandè subrisit, atque hæc verba D. Hieronymi dicere protulit: Sancta simplicitas. Tandem his undique Hussium ceruicetenus, mistis straminibus circumsepserunt.
units.tr: But some of those standing there were troubled that he had been placed facing east. So they ordered him to turn his face toward the west, since facing east was heretical, and this was done at once. Moreover, his neck was fastened to this plank by a black chain covered with soot, since perhaps someone had once hung a cauldron from it. When Hus, turning his head slightly, saw this, he exclaimed: "The Lord Jesus Christ, my redeemer and most dear saviour, was bound for me with a far crueler and harsher chain; why then should I, wretch that I am, be ashamed to be bound with this sooty thing for the sake of his holy name?" Then they placed two bundles of wood under his feet (he still wore his leggings, and was bound with one fetter). When he saw a country man bringing wood, he smiled kindly and spoke these words of St. Jerome: "Holy simplicity!" At last they heaped mixed straw around Hus on all sides, up to his neck.

units.la: Et priusquam ligna incensa essent, accessit ad eum ciuitatum Imperialium quidam, quem vulgo Marschalcum vocant, vna cum Clemetis filio, Hussium exhortando, vt seruadæ suæ vitæ causa, adhuc dogmata sua & conciones retractaret & abiuraret.
units.tr: Before the wood was lit, a certain man from the imperial cities, commonly called the Marshal, came to him together with Clement's son, urging Hus, for the sake of saving his life, to still retract and abjure his teachings and sermons.

units.la: Tum ille cælum suspiciens, alta voce respodit: Deum testor, ea quibus me per falsos testes insimulant, numquam me nec docuisse, necscripsisse, sed conciones nostras, dogmata, & scripta, denique omnia opera eo animo instituimus, ac ad eum scopu direximus, quo mortales à tyrannide peccati eriperemus. Quapropter veritate eam, quam docui, scripsi, & vulgavi, lege diuina, ac doctoribus sanctis firmatam, hodie lætus hoc mortis pignore obsignare volo. Quo audito, Ludouicus cū Collega suo manibus complosis, ab eo discedunt.
units.tr: Then he, looking up to heaven, answered in a loud voice: "I call God to witness that the things they charge me with through false witnesses I never taught or wrote. Rather, we established our sermons, teachings, writings, and indeed all our works with the purpose and aim of rescuing mortals from the tyranny of sin. Therefore, the truth that I taught, wrote, and published, confirmed by divine law and holy teachers, I today gladly wish to seal with this pledge of death." When they heard this, Louis and his colleague clapped their hands and withdrew from him.

units.la: Ac carnifices statim pyram accendunt, Hussius verò præalta voce exclamauit semel atque iterum: Christe fili Dei viui, miserere mei. Tertio canentem: Qui natus es ex Virgine, ventus repente obortus, flamma eum præfocauit, atque ita coticuit. Ac interea tam diu nutabat capite, ac ora mouebat, dum quispiam Dominicam orationem bis aut ter repetendo absoluere posset. Deinde ita tacitus intra se orans, emisit spiritum.
units.tr: The executioners immediately lit the pyre, and Hus cried out in a loud voice, once and again: "Christ, Son of the living God, have mercy on me." When he began singing a third time, "Who was born of the Virgin," a sudden wind arose, the flame smothered him, and he fell silent. Meanwhile he kept nodding his head and moving his lips for as long as someone could recite the Lord's Prayer two or three times. Then, praying silently within himself, he gave up his spirit.

units.la: Porrò vbi fasces lignorum ambusti ccidissent [?], ac corpus ipsius ad asserem catena ligatum hæreret, tortores id cum affere in ignem intruserunt fustibus, ac tum circumcurrentes, ligna aggerebant, cadauer vrentes. Ibi videas carnificum exquisitā in singula membra crudelitatem. Nam proh dolor, ipsius ossa fustibus comminuentes tundebant, quo citius igne absumerentur. Deinde caput inuentum palo dissecuerunt. Porrò cor in intestinis repertum, ac veru ligneo acuminatóque infixum inter comburedum [?] fustibus cædebant. Interea carnifex quidam vestem Hussij tenebat, Ludouicus autem simulatque cognouit esse tunicam Hussij, vsurit [?] eam ac cingulum, denique quicquid ipsius esset effet inijcere in ignem, dicens: Bohemi enim id vice sacramenti haberent ac colerent. deinde carnifici pollicitus est iacturam hanc compensaturum esse. Postremò omnia igne in cinerem concremata, cum pulvere ac terra altius effossa in bigas imposuere, deinde in Rhenum praeterlabentem disiecerunt, quo ipsius nomen prorsus apud fideles extinguerent, ne vel tenuissimus pulvis in terra superesset eius viri: cuius tamen memoria neque igne, neque aqua, neque vllo genere supplicij ex animis piorum vnquam poterit aboleri.
units.tr: When the bundles of wood had burned down and his body, still bound with a chain to the plank, hung there, the torturers thrust the plank with the body into the fire with poles, and then, running around, heaped on more wood, burning the corpse. There you might see the executioners' elaborate cruelty against each limb. For, alas, they beat his bones with clubs, crushing them so that they would be consumed by the fire more quickly. Then they found his head and split it with a stake. The heart, found among the entrails and fixed on a pointed wooden spit, they beat with clubs while it burned. Meanwhile one executioner held Hus's clothing, and Louis, as soon as he recognised it as Hus's tunic, seized it, along with the belt, and ordered whatever belonged to him to be thrown into the fire, saying: "The Bohemians would hold these things as a kind of sacrament and worship them." He then promised the executioner that he would make up for this loss. Finally, when everything had been burned to ashes, they gathered the ashes together with the dust and the earth dug up deeper, loaded them into carts, and threw them into the Rhine flowing past, so that they might utterly extinguish his name among the faithful and not even the finest dust of that man would remain on earth. Yet his memory can never be erased from the minds of the pious by fire, water, or any kind of punishment.

units.la: Habes, Christiane Lector, historiam confessionis & mortis Ioannis Husii nostra memoria protomartyris: in qua ne quid fictum aut commentitum credas, αὐτόπτης[?] testis cauit in hanc sententiam.
units.tr: You have, Christian reader, the history of the confession and death of John Hus, the first martyr of our memory. So that you may not believe anything in it to be fictitious or made up, an eyewitness has testified to this effect.

units.la: Haec scio admodum tenuiter à me perscripta esse, de Ioannis Hus, Martyris sanctissimi laboribus, cum quibus illi Herculei nullo modo sunt comparandi. Hercules enim ille vetus, pauca quaedam monstra confecit: hic vero noster Hercules, fortissimo animo omnium monstrorum & immanissimarum bestiarum matrem, mundum ipsum superauit. Digna erat res alio quodam genere orationis magis eleganti. Ego vero, cum praestare aliud non possem, veritate ipsa volui, ea quae complexus sum, piis animis commendare. Neque enim ab aliis accepi, sed ipse his omnibus interfui, atque ita vt potui, literis mandaui, vt sanctissimi viri & egregij veritatis Euangelicae Doctoris memoriâ, qualicunque hoc meo officio conseruarem.
units.tr: I know that what I have written about the labours of John Hus, the most holy martyr, has been set down very meagrely by me, and that those Herculean labours cannot be compared with his in any way. For that ancient Hercules overcame only a few monsters; but this our Hercules, with the most courageous spirit, overcame the mother of all monsters and most savage beasts, the world itself. The matter deserved a more elegant kind of discourse. I, however, since I could do nothing else, wished to commend what I have gathered to pious minds by the truth itself. For I did not receive these things from others, but was myself present at all of them, and as best I could I committed them to writing, so that by this humble duty of mine I might preserve the memory of that most holy man and distinguished teacher of the Evangelical truth.

units.la: EX MULTIS EPISTOLIS QUAS IOANNES HUS SCRIPTAS RELIQUIT, SE- legimus has sequentes, plenas pietatis, consolationum & prophetici spiritus.
units.tr: FROM THE MANY LETTERS THAT JOHN HUS LEFT BEHIND, we read the following, full of piety, consolation and prophetic spirit.

units.la: EPISTOLAM SEQUENTEM RELIQUIT BO- hemis Ioannes Hus, dum ei ad concilium proficiscendum esset, in vul- gari Bohemico scriptam.
units.tr: A LETTER THAT JOHN HUS LEFT FOR THE BOHEMIANS, WRITTEN IN THE VULGAR BOHEMIAN TONGUE, when he was about to set out for the council.

units.la: Ea fuit variè versa Latinè ab aduersariis, scilicet ut damnum daret Husio, in concilio.
units.tr: His adversaries translated it into Latin in various ways, namely so as to do harm to Hus at the council.

units.la: F[?]IDELES & dilecti fratres, scitis quòd longo iam tempore bona fide vos instituì, docès vos verbum domini Dei, non res alienas à fide Christi, non doctrinam falsam. nam ego semper quaesiui, quaero, & quaeram quoad vixero, vestram salutem. Constitucram[?] quidem vobis loqui verbum Dei, antequam migrarem ad concilium Constantiense: deinde confutare falsa testimonia & testes falsos, quibus testimoniis atque testibus volunt me perducere ad supplicium: sed temporis inopia nihil tale permittere mihi videbatur, quod tamen post faciam. Proinde vos qui haec de me scitis, nolite credere, nolite suspicari, me ob vllam falsam doctrinam indignis modis tractandum esse. Manete in veritate, fidentes misericordiae Dei, quam veritatem dedit vobis Deus, & cognoscendam & defendendam per me fidum concionatorem vestrum. Et cauete falsos concionatores. Ego proficiscar nunc cum literis publicae fidei, a Rege mihi datis, ad multos & maximos inimicos meos, id quod luce clarius apparebit dum hostiliter astantes aduersum me falsum testimonium daturi sunt. Porro, in ipso concilio plures erunt inimici mei, quam fuerunt aduersus Saluatorem nostrum, primum ex Episcopis & magistris, deinde etiam ex Principibus huius saeculi, & ex Pharisaeis. Verum ego confido Deo saluatori meo omnipotenti, quod propter suam promissionem, & propter vestram ardentem orationem, daturus sit mihi prudentiam & os eruditum, ita ut eis resistere valeam. Praeterea etiam Spiritu sanctu suu[?] , ut possim perdurare in eius veritate, adeo ut nullae inferorum portae queant me ab ea auellere. Item dabit, ut possim esse contemptore animo aduersus tentationes, carcerem, & supplicium dirae mortis. Quemadmodum videmus Christum ipsum passum esse propter dilectos suos, nimirum relinquens nobis exemplum, ut propter ipsum nostramque salutem patienter omnia sufferamus, ipse enim est Deus, nos creaturae eius: ipse Dominus, nos serui eius, ipse vniuersi mundi Dominus, & nos homunculi infirmi eius, ipse nulla re egens, nos egetes: ipse passus, cur & nos non pateremur? praesertim quum nostra passio sit purgatio peccatorum? Profecto impossibile est ut pereat, quicunque in eum crediderit, & permanserit in eius veritate. Proinde dilecti, orate instanter, si modo sit ad eius gloriam, ut det mihi spiritum, qui efficiat, ut constantem in eius veritate, & liberet me ab omni iniquitate. Porro si mea mors illustratura est eius gloriam, accelerat eam, atque det gratiam, ut aequo animo, hoc quicquid est mali, perferre queam. Si vero salutis meae magis commodum fuerit, ut ad vos reuertar, hoc rogabimus Deum, ut ad concilium profectus, reuertar sine iniquitate, hoc est,ne quid imminuam de Euangelij Iesu Christi veritate,adeò vt valeamus eius veritatem purius subinde agnoscere, & Antichristi doctrinam extirpare,nostrisque fratribus bonum exemplū, quod bonestè imitentur,relinquere. Iam forte Pragæ me porrò non visuri estis. Si autem omnipotens Deus,pro sua voluntate dignabitur me reddere vobis,animo eò hilariore in lege Dei proficiemus:maximè verò quū in æterna gloria congregati fuerimus. Deus est misericors & iustus, & dat pacem suis hìc & post mortem. Custodiat vos,qui purgauit nos omnes suas sancto suo atque pretioso sanguine, qui sanguis est salutis nostræ testis æternus: & largiatur vobis,vt possitis implere eius voluntatem,& cùm ei satisfeceritis[?],vt pacem habeatis & gloriam æternam, per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, qui est Deus perpetuus, & homo verus, natus ex Maria virgine. Cui est gloria & erit in perpetuum,cum omnibus qui permanserint in eius veritate.
units.tr: Faithful and beloved brethren, you know that for a long time I have instructed you in good faith, teaching you the word of the Lord God, not foreign matters alien to the faith of Christ, nor false doctrine. For I have always sought, I seek, and I will seek as long as I live, your salvation. I had intended to speak the word of God to you before I departed to the Council of Constance, and then to refute the false testimonies and false witnesses by whom they wish to bring me to punishment. But the shortness of time seemed to me to forbid any such thing, though I will do it afterwards. Therefore you who know these things about me, do not believe or suspect that I am to be treated shamefully on account of any false doctrine. Remain in the truth, trusting in the mercy of God, who gave you this truth to know and to defend through me, your faithful preacher. And beware of false preachers. I now set out with a letter of public safe-conduct given to me by the King, to face many and great enemies of mine, which will become clearer than daylight, while they stand over me in hostility, ready to give false testimony against me. Moreover, in the council itself my enemies will be more numerous than those who opposed our Saviour: first from the bishops and masters, then also from the princes of this age, and from the Pharisees. But I trust in God my almighty Saviour, that, because of his promise and because of your fervent prayer, he will give me wisdom and a learned mouth, so that I may be able to resist them. Likewise, by his Holy Spirit, that I may persevere in his truth, so that no gates of hell may tear me away from it. He will also grant that I may be of a mind that despises temptations, prison, and the punishment of a dreadful death. Just as we see that Christ himself suffered for his beloved, leaving us the example that, for his sake and for our own salvation, we should patiently endure all things. For he is God and we are his creatures; he is Lord and we are his servants; he is the Lord of the whole world and we are his weak little men; he, needing nothing, and we, in need. He suffered: why should we not suffer too, especially since our suffering is the cleansing of sins? Surely it is impossible that anyone perish who believes in him and remains in his truth. Therefore, beloved, pray earnestly, if it is for his glory, that he give me a spirit that makes me steadfast in his truth and frees me from all iniquity. Moreover, if my death is to illustrate his glory, let him hasten it and grant me the grace to bear with an even mind whatever evil this may be. But if it should be more profitable for my salvation that I return to you, we will ask God that, having gone to the council, I may return without iniquity, that is, without diminishing in any way the truth of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, so that we may recognize his truth ever more purely, root out the doctrine of Antichrist, and leave our brethren a good example to imitate honorably. Perhaps you will not see me again in Prague. But if almighty God, according to his will, deigns to restore me to you, we will advance in the law of God with a more cheerful heart, especially when we have been gathered together in eternal glory. God is merciful and just, and gives peace to his own here and after death. May he keep you, who has cleansed us all with his holy and precious blood, which is the eternal witness of our salvation; and may he grant you to fulfil his will, and, when you have satisfied him, to have peace and eternal glory, through our Lord Jesus Christ, who is perpetual God and true man, born of the virgin Mary. To him be glory, and it shall be forever, with all who remain in his truth.

units.la: ALIA AD POPVLVM SCRIPTA EPISTOLA, è vulgari versa.
units.tr: ANOTHER LETTER WRITTEN TO THE PEOPLE, translated from the vernacular.

units.la: CHARISSIMI, rogo vos qui iuxta legem Dei inceditis, ne abiciatis curam salutis animarum vestrarum, cùm verbum Dei audientes intelligatis, ne pseudoapostoli vos decipiant, qui hominum peccata non reprehendunt, sed cleuant. Præsbyteris blandiuntur, populi peccata non ostendunt, seipsos magnificiant, sua opera prædicant, ij virtutem suam mirificè extollunt, sed Christum dominum in humilitate, inopia, cruce, & multifariis afflictionibus imitari non dignantur. De quibus prædixit clementissimus Salvator, inquiens, Surgent pseudochristi & pseudoprophetæ, multósque seducent. Et cùm dilectos suos præmonens, ait, Cauete vobis à pseudoprophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestitu ouium, sed intrinsecus sunt lupi rapaces: à fructibus ipsorum agnoscetis eos. Et quidè valdè opus est Christi fidelib°[?], vt diligeter[?] sibi caveat ac prospiciat. nam vt Salvator ipse dicit, Etiā electi, si fieri posset, in errore inducentur. Proinde dilectissimi vigilate, ne diaboli insidiis circumueniamini. Eò autem circunspectiores vos esse oportet, quò magis vobis Antichristus negotium facessit. Iudicium extremum prope est, mors absorbet multos: at electis Dei filijs appropinquat regnū Dei, quia pro illis tradidit corpus suum. Ne timeatis mortem, diligite vos invicem, perseuerate in intelligentia bonæ voluntatis Dei, sine intermissione, dies iudicij terribilis & horrendus semper vobis ob oculos versetur, ne peccetis: deinde vitæ æternæ gaudium, ad quod vobis enitendum est. Præterea passio Saluatoris nostri, ut cum ipso & pro ipso libenter, quicquid fit, feratis. Nam si illius afflictiones & crucem animo reputabitis, nihil vobis graue accidet, & libenter locum dabitis tribulationibus, maledictis, conuiciis, verberibus & vinculis, ut si res postulet, vitam pro sanctissima ipsius veritate impendere non dubitetis. Scitote charissimi, Antichristum in vos irritatum, varias excogitare persecutiones: multis autem nec pilo quidē nocuit, quæ madmodum meo exemplo docere possum, quantumuis vehementer mihi sit infensus. Quapropter vos omnes rogo, ut precibus vestris apud Deum pro me intercedatis, quo mihi intelligentiam, tolerantiam, patientiam & constantiam, ne unquam a divina eius veritate desciscam, suppeditet. Ille me jam Constantiam perduxit. In toto autem itinere aperte & manifeste, ut Dei seruum decet, nomen meum professus sum, nullibi occultus egi: sed non alio loco pestilentiores ac manifestiores hostes offendi, quos nec ibi habuissem, nisi Bohemici nonulli impostores, ob beneficia accepta, & auaritia capti, ostentantes, persuasissent me populum a certa via seducere. Sed bona me spes habet, fore ut per misericordiam Saluatoris nostri, & ve-stras orationes, in irrefragabili Dei veritate usque ad extremum spiritum fortiter perdurem.
units.tr: Dearly beloved, I ask you who walk according to the law of God not to abandon care for the salvation of your souls, and, when you hear the word of God, to understand it, so that false apostles do not deceive you. They do not rebuke people's sins but flatter them. They fawn on the elders, do not point out the sins of the people, magnify themselves, proclaim their own works, and extol their power wonderfully, but they do not deign to imitate Christ the Lord in humility, poverty, the cross and manifold afflictions. Of such the most merciful Saviour foretold, saying: "False Christs and false prophets will arise and will lead many astray." And warning his beloved ones, he said: "Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravening wolves; you will know them by their fruits." Indeed, the faithful of Christ very much need to take diligent heed and watch over themselves, for, as the Saviour himself says, "even the elect, if it were possible, would be led into error." Therefore, most beloved, watch, lest you be ensnared by the wiles of the devil. You ought to be all the more wary because Antichrist is busily at work against you. The last judgement is near; death swallows up many; but the kingdom of God draws near to the elect children of God, because he gave his body for them. Do not fear death; love one another; persevere without ceasing in the understanding of the good will of God; let the dreadful and terrible day of judgement always be before your eyes, so that you do not sin; and then the joy of eternal life, to which you must strive. Moreover, the passion of our Saviour: whatever happens, bear it willingly, with him and for him. For if you consider his afflictions and cross in your mind, nothing grievous will befall you, and you will gladly give way to tribulations, curses, reproaches, blows and chains, and will not hesitate, if the matter requires it, to lay down your life for his most holy truth. Know, dearly beloved, that Antichrist, enraged against you, is devising various persecutions; yet to many he has not done the least harm, as I can show by my own example, however fiercely he is set against me. Therefore I ask you all to intercede for me in your prayers before God, that he may grant me understanding, endurance, patience and steadfastness, so that I never fall away from his divine truth. He has now brought me to Constance. On the whole journey I have openly and plainly professed my name, as becomes a servant of God; I have acted nowhere in hiding. But I have met no more pestilent and open enemies anywhere else than here, and I would not have had them here had not some Bohemian impostors, won over by benefits received and seized by greed, persuaded me that I was leading the people away from the sure path. But I have good hope that, through the mercy of our Saviour and your prayers, I shall persevere bravely in the unshakable truth of God even to my last breath.

units.la: Magister Joannes Hus seruus Dei in spe.
units.tr: Master John Hus, servant of God in hope.

units.la: Acta sunt hæc anno Domini M.CCCC.XV. Constantiæ in carcere apud Minores.
units.tr: These things were done in the year of the Lord 1415, at Constance, in prison at the Minorites'.

units.la: HANC EPISTOLAM SCRIPSIT IOANNES HUS propria manu Constantiæ, in carcere, ad commonefaciendum & con- solandum Regem atque regnum Bohemiæ, ne deserant veram doctri- nam Euangelii.
units.tr: JOHN HUS WROTE THIS LETTER with his own hand at Constance, in prison, to admonish and console the King and the kingdom of Bohemia, that they not abandon the true doctrine of the Gospel.

units.la: M[?]agister Joannes Hussius, in spe seruus Dei, omnes fideles Bohemos, qui diligunt Deum, optat in gratia Dei esse & mori, tandemque peruenire ad vitam æternam. Amen.
units.tr: Master John Hus, in hope a servant of God, wishes all the faithful Bohemians who love God to be and to die in the grace of God, and at last to come to eternal life. Amen.

units.la: Qui præestis aliis, diuitésque & pauperes in Deo dilecti & fideles, obsecro vos & moneo, ut Deo obtemperetis, verbum eius magnisicetis[?], & libenter audiendo, re ipsa praestetis. Obsecro, ut adhaereatis veritati Dei, quam ex lege eius & sermonibus Sanctorum scripsi & concionatus sum. Obsecro etiam, si quispiam, sive in publicis concionibus, sive in colloquutionibus privatis, aliquid a me audiverit, aut scriptum legerit, quod sit contra veritatem Dei, ne id sequatur, quanquam nihil unquam huiusmodi me vel loquutū esse, vel scripsisse mihi conscius sum. Obsecro praeterea, si quis leuitatem, sive in sermone meo, sive in moribus aliquando animadverterit, ne illam imitetur, sed oret pro me Deū, ut id peccatum leuitatis nubi condonet. Obsecro, ut sacerdotes bonorum morum amétis, praeferatis aliis & honoretis, praecipuè eos qui in verbo Dei desudant. Obsecro, ut caveatis vobis a fraudulentis hominibus, maximeque a sacerdotibus impiis, de quibus Salvator dicit, quod sint in vestitu ovium, intrinsecus autem lupi rapaces. Obsecro dominos, ut suos subditos pauperes tractet humaniter, reddantque iustè. Obsecro cives, ut in suo genere vitae, cū conscientia bona versentur. Obsecro opifices, ut sua artificia diligenter exerceant, ut eis cum timore Dei vtantur. Obsecro seruos, ut suis heris fideliter serviant. Obsecro magistros, ut ipsi honestè viuentes, discipulos suos bene & bona fide instituant, doceántque eos, primum ut Deum timere discant, deinde propter gloriam Dei & utilitatem rerū publicarū, propriamque salutem: non autem propter auaritiam & huius mundi honores, in honestas disciplinas incumbant. Obsecro studiosos scholae publicae, & omnes alios scholasticos, ut in honestis rebus omnibus obtemperent suis magistris, eósque imitentur, utque cum magna diligentia studeant, quo utiles esse possint ad gloriam Dei illustrandam, & ad salutem tum suam, tū aliorum hominum. Obsecro vos simul omnes, ut generosis dominis, domino Bohuslao Dubensi, domino Ioani Chlumensi, domino Henrico Plumlouio, domino Vylemo Zagecio, domino Nicolao, & aliis dominis Bohemis, Moravis & Polonis, gratias agatis, vtque vobis omnibus grata sit eorum sedulitas: propterea quòd tanquam strenui defensores Dei veritatis, opposuerunt se saepius toti illi concilio, pro liberatione mea omnibus viribus cū eo cōtendentes, praefertim D. wenceslaus Dubensis & Ioānes Chlumensis. Illis, quaecunque referent, fidem habete. illi nanque erant in concilio, quum respondebam per plures dies. Illi sciunt, qui Bohemi, & quam multa & indigna aduersum me protulerint: quo pacto congregatio illa contra me vociferabatur. Ego autem, vt dabā[?] responsa ad omnia de quibus interrogabar. Obsecro vos etiam, vt pro rege Romanorum & vestro eiusque vxore Regina vestra, Deum oretis, vt misericors Deus cum illis & vobiscum maneat nunc, & deinde in vita aeterna, Amen.
units.tr: You who are set over others, rich and poor, beloved and faithful in God, I beg and admonish you to obey God, to hold his word in esteem, and by listening gladly to put it into practice. I beg you to cling to the truth of God, which I have written and preached from his law and the sermons of the saints. I beg also that, if anyone has heard anything from me, whether in public sermons or in private conversations, or has read anything I have written that is contrary to the truth of God, he not follow it, although I am conscious of never having said or written anything of the kind. I beg further that, if anyone has at any time noticed lightness in my speech or in my conduct, he not imitate it, but pray God for me, that he may pardon that sin of lightness in his mercy. I beg you to love priests of good morals, to prefer and honour them above others, especially those who labour in the word of God. I beg you to beware of deceitful men, and above all of impious priests, of whom the Saviour says that they are in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravening wolves. I beg masters to treat their poor subjects humanely and to deal justly with them. I beg citizens to live in their own station with a good conscience. I beg craftsmen to carry out their trades diligently, so that they use them with the fear of God. I beg servants to serve their masters faithfully. I beg teachers, living honourably themselves, to instruct their pupils well and in good faith, and to teach them first to learn to fear God, then to apply themselves to honourable studies for the glory of God, the benefit of the commonwealth and their own salvation, and not for greed and the honours of this world. I beg the students of the public school and all other scholars to obey their masters in all honourable matters, to imitate them, and to study with great diligence, so that they may be useful for the glory of God and for the salvation both of themselves and of other people. I beg you all together to give thanks to the noble lords: Lord Bohuslaus of Duba, Lord John of Chlum, Lord Henry of Plumlov, Lord Wilhelm of Zagec, Lord Nicholas, and the other Bohemian, Moravian and Polish lords; and may their diligence be welcome to all of you, because, like brave defenders of the truth of God, they have often opposed that whole council, contending with it with all their might for my release, especially Lord Wenceslaus of Duba and John of Chlum. Put your trust in whatever they report, for they were in the council when I was answering over several days. They know, as Bohemians, how many and how unworthy the charges were that were brought against me, and how that assembly clamoured against me. As for me, I gave answers to everything I was asked. I beg you also to pray to God for the King of the Romans and for your own king, and for his wife, your queen, that merciful God may remain with them and with you now, and afterwards in eternal life. Amen.

units.la: Hanc epistolam scripsi vobis ex carcere & in vinculis, expectans postridie huius diei, qua scripta est, concilij sententiam de morte mea, habensque plenam fiduciam in Deo, quod non deseret me, neque sinet me veritatem suam abnegare, & errores, quos contra me falsi testes malitiosè commenti sunt, reuocare. Quàm clementer dominus Deus mecum agat, mecumque sit in mirabilibus tentationibus, cognoscetis, cum in gaudio futuri seculi, auxilio Christi vnà conueniemus. De magistro Hieronymo, dilecto socio meo, non aliud audio, quàm quòd in vinculis duris detineatur, expectans mortem, quemadmodum & ego, idque propter fidem, quam gnauiter Bohemis ostendebat. Bohemi vero crudelissimi nostri hostes, tradiderunt nos in aliorum hostium potestate & vincula. Obsecro vt pro illis Deum oretis. Adhæc obsecro vos, præcipuè Pragenses, vt templū Bethlemiticū ametis, defisque[?] operam, quàdiu Deus concesserit, vt in eo verbū Dei concionetur. Propter illum enim locum satanas iratus est, & contra illum parochos & canonicos concitauit, animaduertens quòd in eo regnum suum infirmaretur. Spero in Deum, quòd illam ædem sacram seruabit, quandiu volet, faciétque in ea profectu verbi sui maiorem per alios, quàm fecit per me imbecillem. Obsecro etiā, vt vos mutuò diligatis, & neminē prohibetes à veritate Dei, curetis ne probi vi opprimantur. Data die Lunæ, noctu ante Viti, per bonum & fidum Germanum.
units.tr: I have written this letter to you from prison and in chains, awaiting the decision of the council about my death, which will be on the day after the day on which this was written, and I have full confidence in God that he will not forsake me, nor allow me to deny his truth or to recant the errors which false witnesses have maliciously invented against me. You will know how mercifully the Lord God deals with me, and whether he is with me in my wonderful trials, when we meet together with Christ in the joy of the age to come. Of Master Jerome, my dear companion, I hear nothing except that he is held in harsh chains, awaiting death as I am, and that for the faith which he bravely showed to the Bohemians. But the Bohemians, our most cruel enemies, have handed us over into the power and chains of other enemies. I beg you to pray to God for them. Furthermore, I beg you, especially the people of Prague, to love the Bethlehem chapel, and to take care, for as long as God allows, that the word of God be preached in it. For Satan is angry on account of that place, and has stirred up the parish priests and canons against it, perceiving that his kingdom is weakened there. I hope in God that he will preserve that holy building for as long as he wishes, and will make his word advance in it more through others than he did through me, a feeble man. I beg you also to love one another, and, hindering no one from the truth of God, to take care that the upright are not oppressed by force. Given on Monday, the night before St Vitus, through the good and faithful German.

units.la: Hac Epistola ostendit suis, cur Deus non patiatur perire suos, afferens varia exempla.
units.tr: This letter shows his people why God does not allow his own to perish, setting out various examples.

units.la: D[?]eus vobiscum. Multæ causæ, charissimi in Deo dilecti amici, in eam opinionem me adduxerunt, vt literas, quas proximè ad vos dedi, postremas esse putarem, propter instantem mortem. Nunc autem cognita eius dilatione, ducens loco oblectationis, quòd licet mihi vobifcum per literas colloqui, iterum vobis scribo, vt sic saltem mea erga vos ostendam gratitudinem. Quòd autem ad mortem attinet, Deus nouit cur differat & meam, & mei charissimi fratris magistri Hieronymi, quem spero sanctè & sine culpa moriturum: scióque nunc etiam magis strenuè eum agere & pati, quàm me miserum peccatore.Concessit nobis Deus longum tempus, vt melius peccata nostra nobis in memoriam reduceremus, & ageremus fortiori animo pœnitentiam. Concessit nobis tempus, vt longa & magna tentatio delere grauia peccata, & adferet consolationem. Concessit nobis tempus, in quo recoleremus nostri regis, domini nostri Iesu Christi misericordis horrenda opprobria, & pensitaremus crudelem mortem, sicque æquiori animo mala perferremus: præterea, vt in memoria teneremus, non dari immediatè gaudia vitæ futuræ, post gaudia huius mundi: sed quòd per multas tribulationes Sancti intrauerunt in regnum cælestè. Quidam enim eorum sunt frustatim concisi, quidam terebrati, alij cœsi, nonnulli assati, alij viui excoriati, viui terra obruti, lapidati, cruci affixi, triti inter molares lapides, huc atque illuc tracti vsque ad necè, in aquis submersi, combusti, laqueo suffocati, frustatim decerpti, & ante mortem probris affecti, macerati in carceribus & vinculis: & quis poterit omnia omnium Sanctorum tormenta ac supplicia describere, quæ sub veteri & nouo Testamento propter veritatem Dei pertulerunt, præcipuè, qui sacerdotum malitiam exprobrauerunt, & contra illam sunt concionati?mirúmque erit, si quis etiam nunc impunè feret, fortiter resistendo peruersitati, præsertim sacerdotum, quæ non patitur reprehensionem. Et gaudeo, quòd iam meos libros coacti sunt legere, in quibus malitia eorum vtcunque depicta est. Scióque quòd eos perlegerunt accuratius, quàm sacrum Euangelium, volentes inuenire errores. O piissime Christe, trahe nos debiles post te: da Spiritum promptum, cor impauidum, fidem certam, spem firmam, charitatem perfectam, vt pro te exponamus patientissimè & cum gaudio vitam nostram, Amen.
units.tr: God be with you. Many reasons, dearest friends beloved in God, have led me to think that the letter I sent you most recently would be my last, because of my impending death. But now that its postponement is known, I take it as a comfort that I may talk with you by letter again, and so I write to you once more, so that at least in this way I may show my gratitude toward you. As for death, God knows why he delays both mine and that of my dearest brother, Master Jerome, whom I hope will die holily and without fault. And I know that he now acts and suffers more vigorously than I, a wretched sinner. God has granted us a long time so that we might better call our sins back to memory and undertake repentance with a stronger spirit. He has granted us time so that a long and great trial might blot out grave sins and bring consolation. He has granted us time in which we might recall the dreadful reproaches endured by our King and Lord Jesus Christ, and weigh his cruel death, and so bear evils with a more even mind. Moreover, he has given us time to keep in memory that the joys of the future life do not come immediately after the joys of this world, but that the saints entered the heavenly kingdom through many tribulations. For some of them were cut to pieces, some bored through, others beaten, some roasted, others flayed alive, some buried alive in the earth, stoned, fixed to the cross, ground between millstones, dragged hither and thither until death, drowned in water, burned, strangled with a noose, torn apart piece by piece, and before death abused with insults, wasted away in prisons and chains. And who can describe all the torments and punishments of all the saints, which they endured under the Old and New Testament for the sake of God's truth, especially those who denounced the wickedness of the priests and preached against it? It will be a marvel if anyone even now goes unpunished, resisting strongly a perversity that, especially among the priests, will not suffer reproof. And I rejoice that they have now been forced to read my books, in which their wickedness is in some measure depicted. And I know that they have read them more carefully than the holy Gospel, wishing to find errors. O most merciful Christ, draw us weak ones after you; give us a ready spirit, a fearless heart, a certain faith, a firm hope, and perfect charity, so that we may for your sake give up our lives most patiently and with joy. Amen.

units.la: Scriptum in carcere. Ioannes Hus in spe seruus Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Written in prison. John Hus, in hope a servant of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Confirmat suos hac epistola, ne terreantur propterea quòd eius libros igni tradendos iudicauerit concilium.
units.tr: He strengthens his people by this letter, so that they will not be terrified because the council has judged that his books should be handed over to the fire.

units.la: Monendos[?] vos esse duxi, charissimi, ne paueatis, neue terreamini, eo quod aduersarij libros meos comburendos decreuerint. Sitis.memores, quomodo Hieremiæ Prophetæ conciones combusserint Israelitæ: non tamen quod in eis prophetatum erat, euitauerint. Post combustionem enim illarum, præcepit Deus eandem prophetiam, imo auctiorem conscribere, quod & factum est. Nam Hieremias in carcere sedens, dictabat, & Baruch, qui ei erat à manibus, excipiebat. Hoc scriptum est aut XXXV. aut XL. capite visionis Hieremiæ. Scriptum est etiam in libris Machabæorum, quod exurebant legem Dei impij, & eos, qui eam habuerant, trucidabant.
units.tr: I thought I should warn you, dearest ones, not to be afraid or terrified because our adversaries have decreed that my books are to be burned. Remember how the Israelites burned the sermons of the prophet Jeremiah, yet they did not avert what had been prophesied in them. For after their burning, God commanded that the same prophecy be written down again, indeed expanded, and this was done. For Jeremiah, sitting in prison, dictated, and Baruch, who was at his side, took it down. This is written in either chapter 35 or chapter 40 of the vision of Jeremiah. It is also written in the books of the Maccabees that the impious burned the law of God and slaughtered those who had kept it.

units.la: Post deinde sub nouo Testamento, Sanctos comburebant, cum libris Diuinæ legis. Cardinales condemnauerunt, & igni tradiderunt quosdam libros sancti Gregorij, & omnes tradidissent, nisi à Deo per Petrum, Gregorij ministrum, essent defensi. Sanctum Chrysostomum, licet duo concilia sacerdotum hæreticum pronuntiauerint, tamen misericors Deus eorum mendacium, post mortem illius aurei oris, fecit manifestum. Hæc habentes præ oculis, cauete ne præ timore meos libros non legatis, & tradatis eos aduersarijs ad comburendum. Mementote dicti Saluatoris clemetis, quo nos præmunitos esse voluit. Erit, inquit, ante diem iudicij tribulatio magna, qualis non fuit ab initio mundi, ad hoc vsque tempus, neque fiet: ita vt in errorem inducantur, si fieri possit, etiam electi Dei. Sed propter hos, decurtabitur dies illi. Horum memores, charissimi, sitis imperterriti. Confido enim in Deo, quod schola illa Antichristi vos reformidabit, sinetque esse quietos. Neque concilium Constantiense ad Bohemia proficiscetur. Nam puto multos ex illis, qui in eo sunt, prius morituros esse, quàm à vobis libros meos extorserint. Et ex concilio per partes mundi, huc atque illuc more ciconiarum dispergentur, cognoscentque adueniente hyeme, quod egerunt in æstate. Considerate quod suum caput Pap.æ[?], propter quædam horrenda scelera, dignum morte iudicauerunt. Agitedum, respondete ad hæc prædicatores, qui concionamini quod Papa sit deus terrestris, quod possit sacra diuendere, vt dicunt iurisperiti, quod sit caput totius Ecclesiæ sanctæ, eam optime administrando: quod sit cor Ecclesiæ, eam vivificando spiritualiter: quod sit fons ex quo promanat omnis virtus & bonitas: quòd sit sol Ecclesiæ sanctæ: quòd sit refugium tutissimum, ad quod quemlibet Christianum confugere oportet. En caput illud jam gladio amputatum, jam deus terre-stris vinctus, jam eius peccata palàm declarata, jam fons ille siccatus, sol obscuratus, cor extractum abiectúmque, ne quispiam ad illud refugiat. Concilium caput illud huius etiam scelcris[?] condemnauit, quòd indulgentias, episcopatus, & id genus alia diuendebat. Sed illi eum condemnauerunt judicio, quorum multi ab eo emptores talium rerum extiterant, & vicissim alijs eas vendendo, mercaturam exercuerunt. Aderat ibi Joannes episcopus Litomyslius, qui bis episcopatum Pragensem emere conabatur: sed alij eum anteuerterunt. O homines perditos! cur prius trabem ex oculo suo non eiecerunt, cum ius eorum dicat, Quisquis dignitatem aliquam argento consecutus fuerit, ea priuetur? Venditor igitur & emptor, quíque interponebat se illi contractui, palàm estote condemnati. Sic sanctus Petrus condemnauit & fecit anathema Simonem, volentem emere virtutem Spiritus sancti. Hi venditorem anathema fecerunt, & condemnauerunt, ipsi autem emptores & huius contractus assensores sunt sine periculo. Quid, quòd domi suæ mercatum hunc exercent? Constantiæ enim est unus Episcopus, qui emit, & alter qui vendidit. Papa autè, qui approbauit factum, ab utroque munera accepit. ita fit, ut scitis, etiam in Bohemia. Utinam dixisset Deus in concilio illo, Qui ex vobis est sine peccato, is ferat sententiam adversus Papam Joannem. procul dubio, alius post aliū[?] exiuisset. Cur ante hunc istius casum, genua ante eum flectebant, eius pedes osculabantur, sanctissimumque nominabant, cùm viderent hæreticum esse, homicidam esse, perditum peccatorem esse, quæ omnia de eo jam palàm fecerunt? Cur Cardinales in Papam eum elegerunt, cùm scirent ipsum occidisse patrem sanctissimum? Cur permiserunt ei in sacris negotiari tum, cùm jam Papæ officium sustinebat? nam ideo ei à consilijs sunt, ut eum recta moneant. annon & ipsi horum criminum æquè rei sunt ac ille? Quandoquidè hæc nonnulla vitia in eo ferebant, quorūdā autè participes erat: cur priusquā Constātia profugerat, nemo quicquā ausus est ei obiicere, sed omnes ut sanctissimum patrem metuebāt? Cùm autè secularis potestas[?], sic permittente aut volente Deo, cum comprehendissent, tu primum conspirauerunt, ne ullo modo a morte liberaretur. Jam certe malitia, abominatio, & turpitudo Antichristi reuelata est in Papa, & in aliis huius coetus. Jam fideles serui Dei possunt intelligere, verba quid sibi velint Saluatoris, qui dicit, Cum videritis abominationem desolationis, quae dicta est a Daniele, &c. qui potest capere capiat, certe abominatio maxima est superbia, avaritia, simonia, in loco deserto, hoc est, dignitate, quae est deserta a bonitate, ab humiliatate, & aliis virtutibus, ut nunc clare videmus in illis, qui constituti sunt in aliquo magistratu & dignitate. O quam gratum esset, si per tempus liceret mihi improbitates nunc cognitas patefacere, ut fideles serui Dei possent eas cauere. Sed spero in Deum, quod mittet post me magis strenuos, & nunc sunt, qui melius patefacient malitiam Antichristi, & exponent animas suas ad mortem, propter veritatem domini nostri Jesu Christi, qui & vobis & mihi daturus est gaudium vitae aeternae. Scripta epistola in die sancti Joannis Baptistae in carcere, in compedibus, in illa meditatione, quod sanctus Joannes in vinculis carceris decollatus sit propter verbum Dei.
units.tr: Afterwards, under the New Testament, they burned the saints together with books of divine law. Cardinals condemned and handed over to the fire some books of Saint Gregory, and would have handed over all of them, unless they had been defended by God through Peter, minister of Gregory. Although two councils of priests pronounced holy Chrysostom a heretic, merciful God made their lie manifest after the death of that golden-mouthed man. Keeping these things before your eyes, take care that, out of fear, you do not fail to read my books, or hand them over to the adversaries to be burned. Remember the merciful word of the Saviour, by which he wanted us forewarned. "There will be," he says, "before the day of judgment, a great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until this time, nor will be; so that, if it were possible, even the elect of God would be led into error. But for the sake of these, those days will be cut short." Mindful of these things, dearest ones, be undaunted. For I trust in God that that school of Antichrist will fear you and will let you be at peace. Nor will the Council of Constance go to Bohemia. For I think many of those who are in it will die before they extort my books from you. And from the council they will be scattered through the parts of the world, hither and thither, like storks, and in the coming winter they will know what they did in summer. Consider that they judged their own head, the Pope, worthy of death for certain horrible crimes.
