Quum enim coram iudicibus productus esset, ea spiritus tum sapientia tum constantia eis respondit, vt confusi & attoniti huiusmodi poenam in eum constituerint, vt viuus combureretur. A qua sententia is nullo modo vnquam prouocare voluit. Itaque tractus crate ad vltimum supplicium, insigne morte sua testimonium veritati dedit, ad finem mensis Iunij, anni M.D.XXXV.
units.tr: In May 1535, at Mâcon, John Cornon was seized on account of the Gospel and shut up in prison. He was a native of that very region of Mâcon, a farm labourer given to tilling the fields, who had been very piously instructed and well trained in the doctrine of God's Word itself, although he knew no letters. When he was brought before the judges, he answered them with such spirit, wisdom and constancy that they, confused and astonished, decreed this punishment against him: that he should be burned alive. He never wished to appeal from this sentence in any way. So, dragged on a hurdle to the final punishment, he gave a notable testimony to the truth by his death, at the end of June in the year 1535.

units.la: CLAVDIVS PICTOR.
units.tr: CLAUDIUS PICTOR.

units.la: Laudius Pictor, natus Lutetiæ in suburbano sancti Marcelli, professione aurifex, est Geneuæ in ecclesia Dei annos circiter tres commoratus. Deinde Lutetiam reuertendi cepit consilium, vt propinquos, parentes, amicosque, gratiæ quam à Deo acceperat, participes faceret, eosque in cognitione veritatis instituerct, ab illis traditus est Morino præfecto rerum capitalium. qui audita eius confessione puræ Christianæque doctrinæ plenissima, condemnauit eum vt viuus igni cremaretur. Curia parlamenti suprema, Morini sententiam suo more corrigens, addidit etiam, vt ei lingua præcideretur. Cùm in plateam Malberti ad supplicium, eo in loco constitutum, duceretur, admirabilis eius fuit constantia & animi moderatio in vultu atque gestu declarata, cùm probra, quibus homines eum ad supplicium euntem prosequebantur, æquo animo ac vultu alacri & hilari exciperet ac ferret. Eandem animi æquitatem atque alacritate retinuit & declarauit in ipso genere mortis suscipiendo, quo viuus igni consumptus est, anno M.D.LX.
units.tr: Claudius Pictor, born at Paris in the suburb of St Marcel, by trade a goldsmith, stayed at Geneva in the Church of God for about three years. Then he resolved to return to Paris, so that he might share the grace he had received from God with his relatives, parents and friends, and instruct them in the knowledge of the truth. He was betrayed to Morin, the prefect of criminal matters, who, having heard his confession, which was full of pure Christian doctrine, condemned him to be burned alive. The supreme Parlement, modifying Morin's sentence in its usual manner, added that his tongue should be cut out. When he was led to the execution at the Place Maubert, the place appointed for it, his remarkable constancy and composure were shown in his face and bearing. He received and endured with an even mind and a cheerful, joyful countenance the insults with which people followed him on his way to death. He kept the same calm and cheerfulness, and showed them, in undergoing the very manner of death by which he was burned alive, in the year 1560.

units.la: STEPHANVS BRVNVS, Reorterensis, diœcesis Ebredunensis.
units.tr: STEPHANUS BRUNUS, of Reorterium, diocese of Embrun.

units.la: Tephani[?] huius, quem merito inter alios constantes ac fideles Christi martyres numerandum censemus, historia vel ob id admiranda magis omnibus accidere debet, quòd ipse qui rei rusticæ colendisque agris toto vitæ tempore operam dederat, natus scilicet atque in Reorterio pago quodam Delphinatus, scietia veritatis omnes Ebredunensium astutias confutarit, atque Archiepiscopatus Ebreduni larvas facile detraxerit, præsentique animo hypocrisim sacrificorum reprehenderit. Quanuis autem liberales artes in scholis non addidicisset vnquam, Gallicèque tantummodo legere & scribere nosset, lectioni noui Testamenti magnopere addictus, ex quo sacrificorum errores deprehenderat: tamen quæ erat innata hominis ingenio dexteritas, quò certius omnes Papistarum tergiuersationes & fallacias cognosceret, summo labore tandem perfecit, vt conferendo assiduè exemplar Gallici testamenti cum Latino, ipse etiam Scripturæ testimonia Latine è & recitare & intelligere potuerit.Cæterum cùm hæc lux lippitudini multorum molestior esset, accidit ut anno millesimo quingentesimo trigesimo octauo in carcerem Archiepiscopi inclusus fuerit, ubi primùm [?]circunuentus aduersariorum nescio quibus technis (quas honos & simplex, nec callidus admodum, parùm intellexit) formulam abiurationis latinè scriptam recitauit. Verùm carcere illo liberatus ubi fraus inimicorum ei suboleuit, re & verbis sæpius animi dolore testatus est, suæque carni succensuit, quòd tā propensa fuisset ad defectionem; sibi quoque ipse subinde ita minans, Me miserum, haudquaquā[?] cadauer istud euadet, si me rursum capi contingat, sed periurij poenas dabit, spero.
units.tr: The history of this Stephanus, whom we rightly count among the other steadfast and faithful martyrs of Christ, ought to strike everyone as all the more admirable for this reason: he himself, who had devoted his whole life to farming and working the fields, being born in the village of Reorterium in Dauphiné, by his knowledge of the truth confuted all the cunning of the Archbishopric of Embrun's clergy, easily tore away the masks of the Archbishopric of Embrun, and with ready wit rebuked the hypocrisy of the priests. Although he had never learned the liberal arts in schools, and knew only how to read and write in French, he was greatly devoted to reading the New Testament, from which he had detected the errors of the priests. Yet the natural quickness of his mind, so that he might know more surely all the evasions and deceits of the Papists, at last achieved, by constantly comparing the French copy of the Testament with the Latin, that he could both recite and understand the testimonies of Scripture in Latin. But since this light was more troublesome to the eyes of many, it happened in the year 1538 that he was shut up in the Archbishop's prison, where, first surrounded by his adversaries with I know not what tricks (which he, being simple and not very crafty, understood little), he recited a formula of abjuration written in Latin. But once freed from that prison, when the enemies' fraud dawned on him, he often testified by word and deed his grief of mind, and was angry with his own flesh for being so prone to defection; threatening himself from time to time: "Wretched me, this carcass will not escape if I am captured again; but it will pay the penalty for perjury, I hope."

units.la: Anno itaque M.D.XL. Brunus iterum in vincula coniectus Ebredumi fuit, persequente eum Gasparo Augerio Vapincensi, redituum Archiepiscopi redemptore, qui bona Bruni publicanda atque in fiscũ redigenda, jam tota spe, animo & cogitatione deuorarat. Ille, inquam, opera Inquisitoris Franciscani, cui Domicelli erat nomen, & alterius cuiusdã Vicarij nequitia utés[?], omni ratione vitæ Stephani insidias struxit.
units.tr: In the year 1540, therefore, Brunus was thrown into chains again at Embrun, Gaspard Augier of Vapincum, the buyer of the Archbishop's revenues, pursuing him; for he had already devoured in hope, mind and thought the goods of Brunus, which were to be confiscated and turned into the treasury. He, I say, with the help of a Franciscan inquisitor whose name was Domicellus, and the wickedness of another vicar, laid plots against Stephanus's life by every means.

units.la: Stephanus autē in carcere per aduersarios lacessitus ad palinodiā canendam (ut prius imprudens fecerat) ne latum quidem unguem eis cessit, sed minas & preces illorum præposteras fortiter contempsit.
units.tr: Stephanus, however, harassed in prison by the adversaries to sing a palinode (as he had previously done, unwisely), did not yield them so much as a hair's breadth, but bravely scorned their threats and absurd entreaties.

units.la: Quum illi proponeretur, uxori adhuc iuveni, & quinque liberis penuriam fore, illo mortuo: Modò, inquit, liberis meis pabulum animi, quod est Verbum Dei, concedatur, de pane corporis non sum solicitus.
units.tr: When it was put to him that his wife, still young, and his five children would be in want after his death, he said: "Now let my children be given food for the soul, which is the Word of God; I am not anxious about bread for the body."

units.la: Mense autem Iunio eiusdem anni duƈtus ad Iudices ut ei sententia capitis pronuntiaretur, sic eos intrepido animo est allocutus, Quid agetis miseri? mortisne me damnabitis, qua mihi ex hac vita demigrandum sit? mors sanè mihi terribilis non est, quum ex miseriis ad beatam immortalitatem transiturus sim. Ad locum supplicij Planuol appellatum quum duceretur, plebem ad pietatis studium hortatus est, ibi vi & impetu venti flammam huc illuc abripientis ac deprimentis, intactus fere unius horæ spatio ad palum ligatus stetit, adeo ut vt noua sarmenta & vasa olei plena, consumptis lignis, afferri necesse esset, quibus ignis adiuuari posset: nec tamen ita recte comburi potuit quin saluus adhuc euadere posse videretur. Quo viso carnifex fustem in hominis caput totis viribus impegit. Cui etiamnum viuens dixit Stephanus, Cum igni adiudicatus sim, ecquid me vis baculis enecare velut canem? Tum carnifex praepilato baculo viscera Bruni traiecit, quem prostratum in cineres redegit: atque eos postea in rupe collocatos ventis tradidit. Magistratus autem per praconé vetuit ne quis mentionem vllam mortis illius faceret, nisi haereticus haberi vellet, eundemque casum & exitium experiri.
units.tr: In June of the same year he was led before the judges so that sentence of death might be pronounced on him, and he addressed them with a fearless spirit: "What will you do, wretched men? Will you condemn me to death, by which I must depart from this life? Death is certainly not terrible to me, since I am about to pass from miseries to blessed immortality." As he was led to the place of execution called Planuol, he exhorted the people to zeal for piety; there, by the force and violence of the wind which drove the flame hither and thither and beat it down, he stood tied to the stake almost untouched for the space of an hour, so that fresh faggots and vessels full of oil had to be brought, once the wood was used up, by which the fire could be helped; yet he could not be burned so thoroughly that he did not still seem likely to escape unharmed. Seeing this, the executioner struck the man's head with all his strength with a club. To him, still living, Stephanus said: "Since I have been condemned to the fire, will you kill me with clubs like a dog?" Then the executioner, with a club tipped with lead, pierced Brunus's bowels; he struck him down and reduced him to ashes, and afterwards laid the ashes on a rock and gave them to the winds. The magistrate, moreover, forbade by herald that anyone make any mention of that death, unless he wished to be held a heretic and to undergo the same fate and ruin.

units.la: ROBERTVS BARNEVS.
units.tr: ROBERTVS BARNEVS.

units.la: Martyrium Roberti Barnei, qui Londini vitam profudit pro tuendo Iesu Christi Euan- gelio.
units.tr: The martyrdom of Robert Barnes, who gave up his life at London for defending the Gospel of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Robertus Barneus doctor theologus anno 1540 Londini vstulatus[?] fuit. Is autem pro Euangelij doctrina aliquandiu ab Anglia exulauit: sed cum postea intellexisset Henricum Regem partem aliquam verae pietatis & cognitionis veritatis degustauisse, domum reuersus est. Post autem aliquanto, anno scilicet 1535, Rex cum legatum constituit & misit vnà cum Edouardo Foxo Episcopo Herfurdesi ad Conuentum, qui Smalcaldae celebrabatur pro conciliandis religionis Christianae capitibus cum protestatibus Germanis, & pro foedere cum eis feriendo. Cum vero susceptum munus expleuissent, sese wittembergam contulerunt ad hybernandum. Interea temporis cum Theologis eius Academiae de causa religionis contulerunt: imprimis vero id studuerunt, vt approbationem repudij, quo Rex Catharinam vxorem dimiseret, elicerent. Quam tamen Theologi wittembergenses concedere omnino recusarunt, literarum scilicet sacrarum authoritate adducti. Dum haec geruntur, Rex Annam Boleniam vxorem suam capite plecti iussit, quae Euangelio fauebat, & veritatis doctrinam magnopere promouebat. Quae quidem res, magnas excitauit turbas & quo minus Protestantes societatem cum eo coirent, obstitit & impediuit. Paucis post diebus, ab exiguo illo verae religionis sensu Rex foede deficere coepit ad Papisticam doctrinam, quam fere integram postea pertinaciter retinuit. Nihilo tamen secius Robertus Barneus constanter in sententia perseuerauit, nullaque in re à sanctissima Filij Dei veritate dimoueri potuit. Quapropter comprehensus est & in carcerem coniectus. Quoniam vero in proposito susceptáque Euangelij defensione constanter permanebat, anno M.D.XL. vivus exustus est. In area supplicio mortis destinata prolixam edidit suae fidei confessionem, & summa cum libertate populum ad verae pietatis studium hortatus est. Duo denique alij pro tuenda eadem causa & pro eadem veritatis fideique Christianae confessione asserenda, simul cum eo combusti sunt.
units.tr: Robert Barnes, doctor of theology, was burned at London in 1540. For the teaching of the Gospel he had been an exile from England for some time, but when he later learned that King Henry had tasted some part of true godliness and knowledge of the truth, he returned home. Some time afterwards, namely in 1535, the King appointed an envoy and sent him, together with Edward Fox, Bishop of Hereford, to the assembly that was being held at Smalcalden, to settle the heads of the Christian religion with the Protestant Germans and to make a covenant with them. When they had finished the task entrusted to them, they went to Wittenberg to spend the winter. Meanwhile they conferred with the theologians of that university about the matter of religion, and above all they worked to obtain their approval of the divorce by which the King would dismiss his wife Catherine. The Wittenberg theologians, however, flatly refused to grant this, being moved by the authority of the holy writings. While these things were happening, the King ordered his wife Anne Boleyn, who favoured the Gospel and greatly promoted the doctrine of the truth, to be beheaded. This act stirred up great disturbances and hindered and prevented the Protestants from joining fellowship with him. A few days later, the King began to fall away shamefully from that slight sense of true religion to Papist doctrine, which he afterwards stubbornly retained almost entire. Nevertheless Robert Barnes persevered constantly in his opinion, and he could not be moved from the most holy truth of the Son of God in any matter. Therefore he was seized and thrown into prison. Since he remained steadfast in his purpose and in the defence of the Gospel he had undertaken, he was burned alive in the year 1540. On the open place set aside for the punishment of death he delivered a lengthy confession of his faith, and with great boldness he exhorted the people to devote themselves to true godliness. Finally, two others were burned together with him for defending the same cause and for asserting the same confession of the truth and of the Christian faith.

units.la: CONSTANTINVS NORTHMANVS.
units.tr: CONSTANTINE THE NORTHMAN.

units.la: Rothomagi, cuius urbis ciues à Cæsare Aulerci sunt appellati, fuit quidam Constantinus, qui anno M.D.XLII pro tuenda Euangelij doctrina, cum aliis tribus confessionis Christianae sociis & comitibus, insignem martyrij laudem tulit. Is quum plaustro, quo lutum & quisquiliae urbis cuebi[?] solent, ad ultimum supplicium duceretur, laetabundus ita loquutus dicitur, Nos quidem nunc excrementa mundi ac reiectamenta sumus, teterrimi coram hominibus foetoris: sed laetemur & gaudeamus, quoniam odor mortis nostrae suavissimus & pretiosissimus coram Deo est futurus.
units.tr: At Rouen, whose citizens were called Aulerci by Caesar, there was a certain Constantine who, in 1542, together with three other companions and fellow-confessors of the Christian faith, won distinguished praise for martyrdom in defence of the doctrine of the Gospel. As he was being led to the final punishment on a cart in which the mud and rubbish of the city are usually carried, he is said to have spoken joyfully in this way: "We are now the off-scouring and refuse of the world, most foul in the sight of men, but let us rejoice and be glad, since the odour of our death will be most sweet and precious before God."

units.la: IOANNES DV BEC.
units.tr: IOANNES DV BEC.

units.la: Oannes[?] Becus, Effaris natus prope Sedanam in Bria, quum propter doctrinam Euangelij diu inclusus in carcere multa grauia & acerba perpessus esset, semper tamen & constanter consessionem Christianae fidei antea editam retinuit, quum ad iudices productus, tum vero publice eo tempore quo de gradu Papalis sacerdotij motus est. Postremo Trecis in urbe Campaniae maxima, vivus est combustus mense Iunio, anni M.D.XLIII.
units.tr: John Becus, born at Effaris near Sedan in Brie, was long shut up in prison on account of the doctrine of the Gospel and endured many grievous and bitter things. Yet he always and steadfastly held to the confession of the Christian faith he had published earlier, both when he was brought before the judges and publicly at the time when he was deposed from the rank of the Papal priesthood. Finally, at Troyes, a great city of Champagne, he was burned alive in the month of June, in the year 1543.

units.la: FRANCISCVS BRIBARD.
units.tr: FRANCIS BRIBARD.

units.la: Franciscus Bribardus, Clemonensis in Solognia, qui Secretarius Cardinalis Bellaij dicebatur, post linguam excisam, mortem pro confessione Euangelij fortiter constanterque pertulit.
units.tr: Francis Bribard, of Clermont in Sologne, who was called secretary to Cardinal Bellay, after his tongue had been cut out, bore death bravely and steadfastly for the confession of the Gospel.

units.la: PETRVS BRVLI.
units.tr: PETER BRULI.

units.la: Agister Petrus Brulius, natione Lotharingus, Argentinae minister ecclesiae Gallicanae. Hunc fideles homines inferioris Germanie ac ditionis Imperatoris rogarunt, ut urbes Fladriæ, Hannoniæ, Arthesiæque inuiserent, in quibus multi erant pij Deumque metuentes, qui fame cibi cœlestis laborabant, & verbi Dei consolationem magnopere desiderabant. Itaque illud iter pietatis plenum suscepit Brulus, ex sententia & permissu ecclesiæ, cui tum seruiebat, eoque est prosectus cum testimonio scripto Martini Buceri, qui eo tempore præcipuum ecclesiæ ministerium Argentinæ sustinebat. Cum autem fideliter ac diligenter munus iniunctum obiuisset, atque urbes, Vallencenas, Tornacum, Atrebates, eamque, quæ Insula appellatur, inuisisset, Tornacum postea reuersus, tanto animi studio verbum Dei ea in urbe annuntiare cœpit, ut aliquando ianuis apertis pios homines doceret. Quamobrem magistratus eius ciuitatis certior factus, portas urbis tribus prope diebus claudi iussit, ipsumque Brulium diligentissime coquiri, præmio ei constituto, qui eum viuum aut mortuum tradidisset. Quare fideles magnopere perculsi, cum eum apud se aliquot dies occultassent, ac saluum cuperent emittere, in sporta positum nocte per murum demiserunt. Sed cum iam in fossam descendisset, lapis magnus e superiore muro delapsus, tibiam ei fregit. Eo factum est, ut mane ibi deprehensus sit, & comprehensum in arcem urbis detulerunt. Cum autem eo deferretur, maximas Deo agebat gratias, cuius admirabili prouidentia retetus esset tum, cum vellet effugere eam persecutionem, quam ipse sua prædicatione excitasset. Is igitur quamdiu fuit in carcere, officio semper functus est veri & constantis testis ac martyris, cum priuatim, tum etiam apud magistratus, quibus Iesum Christum eiusque Euangelium, non minus libere & constanter, quam integre ac fideliter confessus est. Eo toto tempore, quo captiuus in carcere diu fuit, permulti eum inuisebant: quidam stulta curiositate, ut Germanicum prædicatorem captiuum viderent: alij improba cupiditate, ut illi resisterent, nonnulli meliore mente, studio ac voluntate, ut cognitione Dei & doctrina Euangelij ab eo instituerentur, quibus summa cum gratia satisfaciebat. Ut autem studio amicorum satisfaceret, consessionem fidei suæ editam conscripsit, nomine uxoris eam ad omnes fideles mittens, quam nos conuersam in Latinum sermonem huic loco intexere voluimus. Ego, charissima soror in Christo Iesu, literas tuas legi, ad me per Margaritam missas, quae animum meum vehementer affecerunt: propterea quod ex his facile perspexi, te ac fratres omnes, deme maximopere laborare. Quòd autem ad vincula mea pertinet, sintne mihi ingrata & tristia, an cum magna mea consolatione ac laetitia coniuncta facile tu intelligere poteris ab exemplo earum literarum, quas ad fratres meos, una mecum captos propter verbum Iesu Christi, hisce diebus misi, ex quibus tu plane cognoscere poteris, quid ego in meipso feferim[?], & quid aliis voluerim persuadere, ac quemadmodum nihil postulem ab his ac pro his, quod in meipso nolim praestari. hoc autem (testis est Deus) ut Dominus noster me in sua protectione, atque in vera confessione veritatis custodiat. Quanquam domesticus quidem inimicus magnopere me affligit: tamen sancti spiritus virtute conteretur. Nam Christus Iesus, in quo ego spem meam posui, plus boni mihi praestabit, quam ego possem ulla cogitatione comprehendere. Pro illius honore ego me semper exponam, sive igni sive aquae, aut alteri tormento, quod ab adversariis excogitari poterit: huiuscemodi tamen quod Deo placuerit. Reliquum est ut ad te scribam ea quae ex me requiris, quemadmodum ego interrogatus fuerim, & tum iudicibus, tum doctoribus responderim. In quo quidem nimium longa esset oratio, si omnia, quae ab illis ex me sunt quaesita atque interrogata, aut a me eis responsa, vellem perscribere, ne possem commode quidem ea ad vos scribere. Neque existimo te ea omnia quaerere: sed tantummodo ea & interrogata & responsa, quae ad fidem doctrinamque Christianam pertineant. de his igitur scribam. Ac primum doctor Hasardus, monachus sanctae Franciscanae XXVI. die Novembris cum adesset praefectus arcis Tornacensis, & vicarius sive locum tenens, ut vocant, praefectorum ac iuratorum eius urbis atque iurisdictionis Imperatoris, me interrogavit quid de sacramento altaris & Missa sentirem. Cui ego respondi, fideles qui a ministro panem & vinum accipiebant, vere corpus & sanguine Domini nostri Iesu Christi accipere, non ventre, aut ore, sed mente, animo, corde: idque beneficio Spiritus, in eis fidem excitantis & confirmantis, quae promissiones ibi propositas amplectitur. harum prima est, Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis traditur. Altera, Hic est sanguis meus noui testamenti, qui in remissionem peccatorum effunditur. Quaesiuit idem doctor ex me, si transubstantiationi vllam fidem adhiberem. Cui respondi, me eam non credere, sed panem manere panem, & vinum eodem modo suam naturam retinere. itaque Spiritu sanctum nominare panem & vinu, etiam post Cœnam, atque ita me non vereri ut errarem, cum ita loquerer, ut Scriptura sancta consueuisset.
units.tr: Master Peter Brulius, a native of Lorraine, was minister of the French church at Strasbourg. Faithful men of lower Germany and of the Emperor's dominions asked him to visit the cities of Flanders, Hainault and Artois, in which there were many godly men who feared God, who were suffering from hunger for heavenly food and greatly desired the consolation of the Word of God. Brulius therefore undertook that journey, which was full of godliness, with the approval and permission of the church he then served, and he set out with a written testimony from Martin Bucer, who at that time held the chief ministry of the church at Strasbourg. When he had faithfully and diligently discharged the task laid upon him, and had visited the cities of Valenciennes, Tournai, Arras, and the one called Lille, he afterwards returned to Tournai and began with such zeal of spirit to proclaim the Word of God in that city that at last he taught godly people with the doors open. Therefore the magistrates of that city, being informed of it, ordered the gates of the city to be shut for about three days and Brulius himself to be searched for most diligently, a reward being set for whoever should hand him over alive or dead. Consequently the faithful, greatly alarmed, hid him among themselves for some days, and since they wished to send him away safe, they lowered him by night over the wall in a basket. But when he had already gone down into the ditch, a large stone fell from the upper wall and broke his leg. As a result, he was caught there in the morning, and they took him captive to the citadel of the city. As he was being carried there, he gave the greatest thanks to God, whose wonderful providence had held him back at the very moment when he wished to escape the persecution which he himself had stirred up by his preaching. So, as long as he was in prison, he always discharged the duty of a true and steadfast witness and martyr, both in private and before the magistrates, to whom he confessed Jesus Christ and his Gospel no less freely and constantly than faithfully and sincerely. During the whole time that he was kept a captive in prison, very many visited him: some out of foolish curiosity, to see a captive German preacher; others out of wicked desire, to oppose him; some with a better mind, eagerly and willingly, to be instructed by him in the knowledge of God and the doctrine of the Gospel, to whom he gave satisfaction with great kindness. Moreover, to satisfy the eagerness of his friends, he wrote out a confession of his faith, sending it to all the faithful in the name of his wife, which we have wished to insert here translated into Latin. "I, most dear sister in Christ Jesus, have read your letter, sent to me through Margaret, which greatly moved my spirit, because from it I could easily perceive that you and all the brothers are labouring very much over me. As for my chains, whether they are unpleasant and sad to me, or whether they are joined with great consolation and joy for me, you can easily understand from the copy of the letter which I have sent these days to my brothers, who were taken with me for the word of Jesus Christ, from which you can clearly learn what I have shown in myself and what I have wished to persuade others of, and how I ask nothing from them or for them which I am unwilling to have done in myself. God is my witness that our Lord may keep me under his protection and in the true confession of the truth. Although indeed a domestic enemy troubles me greatly, yet he shall be crushed by the power of the Holy Spirit. For Christ Jesus, in whom I have placed my hope, will give me more good than I could comprehend by any thought. For his honour I shall always expose myself, whether to fire or water or any other torment that the adversaries may devise; yet let it be such as shall please God. It remains that I write to you the things you ask of me, how I was questioned and how I answered the judges and the teachers. In this matter indeed my speech would be too long if I wished to write down everything that was asked and questioned of me by them, or what I answered, nor could I conveniently write it all to you. Nor do I think you seek all of that, but only those questions and answers which pertain to the Christian faith and doctrine. I shall therefore write about these. And first, Doctor Hasard, a monk of the Franciscan order, on the 26th day of November, when the governor of the citadel of Tournai was present, and the vicar, or deputy, as they call him, of the governors and jurors of that city and of the Emperor's jurisdiction, asked me what I thought about the sacrament of the altar and the Mass. To him I replied that the faithful who receive bread and wine from the minister truly receive the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, not with the belly or mouth, but with the mind, spirit and heart; and this by the benefit of the Spirit, who stirs up and confirms faith in them, which embraces the promises set forth there. The first of these is, 'This is my body, which is given for you.' The second is, 'This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for the remission of sins.' The same doctor asked me whether I gave any credence to transubstantiation. To this I replied that I did not believe it, but that the bread remains bread and the wine keeps its nature in the same way; and so I call the bread and wine by their names even after the Supper, and I do not fear to err in speaking thus, as holy Scripture is accustomed to speak."

units.la: Deinde quaesiuit, an cum verba sacramentalia a sacerdote pronuntiata essent, ibi in altari verum corpus & sanguinem Iesu Christi esse crederem. Cui respondi, me nullam aliam recipere consecrationem, quam eam quae a ministro in Cœna celebranda adhibetur, cum minister populo, qui eo conuenit, institutionem Iesu Christi recitat eo genere sermonis, quod ab omnibus intelligatur, cum commemoratione mortis ac passionis Iesu Christi, qua memoria tanti beneficij renouatur. Eam esse veram consecrationem, quae ex instituto Domini in Cœna fieri debeat. Illum vero obscurum ac tacitum cum pane sermonem atque obmurmurationem, non esse consecrationem, sed actionem huiusmodi, quae ad incantatores, exorcistas & magos potius, quam ad Christianos pertineret. Nam, quemadmodum satis constat, Christus Cœnam faciens, verba sua ad Apostolos qui aderant, nō ad panem & ad vinum dirigit. Tum quaesiuit ex me, quid de Missa sentirem. Ego ei respondi, Missam, quemadmodum hodie quidem in ecclesia Romana dicitur, nullo modo esse Cœnam Iesu Christi, sed potius eius corruptionem, cum summa Christi iniuria, atque abolitione mortis ac passionis eius.
units.tr: Then he asked whether, when the sacramental words had been pronounced by the priest, I believed that the true body and blood of Jesus Christ were there on the altar. I replied that I accept no consecration other than the one used by the minister when the Supper is celebrated, when the minister recites to the gathered people the institution of Jesus Christ, in a form of speech that everyone understands, together with the commemoration of the death and passion of Jesus Christ, by which the memory of so great a benefit is renewed. That is the true consecration, which ought to be made according to the Lord's institution in the Supper. But that obscure and silent muttering over the bread is not consecration. It is an action of the kind that belongs to enchanters, exorcists and magicians rather than to Christians. For, as is well established, Christ in making the Supper directed his words to the apostles who were present, not to the bread and the wine. Then he asked me what I thought of the Mass. I replied that the Mass, as it is said today in the Roman church, is in no way the Supper of Jesus Christ but rather its corruption, to the great injury of Christ and the abolishing of his death and passion.

units.la: De adoratione vero quae ibi fit, ego eis concessi, ipsos panem ac creaturam adorare. In quo cum mihi respondissent, Nos igitur omnes sumus idololatrae: ego statim, Vos ergo, inquā, videtis in quanta mala vos ij coniiciunt, qui vos a verbo Dei abducentes, ad somnia sua audienda, & doctrinas hominum traducunt. Multa alia ea de re dicta fuerunt: sed haec sunt praecipua.
units.tr: As for the adoration that takes place there, I granted to them that they adore the bread, a creature. When they answered me, "So then we are all idolaters," I immediately said: "You see, then, what great evils those men bring upon you, who lead you away from the Word of God and turn you to listen to their dreams and the doctrines of men." Many other things were said on this matter, but these are the main points.

units.la: Postea interrogatus fui de purgatorio, an crederem aliquem esse locum, in quem animae ex hac vita descenderent, ut poenā peccatis debitam luerent. Ego tum respondi, me non aliud purgatorium credere, quàm sanguinem Iesu Christi, neque aliam purgationem quærere. Tu quæsiuit ex me, an crederem culpam simul & pœnam condonari. Cui respondi, utramque Deum homini remittere, neque dimidiam gratiam facere: sed cum aliquid ignoscit, simul & culpam & pœnam ignoscere. Ex quo illa interrogatio est consecuta, quid mihi videretur de tot egregijs Missis, precibus, aliisque bonis operibus, quæ pro mortuis hominibus quotidie fieret. Dixi huiusmodi opera cultus esse, sine verbo Dei in ecclesia institutos, eámque ob causam esse vanos atq; infructuosos, atque etiam, quia sine fide fierent, peccata esse. scriptum enim est 14.Roman. Quicquid non est ex fide, peccatum est.
units.tr: Afterwards I was questioned about purgatory, whether I believed there is a place into which souls descend from this life to pay the punishment owed for their sins. I then replied, that I believe there is no other purgatory, than the blood of Jesus Christ, and I seek no other purgation. Then he asked me whether I believed that guilt and punishment are remitted together. I replied that God remits both to man, and does not grant half a grace; when he forgives something, he forgives both the guilt and the punishment at once. From this followed the question of what I thought of so many excellent Masses, prayers and other good works that were performed every day for dead people. I said that such works are acts of worship instituted in the church without the Word of God, and for that reason they are vain and unfruitful, and also, since they are done without faith, they are sins. For it is written in Romans 14: Whatever is not of faith is sin.

units.la: Cùm autem mihi dixissent, omnes Sanctos qui ante fuerunt, & eadem pro mortuis egerunt, errauisse: respondi, omnes Sanctos superiorum ætatū, qui mortuis huiusmodi officia ac iura tribuerunt, ignorantia & peccato implicatos fuisse. ita minime mirum videri debere, si consuetudines suo tempore receptas sequuti fuerunt. In his quidem rebus me nolle eos à peccato eximere ac excusare. De veneratione autem Sanctorum, quæsiuerunt ex me, quid de ea sentirem. quibus ego respondi, nos melius non posse Sanctos honorare, quàm si fidem, quæ fuit in illis, sequeremur: eodemque modo charitatem, patientiam, humilitatem, aliasque eorum virtutes imitaremur, quibus illi Iesum Christum sequuti sunt & imitati. Nam in eo quidem tantummodo nobis ad imitationem proponi debent, in quo Christo domino conformes extiterunt, eiusque exemplum sequuti sunt, sicut monet Apostolus, Estote mei imitatores, sicut ego sum Christi. Festos vero dies Sanctorum instituere ac celebrare, ieiunia vigiliis eorum indicere atque obire, imagines effingere, eisque accendere candelas, hoc non est Sanctos honorare, sed potius ex his idola facere, eosque omni dedecore afficere. Hoc autem ita esse, illud facile declarat, quòd illi in hac manentes vita, huiusmodi cultus semper detestati fuerunt.
units.tr: When they had told me that all the saints who lived before us, and did the same things for the dead, had erred, I replied that all the saints of earlier ages, who ascribed such offices and rights to the dead, were entangled in ignorance and sin. It should therefore seem by no means surprising if they followed the customs received in their own time. In these matters I am not willing to free them from sin or to excuse them. About the veneration of the saints they asked me what I thought of it. To them I replied that we cannot honor the saints better than by following the faith that was in them, and in the same way by imitating their charity, patience, humility and their other virtues, by which they followed and imitated Jesus Christ. For they ought to be set before us for imitation only in that respect in which they were conformed to the Lord Christ and followed his example, as the Apostle admonishes: "Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ." But to institute and celebrate feast days of the saints, to appoint and keep fasts and vigils for them, to make images and light candles before them: this is not to honor the saints, but rather to make idols of them and to heap every disgrace upon them. That this is so is easily shown by the fact that they, while remaining in this life, always detested such worship.

units.la: Quæsiuerunt etiam ex me, quid mihi videretur de ijsdem Sanctis orandis atque inuocandis, eorumque intercessione apud Deum. Respondi eam doctrinam non esse Dei, sed potius blasphemiam eius non ferendam. Hoc enim modo illis attribui, quod ad unum Deum pertinet, qui solus res cognoscit absentes: quam potestatem sanctis defunctis attribuunt, cùm credunt illos audire preces ipsorum, cùm eos orant, quasi necessitates ipsorum cognoscerent. Præterea huiusmodi doctrina cum Christi contumelia est coniuncta, qui vnus mediator, aduocatus, atque etiam intercessor à Deo patre est constitutus. Atque hoc quidem de iis, qui ex hac vita decesserunt, intelligendum puto. Ceteri verò, qui in ea remanserunt, alij pro alijs orare possunt, & se mutuis precibus orationibusque adiuuare.
units.tr: They also asked me what I thought about praying to and invoking these same saints, and about their intercession with God. I replied that this doctrine is not of God but is a blasphemy that must not be tolerated. For in this way what belongs to the one God is attributed to them, for he alone knows things that are absent. They ascribe this power to the departed saints when they believe that they hear the prayers of those who pray to them, as if they knew their needs. Moreover, such doctrine is joined with contumely toward Christ, who has been appointed by God the Father as the one mediator, advocate and also intercessor. And this, I think, is what must be understood of those who have departed from this life. But the others who remain in it can pray for one another, and help one another by mutual prayers and supplications.

units.la: Quæstio verò de libero arbitrio minimè fuit prætermissa: in qua diligenter à me quæsitum est, quid de eo sentirem. Respondi, vt sermo de libero arbitrio pro dignitate rei haberi possit, hominem pro diuerso ac vario ipsius statu, in quo versatus est, variè considerandum esse. Primum, credo hominem primum ad similitudinem Dei atque imaginem creatum, habuisse libertatem tam ad bonum quàm ad malum, cumque solum quæ esset vis & facultas liberi arbitrij cognouisse, quoad in integritate sua permansit. Sed homo miser atque infelix, hoc Dei donum non diu retinuit, sed suo peccato illud amisit. neque is solùm, verumetiam ij omnes, qui ex naturali Adæ semine sunt orti ac propagati, adeo vt nullam prorsus facultatem habeant, qua relicti in sua natura, aliquid boni coram Deo facere possint: sed omnia in ipsis praua reperiuntur. Nunc quidem, vt quod verum est dicatur, nullus est ex filijs Adæ, qui vllam boni scintillam habeat, nec quidem potest vllum liberum arbitrium habere: omnes enim homines natura sua currunt ad malum. Itaque Apostolus dicit animalem hominem non percipere quæ sunt Dei, ea etiam stultitiam illi esse. Apud Oseam Dominus ita inquit, O Israel, perditio tua ex te. Et alio loco dicit Apostolus, prudentiam carnis inimicam esse Deo. Hæc Spiritus testimonia satis ostendunt nullum liberum arbitrium ad bene agendum, nunc esse in homine coram Deo. Dico autem nominatim coram Deo, propterea quòd homo multa egregia opera, ipsa specie bona, coram hominibus facere poterit, vt parere legibus, ijs in rebus quæ extrinsecus præstantur: sed iudicio Dei huiusmodi opera omnia nullius sunt pretij, atque etiam peccata sunt. Quæ autem hactenus dixi, intelligite de eo, qui Spiritu Dei regeneratus non est. Veniamus nunc ad hominem Christianum, sanguine Christi baptizatum, qui jam in nouitate atę vitæ ambulat. Huiusmodi homini Christus Iesus liberum arbitrium restituit, eiusque voluntatem ad omnia bona opera reformat. Neque tamen id perfectè. Nam vt bonum opus plenè perfectèque præstetur, nunquam in eo reperitur: sed novo subinde Dei auxilio indiget. Hoc enim Apostolus de se testatur, Romanor. VII. Velle quidem mihi adest, sed perficere in meipso non reperio. Itaque nostrum liberum arbitrium, amplius non est in nobis, sicut in primo fuit homine, qui bonum vt volebat, ita efficere ac præstare poterat. Atque hic quidem defectus à corruptione naturæ nostræ proficiscitur, nō ab imbecillitate vlla Iesu Christi restauratoris. Et de libero quidem arbitrio hæc sunt, quæ ego & sentio & credo.
units.tr: The question of free will was not passed over at all, and I was carefully asked what I thought of it. I replied that, so that the discussion of free will may be held in a manner worthy of the subject, man must be considered in different ways according to the different and varying states in which he has been. First, I believe that man, created first in the likeness and image of God, had freedom to good as well as to evil, and as long as he remained in his integrity he knew only what the power and faculty of free choice was. But wretched and unhappy man did not keep this gift of God for long, but lost it through his sin. Not he alone, but all who have been born and propagated from Adam's natural seed, so that they have absolutely no faculty by which, left in their nature, they could do anything good before God; but all things in them are found to be evil. Now, to say what is true: none of the sons of Adam has any spark of good, nor indeed can any of them have free will, for all men by nature run to evil. Thus the Apostle says that the natural man does not perceive the things of God, and that these are foolishness to him. In Hosea the Lord says: "O Israel, your destruction is from yourself." And in another place the Apostle says that the wisdom of the flesh is hostile to God. These testimonies of the Spirit sufficiently show that there is now no free will in man for acting well before God. I say "before God" expressly, because a man can perform many excellent works that are good in appearance before men, such as obeying laws in those matters which are performed outwardly; but by the judgment of God all such works are of no worth and are even sins. But what I have said so far, understand it of one who has not been regenerated by the Spirit of God. Let us now come to the Christian man, baptized in the blood of Christ, who now walks in newness of life. To such a man Christ Jesus restores free will, and reforms his will toward all good works. Yet not perfectly. For in order that a good work be performed fully and perfectly, it is never found in him, but he constantly needs fresh help from God. For the Apostle testifies this of himself, Romans 7: "To will is indeed present with me, but to perform what is good in myself I do not find." Thus our free will is no longer in us as it was in the first man, who could bring about and perform the good as he willed. And this defect proceeds from the corruption of our nature, not from any weakness in Jesus Christ the restorer. These are the things about free will that I both think and believe.

units.la: Postea de bonis operibus ita ex me quæsiuerunt. Cùm homo non habeat in seipso facultatem præstandi bonum quod vult, nulla igitur potest bona opera efficere. Quibus tum respondi, hominem quidem per se non posse, adiutum vero Spiritu Dei, bona opera & Deo grata posse facere. Quòd autem opera sint bona, aut Deo accepta, id ex ipsius hominis natura aut facultate nō existere, sed totum proficisci à virtute & gratia Christi, eo in homine habitantis, eáque opera efficientis. Dixi illis idē in homine fieri, quod in arbore, quam prius oportet bonā esse, quàm fructum bonum adferat: in his etiam ipsum hominem agere, & cooperatorem esse eorum operum, quibus etiam vita æterna in Scriptura promittitur.
units.tr: Afterwards they questioned me about good works in this way: since a man has not in himself the ability to perform the good that he wills, therefore he can perform no good works. To this I replied that a man indeed cannot do so of himself, but that, aided by the Spirit of God, he can do good works that are pleasing to God. As for the works being good or acceptable to God, this does not arise from the man's own nature or ability, but comes wholly from the power and grace of Christ, who dwells in the man and produces those works. I told them that in a man what happens is the same as in a tree, which must first be good before it can bear good fruit: the man himself acts in these things and is a co-worker in those works, to which eternal life is also promised in Scripture.

units.la: Sequuta deinde est quæstio de Iustificatione, in qua respondi, nos fide iustificari, quemadmodum dicitur tertio ad Romanos capite, Quomodo, inquiunt, sola fide? annon etiam bonis operibus & charitate iustificamur? Quibus ego respondi, nulla huiusmodi opera, nec charitatem reperiri in vllo homine, qui non sit iustificatus. Quid, inquiunt, non poterit homo, etiamsi in peccato mortali sit, dare eleemosynam propter honorem Dei, quem super omnia diligit? Non inquam, nam peccator quidem aliquis pauperi bona sua elargietur, sed non tam causa honoris Dei, quem super omnia diligat, quàm humano aliquo studio permotus. Nam si Deum in primis diligeret, peccatum non ita placeret ei, veniámque à Deo peteret. Ac de bonis operibus vt supra illis respondi.
units.tr: Then followed a question about justification, in which I replied that we are justified by faith, as is said in the third chapter of Romans. "How," they said, "by faith alone? Are we not also justified by good works and by charity?" To this I replied that no such works, nor charity, are found in any man who is not already justified. "What," they said, "can a man not, even if he is in mortal sin, give alms for the honour of God, whom he loves above all things?" No, I said, for a sinner may indeed give his goods to the poor, but not so much for the honour of God, whom he loves above all things, as moved by some human motive. For if he loved God above all, he would not so take pleasure in sin, and he would seek pardon from God. As for good works, I answered them as above.

units.la: Tum quæsierunt ex me, quid ego nominarem Fidem, quæ ita sit potens, vt sola hominem iustificet. Quibus ego respondi, Fidem esse certam animi perfuasionem, per Spiritum sanctum factam de misericordia Dei, eiusque bona in nos voluntate, in Euangelio promissa & oblata. Hæc autem promissiones de amore ac benevolentia Dei erga nos in Christo Iesu filio eius exhibentur ac præstantur. Hac fide nos statuimus, ac persuademus nobis, & sentimus, Deum velle nobis peccata nostra ignoscere propter Filium suum, in quem nos credimus. Ea, inquiunt, non est definitio à Paulo posita, Hebr. XI. Ego vero, inquam, in Diuo Paulo eam reperio.
units.tr: Then they asked me what I would call faith, which is so powerful that it alone justifies a man. To them I replied that faith is a certain assurance of the mind, wrought by the Holy Spirit, concerning the mercy of God and his good will towards us, promised and offered in the Gospel. These promises concerning the love and kindness of God towards us are set forth and made good in Christ Jesus, his Son. By this faith we are persuaded, we make ourselves certain, and we feel that God wishes to forgive us our sins for the sake of his Son, in whom we believe. "That," they said, "is not the definition given by Paul in Hebrews 11." But I, I said, find it in the divine Paul.

units.la: De traditionibus hominum interrogatus ab illis, si eas amplecterer an omnino aspernarer: respondi, me eas approbare ac recipere vt bonas, quæ ad finem aliquem politicum & ciuilem referuntur: cæteras vero improbare ac repudiare: cuius generis sunt, prohibitio coniugij factæ sacerdotibus ac monachis; item interdictum vescendi carnibus certis diebus, aliæque quisquiliæ, ac ceremoniæ huiusmodi, quibus obligare volunt animas, etiam pœna peccati mortalis proposita.
units.tr: When they asked me about the traditions of men, whether I embraced them or utterly rejected them, I replied that I approved and accepted as good those which relate to some political and civil end, but disapproved and rejected the others. Of this kind are the prohibition of marriage imposed on priests and monks; likewise the ban on eating meat on certain days; and other trifles and ceremonies of this sort, by which they wish to bind souls, even with the penalty of mortal sin proposed.

units.la: Postea de imaginibus interrogatus, an fas esset hominibus fidelibus eas habere: respondi, quod ad me quidem attineret, me nullas plane requirere, eásque in templis Christianorum minimè ferri debere. His enim simulachris, ipsa templa profanari, quæ dedicata essent ad verbum Dei audiendum, ad ministranda sacramenta, ad preces publicas faciendas, quarum rerum sanctitas, imaginibus & simulachris anteponenda est. Demonstrabam autem huiusmodi aut ficta simulachra, aut pictas imagines, sæpe ipsos homines à verbo Dei deuocare. Caterum inquam, in ædibus priuatis admittuntur & ponuntur, vt res indifferentes, modò nulla idololatria adhibeatur: nam tum quidem ex domibus sunt auferendæ. Veruntamen, quod ad me attinet, cùm videam eas verbo Dei tam præcisè prohiberi, ego statuo eas nullo modo admittendas, neque vllum posse earum vsum esse bonum. Nam cùm effictor efsectórque imaginis maledictus est à Deo, tum etiam ipsa imago, quemadmodum satis perspicitur ex Sapientiæ libro, capite III. XII. XIII, & XV.
units.tr: Afterwards, being asked about images, whether it was lawful for faithful men to have them, I replied that, as far as I was concerned, I altogether required none, and that they ought in no way to be carried into the churches of Christians. For by such images the very churches are profaned, which have been dedicated to hearing the Word of God, to administering the sacraments, and to offering public prayers; the holiness of these things ought to be placed before images and likenesses. I showed, moreover, that such fashioned likenesses or painted pictures often call men away from the Word of God. Yet, I said, in private houses they are admitted and set up as indifferent things, provided no idolatry is practised with them; for then indeed they must be removed from the houses. Nevertheless, as far as I am concerned, since I see that the Word of God forbids them so precisely, I hold that they must by no means be admitted, and that no use of them can be good. For since the maker and worker of an image is cursed by God, so too the image itself is cursed, as is sufficiently clear from the Book of Wisdom, chapters 3, 12, 13 and 15.

units.la: De Baptismo me etiam interrogarunt. in quo existimo eos me aliquem Anabaptistam esse arbitratos. Ego autem respondi, Baptismum esse signum eius foederis, quod Deus cum Christianis instituit, testificatus se Deum nostrum ac seminis nostri esse velle: in quo etiam testificatur se nobis peccata remittere. Hanc autem Dei promissionem, Baptismus aquæ nobis confirmat. Nam sicut aqua abluuntur corporis sordes, ita maculæ animarum in Baptismo eluuntur ac tolluntur, idque virtute sanguinis Christi, qui tū[?] operatione Spiritus sancti nobis communicatur. Præterea Baptismus est signum assiduæ mortificationis, quæ in nobis esse debet. Nam quemadmodum aqua capiti injicitur, ad momentum tamen temporis, non ut prorsus submergamur: ita eadem mortem vitæ præcedentis significat, ut vitam suscipiamus novam & degamus. Ac Baptismus quidem communicari debet omnibus, tum pueris ac infantibus, tum hominibus adultis, qui nomen Christi profiteri volunt. Dico autem homines ad grandiorem ætatem provectos, qui in infantia pueritiaque baptizati non fuerunt. Itaque tunc cum ad fidem veniunt Christianam, baptizandi sunt. Quod si noluerint facere, habentes opportunitatem, ut contemptores sanctorum Dei institutorum, nunquam in regnum cælorum ingredientur. Infantes autem fidelium, quanquis non habeant fide actu efficacem eius quod credendum est, propter ætatem: tamen in fide parentum, in Baptismo præsentandi sunt. nam virtute promissionis Dei, eiusque testificationis ad ipsum pertinent. Quod autem ad infantes pertinet, qui sine Baptismo moriuntur, quorum quidem parentes sunt fideles, aut alter eorum, credo eos ad Deum pertinere, neque in Limbo esse, quemadmodum hactenus persuasum fuit. Neque enim Deus gratiam suam alligat sacramento, ut sine eo sui esse non possint, modo infantes huiusmodi sint, ut sacramentum accipere potuerint.
units.tr: They also questioned me about Baptism, in which I think they supposed me to be some Anabaptist. I replied that Baptism is the sign of that covenant which God established with Christians, testifying that he wishes to be our God and the God of our seed; in it he also testifies that he forgives us our sins. This promise of God, Baptism with water confirms to us. For just as the filth of the body is washed away with water, so the stains of souls are washed away and removed in Baptism, and this by the power of the blood of Christ, which is then communicated to us by the working of the Holy Spirit. Moreover, Baptism is a sign of the constant mortification which ought to be in us. For just as water is poured on the head, yet only for a moment, and not so that we are utterly drowned, so it also signifies the death of the former life, that we may take up a new life and live it. Baptism ought indeed to be given to all, both to boys and infants, and to adults who wish to profess the name of Christ. I mean men advanced to a more mature age who were not baptized in infancy or boyhood. Therefore, when they come to the Christian faith, they must be baptized. But if they refuse to do so, although they have the opportunity, as despisers of the holy institutions of God, they will never enter the kingdom of heaven. The infants of believers, although on account of their age they do not have the faith that actively grasps what is to be believed, must nevertheless be presented for Baptism in the faith of their parents, for by the power of God's promise and his testimony they belong to him. As for infants who die without Baptism, whose parents are believers, or one of them is, I believe they belong to God and are not in limbo, as has hitherto been believed. For God does not so bind his grace to the sacrament that they cannot be his without it, provided they are infants of such a kind that they could have received the sacrament.

units.la: De votis autem quæsiuerunt ex me, an homo Christianus vovere posset atque perpetuis rei alicuius votis se obstringere. Ego respondi, hominem Christianum posse vota nuncupare earum rerum, quas gratas Deo esse certò scit, & in sua esse potestate: non aliter. Et quoniam facile cognoscebam eos præcipuè de votis monasticis quærere, respondi hominem non posse votum facere perpetuæ paupertatis aut obedientiæ, multò verò minus castitatis. Quamobrem cos qui ita vouissent, veniam eorum votorum debere à Deo petere, vocatosque ad rationem vitae contrariam ei quam ante vouerant, posse eam suscipere sine vllo scrupulo conscientiae eius, quae prioribus votis obstricta & obligata videri posset. Verum quidem est, quod ad tempus aliquod, harum rerum vota nuncupari ac fieri possunt, sed non in perpetuum.
units.tr: They also asked me about vows, whether a Christian man could vow and bind himself by perpetual vows to something. I replied that a Christian man may make vows of those things which he knows for certain are pleasing to God and within his own power, and not otherwise. And since I readily perceived that they were asking chiefly about monastic vows, I replied that a man cannot make a vow of perpetual poverty or obedience, and much less of chastity. Wherefore those who have so vowed ought to seek pardon for those vows from God, and, when called to a way of life contrary to that which they had vowed before, they may take it up without any scruple of conscience, which might seem bound and obligated by the earlier vows. It is true that vows of these things may be made and fulfilled for some time, but not for ever.

units.la: De Confessione vero respondi, me debere tum coram Deo meo quotidie, atque omni loco, tum etiam coram hominibus recognoscere miserum peccatorem, qui quotidie damnationem mereatur, nisi esset gratia Dei, quae nobis per Christum impertitur. Ita delicta & peccata mea Deo confiteri debeo, eorumque veniam ab eodem postulare. Huiusmodi confessione referta est Scriptura, eaque vsi Prophetae, Apostoli, caeterique omnes, qui pie Deum coluerunt. Quod autem ad homines pertinet, si proximum meum verbo aut re offendi, debeo ei delictum meum, aut etiam plura, quibus eum offendi, confiteri, ut & ego ei, & ipse mihi placatus reconcilietur, omnisque animi offensio deponatur, & mutua benevolentia conseruetur. Est etiam aliud confessionis genus, quod versatur in consilio petendo de iis rebus, quae in aliquam dubitationem conscientiae scrupulosae ac perplexae venire possunt. Ut si quispiam dubitet de re aliqua, propter quam conscientia ipsius sit perturbata, quamuis misericordiam Dei cognoscat in promissionibus: quia tamen eas generaliter considerat, non proprie ad se applicat, in aliqua dubitatione perplexitateque versatur: tum recte fiet & sapienter, si homo ita perplexus ac perturbatus, prudentem aliquem quaerat, & consulat, cui possit molestiam animi sui declarare. Tu vero is a quo consilium petitur, debet proponere particulares Scripturae sententias de misericordia Dei, quibus alterum consoletur, eumque omni scrupulo liberet. Hoc autem confessionis genus maximopere laudandum est, ut a Deo profectum: ex quo etiam confessio auricularis fuit introducta. Nam illud quidem fiebat in secreto, atque inter duos, quemadmodum isti fieri volunt in confessione auriculari: quae quidem ex Deo non est, neque testimonio Scripturae sanctae approbata. Neque enim Dominus superstitiosam peccatorum enumerationem ab homine requirit, ne fieri quidem potest: quemadmodum propheta[?] ropheta Dauid satis ostendit, cùm dicit, Domine, peccata quis intelligit? Et mox eo in Psalmo XIX. Ab occultis munda me. Papa tamen hoc iubet, etiam sub peccato mortali, ad minimum quidem semel in anno. Itaque ego huiusmodi confessionem reijcio, ut gehennam conscientiarum, abyssum & gurgitem inferorum, ad absorbendas ac devorandas miseras animas accommodatum.
units.tr: As for confession, I replied that I ought to acknowledge myself, every day and in every place before my God, and also before men, a miserable sinner who deserves damnation every day, were it not for the grace of God which is bestowed on us through Christ. Thus I ought to confess my offences and sins to God and to ask pardon of him. Scripture is full of such confession, and the prophets, the apostles, and all others who worshipped God devoutly have used it. As for men, if I have offended my neighbour in word or deed, I ought to confess to him my offence, or even the several things by which I have offended him, so that both he may be reconciled to me and I to him, being appeased, and every offence of mind may be laid aside and mutual goodwill preserved. There is also another kind of confession, which consists in seeking counsel about those matters which may fall into some doubt of a scrupulous and perplexed conscience. For example, if someone doubts about some matter on account of which his conscience is troubled, although he knows God's mercy in the promises, yet because he considers them in general and does not apply them properly to himself, he remains in doubt and perplexity. Then it is right and wise for such a perplexed and troubled man to seek out some prudent person, and consult him, to whom he may declare the anxiety of his mind. The one from whom counsel is sought ought to set forth particular sentences of Scripture about God's mercy, by which he may console the other and free him from every scruple. This kind of confession is greatly to be praised, as coming from God; from it also auricular confession was introduced. For that was done in secret and between two persons, as these men wish it to be done in auricular confession; but that is not from God, nor approved by the testimony of holy Scripture. For the Lord does not require from man a superstitious enumeration of sins, nor indeed could it be done; as the prophet David shows well when he says, "Who understands his sins?" and soon after, in the nineteenth Psalm, "Cleanse me from secret faults." Yet the Pope commands this, even under mortal sin, at least once a year. Therefore I reject this kind of confession, as a hell of consciences, and an abyss and whirlpool of the underworld, fitted to swallow up and devour miserable souls.

units.la: Ex me praeterea quaesiuerunt, quid ego de virginitate Mariae senserim, an crederem eam virginem filium suum peperisse, ac postea permansisse virginem. Ego autem respondi articulum symboli, Credo conceptum fuisse de Spiritu sancto, natum ex Maria virgine: atq; etiam credo eam in virginitate perseuerasse. Tum doctor Hasardus, ut est homo plane stupidus & indoctus, Quid, inquit, te mouet, ut credas virginitatem Virginis, cùm non sit locus Scripturae quo id probari queat? Cui respondi, me satis clare & manifeste reperisse. nam scriptum est, quod Ioseph eam non cognouerat, quum filium suum primogenitum peperit. Tum ille tacuit, nec postea quicquam dixit. Multa sunt alia, quae ex me quaesiuerunt: sed haec sunt praecipua & maxima, quae tibi satis esse debent. Die veneris doctores supremi templi, magister Fiablus, & magister Auertinus, me sunt aggressi: ut & hodie doctor Hasardus. Hi omnes conantur me haereticum conuincere, praecipuè in ea parte doctrinae, quae ad Missam pertinet. Neque dubito, quin magnopere cupiant eam sibi salua[?] relinquinec immerito, ut quae culinae ipsorum maximè inseruiat, & unde quaestus uberrimus ad illos redeat. Sed Dei gratia magistratus & iudices optimè animadverterunt, me minimè mutum, neque verbo destitutum. Nam eis planè nihil concessi: sed quod de illis dicendum erat, praeter illorum expectationem, verè liberèque demonstraui. Cùm ipsi ad me venerunt, satis asperè sum loquutus. In quo quidem si verbis paulò liberior, modestiam Christianam non conseruaui, oro Dominum ut mihi ignoscat. Amor & zelus honoris ac verbi eius, me ita animatum reddidit, atque impulit, idque praesente magistratu. Quae res quosdam laetitia, alios affecit moestitia, ut à me cum contumeliis discederent. verùm id me non conturbat. Neque enim melior sum, quàm Dominus meus & magister & caput, Iesus Christus. Tu mea soror atque omnes fratres, Patrem optimum nostrum orate per Jesum Christum filium eius, ut me Spiritu suo sancto confirmet in veritate verbi sui, atque incrementum fidei bonorumque caelestium mihi tribuat. Equidem, quod mei est officii, eum pro tota ecclesia orabo, privatimque pro te ac Margarita optima sorore mea. Dominus memor sit eorum studiorum & officiorum, quae in me ea contulit, & adhuc confert. Gratia Domini nostri tecum sit.
units.tr: Moreover, they asked me what I thought about the virginity of Mary, whether I believed that she gave birth to her son as a virgin and remained a virgin afterwards. I answered with the article of the creed: I believe that he was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary; and I also believe that she persevered in virginity. Then Doctor Hasardus, who is a thoroughly stupid and unlearned man, said: "What moves you to believe in the virginity of the Virgin, when there is no passage of Scripture by which it can be proved?" To him I replied that I had found it stated clearly and plainly enough, for it is written that Joseph "knew her not until she had brought forth her firstborn son." Then he fell silent and said nothing more. There are many other things they asked me, but these are the main and chief points, and they should be enough for you. On Friday the doctors of the cathedral, Master Fiablus and Master Auertinus, attacked me, and today Doctor Hasardus did so as well. All of them try to convict me of heresy, especially on that part of doctrine which concerns the Mass. I do not doubt that they very much want to keep it safe for themselves, and not without reason, since it serves their kitchen most of all and brings them a very rich profit. But by the grace of God the magistrates and judges have clearly seen that I am neither silent nor lacking in words. For I conceded nothing to them at all; rather, I demonstrated truly and freely what had to be said about them, beyond their expectation. When they came to me, I spoke quite harshly. If in this I was rather free in my words and did not keep Christian modesty, I pray the Lord to forgive me. Love and zeal for his honour and his Word so inflamed and impelled me, and that in the presence of the magistrate. This affected some with joy and others with sadness, so that they left me with insults; but that does not trouble me. For I am no better than my Lord and Master and Head, Jesus Christ. You, my sister, and all the brethren, pray to our most good Father through Jesus Christ his Son, that he may strengthen me by his Holy Spirit in the truth of his Word, and grant me an increase of faith and of heavenly good things. Indeed, as is my duty, I will pray to him for the whole Church, and privately for you and for Margarita, my most excellent sister. May the Lord remember the labours and kindnesses which you have shown and still show to me. The grace of our Lord be with you.

units.la: Epistola ciusdem Petri Brulii.
units.tr: The letter of the same Peter Brulius.

units.la: OMnibus fidelibus, qui persecutionem patiuntur propter praedicationem Euangelii auditam, aut domi ipsorum defensam, qui sunt Tornaci, Vallencenis, Insulis, Atrebati, Douaci, atque in caeteris urbibus ac locis, Petrus Brulius, servus Dei, missus ad vos invisendos, & animos vestros aeterno Dei verbo consolandos, gratiam, pacem & misericordiam a Deo patre, & dilecto filio eius Jesu Christo domino nostro, exoptat dari vobis, & perpetuo in cordibus vestris conservari, Amen.
units.tr: To all the faithful who suffer persecution for the preaching of the Gospel that they have heard, or for defending it in their homes, who are at Tournai, Valenciennes, Lille, Arras, Douai, and in other cities and places: Peter Brulius, servant of God, sent to visit you and to comfort your hearts with the eternal Word of God, wishes you grace, peace and mercy from God the Father and from his beloved Son Jesus Christ our Lord, and wishes that they may be given to you and kept forever in your hearts. Amen.

units.la: Ego, fratres, semper gratias Deo meo ago in meis precibus, quod voluerit nos suos esse declarare, ea communione ac participatione disciplinae, qua filios suos castigare solet. in quam etiam vocavit ac recepit nos, ne cum maligno mundo pereamus, a quo quidem nos morte charissimi filii sui Jesu Christi redemit. Certe, fratres mei, nobis, nobis datum est e caelo, non solum ut credamus in Christum, verum etiam ut aliquid pro eo patiamur: quod quidem omnibus credentibus non est impertitum. Sed quemadmodum testatur Paulus in sua epistola ad Philippenses, est donum Dei singulare. Hac ratione nos cognoscimus ac scimus nos eius esse, atque etiam ex domesticis ipsius, istaque omnia nobis in bonum cedere: cum optimus Pater nos ita amet, ut cruci atque afflictionibus Filii primogeniti conformes efficiat: qui quidem peccatum nunquam fecit, nec dolus inventus est in ore eius: & tamen crucem perpessus est. Hanc autem acerbissimam mortis poenam propterea sustinuit, ut nos a morte redimeret, cuius imperio oppressi tenebamur. Is, inquam, ita est passus, ut suis doloribus nostros dolores & afflictiones sanctificaret. Nam nunc quidem nos carceres, verbera, iudicia, ignem, catenas ferreas, irrisiones, ludi-bria, bria, & contumelias non metuemus: nullas denique machinationes atque incursiones diaboli & mundi ut maledictas pertimescemus:sed ea omnia perferemus ut testimonia & signa summae clementiae ac benevolentiae Dei erga nos.Plane,fratres mei, Jesu Christi mors nos à morte aeterna,quam meriti eramus,liberat,atque etiam corporalem nostram mortem sanctificat. Carceres eius nostros sanctificant: eius flagellatio,nostram:judicium illius,nostrum: vincula eius, ignominiae contumeliaeque,nostras sanctificat . deniq; quicquid nos patimur,eius communione fit sanctum,quoniam eius causa toleramus. Quare ne perturbemur in nostris aerumnis & calamitatibus, quasi novae atque alienae nobis cvenirent:sed contra potius laetemur cum in varias huiusmodi calamitates incidimus,scientes quod afflictio parit patientiam, patientia probationem,probatio spem in Deo,quae non confundit: propterea quod charitas Dei in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctū diffusa est,fidesque nostra non aliter,quam aurum & argenti in fornace perficitur & illustratur. Quemadmodum enim de bonitate auri & argenti,non facile judicari potest,nisi ea in indice lapide aut igne explorentur ac probentur:ita qualis sit fides vniuscuiusque non bene perspici potest,nisi ad examen afflictionum & probationem adducatur.
units.tr: Brothers, I always give thanks to my God in my prayers that he has willed to declare us to be his own, through that fellowship and participation in discipline by which he is accustomed to chastise his sons, into which he has also called and received us, so that we might not perish with the wicked world, from which indeed he has redeemed us by the death of his most beloved Son Jesus Christ. Truly, brothers, it has been given to us from heaven, to us, not only to believe in Christ but also to suffer something for him; and this has not been granted to all believers. But as Paul testifies in his epistle to the Philippians, it is a singular gift of God. By this we know and are sure that we are his, and of his household, and that all these things turn out for our good, since the best Father loves us in such a way that he makes us conformed to the cross and afflictions of his firstborn Son. He indeed never committed sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth, and yet he endured the cross. But he bore this most bitter penalty of death for this reason, that he might redeem us from the death under whose rule we were held captive. He, I say, suffered in such a way that by his sorrows he might sanctify our sorrows and afflictions. For now we do not fear prisons, scourgings, trials, fire, iron chains, derision, mockeries, and insults; finally we do not dread the plots and assaults of the devil and the world as accursed things, but we will bear all these things as witnesses and signs of the highest mercy and goodwill of God toward us. Plainly, brothers, the death of Jesus Christ frees us from eternal death, which we had deserved, and also sanctifies our bodily death. His prisons sanctify our prisons; his scourging, ours; his judgment, ours; his chains, his disgrace and insults, ours. Finally, whatever we suffer becomes holy through its fellowship with him, because we endure it for his sake. Therefore, let us not be disturbed in our hardships and calamities, as though they came upon us as something new and strange; but rather let us rejoice when we fall into various calamities of this kind, knowing that affliction produces patience, patience proof, proof hope in God, which does not disappoint, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit; and our faith is perfected and made bright in no other way than gold and silver are in the furnace. For just as the goodness of gold and silver cannot easily be judged unless they are tested and proved on the touchstone or by fire, so the quality of each one's faith cannot be well seen unless it is brought to the test and proof of afflictions.

units.la: Tum enim cognoscimus supernè petra,an super arenâ aedificati simus: seménne simus sparsiû in terra bonam,an jactum inter saxa, atq; subito enatum & sublatum:aurum & argentū,pretiosíque lapides in verofundamento aedificati,an ligna,stipulae,stramina,ad ignis,id est,afflictionis consumptionem opportuna. Fratres, revocate in memoriam eos,qui fuerunt ante vos,Dominóque placuerunt. Cogitate omni tempore,quid usu venerit servis Dei. tum vos maximam laetitiae causam habebitis,cum videbitis vos jis similes atque conformes,qui Deo purê castéque servientes , huiusmodi molestias vitae & aerumnas perpessi fuerunt. Testis certè est Jesus Christus,ante cuius Apostolos impij Prophetas persequuti fuerant,quemadmodum postea Apostolos sunt persequuti, & post eos Evangelistas, ac pastores primae ecclesiae Christianae:omnésque qui à primis mundi temporibus, usque ad haec novissima,integrè Deo inservire voluerunt,ab impiis hominibus huic mundo deditis afflicti & vexati fuerunt . Etiam in ipsa domo & familia patris nostri Abrahæ, huius conditionis specimen editum fuit. Nam is qui erat secundum carnem, filius ancillæ Agar, persequebatur cum qui erat secundum spiritum, filium liberæ, Saræ matrisfamilias. Si qui infestantur & vexantur à fratribus ac proximis, cogitent nihil ipsis accidere, cuius exemplum in pijs ac sanctis hominibus, Deum metuentibus, non editum fuerit. Videant Abelum, probum filium Deique amicum, à fratre Caino per invidiam interfectum. Diuus Joannes in prima sua epistola, eius cædis factæ rationem adfert, Videbat, inquit, opera sua mala esse, fratris vero esse bona. itaque invidia motus, fratrem occidit, non aliam ob causam, nisi quòd à vitæ impiæ ratione consuetudineque abhorrebat ac dissidebat. Qui talia patiuntur, memoria teneant, quæ Matthæi X, & Lucæ XII, à Domino nostro dicta sunt.
units.tr: For then we learn whether we are built upon the rock above or upon the sand; whether we are seed sown on good ground or a seed cast among stones, which springs up suddenly and is taken away; whether we are built upon the true foundation with gold, silver and precious stones, or with wood, stubble and straw, which are fit for the consumption of fire, that is, of affliction. Brothers, call to mind those who went before you and pleased the Lord. Consider at all times what has happened to the servants of God. Then you will have the greatest cause for joy, when you see yourselves like and conformed to those who, serving God purely and chastely, endured such troubles and hardships of life. Jesus Christ is surely a witness, before whose apostles the wicked persecuted the prophets, just as afterward they persecuted the apostles, and after them the evangelists and the ministers of the first Christian Church; and all who, from the first times of the world until these latest, have wished to serve God wholeheartedly have been afflicted and harassed by impious men devoted to this world. Even in the very house and family of our father Abraham, an example of this condition was shown. For he who was according to the flesh, the son of the slave Hagar, persecuted him who was according to the Spirit, the son of Sarah, the free mistress of the household. If any are harassed and harmed by brothers and kinsmen, let them consider that nothing has happened to them that has not been seen in pious and holy men who fear God. Let them look at Abel, the upright son and friend of God, killed by his brother Cain out of envy. The divine John, in his first epistle, gives the reason for that murder: "He saw," he says, "that his own works were evil, but his brother's were good." So, moved by envy, he killed his brother, for no other cause than that he shrank from and disagreed with the ungodly manner and custom of life. Let those who suffer such things keep in mind what our Lord said in Matthew 10 and Luke 12.

units.la: Quòd si qui à proprijs liberis aut uxore afflguntur[?], contemnuntur, irridentur, exemplum Noë & Job sibi proponant. Videant Mosen & Aaronem à familia Chore, Dathan, & Abiron, magnis injurijs contumeliisque affectos. Considerent Dauidem, qui tamen fuit rex: & intelligent cum à Saule & à fratribus atque etiam propriis filijs eiectum atque expulsum, irrisum, coque compulsum, ut in montibus locisque desertis vagaretur, atque probris omnibus à Semei afficeretur. Jam vero quid Eliæ usu venit, ciusq; successori Elisæo, Esaiæ, Jeremiæ, Ezechieli, aliisque Prophetis? itaque ob hanc causam, Stephanus Judæis eadem omnium piorum ac fidelium seruorum Dei exprobrat. Manasses vero, nonne uno eodemque die eam cædem edidit, in qua Hierosolyma sanguine Prophetarum redundauit? Atque hoc quidem Christus Matth. XXI, ijsdé Judæis memorat & exprobrat, proposita parabola eius, qui operarijs vineã suam reliquerat: cuius seruos necauerunt, tum eius etiam filium. Existimo, fratres, hæc quæ vobis commemoraui ac proposui, nullam animis vestris perturbatione allatura. Intelligitis enim ea ciusmodi esse, ut à Deo authore ac gubernatore ecclesiæ proficiscatur. Quæ ego hoc quidem tempore ad vos scripsi, idem antea libeter facturus, si mihi ullo modo licuisset in domo hospitis mei, & custodis ipsius arcis. est enim homo plane ignarus, à quo nec chartam nec atramentum obtinere potuissem. Nunc autem etsi in maioribus sim loci angustijs, quàm fuerim apud illum, possum ta[?]ien cor magis quàm antea dilatare, ac vobis liberius explicare. Quae accipietis hanc epistolam, ut ab eo qui gratiam Domini nostri non minus[?] vobis quàm sibiipsi exoptat.
units.tr: But if any are afflicted, despised or mocked by their own children or wife, let them set before themselves the example of Noah and Job. Let them look at Moses and Aaron, greatly wronged and insulted by the family of Korah, Dathan and Abiram. Let them consider David, who was nevertheless a king, and let them understand how he was cast out and expelled by Saul and by his brothers and even by his own sons, mocked, and so driven to wander in the mountains and desert places, and subjected to every kind of reproach from Shimei. And indeed what happened to Elijah, and to his successor Elisha, to Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and the other prophets? For this reason Stephen also charged the Jews with the same treatment of all the pious and faithful servants of God. Did not Manasseh, on one and the same day, carry out that slaughter in which Jerusalem overflowed with the blood of the prophets? And Christ indeed recalls and reproaches these same Jews in Matthew 21, in the parable of the man who left his vineyard to the workers: they killed his servants, and then his son as well. I think, brothers, that these things which I have mentioned and set before you will bring no disturbance to your minds. For you understand that they are of such a kind that they proceed from God, the author and governor of the Church. These things I have now written to you, and I would gladly have done the same earlier, if it had been possible for me in any way in the house of my host and of the keeper of the citadel. For he is a man entirely ignorant, from whom I could not obtain paper or ink. Now, although I am in narrower quarters than I was with him, I can nevertheless enlarge my heart more than before and explain myself to you more freely. Whoever receives this letter, [receive it] from one who wishes the grace of our Lord no less for you than for himself.

units.la: Alia eiusdem M. Petri Brulii epistola, ad fideles missa.
units.tr: Another letter of the same M. Peter Brully, sent to the faithful.

units.la: Fratres mei, mihi bonum videtur, si hoc modo vos afficiam ea laetitia, quam capio ex iis afflictionibus, quae nobis acciderunt, ut vos quoque mecum gratias Domino agatis, atque unà in meis vinculis & afflictionibus gaudeatis. Isti enim sunt fructus eius doctrinae, quam nos didicimus, si quidem Iesum Christum crucifixum didicimus & cognouimus. Nullus ergo nostrum deficiat ac despondeat animum: perseueret autem in proposita disciplina breui adhuc tempore: & is qui venturus est veniet, nec moram ullam faciet. interea iustus meus [?]ide viuet: quòd si se subtraxerit, inquit Dominus, animae meae nō placebit. Quare id quidem nobis cauendum est. nam vos scitis eos salvos futuros, qui usque in finem perseueraucrint: etiam eos, qui certant lucta aut cursu, ut victores corona non donari, nisi legitimè certauerint.
