In te enim vnicè omne curã meã iacto, ac fiducia colloco. Viribus ac telis omnibus impetũ in me faciunt, pauperculã creaturã tuã oppugnaturi. Adsit quæso robur gratiæ tuæ, vt ne quid extimescam eos, qui tibi aduersantur. In te enim omnis spes meã ac fortitudo sita fixáq; est. Præterea ex animo te obtestor mitissime atq; idẽ factiss. Deo, pro infinita pietate tua, hac ipsis in me violetiã & iniuriã condonet misericordia tua: simulq; pro eadem bonitate tua, dignetur quaeso tua pietas occæcatas eorum mentes aperire, ut quae tibi accepta sunt sequentes, simplici verbo doctrinae tuae, sine asciritijs[?] humanae inuentionis nugamentis, sese regendos praebeant in omnibus, Amen:ô Domine, Amen.
units.tr: O Lord, I have more enemies than the hairs of my head. Yet grant, most merciful God, that I may nowhere yield, overcome by the allurements of words. But you, O Lord, fight for me and answer for me. For in you alone I cast all my care and place my trust. They make their assault on me with all their strength and weapons, intending to overwhelm your poor little creature. May the strength of your grace be present, I pray, so that I may fear nothing from those who oppose you. For in you all my hope and strength is set and fixed. Further, I beseech you from my heart, most gentle and most merciful God, that by your infinite goodness you would, through your mercy, pardon them for this violence and injury done to me; and at the same time by that same goodness, let your mercy deign to open their blinded minds, so that, following what has been revealed to them, they may submit themselves to be ruled in all things by the simple word of your teaching, without the trifles of human invention. Amen: O Lord, Amen.

units.la: Hactenus de carceribus & tormentis laudatissimae huius fœminae dictum est. Restat nunc quae de exitu, & vltimo eius supplicio subsequuta sunt, attingamus. Postquam igitur cō[?] nata loco & genere Anna Askeua, in quo magna cum dignitate viuere ei licuisset, si mundum maluisset quam Christum sequi, ita tormentis confecta esset, vt neque viuere in tanta ægritudine diu, neque occulte mori per aduersarios posset: dicto tandem supplicij die, in forum equinum producitur, sella quidem fulta, quoniam pedibus ipsa incedere prae tormentis haud potuit. Sic itaque ad palum peruentum est, vbi catena ferrea per medium reducta corpus affixam tenebat. Præparatis iam rebus quæ ad incendium pertinerent, allatæ tandem regis literæ quæ veniam reuocaturæ vitamque offerrent, proponebantur, quas illa tantum abest vt amplecteretur, vt ne aspicere quidem sustineret. Adhibebatur & Shaxtonus, qui publicè reuocatis eo die opinionibus, simul & ipsam reflectere ad suam leuitatem longa oratione satagebat: cui non minus fortiter & illa reclamabat. Sicq; tot exercita molestijs, tot perfuncta tormentis, finito longo agonum cursu, sacra Dei victima flammis circundata obdormiuit in Domino. anno M.D.XLVI: singularis constantia vel laude relinques posteris, quam admirari possent: vel exemplum quod debeant imitari.
units.tr: So far we have spoken of the prisons and torments of this most praiseworthy woman. It remains now to touch on what followed her departure and her final punishment. Anna Askew, born of a family and rank in which she could have lived with great dignity, had she preferred the world to following Christ, was so worn down by torments that she could neither live long in such sickness nor die secretly, away from her adversaries. At last, on the appointed day of punishment, she was led into the Horsefair, carried in a chair, since she could not walk on her feet because of the torments. So she was brought to the stake, where an iron chain drawn round her middle held her body fastened. When the things needed for the fire were now prepared, the king's letters were brought forward, which offered pardon and life if she would revoke, but she was so far from embracing them that she could not even bear to look at them. Shaxton was also brought in, who, after the opinions had been publicly recanted that day, strove with a long speech to turn her too back to his own inconstancy; but she protested against him no less firmly. So, worn by so many troubles and having endured so many torments, when the long course of her struggle was finished, the holy sacrifice of God, surrounded by flames, fell asleep in the Lord, in the year 1546. She leaves to posterity a singular constancy, which they may admire for its praise, or an example which they ought to imitate.

units.la: IOANNES LACELLVS, IOANNES ADA- mus, Nicolaus Belenianus.
units.tr: John Lacellus, John Adamus, Nicholas Belenianus.

units.la: RANT in eodem rogo cum illa impositi, paritérque exusti[?] Nicolaus Belenianus quidam è[?] comitatu Salopiensi sacerdos Ioannes Adamus vestiarius, & Ioannes Lacellus, vir & genere & virtute nobilis, tum etiam ex aula & familia Henrici regis. Huius extat succincta quaedam de corporis & sanguinis sacramento è carcere scripta epistola apologetica, qua tum errorem illorum, qui non contenti spirituali Cœnæ perceptione, panis nullam relinquunt materiam in sacramento, confutat: tum etiam sinistram quorundam de se interpretationem oretationem propulsat. Istis non infeliciter id accidit, quòd cum Anna Askeua simul commorarentur. Siquidem huius exemplo ac oratione adanimati, viri licet per se & fortes & alacres, maioris tamen consolationis materiam ex fœmina, in tam tristi hoc mortis genere percipiunt: dum non solùm eius intrepidam constantiam suspiciunt, sed & verbis subinde illius appellati, magis magisque omnem exuunt formidinem. Itaque mutuis sese hortatibus communientes, lictore atque ignes expectant qui demum per circumfusam materiam grassantes, beata eorum corpora felici hauserunt martyrio, inq; cineres redegerunt, anno Domini & salutis nostræ M.D.XLVI. circa mensem Iunium.
units.tr: were placed on the same pyre with her and burned alike Nicholas Belenianus, a certain priest of Shropshire; John Adamus, a clothier; and John Lacellus, a man of noble birth and virtue, who was also from the court and household of King Henry. There survives from Lacellus a brief apologetic letter on the sacrament of the body and blood, written from prison, in which he refutes the error of those who, not content with the spiritual reception of the Supper, leave no material bread in the sacrament, and also repels the unfavourable interpretation put upon him by some. For these men it was no misfortune that they stayed together with Anne Askew. Encouraged by her example and words, although they were brave and eager men by nature, they drew greater comfort from a woman in so grim a kind of death: they not only admired her fearless constancy but, being addressed by her from time to time, cast off every fear more and more. So, strengthening one another by mutual exhortation, they awaited the executioner and the fires, which at last, spreading through the piled-up material, consumed their blessed bodies in a happy martyrdom and reduced them to ashes, in the year of the Lord and of our salvation 1546, around the month of June.

units.la: Quorum post auspicatissima martyria, Henricus Rex sexto post mense morbo implicitus moritur anno M.D.XLVII. mense Ian. anno autem ex quo regnare cœpit, XXXVIII. cuius mors optatâ sanè Brytannicæ ecclesiæ tranquillitatem attulit, quàdoquidem permulta in catalogo excepta hominum nomina, atque ad regem eo tempore delata per wintoniensem & episcopos dicebantur, quorum breui sequuturum erat supplicium, nisi mors interuenisset Regis. Hæc ex Ioan. Foxo.
units.tr: After their most auspicious martyrdoms, King Henry, afflicted by illness six months later, died in January 1547, in the thirty-eighth year of his reign. His death brought a much-desired tranquillity to the British church, since it was said that many names had been drawn up on a list and reported to the king at that time by the Bishop of Winchester and the other bishops, and that their execution would soon follow, had the king's death not intervened. This from John Foxe.

units.la: Liber quintus Actionum MARTYRUM.
units.tr: Book Five of the Acts of the MARTYRS.

units.la: N. ENZINAS BVRGENSIS Hispanus, Romæ pro sancta Euangelii veritate exustus.
units.tr: N. Enzinas of Burgos, a Spaniard, burned at Rome for the holy truth of the Gospel.

units.la: Ic[?] rursus ad Hispanos orationem nostram reuocat memoratu dignum martyrium insignis viri, cui Enzinas popu-lari lingua, à quercu scz cognomen erat. Huius frater Franciscus cognominis illius appellatione Græcè reddita, Dryander dictus est, & apud Germanos ob pietatem atque eruditionem clarus extitit, de quo id obiter dicendum est. Quū inusitata lingua, hoc est, Hispaniensi Christus loqui cœpisset, id nullo modo ferre potuit auris Hispanica. Bruxellis etenim in aula Brabantica quum Euangelij in Hispanicam linguam versionem Carolo V. Cæsari obtulisset, in carcerem coniectus fuit, quúmque totos xv. menses in summis angusuis[?] detentus fuisset, nec aliud quàm præsentem mortem expectaret, tandem insperato Dei beneficio inde ereptus fuit 1. die mensis Februarij anni M.D.XLV. ostaua hora post cœnam offendit ianuas carceris apertas quæ eum ad liberationem muitabant: ipse vero tantum tamque optatum Dei beneficium amplexus, incolumis euasit, atque in Germaniam redijt, in qua quod reliquum vitæ fuit, in cœtu fidelium cum summa virtute peregit: ipsius frater de quo nunc dicere instituimus, studio nõ inferior, quũ multis suæ nationis hominibus ea quæ à Deo acceperat Euangelij luce præluxisset ac profuisset, (in quorum numero fuit Ioannes Diazius cuius historiam superiori libro contexuimus) alio tandem à Domino euocatus fuit. nam vt stultis parentum & propinquorum studijs morem gereret, Romæ visendæ gratia profectionem instituit, qua in vrbe (quæ impietatis sentina, & malorum omnium lerna merito habetur) vir pius aliquandiu cum summa animi molestia vixit: ac quèadmodum de Lot quum Sodomæ habitaret, Scriptura dicit: quotidie animam iustam iniqua illorum facta, & videndo & audiendo, excruciabat. Attamen quæ immensa Patris æterni est bonitas hominum iniquitate infinitis partibus maior, etiam in ea vrbe (quæ abominationum omnium est sedes atque ἀθέτου[?] nefanda schola) voluit Dominus hunc veritatis suæ testem proponere, qui ante ora patrum, Romæ sub mœnibus altis pulchram mortem oppeteret, ac ignis splendore quo viuus concrematus est, purpuratorum & magnæ illius bestiæ oculos perstringeret. Captus itaq; & proditus à suis Hispanis, in arctissimum carcerem conjectus inclususque est, ac deinde in maximo amplıssimorum hominum conuentu interrogatus, cùm adessent Cardinales qui tum Romæ erant, ac tota cohors Pontificia, intrepidè constantérque defendit puram Euangelij doctrinam: omnes etiam Romanenses impietates atque imposturas condemnauit. Itaque hac eius libertate & constantia offensi non Cardinales solùm, verùm maximè ipsi Hispani ac qui sanguine coniunctì erant, clamare omnes vno ore cœperunt, comburendum esse: plerique Cardinalium vt hominis constantiam frangerent, antequam mortis sententia ferretur, hanc illi conditionem proposuerunt, vt Hispanensi more eam reconciliatorum notam acciperet, quæ à San-benito pãno nomen habet. ea in formam manticæ vtrinque pendentis cõsi itur, antica & postica parte crucis rubrae signum repraesentans: frequēs in usu est in judicijs inquisitionis Hispanicae, quum aliquem ecclesiae reconciliatum populo declarare volunt: id est, quum aliquem furciferi habitu multitudini exhibere, atque exauctoratione judiciali perpetuæ infamiæ tradere volunt. Ipse vero Enzinas nullam conditionem accipere voluit, contentus ea unica quam adeo nobilem illi Dominus tum proponebat: nempe ut sanguine suo testatam redderet verae religionis doctrinam. Eo tandem res deducta est impijs adversariorum conatibus, ut optimus vir ac Christi seruus fidelissimus, illustri martyrio ac testimonio vitam finierit in ea urbe in qua sedes non Apostolica, sed impia & scelerata perditi illius Antichristi adversus omnem Dei maiestatem se efferentis, erecta est: anno M.D.XLVI. non multò post Diazij mortem.
units.tr: Here again our account calls the Spaniards back to a memorable martyrdom of a distinguished man, whose surname in the popular tongue was Enzinas, that is, "of the oak." His brother Francis, who took the name in its Greek form, was called Dryander. He became famous among the Germans for his piety and learning, and something should be said of him in passing. When Christ had begun to speak in an unfamiliar tongue, that is, in Spanish, the Spanish ear could not bear it at all. At Brussels, in the court of Brabant, he presented to the Emperor Charles V a Spanish version of the Gospel, and for that he was thrown into prison. He was held there for fifteen months in the greatest distress, expecting nothing but present death. At last, by an unhoped-for gift of God, he was freed from there on the first day of February 1545. At about eight o'clock in the evening he found the doors of the prison open, which were to lead him out to freedom. He embraced this great and longed-for benefit of God and escaped unharmed, and he returned to Germany, where he spent the rest of his life among the company of the faithful with great virtue. His brother, of whom we now undertake to speak, was not inferior in zeal. He had shone with the light of the Gospel, which he had received from God, and had been of use to many men of his nation, among whom was John Díaz, whose history we have related in the previous book. At last he was called away by the Lord to another place. For he set out for Rome, to see the city, in order to comply with the foolish wishes of his parents and relatives. In that city, which is rightly regarded as the sewer of impiety and the hydra of all evils, this godly man lived for some time with great distress of mind. Just as Scripture says of Lot, who lived in Sodom, that he daily tormented his righteous soul by seeing and hearing their unrighteous deeds. Yet the immense goodness of the eternal Father, infinitely greater than human iniquity, willed that even in that city, which is the seat of all abominations and the unspeakable school of impiety, the Lord should set forth this witness of his truth. He was to meet a beautiful death at Rome, under the lofty walls, before the eyes of the fathers, and by the blaze of the fire in which he was burned alive he was to dazzle the eyes of the purple-clad men and of that great beast. Accordingly, he was seized and betrayed by his own Spanish countrymen, cast into a very narrow prison and shut up there. Then, questioned before a great assembly of the most distinguished men, with the Cardinals who were then at Rome present and the whole Papal retinue there, he fearlessly and steadfastly defended the pure doctrine of the Gospel. He also condemned all the impieties and impostures of Rome. Offended by this freedom and constancy of his, not only the Cardinals but especially the Spaniards themselves, and those bound to him by blood, all began to cry with one voice that he must be burned. Most of the Cardinals, in order to break the man's constancy, before the sentence of death was pronounced, offered him this condition: that he accept, in the Spanish manner, the mark of the reconciled, which takes its name from the San-benito cloth. This is made up in the form of a sack hanging front and back, displaying on the front and back the sign of a red cross. It is commonly used in the judgments of the Spanish Inquisition when they wish to declare to the people that someone has been reconciled to the Church; that is, when they wish to present someone to the crowd in the dress of a wretch and to hand him over, by a judicial degradation, to perpetual infamy. But Enzinas himself would accept no such condition, being content with the one and only thing which the Lord then set before him so nobly: namely, to confirm the doctrine of true religion by his own blood. At last, by the impious attempts of his adversaries, the matter was brought to this point: this excellent man, the most faithful servant of Christ, ended his life with an illustrious martyrdom and testimony in that city, in which was set up not an Apostolic seat but the impious and wicked seat of that lost Antichrist, who lifts himself up against all the majesty of God. This was in the year 1546, not long after the death of Díaz.

units.la: JOANNES BRUGERIUS Arvcernus.
units.tr: John Brugerius of Auvergne.

units.la: E[?]TIAM apud Arvernos sequenti anno Dominus veritatis suae testimonia extare voluit, quasi qui genus omne hominum quantumvis indocile ac dispersum motibus altis componere velit, ac radijs suae lucis illustrare. Itaque Joannem Brugerium natum in quodam Arverniae pago, cui nomen est Formal, donatum Evangelij luce in hanc Martyrum arenam evocavit. Bis comprehensus fuit iussu atque authoritate magistratus regij, qui Monferrati praecipuam habet sedem, hoc solo nomine quòd Lutheranus haberetur. Primò quidē eruperat è carcere cum quodam eiusdem accusationis reo, qui prior murum transfilierat absque ullo corporis incommodo. Brugerius posterior illum secutus, alterum crus fregit, adeò ut cum summa difficultate manus insequentium adversariorum euaserit. At vero praeter rupti cruris dolores, alios longè graviores mentis cruciatus sentiebat, quòd vocationem tam excellentem ad ferendum pro veritate testimonium à Domino oblatam refugisset. Ob id saepenumero ingemiscebat & apud familiares lamentabatur, seipsum accusans, ac iustè à Deo puniri & precīu ob ignauiam ferre aiebat: sed si iterum Deus pro sua bonitate ad confessionem sui nominis eum vocaret, magnā concipiebat spē, vacordiam istā propria ac voluntaria obedientia cōpensandi. Id quod re ipsa probauit. nam paulò post per eosdē iudices Moferrati secundò captus, proptissimā atque amplissimam suae fidei confessionem edidit, & tanta animi alacritate locutus est, ut ipsi iudices ad eius verba stupescent: plura enim quam voluissent aut sperassent audire cogebantur: ex quo satis intelligere licet, dolores illos quos prius diximus, nec vanos nec fictos fuisse. Compendiaria igitur cognitione a Iudicibus condemnatus, curiam Parisiensem appellavit: ad quam comitante multa satellitum caterva non multo post deductus est. Quum vero in carcere eius Curiae aliquandiu fuisset, tandem excusso capitalium causarum volumine, Petrus Lisetus natione Aruernus, primus tum Curiae praeses, quum intellexisset Brugerium esse Aruernum ac constanter tueri Euangelij doctrinam, mirum dictu quam indigne tulerit patriam charam ea iam labe infici: coacto consessu tholi seu classis quaestoriae, cuius ipse ductor erat, cum a sententia Brugerium dimovere non possent, tandem condemnarunt ut vivus lento igne vstularetur in urbe Ifforensi, quemadmodum plenius ex decreto adversus ipsum lato patebit: quod quidem ad verbum hic ideo inferendum duximus, ut omnes intelligere possint quanto conatu quantoque molimine nugas veritati Dei opponant ij qui se primos rerum omnium putant, qui caeco animi impetu ac gigantum more cum Deo bellare non desinunt.
units.tr: Even among the Arverni the Lord willed that the testimonies of his truth should appear the following year, as one who wishes to bring the whole human race, however unteachable and scattered, into order by lofty movements, and to illuminate it with the rays of his light. Accordingly, he called John Brugerius, born in a certain district of Auvergne called Formal, and endowed with the light of the Gospel, into this arena of martyrs. He was twice seized by the order and authority of the royal magistrate, whose principal seat is at Montferrand, on the sole ground that he was considered a Lutheran. At first he had broken out of prison together with another man accused of the same charge, who had leapt over the wall first without any injury to his body. Brugerius, following after him, broke his other leg, so that with the greatest difficulty he escaped the hands of the pursuing adversaries. But besides the pains of his broken leg, he felt other and far more grievous torments of mind, because he had refused the very excellent calling offered him by the Lord to bear witness to the truth. On this account he often groaned and lamented to his familiar friends, accusing himself, and said that he was justly punished by God and rightly suffered for his cowardice. But if God, in his goodness, should again call him to confess his name, he conceived a great hope of making up for that cowardice by his own voluntary obedience. And indeed he proved this in fact. For shortly afterwards he was seized a second time by the same judges of Montferrand, and he made a most ready and ample confession of his faith, and spoke with such cheerfulness of spirit that the judges themselves were astonished at his words. For they were compelled to hear more than they had wished or hoped. From this it may readily be understood that those pains which we mentioned earlier were neither vain nor feigned. Therefore, condemned by the judges in a summary hearing, he appealed to the Parisian court, and not long afterwards he was taken there under a large escort of guards. When he had been for some time in the prison of that court, at last, after the volume of capital causes had been searched, Pierre Lizet, a native of Auvergne, then the first president of the court, when he learned that Brugerius was an Auvergnat and steadfastly upheld the doctrine of the Gospel, was wonderfully indignant that his beloved homeland should be stained by such a blemish. A meeting of the chamber, or the criminal bench over which he himself presided, was convened; when they could not move Brugerius from his sentence, they at last condemned him to be burned alive over a slow fire in the town of Issoire, as will be made clearer from the decree issued against him. We have thought it worth inserting this here word for word, so that all may understand with what effort and what machinery those who think themselves the first of all things set their trifles against the truth of God, who with blind impulse and in the manner of giants never cease to wage war against God.

units.la: Exemplum Arcfti excerptum ex archiuis Parlamenti Parisiensis, tertio die Martii M.D.XLVII.
units.tr: Copy of the arrest taken from the archives of the Parliament of Paris, 3 March 1547.

units.la: ISOper Curiam processu facto per Bailliuum Monferrati, aut eius locumtenentem, contra Ioannem Brugicre captiuum in carcere Palatij, propter blasphemias & errores sacramentarios, eidem impositos per conclusiones Procuratoris generalis Regis: visis omnibus ac consideratis ad reparationem blasphemiarum haereticarum, & sermonum scandalosorum, atque errorum contrariorum sanctae fidei catholicae, & doctrinae ecclesiae, dictorum, prolatorum, & scriptorum per nominatum captiuum contra honorem Dei & sancti Sacramenti altaris, matrisque nostrae sanctae ecclesiae, & constitutionum eius, ut plane declaratum est in processu contra ipsum facto: dicta Curia illum condemnavit, & condemnat ut vehatur plaustro a carcere urbis Issorensis usque ad magnum forum & locum publicum eiusdem urbis: ubi ponetur ac erigetur trabs lignea ad quam ipse attolletur, & circa illam fiet magnus ignis in quo ardebit & vretur totus vivus: & ipsius libri cum quibus inventus fuit, in sua praesentia proijcietur in eundem ignem, & in eo ardebunt & comburentur. Declaravit item ac declarat praedicta Curia, omnia & singula bona dicti captivi confiscata esse Regi. Praeterea decernit, ut certi quidam rei facti per dictum processum (quorum nomina ponentur in armamentarium causarum eiusdem [?] [?]ufdé Curiæ: & dabitur per excerpta & extracta registrorum eius) capiatur corpore ubicunq; inuenirí poterunt in hoc Regno, etiã in loco sacro (saluo quòd diintegrabunt, si fieri debeat) & ducentur captiui ad carcerem Monrrati, ut ibi stent iuri, audiantúrque & interrogentur per dictum Bailliuum ut suum locumtenentè super casibus quibus onerati erűt per dictum processum, rovt ratio postulat. Sed quia dicta Curia debitè fuit informata quòd de die in diem ista maledicta & damnata secta Lutherana & alię similes hæreses iam magnopere pullulant in Aruernia, & maximè in urbe Issorensi, & pluribus alijs locis & vrbibus, ac præfectura Monferrati, occultè & latenter cum magno dolore bonorum hominũ habitantiũ in illa regione, ut obuietur ne dicta ecta pestifera, gladius infectionis & contagionis, crescat & augmentetur mais, & ne boni catholici fideles sint aut esse possint infecti & corrupti per publicas aut secretas suasiones infelicium hæreticorum: sed possint viuere in pace & tranquillitate, in vera unitate fidei catholicæ ecclesiæ Universalis: ordinauit & ordinat arestum publicandũ & proclamandũ tam in urbe Issorensi quàm n alijs urbibus principalibus dictæ regionis Aruerniæ, in quibus est sedes Reia mediatè vel immediatè ad dictam Curiam appellans, ad sonum tubæ & roclamatione publicam per omnes plateas: quo aresto dicta curia prohibuit & rohibet expressè & sub pœna ignis, omnibus habitantibus in regione, loqui, diere, tenere, aut proponere publicè aut occultè, directè aut indirectè aliquas doctrinas aut sermones blasphemos, seditiosos contra honorem Dei, gloriosissimæ virginis, suæ benedictæ matris, sanctorúmque ac sanctarum Paradisi, & contra nostram matrem ecclesiam & suam doctrinam: maximè contra sancta Sacramenta eius, & specialiter contra sanctum sacramentum altaris, & formam viuendi quæ semper fuit retenta & obseruata per veros fideles & catholicos Christianos. E contrario iniungit omnibus sub eadem pœna, loqui & viuere secundum doctrinam nostræ matris ecclesiæ, & secundum mandata Dei, & dictæ ecclesiæ catholicæ, non'dando aut facto aut verbo aliquam occasionẽ scandali aut infectionis veris fidelibus catholicis. Prohibet insuper retinere, legere, aut facere legere aliquos libros Gallicè aut Latinè, continentes doctrinas erroneas & hæreticas, impressos in Genevâ [?] aut alijs urbibus suspectis. Ac ne aliqui possint esse seducti, aut prætendere quòd per ignorantiam ipsi peccarint, ordinauit & ordinat dicta Curia, quòd articuli, propositiones, censuræ facultatis Theologiæ universitatis Parisiensis, approbati & confirmati per edictum Regis, lecti & publicatu in dicta curia: quæ quidem censuræ sunt contrariæ infelicibus pestiferisque propositionibus productis per Lutheranos & alios hæreticos eorum complices & adhærentes, publicabuntur per singulas dies Dominicas in suggesto omnium parochiarum, in dictâ regione Aruerniæ, tam in diœcesi Clarimontis quàm sancti Flori, à parocho aut vicario earum parochiarum: & exponentur populo in lingua vulgari, in modo ut quisque possit intelligere quod continetur in dictis articulis dictæ facultatis Theologiæ, sic authorisatis per Regem, sicut suprà dictum est. Et prohibet dicta Curia, sub pœnis quibus antè omnibus habitantibus in dicta regione, tâ summisse quàm altè loqui, sustinere, aut disputare sive publicè sive priuatim, contra ea quæ continentur in dictis articulis, & aliis rebus tam diu obseruatis, prædicatis ac publicatis in ecclesia catholica. Et iniungit dicta Curia aedituis aut luminarijs dictarum Parochiarum sub pœna decem pondo argenti, cum corporis punitione ad discretionem dictæ Curiæ, vt solicitent effectualiter, quatenus publicatio dictorum articulorum & propositionum dictæ facultatis fiat, exponatur, & declaretur in suggesto dictarum Parochiarum, singulis diebus Dominicis. Et similiter exhortatur dictos Parochos & Vicarios sic facere: & vbi essent contradicentes, negligentes, aut contemptores admonitionis dictæ Curiæ, iniungit eadem Curia dictis aedituis & singulis eorum, sub pœnis quibus supra, vt faciant informationem de his per proximum Iudicem Regium, & mitti informationes ad dictam Curiam, vt procedatur cótra delinquentes & culpabiles, prout oportebit. Admonet & exhortatur episcopü Clarimontus & sancti Flori, eorum Vicarios & Officiales, vt ea fieri curent per dictos Parochos aut Vicarios, & eos cogant ad id. Ordinat etiam & iniungit dicta Curia aedituis, & admonet dictos Episcopos, eorum Vicarios & Officiales, vt faciant scribi catalogum in vnaquaque Parochia omnium parochialium qui sunt in ætate ad recipiendum sanctum Sacramentum altaris de Paschæ, & notent eos qui non venerint dicto die: & dent eas notationes Parochis ac Vicarijs qui tenebuntur mittere registros suos ad Procuratorem Regis proximæ sedis regiæ: cui dicta Curia iniungit vt continuò se informet & faciat procedere contra notatos. Et hoc sub pœna suspensionis per annum reditnum[?] ac officiorum pro prima culpa: priuationis verò eorundem pro secunda. Et sub ijsdem pœnis iniungit Iudicibus regijs dictæ regionis, vt instrument[?] diligenter vniuersis negotijs postpositis, contra omnes qui sunt infecti à secta blasphema, hæretica, Lutherana, & perturbatiua tranquillitatis & quietis subiectorum Regis: & faciant ipsis suum processum vsque ad iudicium definitiuum, aut torturæ exclusiuè. Et hoc facto mittant dictos captiuos in custodiam dictæ Curiæ, & ipsorum processus, vt procedatur, sicut oportebit per rationem: & certificent deinceps singulis tribus mensibus dictæ Curiæ, quid fecerint in ea materia sub pœnis quibus supra: & insuper ne reputentur fautores aut receptores hæreticorum, perturbatores pacis publicæ, & pro talibus puniantur ea pœna qua æquum est. Iniunctum etiam erit præconio publico, & sonitu tubæ omnibus habitantibus & commorantibus in dicta regione, mittere ad actuarium proximi iudicis Regij, intra tres dies post publicationem huius ordinationis, omnes libros quos apud se habebunt, concernentes fidem & doctrinam catholicam, factos per hæreticos, & impressos Gencuæ, aut in aliquibus locis suspectis, sub pœna quòd reputabuntur hæretici, & punientur tali pœna qua a iustum est. Et sub iisdem poenis iniunctum omnibus iis qui scient aliquos habere et retinere dictos libros, et non apportasse ad dictum actuarium intra sex[?] dies post publicationem huius ordinationis, eos reuelare dicta propinquae sedi regiae, cuius officiariis dicta Curia iniunxit ut procedant contra delinquentes, culpabiles, et inobedientes prohibitionibus et iniunctionibus dictae Curiae, et ipsis faciant suum processum extraordinarie, usque ad iudium definitiuum exclusiue, ut dictum est. Atque hoc facto remittant captiuos ad custodiam dictae Curiae, cum dicto processu, sequendo edictum Regis.
units.tr: On the process brought before the Court by the Bailiff of Montferrand, or his deputy, against John Brugier, held prisoner in the palace jail, for the blasphemies and sacramentarian errors imputed to him, according to the submissions of the King's Attorney General. Having seen and considered all the evidence, the said Court condemns the prisoner, and does condemn him, for the making amends for his heretical blasphemies, scandalous sermons, and errors contrary to the holy Catholic faith and the doctrine of the Church, spoken, uttered and written by him against the honour of God, the holy Sacrament of the altar, our holy mother the Church and her constitutions, as is plainly declared in the process brought against him. He is to be carried on a cart from the prison of the town of Issoire to the great market and public place of the same town, where a wooden post shall be set up and erected to which he is to be raised; and around it a great fire shall be made, in which he shall be burned and roasted alive. The books with which he was found shall be thrown, in his presence, into the same fire, and shall be burned there. The Court likewise declares and has declared that all the goods of the said prisoner are confiscated to the King. Furthermore, it orders that certain persons named in the said process (whose names shall be placed in the records of the same Court, and given out by excerpts and extracts from its registers) be taken into custody wherever they can be found in this kingdom, even in a sacred place (save that the doors shall be broken open if necessary), and that the prisoners be led to the jail of Montferrand, there to stand trial, and to be heard and questioned by the said Bailiff, as his deputy, on the charges laid against them in the said process, as reason requires. But because the Court has been duly informed that this accursed and condemned Lutheran sect and other similar heresies are daily springing up greatly in Auvergne, and especially in the town of Issoire and several other places and towns, and in the district of Montferrand, secretly and covertly, to the great grief of the good people living in that region; and so that this pestilent sect, the sword of infection and contagion, may not grow and increase its evil, and that good Catholic faithful may not be, or be able to be, infected and corrupted by the public or private persuasions of unhappy heretics, but may live in peace and tranquillity in the true unity of the faith of the universal Catholic Church: the Court has ordered and does order that this decree be published and proclaimed, with the sound of a trumpet and public proclamation through all the squares, both in the town of Issoire and in the other principal towns of the said region of Auvergne in which the seat of the King's bailiffs or seneschals is located, whether they appeal immediately or mediately to the said Court. By this decree the Court forbids and expressly prohibits, under penalty of fire, all inhabitants of the region to speak, say, hold or put forward publicly or secretly, directly or indirectly, any blasphemous or seditious doctrines or sermons against the honour of God, of the most glorious Virgin, his blessed mother, and of the saints of Paradise, and against our mother the Church and her teaching; above all against her holy sacraments, and especially against the holy sacrament of the altar, and against the manner of living which has always been kept and observed by true faithful and Catholic Christians. On the contrary, it enjoins all, under the same penalty, to speak and live according to the teaching of our mother the Church, and according to the commandments of God and of the said Catholic Church, giving by deed or word no occasion of scandal or infection to the true Catholic faithful. It further forbids anyone to keep, read, or cause to be read any books in French or Latin containing erroneous and heretical doctrines, printed at Geneva or in other suspect towns. And lest any should be seduced, or pretend that they sinned through ignorance, the Court has ordered and does order that the articles, propositions and censures of the Faculty of Theology of the University of Paris, approved and confirmed by the King's edict, read and published in the said Court (which censures are contrary to the unhappy and pestilent propositions put forward by the Lutherans and other heretics, their accomplices and adherents), shall be published on every Lord's Day from the pulpit of every parish in the said region of Auvergne, both in the diocese of Clermont and in that of Saint-Flour, by the parish priest or vicar of those parishes; and they shall be set forth to the people in the vernacular, in such a way that each may understand what is contained in the said articles of the said Faculty of Theology, so authorised by the King, as stated above. And the Court forbids, under the penalties stated above, all inhabitants of the said region to speak, uphold or dispute, whether softly or loudly, publicly or privately, against those things which are contained in the said articles, and against other matters so long observed, preached and published in the Catholic Church. The Court also enjoins the churchwardens or lightkeepers of the said parishes, under penalty of ten pounds of silver, and with bodily punishment at the discretion of the Court, to take care effectively that the publication of the said articles and propositions of the said Faculty is made, set forth and declared from the pulpit of the said parishes every Lord's Day. Likewise it exhorts the said parish priests and vicars to do so; and where there are any who contradict, neglect or despise the admonition of the Court, the same Court orders the said churchwardens, each of them, under the penalties stated above, to make an inquiry into these matters through the nearest royal judge, and to send the findings to the said Court, so that proceedings may be taken against the offenders and the guilty, as shall be fitting. It admonishes and exhorts the bishops of Clermont and Saint-Flour, and their vicars and officials, to see that these things are done by the said parish priests or vicars, and to compel them to it. The Court also orders and enjoins the churchwardens, and admonishes the said bishops, their vicars and officials, to have a list written in each parish of all the parishioners who are of an age to receive the holy Sacrament of the altar at Easter, and to note those who do not come on that day; and they shall give these notes to the parish priests and vicars, who shall be bound to send their registers to the Procurator of the King of the nearest royal seat; to whom the Court enjoins that he continually inform himself and cause proceedings to be taken against those noted. This under penalty of suspension from their benefices and offices for a year for a first offence, and deprivation of the same for a second. And under the same penalties the Court enjoins the royal judges of the said region that they diligently, all other business set aside, proceed against all who are infected by the blasphemous, heretical, Lutheran sect, and who disturb the tranquillity and peace of the King's subjects; and that they bring their process against them to a definitive judgement, or to torture exclusively. And when this is done, they shall send the said prisoners into the custody of the said Court, with their processes, so that proceedings may be taken as reason requires; and they shall henceforth certify to the said Court every three months what they have done in this matter, under the penalties stated above. Furthermore, so that they are not regarded as favourers or receivers of heretics, disturbers of public peace, they shall be punished with such penalty as is fitting. It shall also be enjoined by public proclamation and the sound of a trumpet on all inhabitants and sojourners in the said region that, within three days after the publication of this decree, they send to the clerk of the nearest royal judge all the books they have that concern the Catholic faith and doctrine, made by heretics and printed at Geneva or in any suspect places, under penalty that they shall be regarded as heretics and punished with such penalty as is just. And under the same penalties it is enjoined on all who know that any persons have and keep the said books, and have not brought them to the said clerk within six days after the publication of this decree, that they shall reveal them to the said nearest royal seat, whose officers the Court has charged to proceed against the offenders, the guilty and those disobedient to the prohibitions and injunctions of the said Court, and to bring their process against them in an extraordinary manner, up to a definitive judgement exclusively, as has been said. And when this is done, they shall send the prisoners back into the custody of the said Court, with the said process, following the King's edict.

units.la: Iniunxit quoque dicta Curia omnibus habitantibus et commorantibus in diis regionibus, qui sciunt aut cognoscunt, aut qui sciuerit aut cognouerunt alios infectos a dicta secta, ut significent magistratui, ac magis proximo iudici regio, ut is inquirat, et procedat contra culpabiles, ut supra. Insuper iniunxit Substitutis Procuratoris generalis in sedibus Regis, resortientibus immediate in dictam curiam, ut obtineant literas monitorias in forma malefactorum, et iubeant diuulgari singulis diebus Dominicis in suggesto ecclesiarum parochialium, quibus admonebuntur omnes qui sciunt aut cognouerunt aliquos infectos hac pestifera doctrina, ut veniat ad reuelationem versus Parochum aut eius vicarium, in praesentia aedituorum, aut vnius eorum: quae reuelatio scribetur et signabitur a dicto Parocho aut Vicario, et dictis aedituis ut vno eorum, cui dicta Curia iniunxit sub poenis quibus supra, ferre aut iubeE perferri continuo ad officiarios proximae sedis Regiae, resortientis in dictam curiam sine medio, cui dicta curia iniunxit examinare per inquisitionem testes qui venerint ad reuelationem, et procedere, ut supra, contra eos quos inuenerint delinquentes et culpabiles sub poenis supradictis: omnibus aliis negociis postpositis. Atque ut mandetur istud praesens arestum executioni secundum formam suam et tenorem, contra dictum incarceratum, dicta curia eum remisit et remittit in statu quo est apud Bailliuum aut suum Locumtenentem. Factum in Parlamento tertio die Martij Anni M.D.XLVII. et subtus signatum, Malon.
units.tr: The Court also ordered all inhabitants and residents of those regions who know, or who have known or shall know, of others infected with this sect, to report them to the magistrate, or to the nearest royal judge, so that he may inquire into and proceed against the guilty, as above. Furthermore, the Court ordered the substitutes of the Procurator General in the royal seats, who answer directly to this Court, to obtain monitory letters in the form used for malefactors, and to have them read out every Sunday from the pulpit of the parish churches. By these letters all who know or have known of anyone infected with this pestilent doctrine are admonished to come forward and make a disclosure to the parish priest or his vicar, in the presence of the churchwardens or one of them. The disclosure is to be written down and signed by that priest or vicar and by the churchwardens (or one of them), under the penalties stated above, and is to be sent at once to the officials of the nearest royal seat, which answers directly to this Court. The Court has ordered these officials to examine by inquiry the witnesses who come forward with information, and to proceed as above against any they find guilty and culpable under the penalties mentioned, all other business being set aside. And so that this present decree may be carried out in accordance with its form and tenor, the Court has sent back the prisoner, in his present condition, to the bailiff or his deputy, against whom it has acted. Given in Parlement on the third day of March, in the year 1547, and signed below, Malon.

units.la: Haec pronuntiauit Curia Parisiensis Liseto Aruerno praeside digna locuta.
units.tr: The Parisian Court pronounced these things, Liset the Auvergnat presiding, and spoke worthily.

units.la: Brugerius itaque remissus fuit ad priorem iudicem, ut in urbe Issorensi executioni mandaretur arestum Senatus quod modo recitauimus. Orrius autem inquisitor, professus iampridem veritatis hostis, ibi tum erat, quem non puduit in differto foro eius urbis, quiritari ac vociferari ut sibi quisque caueret, seque muniret aduersus Lutheranorum, ut vocabat, fallacias. Nam ipsa, inquit, quicquid affirmant illi, verum est, sed quod idem negant, salsissimum. Consentiunt quidem nobiscum in eo quod credimus Deum esse omnipotentem, et veracem. ac Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum esse Saluatorem mundi: sacra Scripturam per Spiritum sanctum reuelatam esse: praeterea in omnibus quae nostrum Credo continet, id est in fidei nostrae articulis, a nobis non discrepat. Sed hic, aiebat ille, latet venenum, in negatiua scilicet ipsorum oratione. nam quum negant Deum esse in sacro crustulo: Purgatorium & indulgentias sancti patris nostri Papae pro nihilo habent: adorationem atque inuocationem Sanctorum detestantur, aliaque traditiones & constitutiones decretales per matrem nostram sanctam ecclesiam factas ac confirmatas, reijciunt. in his, inquit, falluntur, atque hi praecipui ipsorum sunt erro res. quocirca monitos velim ut ne vos illi decipiant praecauere possitis. Sic autem pseudoprophbeta ille Orrius populum Issorensem[?] est adhortatus: quemadmodum & in aliis locis, per quae vagabatur, facere consueverat. Postquam decretum illud aduersus Brugerium pronunciatum fuisset in auditorio Isiorensi per suppraefectum Monferrati, qui sibi habebat comites, aduocatum, procuratorem & alios administros regios eiusdem praefecturae: ne suo etiam officio deesset organum illud Sathanae Orrius, omnia expertus est, ut hunc a vera confessione abduceret, inculcans praecipue articulum sacramenti altaris. Quod aut assidue instaret ut ei persuaderet, panis ac vini substantiam tenues evanescere in auras, cuius in locum succederet substantia corporis & sanguinis Christi, eadem longitudinis & latitudinis quantitate, qua in cruce pependit. Brugerius ei ad id respondit, Si nudis & detractis a substantia qualitatibus nutriri corpora nostra possent, captiosa profecto oratione tuae esset probabilitas: sed cum id fieri non possit, quaenam dabitur inter signum & rem signatam conuenientia? quae quidem in sacramentis omnino desideratur, nisi velimus fingere nescio quod phantasma aut idolum, a quo ut hemeter[?] meus abhorret animus. Excepit Orrius, Si negas corpus Domini nostri esse in sacro crustulo, postea quam sacrificus sacramentalia verba pronuntiauit: aio mehercule te potentiam Dei negare, qui quod vult, efficere potest. Non nego, inquit ille, Dei potentiam. neque enim ita disputamus, possit-ne Deus id efficere necne, sed quid ille in sancta Coena fecerit, atque a nobis fieri velit. Orrius autem huic fine disputationi imponere cupis: Hem, inquit, quin ita Parisius cum esses Praesidi loquebaris? nec sane, inquit Bruger. sec[?] Praesidi sum locut. Tum magister noster Orrius capite inter utrumque humerum (qui eius erat gestus) contracto, hominem dimisit: ac quibusdam sibi familiaribus (qui huius rei locuples dederunt testimonium) magnam misero homini iniuriam fieri, seque ob id non mediocriter dolere aicbat, quia ipsius de sacramento opinio sibi non omnino mala videretur.
units.tr: Brugier was therefore sent back to the former judge, so that the decree of the Senate that we have just recited might be carried out in the town of Issore. Meanwhile the inquisitor Orrius, who had long since declared himself an enemy of the truth, was there. He was not ashamed to rant and shout in the crowded marketplace of that town, warning everyone to beware and to guard themselves against the deceits of the Lutherans, as he called them. "Whatever they affirm," he said, "is true; but whatever they deny is most false. They agree with us that God is almighty and truthful, that our Lord Jesus Christ is the Saviour of the world, that Holy Scripture was revealed by the Holy Spirit, and in general they do not differ from us in anything that our Creed contains, that is, in the articles of our faith. But here, he said, lies the poison, namely in their negative assertions. For when they deny that God is in the sacred wafer, and when they hold the Purgatory and the indulgences of our holy father the Pope as nothing, and detest the adoration and invocation of the saints, and reject the other traditions and decretal constitutions made and confirmed by our mother, the holy Church, in these matters, he said, they are mistaken, and these are their chief errors. Therefore I would have you warned, so that you may be able to guard against their deceits." In this way that false prophet Orrius exhorted the people of Issore, as he had been accustomed to do in the other places through which he wandered. After the decree against Brugier had been announced in the hall of the court at Issore by the sub-prefect of Monferrato, who had with him the advocate, the procurator and the other royal officers of that prefecture, Orrius, lest he fail in his duty, that instrument of Satan tried every means to draw him away from true confession, pressing especially the article of the sacrament of the altar. He kept insisting that he should be persuaded that the substance of bread and wine melts away into thin air, and that in its place succeeds the substance of the body and blood of Christ, of the same length and breadth as it hung on the cross. Brugier answered him: "If our bodies could be nourished by stripped qualities apart from substance, your argument would certainly have some plausibility. But since that cannot happen, what correspondence will there be between the sign and the thing signified? Such correspondence is entirely lacking in the sacraments, unless we wish to invent I know not what phantom or idol, from which my soul shrinks." Orrius replied: "If you deny that the body of our Lord is in the sacred wafer after the priest has pronounced the sacramental words, I say, by heaven, that you deny the power of God, who can do whatever he wills." "I do not deny God's power," he replied. "For we are not disputing whether God can bring this about or not, but what he did in the holy Supper and what he wishes us to do." Orrius, wishing to bring this disputation to an end, said: "Come now, did you not speak like that in Paris when you were before the President?" "Indeed not," said Brugier, "I spoke to the President in a different manner." Then our master Orrius, with his head drawn down between his shoulders (which was his habit), dismissed the man. He said to some of his intimates (who gave testimony of this matter) that a great wrong was being done to the wretched man, and that he grieved not a little for this reason, since his opinion about the sacrament did not seem to him altogether bad.

units.la: Hic quidam familiarium, Ecquid igitur, Orri, subscripsisti sententiæ aduersus ipsum perlatæ, & consensisti, qui debueras hæc declarasse Senatui, nec eius perpeti executionem? Quid facerem? inquit Orrius, nõ possim vllum remedium afferre: dabo quidem operam, quoad potero, ut sententiæ rigor mitigetur, ne ignem sentiat. Attamen ne id etiam impetrare potuit ab Officiarijs regiis, qui negabant se quicquâ praeter summæ Curiæ sententiam facturos, ne forte postea iure reprehederentur. Ad hæc venerunt in custodiæ auditorium sacrifici, exhortadi Brugerium atque in suam opinionem pertrahendi gratia. attulerant enim secum longam crucem, cui quoddam simulachrum affixum erat, quam crucem reuerendi Patres populo videndam exhibent magno illo die Veneris, quem vocant, ut tota spectatorum multitudo acclamet Misericordiam: hanc, inquam, isti, Brugerio ob oculos ponentes: Tu, inquiunt, qui Iesu Christi nomen adeo prædicas, atque in eo solo fiduciam tuam locatam profiteris: nunc id reipsa ut ostendas necesse est: Nonne igitur prostratus hanc veram ac dignam crucem adorare vis, in qua ille communi nostrûm nomine pependit? Brugerius eos obliquè intuitus, & moto nonnihil capite excepit his verbis: O miseri mortales, haudquaquam adoro opera manuum hominis: verum Deum ac Patrem adoro in spiritu & veritate. Vrgebant etiam aduersarij ut Mariam Virginem inuocaret: in quibus erat quidam satelles, dicens ipsum, Virginem quæ aduocata esset miseris peccatoribus, habere despicatui, atque in nullo honore. Obsecro, inquit ille, ut me sinatis, dum parumper antequam moriar cogitationes meas ad Deum erigam: contentus sum vnico aduocato qui à Deo pro peccatoribus constitutus est. in quo Virgine minimè dedecoro, quod fieret, si tâ scelerato sacrilegio consentire, quod à me committi vultis priuando charû ipsius filiû officio aduocati, atq; ad eam tanquâ rem furtiuam deferendo. quod ipsa ne desiderat quidem. Quòd si vos mihi cõceditis ut ad populum dicâ, quæ in sacris literis didici, tum facilè intelligetis quantæ sit apud me sancta virgo existimationis. Sed nequaquam licuit per administros regios, qui instabat, vt in manus sumeret exiguam quandam crucē: inclamauit ille vero, Non hæc mihi lignea crux fereda est, sed lōge aliam & graviorē mox in toto corpore, Dei fultu ope sustinebo. Quoda itaq; die sabbathi frequenti tum in ea vrbe mercatu, ductus fuit ad locū supplicij, vbi patibulū extructū erat, è quo ferrea desuper catena, qua pēsilis tenere tur, per duarum trochlearum orbiculos traiecta dependebat: duoque sub patibulo non ita alti stabant stipites, supra quos asser arctus clauis assixus erat, circucirca fasces cū stramine positi, quibus exuredus erat Brugerius: qui quidē hoc tristi apparatu adeò nō perculsus fuit, vt ipse animum addiderit carnifici, qui cecidit dū ipsum iā catenæ alligandū, in asserē locaret. Brugerius autē porrecta ei manu, Bono animo sis, inquit ō magister Pochete, læsissime te quicquam? Deinde media sui corporis parte catena ligatus, manibus & pedibus vinctis, oculos in cælum sustulit, dicens: Supplico tibi Pater cælestis per Filium tuum, vt me virtute spiritus tui sustentes atq; cōfirmes, quo sic opus quod in me cœpisti, perficiatur ad gloriam tuam & vtilitatem Ecclesiæ. Postquam precatus esset pro inimicis suis, animámque suam Deo commendasset, sponte se ad ignē quē à tergo habebat, vertit. carnifex vero asserē depulit, quo fiebat vt pēdulus in aere & media flamma vstularetur homo, nec se moues, nec vociferas quicquam, donec demisso capite placidè expirauit. Tum in populo spectata hac constantia, & virtute admirabili, ingētes & varij clamores editi sunt: alij miraculū diuinū esse dicebāt, alij gratias Deo agebāt, quòd sua ætate martyrē extremo supplicio affici vidisset. Hoc tumultu populari exorto, administri regij & Orrius ipse metu perterriti, nō secꝰ acsi iā certa mors impederet, fuga sibi quiq; cōsulere quàm ad hospitia reuertisati esse iudicarunt: rectāq; Moferratū cōtederunt, quod oppidū ab Ifforensi sex milliaribus distat. Carnifex cū vidisset cæteros aufugisse, homine semiustū reliquit. Parochꝰ aut Ifforesis, qui adfuerat Brugerio ad supplicium cuti, quanuis insignis haberetur hypocrita, rogatus tamē à quodā, quid de eo sentiret: palā multisq; audictibus dixit: faxit Dominus vt in fide Brugerij moriar.
units.tr: One of his intimates then said: "Why, Orrius, did you subscribe to the sentence brought against him and consent to it, when you ought to have declared these things to the Senate and not allowed its execution?" "What could I do?" said Orrius. "I cannot offer any remedy. I will indeed take pains, as far as I can, that the rigour of the sentence be softened, so that he may not feel the fire." Yet he could not even obtain this from the royal officials, who said they would do nothing beyond the sentence of the supreme Court, lest they should later be rightly blamed. Thereafter the priests came into the prison hall to exhort Brugier and to draw him over to their opinion. For they had brought with them a long cross, on which a certain image was fixed, which the reverend Fathers display to the people to be seen on that great day which they call Good Friday, so that the whole crowd of spectators may cry out for mercy. Setting this cross before Brugier's eyes, they said: "You, who preach the name of Jesus Christ so much and profess that your trust is placed in him alone, must now show it in deed. Will you not therefore fall prostrate and adore this true and worthy cross, on which he hung for the common salvation of us all?" Brugier looked at them sideways, and, moving his head a little, answered in these words: "O wretched mortals, I by no means adore the works of men's hands; rather I adore God the Father in spirit and in truth." The adversaries also urged him to invoke the Virgin Mary. Among them was a certain attendant who said that the Virgin, who is the advocate of wretched sinners, was held in contempt by him and in no honour. "I beg you," said Brugier, "to let me, for a little while before I die, raise my thoughts to God. I am content with the one advocate whom God has appointed for sinners. I do the Virgin no discourtesy in this, for it would be a discourtesy to consent to so wicked a sacrilege, which you wish me to commit, by depriving her beloved Son of his office as advocate and transferring it to her as though it were stolen property, which she herself does not even desire. But if you grant me leave to speak to the people of what I have learned in the sacred letters, then you will readily understand how much I esteem the holy Virgin." But by no means was it permitted by the royal officials, who pressed him to take into his hands a small wooden cross. He cried out: "This wooden cross is not a foul thing to me, but another and much heavier one I shall soon bear in my whole body, with God's help and support." Then on a certain Saturday, when the market in that town was crowded, he was led to the place of execution, where a gallows had been erected, from which hung an iron chain, which held a pulley-block passed through two small wheels; and beneath the gallows stood two not very tall posts, above which a narrow beam was fixed with nails, and all around were faggots laid with straw, with which Brugier was to be burned. He was indeed so little dismayed by this sad preparation that he himself encouraged the executioner, who was just then falling as he tried to place him on the beam to be chained. Brugier, stretching out his hand to him, said: "Be of good courage, master Pochet; have you been hurt at all?" Then, bound by the chain around the middle of his body, with his hands and feet tied, he lifted his eyes to heaven and said: "I beseech you, heavenly Father, through your Son, that you would sustain and strengthen me by the power of your Spirit, so that the work which you have begun in me may be brought to completion, to your glory and the profit of the Church." After he had prayed for his enemies and commended his soul to God, he turned himself willingly towards the fire that was behind his back. The executioner pushed away the beam, so that the man hung swinging in the air and was scorched in the midst of the flames; he neither moved nor cried out at all, until, with his head bowed, he calmly breathed his last. Then, as this constancy and admirable courage were seen by the people, great and varied shouts arose: some said it was a divine miracle, others gave thanks to God that in their own age they had seen a martyr put to the extreme punishment. When this popular tumult broke out, the royal officials and Orrius himself, terrified with fear, as if certain death were threatening, judged that each should look to his own safety by flight rather than return to their lodgings; and they fled straight to Monferrato, which town is six miles from Issore. When the executioner saw that the others had fled, he left the man half-burned. The parish priest of Issore, who had been present with Brugier at his punishment, though he was thought a notable hypocrite, nevertheless, when someone asked him what he thought of him, said openly and in the hearing of many: "May the Lord grant that I die in the faith of Brugier."

units.la: FLORENTIVS VENOTVS.
units.tr: FLORENTIUS VENOTUS.

units.la: Constantia[?] Florentij Venoti, patria Curgiuotensis prope Sedanam in Bria, perdigna est, quae memoriae sempiternae commendetur. Ea enim in Christo profitendo & cofitendo ita insignis fuit ut iniuri[?]issimis atq; infestissimis veritati hominibus, summa admiratione attulerit[?]. Nullum est tormenti genus, quod ipse non fuerit ppessus, spatio quatuor annorum & novē dierū, quib9 Lutetiæ in carcere habitus est. Inter utē[?] cætera carceris tormēta, hoc vnum passus est singulare, inclusus quodā in loco, vbi circiter septē hebdomadas ita collocatus fuit, ut nec agere, nec stare potuerit. Huiusmodi tormenti, magistri tortores appellant Caligam aut ocream ad nectar Hippocratis, eo quod figura est infima in parte acutiore, supra vero latiore atq; ampliore, instar eius instrumenti, quo pharmacopolæ vinum aromatite conficiunt. Itaq; ijdē artifices retulerunt, nullum reum & criminosum hominem fuisse, qui id tormentū vltrà quindeci dies perferre potuerit, quin aut de vita periclitatus fuerit, aut insania correpto ac mente alienato. Porrò cōsilium inimicorū erat, in primisq; Petri Liseti, tū praesidis, qui summā ei9 viri cōstātia iniquissimo animo ferebat, ut eū in maximis acerbissimisq; laguoribus atq; dolorib9 diutissimè teneret, vt hoc modo ei9 animū infringeret aut cū intra carceris parietes vita priuaret, ne suauissim9 odor mortis eius publicè suscepta, fructusq; ad aliorū ædificationē perueninirèt. Sed is singulari Dei virtute munitus ac septus omnibus eorum consiliis ac conatibus costantissimè semper restitit, ita vt cū aliquando esset in ipsa curia, & ea camera, quae Ardesab illis est costituta & appellata, verba sua ad Liseti atq; ad alios quosdā dirigēs, dixerit, eos quidē id agere, vt diuturnis tormētis atq; cruciatibus virtute spiritus in eo debilitet, aut mori ipsum cogant in carcere: sed opera perdere. Nā se eā à Deo gratiā sperare, vt vsq; ad finē perseueret, eiusq; sanctissimū nomen in sua morte, omni laude & gloria celebret. Non multo post optimis eius optatis Deus p sua benignitate respondit, tepusq; ad eam cōfessionē, quam optabat, paccōmodatū ei dedit, vt homines huius mundi omniū maximè gloriosi, intelligeret, eam vi esse veritatis, cui cedat opor-tet omnia hominū cōsilia, quorū quidē magnitudine p infirma atq; stulta huius mundi Deus euertit. Quodam igitur die, quo pompa solemnis à Rege indicta fuit, aliquanto post eius in vrbem Parisiensem introitum, Florentius Vinotus, cum alijs quibusdam captiuus propter vcrbum Dei,cum more ipsorum,de gradu illo sacerdotali motus, & capitis damnatus fuisset,productus est,ut victima Deo offerretur. Atque ut cum maiore dedecore aut timore afficerent,spectatorem caeterorum, qui eo die martyrio diversis in locis urbis erant defuncturi, constituerunt. Florentius autem quum lingua praecisa loqui non posset,signis tamen,& oculis in caelum erectis, aliisque omnibus quibus poterat rationibus,caeterorum animos excitabat.ipse etiam cum in illis admirabilem Dei gratiam videret, magnopere confirmabatur. Is tandem postremus supplicio affectus est,cum maximis corporis laboribus ac doloribus afflictus & confectus esset, vivusque in platea Malberti fuit vstulatus tertia post meridiem hora,nono die Julij,anno M.D.XLIX.
units.tr: The constancy of Florentius Venotus, a native of Curgiuot near Sedan in Brie, is well worth being commended to everlasting memory. In confessing and professing Christ he was so remarkable that he drew great admiration even from the most unjust and hostile enemies of the truth. There was no kind of torment he did not suffer during the four years and nine days he was held in prison at Paris. Among the other torments of the prison, he endured one singular kind: he was shut up in a place where for about seven weeks he was so confined that he could neither walk nor stand. The torturers call this instrument the boot, or the "sleeve of Hippocrates," because it is narrow at the bottom and wider and fuller at the top, like the strainer apothecaries use to make spiced wine. These same craftsmen reported that no criminal or prisoner had ever been able to endure this torment for more than fifteen days without either endangering his life or being driven out of his mind. The purpose of his enemies, especially of Pierre Lizet, then president, who took it very badly that a man of such constancy should hold out, was to keep him for a very long time in the greatest and most bitter sickness and pain, so as to break his spirit this way, or else to end his life within the prison walls, so that the sweet savour of his death would not be made public and its fruit would not reach the building up of others. But he, protected and surrounded by the singular power of God, stood firm against all their plans and attempts. Once, when he was in the court itself, in that chamber which they call and have designated the "Ardesa," he directed his words to Lizet and some others, saying that they were trying to weaken him in his spirit by long torments and sufferings, or to force him to die in prison, but that they were wasting their effort. For he hoped to receive from God the grace to persevere to the end and to celebrate his most holy name in his death with all praise and glory. Not long after, God in his goodness answered his best wishes and gave him a time suited to the confession he desired, so that the men of this world, the most glorious of all, might understand that it is the power of the truth to which all human counsels must yield, since God overturns by the weak and foolish things of this world the greatness of those counsels. So, on a certain day when a solemn procession had been proclaimed by the King, some time after his entry into the city of Paris, Florentius Venotus, together with some others held captive for the Word of God, was brought out, after their manner, having been moved from that priestly rank and condemned to death, that he might be offered to God as a victim. And in order to inflict greater shame and fear, they set the others, who were to die that day in various places of the city, to watch him. Florentius, though his tongue had been cut out and he could not speak, nevertheless by signs, with his eyes raised to heaven, and by every other means he could, stirred up the spirits of the others; and when he himself saw the wonderful grace of God in them, he was greatly strengthened. At last he was put to death as the last of them, worn out and broken by the greatest bodily labours and pains, and he was burned alive in the Place Maubert at three o'clock in the afternoon on the ninth day of July, in the year 1549.

units.la: LEONARDUS GALIMARD.
units.tr: LEONARD GALIMARD.

units.la: LEONARDUS Galimardus, Vendomij natus, comprehensus est Cherij, prope Blaiam, circiter xv. diem Maij, anno M.D. XLIX. Inde Lutetiam deductus, & in carcerem coniectus fuit. Edita deinde fidei confessione, in qua puram Evangelij doctrinam integre ac fideliter defendit, ab ea curia est condemnatus, ut vsitato supplicio assici ceretur vivusque cremaretur, quam quidem poenam summa virtute constantiaque sustinuit, eodem die, quo Florentius Venotus, cuius supra mentio facta est, anno M.D.XLIX.
units.tr: Leonard Galimard, born at Vendôme, was arrested at Chéry near Blois about the fifteenth day of May in the year 1549. He was then taken to Paris and thrown into prison. Afterwards, having published a confession of faith in which he fully and faithfully defended the pure doctrine of the Gospel, he was condemned by that court to be put to the usual punishment, namely, to be burned alive. He endured this penalty with the greatest courage and constancy on the same day on which Florentius Venotus, mentioned above, died, in the year 1549.

units.la: ANNA AUDEBERTE.
units.tr: ANNA AUDEBERTE.

units.la: EODEM anno Anna Audeberta, Aureliae nata, & Petri Gencfti pharmacopolae vidua, in ipso itinere cum Geneuam se ad ecclesiam Dei conferret, in oppidulo Castro-renardo nominato, capta est una cum Stephano Peloquino, teste Iesu Christi fidelissimo: cuius mentio hoc in libro postea fiet. Cum his autem alij quidem comprehensi fuerunt, qui metu hominum doctrinam Evangelij confiteri non sunt ausi. E Castro-renardo Lutetiam abducta fuit: ibique a suprema curia damnata, ut in civitate sua Aureliae viva igni cremaretur. Quam in urbem cum venisset die Sabbathi, xxviii, Septembris, pridie eius diei qui sacer Michaeli colitur, non multo post hora secunda pomeridiana supplicio affecta est. Cum e carcere egrediens, ad locum supplicij, Martyroium appellatum, duceretur, funéque, vt fieri solet huiusmodi hominibus vinciretur, quadam cum gratulatione & lætitia ita loquuta dicitur, Quàm pulchra hæc zona, quam sponsus meus mihi dat: dies erat Sabbathi quum primis meis nuptiis desponsata fui, secundis vero his nuptiis meis, eodem Sabbathi die, Iesu Christo sponso meo nubam. Cùm autem adductum vidisset plaustrum, quo deportanda erat & quo lutum exportari solet, animo læto, hilarique vultu ita ait, Est né istud quo mihi est conscendendum? atque hæc dicens, illud alacriter conscendit: eximiámque constantiam ac virtutem fœmina & vidua vsque in finem ita retinuit, vt Aurelianensis populus qui eam videret, summa admiratione afficeretur: fideles vero Deúmque metuentes confirmaretur eius morte, qua præclarè est defuncta codé anno M.D.XLIX.
units.tr: In the same year, Anne Audeberte, born at Orléans and widow of Pierre Genest, an apothecary, was seized in the little town called Châtillon-Renard, along with Étienne Peloquin, a most faithful witness of Jesus Christ, while on her journey to join the Church of God at Geneva. Of him there will be mention later in this book. Others were arrested with them, who out of fear of men did not dare to confess the doctrine of the Gospel. From Châtillon-Renard she was taken to Paris, and there she was condemned by the supreme court to be burned alive in her own city of Orléans. When she arrived in that city on Saturday, the twenty-eighth of September, the day before the feast of Saint Michael, she was put to death not long after two o'clock in the afternoon. As she was led from the prison to the place of execution, called the Martroi, and was bound with the rope with which such people are customarily tied, she is said to have spoken with a kind of joy and gladness: "How beautiful is this girdle which my bridegroom gives me! It was on a Saturday that I was betrothed at my first marriage, and at this second marriage of mine, on the same Saturday, I shall be wed to Jesus Christ, my bridegroom." When she saw the cart brought in, in which she was to be carried and in which mud is usually carried away, she said with a cheerful heart and a happy face, "Is this the thing I have to climb into?" And saying this, she climbed in eagerly. This woman, a widow, kept her outstanding constancy and courage to the end, so that the people of Orléans who saw her were filled with great admiration, and the faithful and God-fearing were strengthened by her death, by which she died nobly in the same year, 1549.

units.la: SARTOR VESTIARIVS.
units.tr: THE TAILOR.

units.la: Huic coram Henrico rege Galliæ de religionis Christianæ capitibus disserere, & regi at- que aulicis [?] Gallis veritatis præco esse contigit.
units.tr: It fell to him to discourse before King Henry of France on the heads of the Christian religion, and to be a herald of the truth to the king and the courtiers of France.

units.la: Paulò pòst triumphalem Henrici Galliarum regis in vrbem Parisiensem ingressum, vt diximus quum de Florentio ageremus, in eorum numero qui iamdudum carcere inclusi adseruabantur, erat quidam Sartor vestiarius: cuius conditio quanuis hominibus obscura propter inopiam fuerit, adeò vt nomen ipsius quasi silentio obliteratum fuerit, Deus tamen in id tempus huic adseruare voluit, vt Henrico regi serio cum suis satrapis triumphanti veritatem & iudicia sua (quod quidem vix vlli antea contigerat) coram intrepidè annunciaret. is quum in platea illa ampla quæ sancti Antonij dicitur, non procul à regia domo quæ à ludis equestribus nomen habet, paruas ædiculas inhabitaret, à Supprætoriano seu domo regiæ Suppræfecto captus est, quod opificiū exercet eo die qui in Papatu festus obseruatur. Priusquā duceretur in carcerem, Suppræfectus ex eo quæsiuit, quæ res eum ad opus faciendum impulisset, an non faret cum diem esse in quo laborare non liceret. Cui ille respondit, se vitæ suæ tuendæ causa laborare: neque alium diem se intelligere præter Dominicum, in quo arte operáque necessaria vti non posset. Tum Suppræfectus à Sartore multa alia quæsiuit, ad quæ ille ita respondit, vt in carcerem ab eo statim ductus fuerit. Suppræfectus deinde cùm in carcerem illum conicisset, ad regiam accessit: atque ut boni serui ministríque officio fungi videretur, quibusdam è primoribus aulæ significauit se quendam Lutheranum natum esse, quem quum die festo laborantem comprehendisset, atque ab eo multa quæsiuisset, se tulisse huiusmodi responsa, quibus nulla ab homine vllo peiora fieri possent. Id autem cum postea ad Regem delatum esset, postulantibus quibusdam proceribus ab eo est accersitus, ac coram adductus, vt illum loquentem audiret. Qui quidem nobilibus, aliisque administris è cubiculo remotis, paucisque primarijs viris relictis, hunc Sartorem interrogari voluit per Petrum Castellanum tum Matisconensem Episcopum, qui inter omnes aulicos ad eam disquisitionem atque interrogationem ingenio & doctrina maximè aptus esse videbatur. Sartor autem eò cum venisset, Regi honorem, quem principi suo debebat, habuit, gratias agens Deo pro summo honore ab eo sibi tributo, quòd coram tanto Principe ad testificandam fidem suam productus esset. Cùm verò Castellanus multa ex eo quæsiuisset de maximis ac grauissimis Christianæ religionis capitibus: ille sine vlla animi consternatione atque titubatione ita commodè aptèque respondit, vt pura, simplex, syncerâque doctrina postulare videbatur. etsi verò Castellanus ac cæteri aulæ proceres, vt eum terrerent, omnibus probris contumeliisque insectabantur: ille tamen à summa illa constantia & animi magnitudine nunquam deduci potuit, neque vllis propositis minis, terroribus periculisque impediri, quò minus pietatis doctrinam quam amplexus erat, liberè confiteretur. Quæ quidem res summam admirationem iis qui aderant attulit, cùm viderent hominem inopem tanta libertate & constantia, ad ea quæ quærebantur coram Rege respondentem. Sed egregius Episcopus, aulicíque proceres, cùm vidissent obstupefactum Regem, vt omnem melioris cognitionis cogitationem discuterent, dixerunt eum hominem nihili, in opinione obfirmatum, ad iudicémque remittendum, vt pœna merita afficeretur. Ne itaque diutius Henrici aures detineret, mandatum est Suppræfecto, vt in causa illius informaretur: id quod ilico factum est. Paucis enim post diebus, vt viuus cremaretur, à Præfecto aulæ regiæ damnatus est. Nullum antea coram Rege audiuimus prodisse, qui Christum eiúsque Euangelium ita confessus fuerit, vt hic Sartor eo in conuentu auliaulicorum ac procerum respondit. Ac ne aliqua de tam excellenti hominis constantia existimatio in animo Regis remaneret, plerique ex illa Cardinalium & Episcoporum caterua improba aiebant, huiusmodi homines Lutheranos nil nisi fumos ore euomere, qui propius igni admoti statim euanescunt. Itaque Rex spectator supplicij crudelissimi (quod postea de Sartore sumptum est ante vastam D. Virginis aedem) esse voluit, ut videret num hic confessionem illam doctrinae, atque adeo illam animi constantiam ad extremum vitae spiritum retineret. Ita vero auxit Dominus & robur ac vires huic suo Martyri, ut in media flamma immotus conspiceretur. quo quidem spectaculo Rex vehementius quam ante obstupefactus dicitur.
units.tr: Shortly after King Henry of France's triumphal entry into the city of Paris, as we said when dealing with Florentius, there was among those who had long been kept shut up in prison a certain clothes-tailor. His condition was obscure to men because of his poverty, so that his name was, as it were, buried in silence; yet God wished to preserve him until that time, so that he might boldly declare the truth and his judgments to Henry the king, triumphing with his nobles (a thing that had scarcely happened to anyone before). He lived in small cottages in that wide square called Saint Antoine's, not far from the royal house that takes its name from the equestrian games. He was seized by the Subpraetorian, that is, the sub-prefect of the royal house, because he was working at his trade on the day that is observed as a holy day under the Papacy. Before he was led to prison, the sub-prefect asked him what had moved him to work, and whether he did not know that there was a day on which labour was not allowed. He replied that he worked to sustain his life, and that he knew no day other than the Lord's Day on which he could not use his necessary skill and labour. Then the sub-prefect asked him many other things, to which he answered in such a way that he was at once led off by him to prison. The sub-prefect then, having thrown him into prison, went to the palace, and as if to seem to fulfil the office of a good servant and minister, he told some of the chief men of the court that he had seized a certain Lutheran who was working on a feast day, and that when he had asked him many things, he had heard such answers as no man could make worse. When this was afterwards reported to the king, at the urging of some nobles he sent for the tailor and had him brought before him, so that he might hear him speak. The nobles and other attendants were removed from the chamber, and only a few leading men were left. He wished this tailor to be questioned through Peter Castellan, then bishop of Mâcon, who seemed, among all the courtiers, the most fitted by wit and learning for that inquiry and examination. When the tailor came there, he showed the king the respect he owed his prince, giving thanks to God for the great honour given him, that he had been brought before so great a prince to bear witness to his faith. When Castellan had asked him many things about the greatest and most weighty heads of the Christian religion, he answered without any agitation or hesitation, so fittingly and aptly that he seemed to set forth a pure, simple and sincere doctrine. Although Castellan and the other nobles of the court, to frighten him, assailed him with every kind of abuse and insult, he could never be drawn from that great constancy and greatness of spirit, nor was he hindered by any threats, terrors or dangers from freely confessing the doctrine of piety that he had embraced. This brought great admiration to those present, who saw a poor man answering the questions put to him before the king with such freedom and constancy. But the excellent bishop and the courtiers, seeing the king astonished, in order to dispel any thought of better judgment, said that the man was a nobody, hardened in his opinion, and should be sent back for judgment, so that he might receive the punishment he deserved. So, lest he detain the king's ears any longer, the sub-prefect was ordered to inquire into his case, and this was done at once. For after a few days he was condemned by the prefect of the royal court to be burned alive. We have not heard that anyone before came forward before the king and confessed Christ and his Gospel as this tailor did in that assembly of courtiers and nobles. And lest any esteem for the constancy of so excellent a man remain in the king's mind, many of that wicked band of cardinals and bishops said that such Lutherans breathe out nothing but smoke from their mouths, which vanishes as soon as it is brought near the fire. Therefore the king wished to be a spectator of the most cruel execution (which was afterwards carried out on the tailor before the vast church of the Blessed Virgin), that he might see whether this man would keep that confession of doctrine, and that constancy of spirit, to the last breath of life. And the Lord so increased the strength and power of this his martyr that he was seen unmoved in the midst of the flames. At this spectacle the king is said to have been more violently astonished than before.

units.la: MARTYRES QVIDAM apud Hannonienses.
units.tr: Certain martyrs among the people of Hainault.

units.la: Nullum hodie angulum terrarum quantumuis remotissimarum Dominus suae bonitatis ac misericordiae testimonijs expertem reliquit, dum ubique gentium fideles ad causae suae defensionem producit testes, quibus & ignorantes erudiri, & qui cognitione caelesti donati sunt confirmari, denique omnis homo ἀναπολόγητος [?] atque inexcusabilis esse possit, quicunque veritati quoquo modo resistit. Anno M. D. XLIX.orta quaedam apud Hannonienses persecutione, inter alios capti atque in carcerem inclusi fuerunt quidam M. Nicolaus natione Gallus, ciusdemq; coniux Barbara: Augustinus Tonsor & Mariona eius uxor, nati in pago quodam non procul a Bergis Hannoniae. qui postquam Gencuae aliquandiu commorati essent, una se in Germaniam receperunt, illac in Angliam tendentes. Cumque in Hannoniam pervenissent, Augustinus rogauit Nicolaum, qui erat non indoctus, ut pusillum gregem urbis Bergensis invisere[?]t, quaeque spiritus Dei in se dona habebat, cum fratribus benevole communicaret. qui quidem tam aequae petitioni libens assensit, cum praesertim hac ratione regnum Filij Dei propagari non ignoraret.
