Divus Paulus, inquit, vii. cap. ad Rom. ostendit in veteri testamento nihil praeter iram ac minas fuisse: in novo vero gratiam et misericordiam nobis proponi et commendari, cum ita dicit, Ego miser homo, quis me liberabit de corpore mortis huius? gratia Dei per Iesum Christum. Paulus, inquam, eo in loco non loquitur de veteri et novo testamento: sed de pugna et certamine carnis atque spiritus, in quo homo versatur Spiritu Dei regeneratus, quod certamen carnis spiritui resistentis Apostolus in seipso ostendit. Praeterea in iis libris qui de Graeco in Latinum et Gallicum sermonem recte sunt conversi, non legitur, Gratia Dei, sed, Gratias ago Deo per Iesum Christum.
units.tr: We see, however, that the fathers of the Old Testament sought righteousness not in the Law but in Christ Jesus, who is the end of the Law itself, and they believed in him. The divine Paul, he says, in the seventh chapter of Romans, shows that in the Old Testament there was nothing but wrath and threats, while in the New grace and mercy are set before us and commended, when he says, "Wretched man that I am! Who shall deliver me from the body of this death? The grace of God through Jesus Christ." Paul, I say, in that place does not speak of the Old and New Testaments, but of the struggle and conflict between flesh and spirit, in which a man regenerated by the Spirit of God is engaged; this conflict of the flesh resisting the Spirit the Apostle shows in himself. Moreover, in those books which have been rightly translated from Greek into Latin and French, one does not read "The grace of God", but "I give thanks to God through Jesus Christ."

units.la: Interea dum ego cum hoc monacho disputarem, Officialis Primatius ira indignationeque furebat, et magnis crebrisque clamoribus haereticum me appellabat. Cum igitur videret dominum doctorem os habere clausum, nec posse mihi respondere: adversum me vociferans, Tu, inquit, sceleste haeretice, negas sanctum Sacramentum? Minime vero, inquam: sed credo et amplector sicut a Christo Domino est institutum, atque Apostolis ipsius impertitum. Tu, inquit, corpus Iesu Christi in Sacramento esse negas, et panem vocas Sacramentum.
units.tr: Meanwhile, while I was disputing with this monk, the Official Primatius raged with anger and indignation and, with loud and repeated shouts, called me a heretic. Seeing that the lord teacher had his mouth shut and could not answer me, he cried out against me: "You wicked heretic, do you deny the holy Sacrament?" "By no means," I said, "but I believe and embrace it as it was instituted by Christ the Lord and imparted to his Apostles." "You," he said, "deny that the body of Jesus Christ is in the Sacrament, and you call the bread a Sacrament."

units.la: Scriptura, inquit, admonet nos, ut Christi corpus in caelo quaeramus, imprimisque; Paul. Coloss. iii. Si vos cum Christo resurrexistis, quaerite non quae sunt in terra, sed quae sursum in caelo sunt, ubi Christus est ad dexteram Dei collocatus. Quod vero ego dico sacramentum non esse corpus Christi, sed panem, qui suam naturam propriam retineat, idem quoque facit Paulus: 1. Corinth. cap. xi. Nam quater aut quinquies sacramentum Coenae, Panem appellat. Tu monachus, Iesus Christus, inquit, dicit se esse panem vitae. Et Primatius Officialis, Sceleste haeretice, inquit, Iesus Christus dicit se vitèm esse & ostium: vbi quidem figuratè ac per similitudinem loquitur: sed verba Sacramenti non ita sunt intelligenda. Testimonia, inquam, quæ vos allegatis, pro me potius, quàm pro vobis faciunt. Age sceleste, an tu panem Cænæ, atque eum quo in victu quotidiano vtimur, eundem esse, neque quidquam interesse? Natura, inquam, & substantia nihil plane differunt: qualitate verò & vsu magnam habet differetiam. Panis enim Cænæ cum eiusdem sit naturæ cum eo quo quotidie vescimur, aliam tamen qualitatem accipit, cùm ad sacramentum adhibetur, atque ad obsignandam promissionem vitæ spiritualis æternaque proponitur. Tum ille furens, Abi sceleratè hæretice, tu igne cremaberis, atque ad diabolum ibis? Si ego, inquam, comburar pro verbo Dei tuendo, non propterea ibo ad diabolum. Vos quidem nunc iudicatis, atque omnia ad iudicium arbitriúmque vestrum refertis: sed videte quid agatis. Nam alius est summus Iudex, qui de causa nostra verè ac sine acceptione personarum iudicabit. Is innocentes, iustos pronuntiabit, quòd causam ac veritatem suam defenderint: improbos & sceleratos, qui impiè eius verbum persequuntur, condemnabit. Tum ille ut insanus furoréque correptus exclamare cœpit, Abi sceleste, reducite eum in carcerem. Ego autè Officiali Buatherio dixi, Obsecro te, domine, ut concessu vestro liceat mihi confessionem meam absoluere. Sed is, itémque monachus, atque alius Officialis iusserunt, ut ego meum in locum me reciperem. Itaque digressus sum ab illis maxima cum molestia ac dolore animi, eorum causa accepto, quibus meam fidem cumulatè approbare aut certè declarare non poteram. Sed in locum reuersus meum, cœpi Deum invocare, animóque reputare, quâ de impijs hominibus, administris Antichristi atque hostibus veritatis reportaram victoriam, quos verbo Dei plane consecerā[?]. Tu verò Spiritus sanctus in memoriam mihi reduxit id quod Christus Iesus iis promisit, qui pro causa ipsius defendenda coram inimicis eius prodirent. Vos quidem, inquit Dominus, coram regibus, præsidibus, iudicibúsque producemini in testimonium eis: sed ego vobis dabo tum os & huiusmodi sapientiam, cui aduersarij resistere non poterunt. O summam consolationem & lætitiam, quam ego, fratres charissimi, animo meo accepi, cùm vidi illud Christi promissum in meipso completu sse, verbumque Dei adversus Sathanam & Antichristum eiusq; administros superius extitisse? Equidem magnas consolationes Spiritus Dei antea percepi, ex quo Dominus me ad cognitionem verbi sui vocavit, imprimisque dum in ecclesia Dei, in sancto fidelium coetu & contentu vixi: sed minima consolatio & laetitia, quam paulo ante in his vinculis cepi & nunc capio, omnia solatia gaudiaque superat quæ unquam in tota vita mea habuerim. Nunc enim Spiritus sanctus reducit mihi in memoriam tot & tam suaves promissiones factas iis qui pro nomine ipsius patiuntur, gustúque ac sensu cælestium gaudiorum afficit:Tu quidem, inquit, nunc in his locis obscuris tetrisque beatus es, quanvis à toto mundo ut miser & infelix reijciaris, detestandusque existimeris, non ob aliud, nisi quòd nomen meum confiteris: Tu nunc in angore, lachrymis, squaloréque versaris: sed tempus est ut teipsum rigas, in Deoque authore huius tam excellentis vocationis gaudeas, exitumque huius certaminis felicissimum, atque amplissimum victoriæ præmium tibi proponas: Quòd si hoc tempore tu ducaris ad tormenta cum summa ignominia & dedecore, ô beatum hominem qui coram Deo eiusque Angelis omnes reges atque Imperatores huius mundi honore ac dignitate superas! Nam primum hoc modo imagini Filij Dei conformis consimilisque fis, ut eius quoque gloriæ atque immortalitatis particeps sis. deinde Spiritus gloriæ in te honorificentissimè requiescit: cuius quidem ea vis est atque præstantia, ut cætera omnia huius mundi vel ornamenta vel solatia gaudiaque cum eius commendatione atque consolatione comparata evanescat: Denique nunc tu es in schola & disciplina Filij Dei, in qua Pater cælestis omnes diuitias ac thesauros gratiæ suæ, secretáque sapientiæ suæ admiranda, & indicia altissima explicat: in qua omnes Prophetæ, Apostoli, Martyres versati fuerunt, & iniurias, opprobria, contumeliásque perpessi, instar ignis in fornace probati atque explorati exiterunt priusquam adipiscerentur coronam immortalitatis, paratam propositámque iis omnibus qui causam Christi & dignitatem usque ad mortem tueri volunt. Hæc est lectio, fratres charissimi, in qua Spiritus sanctus optimus filiorum Dei doctor, & suavissimus eorum qui affligūtur consolator, nos quotidie in his nostris ærumnis consolatur & hortatur.
units.tr: Scripture, he said, teaches us that we should seek Christ's body in heaven, and especially Paul, Coloss. iii: "If you have risen with Christ, seek not the things that are on earth, but those that are above in heaven, where Christ sits at the right hand of God." But when I say that the sacrament is not the body of Christ but bread, which keeps its own nature, Paul does the same thing in 1 Corinthians 11, where he calls the Supper's sacrament bread four or five times. You monk, Jesus Christ says that he is the bread of life. And Primatius the Official said, "Wicked heretic, Jesus Christ says that he is the vine and the door, where he certainly speaks figuratively and by way of comparison, but the words of the sacrament are not to be understood in that way." I said: "The testimonies you cite favour me rather than you. Tell me, wicked man, are the bread of the Lord's Supper and the bread we eat in our daily food the same, with no difference between them?" "They differ in no way in nature and substance," I said, "but in quality and use they differ greatly. For although the bread of the Supper is of the same nature as the bread we eat every day, it receives another quality when it is applied to the sacrament and set forth to seal the promise of spiritual and eternal life." Then he raved: "Go away, wicked heretic! Will you be burned with fire and go to the devil?" "If I am burned," I said, "in defence of the Word of God, I shall not therefore go to the devil. You now judge, and refer everything to your own judgment and opinion, but see what you are doing. For there is another, the supreme Judge, who will judge our cause truly and without respect of persons. He will pronounce the innocent and just, because they have defended their cause and the truth; and he will condemn the wicked and criminal, who impiously persecute his word." Then he began to cry out, as if he were mad and seized by fury: "Go away, wicked man! Take him back to prison!" But I said to the Official Buatherius, "I beg you, sir, that with your leave I may be allowed to finish my confession." But he, and the monk, and the other Official ordered me to return to my place. So I departed from them with great distress and pain of mind, grieving for the sake of those to whom I could not fully approve or at least declare my faith. But when I returned to my place, I began to call upon God and to consider in my mind what victory I had gained over these impious men, the servants of Antichrist and enemies of the truth, whom I had utterly overthrown by the Word of God. Then the Holy Spirit brought back to my memory what Christ Jesus promised to those who would come forward before his enemies to defend his cause: "You shall be brought before kings, governors and judges for a testimony against them, but I will give you a mouth and wisdom of such a kind that your adversaries will not be able to resist." O what great consolation and joy, dear brothers, I received in my mind when I saw that promise of Christ fulfilled in myself, and the Word of God standing victorious against Satan, Antichrist and his servants! Indeed I had received great consolations from the Spirit of God before, since the Lord called me to the knowledge of his Word, and especially while I lived in the Church of God, in the holy assembly and fellowship of the faithful. But the smallest consolation and joy that I received a little while ago in these chains, and now receive, surpasses all the comforts and joys that I have ever had in my whole life. For now the Holy Spirit brings back to my memory so many and such sweet promises made to those who suffer for his name, and fills me with a taste and sense of heavenly joys: "You," he says, "are now blessed in these dark and foul places, although you are cast off by the whole world as wretched and unhappy, and are judged detestable for no other reason than that you confess my name. You are now in anguish, tears and squalor; but it is time for you to water yourself, and to rejoice in God, the author of this so excellent calling, and to set before yourself the most happy outcome of this contest and the most ample prize of victory. But if at this time you are led to torments with great shame and disgrace, O blessed man, who before God and his angels surpass all the kings and emperors of this world in honour and dignity! For first in this way you are made conformed and like to the image of the Son of God, so that you may also share in his glory and immortality. Then the Spirit of glory rests upon you most honourably; and its power and excellence are such that all the other adornments, comforts and joys of this world, however they are arranged, fade away in comparison with its commendation and consolation. Finally, you are now in the school and discipline of the Son of God, in which the heavenly Father sets forth all the riches and treasures of his grace, the secrets of his wisdom which are to be admired, and the highest signs. In this school all the prophets, apostles and martyrs were trained, and having suffered injuries, reproaches and insults, they came forth tested and proved like gold in the furnace, before they obtained the crown of immortality, which is prepared and set before all those who wish to defend the cause and dignity of Christ even unto death." This is the lesson, dear brothers, in which the Holy Spirit, the best teacher of the sons of God and the sweetest consoler of those who are afflicted, comforts and exhorts us every day in these our troubles.

units.la: Postero autem die, qui erat dies Mercurij, undecimus eius mensis supra notati, ego traductus sum in alium carceris locum non ita obscurum: ubi erat frater & socius huius nostrae captiuitatis propter communem causam Euangelij: quocum meipsum per duos dies magnopere sum consolatus. Summa autem Dei providentia eum in locum translatus fui. Nam cum essem ibi cum eo fratre, admoniti fuimus, ut appellaremus ab iniquitate eius sententiae, in qua nos haereticos pronuntiarent. Cuius quidem rei nunquam mihi venisset in mentem, neque alteri fratri qui in carcere erat inferiore, nisi hoc modo consilium nobis datum fuisset. Itaque cum vesperi in meum pristinum carcerem reducerer, per latrinas id consilium communicavi cum eo fratre qui in loco sub me inferiore erat constitutus. Porro die Veneris sequenti, XIII. eius mensis, janitor me accersit ut ad Officialem adduceret: cum quo nullus erat alius praeter ipsum janitorem & alium quendam qui ex me quaesivit, an ego in oppido nomine Charitatis appellato, unquam fuissem. Cui ego, Minime inquâ: neque scio ubinam sit ea urbs. Num, inquit, tu cum iis fuisti qui Richardum eripuerunt, cum is Lutetiam captiuus ad parlamentum duceretur? Non, inquam, neque unquam Richardum cognovi aut vidi, nisi Laufanna transeuntem: quem quidam eum esse mihi significarunt. Ac sic habeto, domine, credasque mihi pro ea fide ac religione iurisiurandi quo obstrictus me verum dicturum vobis promisi, me nunquam ibi tum interfuisse, nec eam rem ullo modo approbare.
units.tr: On the following day, which was Wednesday, the eleventh day of the month noted above, I was taken to another part of the prison, not so dark, where there was a brother and companion of this our captivity for the common cause of the Gospel, with whom I greatly comforted myself for two days. Yet by the great providence of God I was moved to that place. For while I was there with that brother, we were advised to appeal against the unfairness of the sentence by which they were to declare us heretics. This thing would never have come into my mind, nor into the mind of the other brother who was in the lower cell, had counsel not been given to us in this way. So when in the evening I was led back to my former cell, I communicated this counsel through the latrines to the brother who was placed in the cell below me. Then on the following Friday, the thirteenth of that month, the jailer summoned me to bring me before the Official; no one was with him except the jailer himself and another man, who asked me whether I had ever been in a town called Charity. I said, "No, I do not, and I do not know where that town is." "Were you, then," he said, "one of those who rescued Richard when he was being led captive to Paris before the parlement?" "No," I said, "I never knew or saw Richard, except passing through Lausanne, where some people told me that he was that man. And you may take it, sir, and believe me, that I swore an oath to tell you the truth, by which I am bound, that I was never present there at that time, nor do I approve of that matter in any way."

units.la: Neque enim ea est ratio, qua verbum Dei, aut eos qui illud tuentur defendere debeamus. Vis tu igitur, inquit, error-em tuum & susceptam opinionem retinere? Quod ego amplector, inquam, & tueor, nihil est aliud quam verbum Dei, cui ego nihil repugnans affero. Qui, inquit, scis tu, id quod asseris, purum esse Dei verbum? Quoniam, inquam, id cum doctrina Prophetarum, Apostolorum ac ipsius Iesu Christi convenit, & Spiritus sanctus certissimum mihi de eo testimonium reddit, & ego ita persuasus sum. Praeterea tu ipse, domine, perspexisti & perspicis adversarios nullam rationem, quae quidem valeat, contra afferre: nec me revincere quo minus id quod dico verum sit. Vidisti enim eum qui mecum de Sacramento & aliis quibusdam rebus disputabat, vitium fuisse. Tu, inquit ille sanctum negas sacramentum. Minime, inquam: sed de eo ita sentio, ut Christus Dominus instituit, & Divus Augustinus in Ioannem scribens exponit.
units.tr: For this is not the way in which we ought to defend the Word of God or those who uphold it. "Do you therefore wish to retain your error and the opinion you have taken up?" "What I embrace and defend," I said, "is nothing other than the Word of God, which I put forward without contradicting it." "How do you know," he said, "that what you assert is the pure Word of God?" "Because," I said, "it agrees with the teaching of the prophets, the apostles and Jesus Christ himself, and the Holy Spirit gives me the most certain testimony concerning it, and I am so persuaded." Besides, you yourself, sir, have seen and do see that my opponents bring forward no argument that is effective against it, nor can they refute me so as to prove that what I say is not true. For you saw that the man who was disputing with me about the sacrament and some other matters was at fault. "You," he said, "deny the holy sacrament. "By no means," I said; "but I think about it as Christ our Lord instituted it, and as the divine Augustine sets it out when writing on John."

units.la: Cum autem viderem Officialem alia veste indutum quam uti consueuerat, & quia id mihi ante dixerat, putabam eum tum laturum eam sententiam, qua me haereticum declararet, atque ita de nobis brevi actum fore. tum ego ei dixi, Nos cum Lugduno transfiremus, atque alio iter haberemus, captos esse sine ulla causae inquisitione, cum nihil contra Regis edictū dixissemus aut fecissemus: quod iurigentium repugnat.
units.tr: When I saw the Official dressed in a different robe from the one he usually wore, and remembered that he had told me this beforehand, I thought he was then going to pronounce the sentence by which he would declare me a heretic, and that our affair would soon be finished. Then I told him that when we were passing through Lyon and were travelling on to another place, we had been seized without any inquiry into the cause, although we had said and done nothing against the king's edict; this is contrary to the law of nations.

units.la: Tu interrogasti nos de fide nostra, quid de tota religione sentiremus: nos tibi ex verbo Dei respondimus. Conceditur Turcae aut Iudaeo, ut rationem reddat fidei suae, eiusque doctrinae quam profitetur, sine ullo vitae periculo. cur nobis quoque non concedetur, qui nihil dicimus nisi quod verbo Dei continetur? Nos quidem certo scimus non temere ac fortuito, sed certissima Dei voluntate & providentia in manus vestras incidisse: sed vos quoque a Deo estis constituti, ut de causa nostra, quae iusta & aequa est, iudicetis. Quare considerate, quidnam de ea statuatis ac decernatis. nam si aliter quam oportet iudicaueritis, atque optimam causam veritatemque condemnaueritis, alius est supremus iudex, ad cuius tribunal vos sisti aliquando oportebit, ut sententiam quoque contra vos ipsos audiatis, si nunc quidquam inique in nos eius veritatis testes constitueritis. Cum autem haec a me cum maximo animi studio & summa Spiritus vi dicerentur, homo miser attonitus atque exterritus incedebat, ut nullum verbum loqui posset. Non erat illi eadem facies ac vultus laetus aut compositus quo me antea interrogare consueverat, sed tristis & pallidus, index summae perturbationis: plane nullo loco consistere poterat. Cum ego ei proponerem iudicium Dei, nihil omnino loquebatur, nec tamen a me digredi poterat. Interea Dominus in caput eius fulminabat: mihi vero summam in loquendo libertatem & audaciam concedebat. Ac cum diu postea loquutus esset, ad postremum discedens dixit, verbum Dei quidem tuendum esse. Id cum ille dixisset, ianitor me in meum carcerem reduxit: & quarta horae parte post, me accersuit ut in auditorium ad Officialem, aliosque iudices perduceret, ubi maxima hominum frequentia erat. Tum Buatherius legere coepit ac pronuntiare mea sententia, in qua me ut haereticum, schismaticumque condemnabat. Tum dixi me ab ea sententia appellare, qua ad optimam causam meam condemnandam abuterentur: itaque ab huiusmodi abusu prouocare. Tum Officialis, Cur, inquit, tu appellas? modo non ita loquebaris. Ego, inquam, in mea confessione contra abusus non contra verbum Dei locutus sum. itaque à vestra sententia appello vt abusiua & iniqua. Porro post eam sententiam & appellationem nostram, aduersarij ira & indignatione coeperunt furere. Officialis quidem vicarius Lugdunensis Archiepiscopi, postquam nos condemnassset, domum maximo cum tremore ac terrore reuersus est: ita vt cum de prouocatione nostra loqueretur, in summa perturbatione atque animi angore versaretur. Cum autem domum suam ita attonitus consternatúsque se recepisset, sesquihoram[?] post venit ad eum iudex Melierus, qui se à Suppræfecto Regis missum esse dicebat, vt eos Lutheranos ad Rouanam Regium carcerem traduceret, vt postridie supplicio afficerentur. Cui Officialis respondit, non ita futurum, quoniam nos appellassemus, eámque appellationem repudiare se non posse. Tum ille, quasi leo rugiens, Tu igitur, inquit, non vis in hos sceleratos homines animaduertere? Sane volo, inquit Officialis: sed consilium ante nobis capiendum est, & Lutetiam scribendum, vt sciamus an eorum appellatio sit valitura. Ita Deus mirabiliter defendit nos per eum, qui paulo ante nos condemnauerat: Icoque nobis ad tempus pastor fuit, vt nos aduersus rabiem caeterorum leonum tutaretur. Qua in re Deus manum suam fortem ac potentem exhibuit, atque in conspectu nostro opus admirabile effecit, vt in ipsius bonitate, misericordia, veritate totam fiduciam nostram reponamus, planéque nobis persuadeamus, cum optimus Pater huiusmodi amorem, curam, solicitudinem in nos suscipiat, nullam uim tantam diaboli aut mundi fore, quae nobis nocere possit, ac ne pilum quidem capitis nobis periturum. Quamobrem maximas Deo gratias agere debemus pro huiusmodi liberatione, in qua mirificè nos tutatus est, nostra in ipsa morte uitam conseruans, multosque pios homines suscitans, à quibus magna & corporis leuamenta & animi solatia quotidie accipimus. Confidamus igitur & speremus, Dominum qui ita nobis affuit, nullo unquam loco, tempore, ac re defuturum: atque eius bonitatem, & gratissima animi memoria, & certissima fidutia in eo vno collocata illustremus. Nos quidem hactenus[?] eius singularem gratiam opēmque experti sumus, apud quos nec pericula acerbissimae mortis proposita, nec magna huius suauissimae vitae commoda ab aduersariis promissa, quidquam valuerunt, nec vnquā efficere potuerunt quo minus nos fidem in Deum, Christumque purissimè fusceptam, summa constantia retineremus ac declararemus. Itaque nos totos in eius fidem atque opē permittamus, qui causam suam, honorē, gloriam nobis tuendam commisit: eique nostrum studium & officium, omni constantia, fide, obseruantia approbemus.
units.tr: You questioned us about our faith and asked what we thought of the whole religion, and we answered you from the Word of God. A Turk or a Jew is allowed to give an account of his faith and of the doctrine he professes, without any danger to his life. Why should this not be granted to us as well, who say nothing except what is contained in the Word of God? We certainly know that we have fallen into your hands not by chance or accident, but by the most certain will and providence of God; yet you too have been appointed by God to judge our cause, which is just and fair. Consider therefore what you will decide and determine concerning it. For if you judge otherwise than you ought, and condemn the best cause and the truth, there is another, supreme judge, before whose tribunal you will one day have to stand, and there you will hear the sentence against yourselves, if now you unjustly set yourselves against us as witnesses of that truth. When I said these things with the greatest earnestness and the utmost power of the Spirit, the wretched man went about astonished and terrified, so that he could not say a word. His face was no longer cheerful or composed, as it had been when he used to question me, but sad and pale, a sign of the greatest confusion; he could not stand still anywhere. When I set before him the judgment of God, he said absolutely nothing, yet he could not get away from me. Meanwhile the Lord thundered down upon his head, while he granted me the greatest freedom and boldness in speaking. And after he had spoken for a long time, at last, as he was leaving, he said that the Word of God must indeed be defended. When he had said this, the jailer led me back to my cell; and a quarter of an hour later he summoned me to bring me into the courtroom before the Official and the other judges, where a very large crowd of people had gathered. Then Buatherius began to read out and pronounce the sentence, in which he condemned me as a heretic and schismatic. Then I said that I appealed from that sentence, by which they were abusing it to condemn my good cause, and that I protested against this abuse. Then the Official said, "Why do you appeal? Just now you were not speaking like this." I replied, "In my confession I spoke against abuses, not against the Word of God; therefore I appeal from your sentence as abusive and unjust." Moreover, after that sentence and our appeal, our adversaries began to rage with anger and indignation. The Official, the vicar of the Archbishop of Lyon, after he had condemned us, returned home in great trembling and terror, so that when he spoke of our appeal he was in the utmost confusion and anguish of mind. When he had withdrawn home so astonished and dismayed, an hour and a half later there came to him a judge named Melier, who said he had been sent by the king's sub-prefect to take those Lutherans to the royal prison at Roanne, so that they might be put to death the next day. The Official replied that this would not happen, since we had appealed, and that he could not reject that appeal. Then the other, roaring like a lion, said, "So you do not want to punish these wicked men?" "Indeed I do," said the Official, "but we must first take counsel and write to Paris, so that we may know whether their appeal will be valid." Thus God wonderfully defended us through the very man who had condemned us a little before, and so for the time being he was a shepherd to us, protecting us against the rage of the other lions. In this matter God showed his strong and mighty hand and worked a wonderful deed before our eyes, so that we should place our whole trust in his goodness, mercy and truth, and be fully persuaded that, since our most excellent Father takes up such love, care and concern for us, no force of the devil or the world will be great enough to harm us, and not a hair of our head will perish. Therefore we ought to give the greatest thanks to God for such a deliverance, in which he has marvellously protected us, preserving our life even in the face of death, and raising up many godly people from whom we receive daily great relief for body and comfort for soul. Let us therefore be confident and hope that the Lord, who has been so present with us, will never fail us in any place, time or matter; and let us proclaim his goodness with a most grateful memory and a most certain trust placed in him alone. Indeed, up to now we have experienced his singular grace and help; neither the dangers of a most bitter death set before us, nor the great advantages of this most pleasant life promised by our adversaries, have had any power over us, nor could they ever bring it about that we would not hold fast and openly declare, with the greatest constancy, the faith in God and Christ that we have received in its purity. Therefore let us commit ourselves wholly to his faith and help, who has entrusted to us his cause, his honour and his glory to defend, and let us approve our zeal and duty to him with all constancy, faith and devotion.

units.la: Eiusdem Petri Scribæ epistola qua consolatur quendam amicum unà captiuum.
units.tr: Letter of the same Peter, the scribe, by which he consoles a certain friend who was also a prisoner.

units.la: POstquam optimo Deo ac Patri nostro placuit nos coram inimicis producere, ut simus testes veritatis eius: nostrum nunc officium est, ut ei maximas agamus gratias, laudēsque sempiternas tribuamus, orantes semper ut hoc præclarum atque admirabile opus in nobis institutum perficiat ad gloriam nominis ipsius, tum in vita tum in morte illustrādam. Nos quidem, frater charissime, paulò ante magnos aduersariorum impetus sustinuimus, sed leues adhuc, si cum ijs comparentur, quos Sathan iam facere in nos molitur. Nos pro gloria Dei usque ad hunc diem dimicauimus, sed nō usq; ad sanguinē Iesum Christum eiusque veritatem coram inimicis crudelissimis atque infestissimis confessi sumus. Restat igitur, si voluntas Dei est, ut eandem sanguine nostro obsignemus, atque ita confirmemus. Itaque quoniā huiusmodi certamen nobis est propositum, in quo inimicus ad nos opprimendos ac perdendos, omni ex parte viribus omnibus se armat ac roborat: ad pugnandum contrà nos quoque magnum animū paratumque suscipiamus. Muniamus nos tota armatura spirituali: eaq; instructi ac parati certamen propositum subeamus, sequentes regem ac ducem nostrum Iesum Christū, qui ut coronā immortalitatis obtineret, crucem mortem q; ignominiosam perpessus est, opprobrium mundi aspernatus ut voluntatem Dei Patris sui præstaret, atque hac via perduceret ad vitam aeternam omnes electos, qui ab omni aeternitate ad hanc tam excellentem Filij eius imaginem in vita & morte exprimendam prædestinati fuerunt: pro quo nos etiam patimur, ut in societatem gloriæ ipsius aliquando veniamus. Quod si mundus, mors, diabolus volunt perdere nos & absorbere, audiamus Iesum Christum optimum Magistrum ita loquentem, Vos quidem in mundo afflictionem habebitis: sed confidite, quoniam ego vici mundum. Qui credit in me, ex morte ad vitam transibit. Nam Christus moriendo perfecit, vt mors iam amplius non sit mors, sed via qua ad vitam & summam gloriam perducamur. Si fluctus maris huius mundi ad nos submergendos attolluntur: si inimici nos quamplurimis atque infestissimis copiis aggrediuntur, damemus cum Apostolis, Domine, libera nos: & is omnibus ex periculis eripiet. Quemadmodum Deus etiam promittit perProphetam suum Dauidem, Inuoca me in die afflictionis tuae, & ego eripiam te, & tu honorem mihi tribues. Cum inuocabis me, ego tibi respondebo, eroque tecum in afflictione: liberabo te, atque glorificabo. O maximam & suauissimam consolationem, quam nos in huiusmodi Dei promissionibus habere debemus: quarum fidem ac veritatem nos tam saepe in his nostris vinculis experti sumus, planeque sensimus eum, vt promisit, nobiscum esse velle, vt nos in ipsa afflictione consoletur, atque omni malo liberet. Nam cum ab aduersarijs damnati mortis sumus, atque a societate hominum tanquam quisquiliae reiecti, confidere-mus admirandam Dei bonitatem & misericordiam, qui nos varieest consolatus, tum in corpore tum in animo, nostra corda perfundens huiusmodi laetitia, quae omnem sensum atque intellectum superat, quae non solum tristitiam vincit & absorbet, sed etiam efficit vt in nostris afflictionibus, atque etiam in ipsa morte gloriemur, omnemque inimicorum furorem in nos incitatum despiciamus. ita vt singulari Dei gratia videamus nostros inimicos infinitis partibus magis captiuos & afflictos, quam nos sumus. Etenim si hoc corpus inclusum carceribus tenetur, animus quidem certe iucundissima libertate perfruitur, perfusus omni laetitia consolatione que caelesti per Spiritum sanctum: qui suo testimonio nobis affirmat nos filios Dei esse ac fratres Iesu Christi, certoque reddit de salute nostra, liberatione que beata, tum futura, cum animus ab hoc corpore separabitur, ac tum denique cum in gloriosa resurrectione resurgemus. At vero inimici nostri, quanuis iuxta figuram huius mundi in summa libertate ac felicitate esse videantur: tamen sunt miserrima Sathanae mancipia, perpetuum vermem habent in conscientia cor ipsorum corrodentem atque excedentem, ignémque perpetuò ipsos cruciantem: ut quamuis omni ratione conentur omnem sensum iudicij Divini in animo delere, inuiti tamen infestam Dei iudicis ac vindicis manum sentiant. Quamobrem Apostolū sequentes, in cruce Domini nostri atque afflictionibus nostris agamus gratias, quòd ab ipso nunc castigemur, ne cum mundo condemnemur ac percamus. Afflictio enim nostra levis est, nobisque ad exiguum temporis spatium impositā: consolatio verò sempiterna. O si nos animo reputaremus gloriam infinitam, immortalémque coronam quæ nobis post victoriam repositā in cælo asseruatur! si illa tanta bona, gaudiáq; cogitaremus, illā æternam hæreditatem quam Christus Iesus morte sua acquisiuit! si mentes animósque nostros erigeremus ad eam felicitatem & gloriosam immortalitatem, in qua corpora nostra hac humilitate liberata, glorioso corpori Christi conformia erūt: tum in hac captiuitate nostra, atque etiam in ipsa morte lætaremur, laudésque sempiternas Deo caneremus, ac gratias immortales optimo Patri agieremus, nomine huius tanti honoris ac testimonij, quo nos testes veritatis ac procuratores causæ suæ constituit. Heu, charissime frater, Christum Iesum minimè puduit coram Deo Patre causam nostram detestandam suscipere ac sustinere, tot tantásque iniurias, opprobria, contumeliásque perferre, ita ut cruci affixus inter duos facinorosos homines ipse innocentissimus constituetur, totá Dei iram atque indignatione nobis debitam, in se unum effusam excipere ac tolerare, cū tāto animi angore, ut magnitudine Divini iudicij pressus exclamarit, Deus meus, Deus meus, cur me dereliquisti? An verò pudebit nos nunc quidē causam eius tam iustā æquam que tueri? iustitiam atque innocentiam eius confiteri? morte ac passione in qua salus toti mundi continetur imitari? an dubitabimus insistere eius[?] vestigiis, ac sanctorū Prophetarū, Apostolorū, Martyrúmq; plurimo tum? qui hanc via ingressi, ut gloria Dei & sanctam Euangelij veritatem tucrentur, gravissimis periculis tormentisque vitam suam exposuerunt, ut ad illa excellentē gloriā perveniret, in qua iucundissimè felicissimèq; regnát cū duce & capite suo Iesu Christo, expectates beatā resurrectione, in qua omnes electi Dei in regnū Filij eius colligetur. Tum verò intelligemus quàm sint beati ij qui pro nomine Iesu Christi ciusmodi tormenta atque opprobria perpessi fuerunt, vestésque suas in sanguine purissimi agni dealbarunt. Tum denique illas Christi Domini sententias intelligemus, ac veras esse cum maxima nostra laetitia coperiemus, Qui perdet vitam suam propter me atque Euangelium meum, is eam seruabit: Qui patrem, matrem, uxorem, liberos, domos, vineas, agros amittet propter me, is vitam aeternam possidebit: Qui vincet haec omnia incomoda, difficultates, offendicula, cum ego in throno meo caelesti constituam. Tum denique Patrem nostrum caelestem facie ad faciem videbimus, & cognoscemus sicut ab ipso cogniti sumus, qui tum omnem exterget lachrymam ex oculis filiorum suorum, coronas eos gloria atque immortalitate, ut cum ipso in perpetuum viuant. Tum erit unum ouile & unus pastor: tum sponsa coniunctissimè viuet cum suo sponso, tum Deus omnia erit in omnibus. Omnis tum tyrannica potentia, altitudo, pulchritudo, opulentia, & pompa inimicorum Dei euanescet: qui quidem dignam infidelitatis, idololatriae, impietatisque mercedem recipient, qui tum gement, stridebuntque dentibus, cum nos optatis atque speratis gaudiis suauissimè perfruemur. Tum sentient maledictionem Dei, iustissimè in se effusam, depressi ac demersi in abyssos inferorum cum diabolo ipsorum patre ac duce: cum in regno caelesti Patris nostri, omni felicitate beatitudineque perfruemur. Quid autem his miseris maledictisque hominibus tum proderit gloria, pulchritudo, magnificentiaque huius mundi? Quid inquam, proderit tot ac tantas opes diuitiasque comparasse, tantum auri & argenti cumulasse, liberos, uxoresque forma praestantes habuisse, omnibus denique voluptatibus in hoc mundo affluxisse: cum postea cogantur haec relinquere, istamque[?] vitam commutare cum ea ad quam Dominus Iesus dicit in Euangelio, illum hominem male diuitem translatum esse? Haec omnia ipsorum commoda atque oblectamenta, ut sunt fluxa vanaque, sicut umbra aut fumus, euanescent instar somnii, quo soluti figuram huius mundi non minus fugacem quàm fallacem intelligent. Tum plorabunt, ingemiscent, frendebuntque dentibus, coniecti in ignem, qui nunquam extinguitur, à quo perpetuò torquebuntur neque tamen consumentur. Tum, inquit Diuus Ioannes, causa euitandae eius poenae mortem requirent, neque eam inuenient. Ipsi verò viuent cum diabolis in inferno, ut in aeternum ibi cruciantur. Quare charissimi fratres & amici, hanc nostram conditionem, & felicitatem impiorum ne tam graviter feramus, nostramque vice deploremus. Nunc quidem tempus est, ut capita nostra ad illum tam optabilem redemptionis nostrae diem attollamus. Illud tempus erit liberationis nostrae cum summa laetitia coniunctae, in quo sponsus sponsam suam in aeterna gaudia, solatiaque recipiet. Accensas ergo lampades nostras habetes, exemplo sapientum illarum quinque virginum, simus parati, ut obviam Iesu Christo sponso nostro prodeamus, & unà cum eo in ipsas nuptias ingrediamur. O beatos servos, quos Dominus reuertens offendet in opere laborantes, atque in eam unam curam incumbentes, ut talentum commissum augeant ac multiplicet! Quamobrē cum Christus Dominus noster talentum nobis suum thesaurumque veritatis inaestimabilem commiserit, denique operam ut hoc tantum, ac tam pretiosum bonum optima conscientia conservemus, tueamur, augeamus, omni ornemus illustremúsque sanctissima ratione: denique usque ad ultimam nostri sanguinis guttam ne diminuatur aut eripiatur nobis ac caeteris fidelibus efficiamus. Imprimis vero caveamus, ne illi malo servo similes simus, qui talentum a domino suo acceptum defodit in terram, & argentum domini sui quod in quaestum conferre debebat, abdidit. Ne tanti commoditates, honores, voluptates huius mundi aestimemus, neque parentes, liberos, uxores tanto amore complectamur, non denique vitam nostram ita charam & pretiosam habeamus, ut eam gloriae Dei & Domini nostri Iesu Christi anteponamus: sed potius omnibus huiusmodi rebus, ac mundi commodis oculos claudentes, vocationemque caelestem intuentes, arripiamus clypeum fidei, gladiumque verbi Dei, quo tela ignita sathanae, hostis nobis infestissimi, repellamus. Omnibus impedimentis soliti maximeque expediti summa cum alacritate ad propositū certamen prodeamus, semper ducem ac principem Iesum Christum intuctes[?]. Simus ei fideles, usque ad mortem pro causa eius gloriaque dimicantes, atque ita coronā vitae, omnibus strenuis ipsius militibus promissam expectemus. Expectemus, inquam, omni cum patientia Dominum, ut eius gloriam potentiamque conspiciamus. Tum enim tandem cognoscemus eum in afflictione nostra nullo modo dormiuisse: sed texisse sub alis suis, nec minus accuratè atque studiosè, quàm pupillam oculi coseruasse. Quòd si hanc certitudinem habemus & fiduciam, nullæ sunt tantæ minæ aut blanditiæ, nullum tormenti mortisque genus, denique nulla inferorum vis in nos incitata & illata, quæ possit nos à setentia fidei summaque constantia deducere, aut ab amore ac dilectione Dei Patris & Domini nostri Iesu Christi vnquam diuellere.
units.tr: Since it has pleased our best God and Father to bring us forward before our enemies, that we might be witnesses of his truth, it is now our duty to give him the greatest thanks and to render him everlasting praise, always praying that he may complete this excellent and admirable work begun in us, to the glory of his name, to be made illustrious both in life and in death. Indeed we, dearest brother, a little while ago endured the great assaults of our adversaries, yet these were still light when compared with those which Satan is now striving to bring upon us. Until this day we have fought for the glory of God, but we have not yet confessed Jesus Christ and his truth before our most cruel and hostile enemies, even to the shedding of blood. It remains, then, if it is God's will, that we seal the same with our blood and so confirm it. Therefore, since a contest of this kind has been set before us, in which the enemy arms and strengthens himself in every way with all his powers to crush and destroy us, let us also take up against him a great and ready spirit to fight. Let us arm ourselves with the whole armour of the Spirit, and equipped and prepared with it let us face the contest set before us, following our king and leader Jesus Christ, who, that he might obtain the crown of immortality, endured the cross and an ignominious death, despising the shame of the world, in order to carry out the will of his Father, and by this way to bring to eternal life all the elect, who from all eternity were predestined to be conformed in life and death to this most excellent image of his Son. For this cause we also suffer, that we may one day come into the fellowship of his glory. But if the world, death and the devil wish to destroy and swallow us up, let us hear Jesus Christ, our best Master, speaking thus: "In the world you will have tribulation, but be of good cheer, for I have overcome the world." "He who believes in me passes from death to life." For by dying Christ has brought it about that death is no longer death, but the way by which we are led to life and the highest glory. If the waves of this world's sea rise up to overwhelm us, if enemies attack us with very many and most hostile forces, let us cry with the Apostles, "Lord, save us," and he will rescue us from all these dangers. Just as God also promises through his prophet David: "Call upon me in the day of your trouble, and I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me. When you call upon me, I will answer you, and I will be with you in affliction; I will deliver you and glorify you." O what great and sweet consolation we ought to have in such promises of God! We have so often proved the faithfulness and truth of these promises in these our chains, and have plainly felt that he, as he promised, is willing to be with us, to console us in affliction itself and to free us from every evil. For although we have been condemned to death by our adversaries, and cast out from human society as rubbish, we trust in the wonderful goodness and mercy of God, who has comforted us in various ways, both in body and in mind, filling our hearts with a joy that surpasses all feeling and understanding, which not only overcomes and swallows up sorrow, but also makes us glory in our afflictions, and even in death itself, and despise the whole fury of our enemies raised against us; so that by the singular grace of God we see our enemies far more captive and afflicted in infinite ways than we are. For if this body is held shut up in prisons, the soul indeed enjoys a most delightful freedom, filled with all joy and heavenly consolation through the Holy Spirit, who by his testimony assures us that we are sons of God and brothers of Jesus Christ, and gives us certainty about our salvation and our blessed deliverance, both future, when the soul is separated from this body, and finally when we rise again in the glorious resurrection. But our enemies, although according to the fashion of this world they may seem to be in the greatest liberty and happiness, are nevertheless the most wretched slaves of Satan. They have a perpetual worm in their conscience, gnawing and eating away their hearts, and a fire perpetually tormenting them; so that although they try by every means to blot out all sense of the divine judgment from their minds, they nevertheless, against their will, feel the hostile hand of God, the judge and avenger. Wherefore, following the Apostle, let us give thanks for the cross of our Lord and for our afflictions, because we are now chastened by him, so that we may not be condemned and perish with the world. For our affliction is light, and laid upon us for a small space of time, but the consolation is everlasting. O if we would consider in our minds the infinite glory and the immortal crown which is reserved for us in heaven after the victory! If we would think of those great goods and joys, that eternal inheritance which Christ Jesus acquired by his death! If we would lift up our minds and spirits to that happiness and glorious immortality, in which our bodies, freed from this lowliness, will be made conformable to the glorious body of Christ, then in this our captivity, and even in death itself, we would rejoice, and sing everlasting praises to God, and give immortal thanks to our best Father, for the sake of so great an honour and testimony, by which he has appointed us witnesses of his truth and advocates of his cause. Alas, dearest brother, Christ Jesus was not at all ashamed before God the Father to take up and bear our cause, which men detest, to endure so many and such great injuries, reproaches and insults, so that he, most innocent, was crucified between two wicked men, and received and bore in himself alone the whole wrath and indignation of God due to us, poured out upon him, with such anguish of mind that, pressed by the magnitude of the divine judgment, he cried out, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" Or shall we now be ashamed to defend his cause, so just and so fair, to confess his righteousness and innocence, to imitate his death and passion, in which the salvation of the whole world is contained? Shall we hesitate to tread in his footsteps, and in those of the holy Prophets, Apostles and very many Martyrs, who, entering upon this way, that they might defend the glory of God and the holy truth of the gospel, exposed their lives to the most grievous perils and torments, so that they might attain that excellent glory, in which they reign most joyfully and most happily with their leader and head Jesus Christ, awaiting the blessed resurrection, in which all the elect of God will be gathered into the kingdom of his Son? Then indeed we shall understand how blessed are those who for the name of Jesus Christ have suffered such torments and reproaches, and have whitened their robes in the blood of the most pure Lamb. Then at last we shall understand those sayings of Christ the Lord, and with the greatest joy we shall perceive that they are true: "He who loses his life for my sake and for my gospel will save it; he who for my sake will lose father, mother, wife, children, houses, vineyards, fields, will possess eternal life; he who overcomes all these inconveniences, difficulties and stumbling blocks, I will set on my heavenly throne." Then at last we shall see our heavenly Father face to face, and we shall know even as we are known by him, who will then wipe away every tear from the eyes of his sons, and crown them with glory and immortality, that they may live with him for ever. Then there will be one fold and one shepherd; then the bride will live most closely united with her bridegroom; then God will be all in all. Then all the tyrannical power, height, beauty, wealth and pomp of the enemies of God will vanish away; and those indeed will receive the worthy reward of their unbelief, idolatry and impiety, who will then groan and gnash their teeth, while we enjoy most sweetly the desired and hoped-for joys. Then they will feel the curse of God, most justly poured out upon them, cast down and plunged into the abysses of hell with the devil, their father and leader, while we shall enjoy all happiness and blessedness in the heavenly kingdom of our Father. But what will the glory, beauty and splendour of this world then profit these wretched and accursed men? What, I ask, will it profit them to have gathered together so many and such great riches and wealth, to have heaped up so much gold and silver, to have had children and wives excelling in beauty, and finally to have abounded in all pleasures in this world, when afterwards they are compelled to leave these things and exchange this life for that to which the Lord Jesus, in the Gospel, says that the rich man was carried away? All these comforts and delights of theirs, since they are fleeting and vain, like a shadow or smoke, will vanish like a dream, by which, having awakened, they will understand the figure of this world to be no less fleeting than deceptive. Then they will weep, groan, and gnash their teeth, cast into the fire which is never quenched, by which they will be tormented continually yet never consumed. Then, says the divine John, they will seek death for the sake of escaping that punishment, and will not find it. But they themselves will live with the devils in hell, to be tormented there for ever. Wherefore, dearest brothers and friends, let us not bear so heavily this condition of ours, nor the happiness of the wicked, but rather lament it on their behalf. Now indeed it is time that we lift up our heads toward that most desirable day of our redemption. That time will be of our deliverance, joined with the greatest joy, on which the bridegroom will receive his bride into eternal joys and comforts. Therefore, having our lamps lit, after the example of those wise five virgins, let us be ready to go forth to meet Jesus Christ our bridegroom, and to enter with him into the marriage feast itself. O blessed servants, whom the Lord, returning, will find labouring at their work, and devoting themselves to this one care, that they may increase and multiply the talent committed to them! Wherefore, since Christ our Lord has committed to us his talent and his inestimable treasure of truth, let us above all take care to preserve, protect, increase, adorn and illustrate this so great and so precious good with the best conscience and by the most holy means, and finally, even to the last drop of our blood, see to it that it is not diminished or taken away from us and from the other faithful. Above all let us take care that we are not like that wicked servant who buried the talent received from his lord in the earth, and hid the money of his lord, which he ought to have put out for gain. Let us not value the advantages, honours and pleasures of this world so highly, nor embrace parents, children and wives with such great love, nor finally hold our life so dear and precious that we put it before the glory of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ. But rather, closing our eyes to all such things and to the advantages of the world, and looking to our heavenly calling, let us take up the shield of faith and the sword of the Word of God, by which we may repel the fiery darts of Satan, our most hostile enemy. Freed from all hindrances, and most ready, let us go forth with the greatest eagerness to the contest set before us, always looking to Jesus Christ, our leader and prince. Let us be faithful to him, fighting even to death for his cause and glory, and so await the crown of life promised to all his valiant soldiers. Let us await, I say, the Lord with all patience, that we may behold his glory and power. For then at last we shall know that he in our affliction has by no means slept, but has covered us under his wings, and guarded us no less carefully and zealously than the pupil of the eye. And if we have this certainty and confidence, there are no threats so great or flatteries so strong, no kind of torment or death, finally no power of hell stirred up and brought against us, which can draw us away from the profession of faith and the highest constancy, or ever tear us from the love and affection of God the Father and of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Sequitur BERNARDI SEGUINI fidei confessio iubicibus Lugdunensibus in eadem causae actione oblata.
units.tr: Here follows the confession of faith of Bernard Seguin, presented to the judges of Lyons in the same legal proceeding.

units.la: Spiritus sanctus per os Petri Apostoli loquens, nos admonet, ut simus semper parati ad respondendum unicuique rationem à nobis quaerenti eius spei quae est in nobis, idque cum omni mansuetudine & reuerentia. Per os etiam diui Pauli dicit, corde credi ad iustiam, ore vero fieri confessionem ad salutem. Itaque quoniam ita placuit Deo me in hæc vincula conijcere, non propter cædē, furtum, scortationem, aut alia huiusmodi maleficia flagitiaque à me commissa: sed quia interrogatus de mea fide, nolui certis capitibus assentiri, quæ hodie sunt in controuersia: nec ea vera esse confiteri, verbo Dei meaque conscientia repugnante, sequens illud Spiritus præceptum, meo officio deesse nolui. Et quoniam toto eo tempore quo interrogatus fui non potui commodè scriptam confessionem meam vobis dare, vt primum potestas mihi facta est, & commoditas oblata, eam perscribere volui, vt vos intelligatis non esse vanam opinionem & pertinaciam quandam temerè in animo meo susceptam atque obfirmatam, quæ impedierit me quo minus ea religionis capita approbarim: sed summam veritatis certitudinem, atque animi mei persuasionem, qua certo scio ea plane verbo Dei repugnare, id quod ego spero Deo aduuante, me per singula ordine demonstraturum, relinquentem ea quæ mihi cum omnibus iis sunt communia qui Christiani appellantur, vt est Symbolum Apostolorum, in quo ea omnia fidei capita amplectior atque approbo quæ in eo continentur. Ac primum de libero arbitrio, quod tribuunt homini suo proprio motu per se posse facere bonum & malum: ego dico hominem (quoniam vt Paulus testatur, post lapsum primi parentis Adam, maledictus fuit, filiusque irae ac mortis) sua natura nihil aliud posse quam offendere Deum, & seipsum damnare. Scriptura enim testificatur, S[?]hficatur[?], cor hominis iam inde ab adolescentia atque infantia prauum esse, ad malumque propensum, nec quicquam boni posse inde proficisci, inter ipsos homines ne vnum quidem iustum esse, aut qui Deum quaerat, sed omnes inutiles, corruptos, ac timore Dei vacuos, & propterea omni malitia atque iniquitate abundates: omnem cogitationem atque affectionem hominum esse Deo inimicam, hominem ita esse abominabilem, vt instar piscis aquam sorbentis iniquitatem sorbeat, eumque ipsa vanitate vaniorem esse. Quae cum vera sint omnia, quid est quod homo ex seipso aliud possit producere quam peccatum, non aliter quam mala arbor malum vitiosumque fructum profert? Quare cum huiusmodi sit, nihil boni, ne minimum quidem, per se potest facere: sed Deus in eo efficiat necesse est. Itaque eius totius boni, quod Deus in homine efficit, nulla nobis gloria est tribuenda. Quid enim habes ait Paulus, quod non acceperis? si vero accepisti, cur gloriaris, quasi non acceperis? Tota igitur gloria bonorum omnium quae facimus, soli Deo authori est ascribenda. Praedarum opus est fides: sed ea singulare donum Dei est. Nemo enim, inquit Dominus, ad me potest venire, nisi Pater traxerit. & iterum, Nemo ad me venire potest, nisi datum fuerit a Patre. Diuus vero Paul. aperte dicit, nos ne idoneos quidem esse, vt aliquid ex nobis ipsis cogitemus, sed nostra sufficientia esse ex Deo: Deum esse qui efficit in nobis & velle & perficere pro sua bona voluntate. Denique cum vnum esse, qui quod coepit in nobis, etiam vsque ad extremum diem perficit. Quare prima, media, postremaque in nostra salute, sunt ad Deum referenda. Ex eo enim & origo & progressio, ad eundemque exitus salutis nostrae referendus est. Praeterea Hierem. dicit, Scio Domine, quod non est hominis via eius, neque hominis gressus suos dirigere: Et alio loco, Converte me Domine ad te & ego convertar. Ezechiel autem, quemadmodum Dauid, plane testatur, proprium Dei opus esse, cor renouare, cuiusque mollire duritiem, Legem suam in cordibus nostris inscribere, eaque ita immutare, vt ex lapideis fiat carnea: denique in via praeceptorum eius ambulare, timoreque nominis sui ita infigere in animis nostris, ne vnquam ab ipso declinemus. Si igitur nos credimus in Deum, & in ea fide ac vitae sanctitate perseueramus, id non nascitur in nobis sed a Deo proficiscitur, & vsque in finem continuatur. Nam nos quidem priusquam credamus, nihil aliud possumus quam peccare, quemadmodum ait Apostolus, Quicquid non est ex fide peccatum est. Item, fides donum Dei est, ergo etiam bona opera, ipsaque vita aeterna, propterea quod ea omnia ex fide, ut ex causa originéque sua existunt. Ex quo satis intelligi potest, quae sit facultas hominis propria, & vis in eo liberi arbitrij, cum nihil possit per se nisi male agere. quidquam vero agere non possit, nisi Deus id in eo efficiat, usque ad ipsa voluntatem & cogitationem, quam homo bonam in natura sua relictus cōcipere non potest, sed ut ante demonstratum est, Deus eam in eo excitat, atque ad rectitudinem veritatemque conformat. De iustificatione autem, ego credo hominem iustificari sola fide, quae per dilectionem operatur, ita ut nulla pars eius iustitiae, quae apud Deum valere debet, operibus debeatur. Nam sicut oportet arborem antequam ullum fructum bonum ferat, bonam esse, ita hominem fide iustum esse, priusquam possit ullum bonum opus facere, cum ipsa quidem persona prius Deo placeat, quam ad ullum eius opus respiciat, illudque gratum habeat, sicut satis notum est exemplo Abelis, ad quem Deus ante quam ad munera eius respexit. Sola ergo fides est, quae nos coram Deo iustos efficit, non opera: sicut Paulus in omnibus suis epistolis ostendit, imprimisque in iis quas ad Romanos & ad Galatas scripsit, in quibus omnem hominis gloriam ab ea iustitia excludit, atque integram laudem gratiae Dei ac misericordiae tribuit. Etenim si iustitia, ut ait idem Apostolus, est ex Lege, Christus frustra mortuus est. Omnes autem peccaverunt, gratisque nunc sine ipsa Lege iustificantur, gratis per gratiam, per redemptionem Iesu Christi, quem Deus propitiatorium proposuit intercedente eius sanguine. Haec autem iustitia nobis donatur, cum ea in Euangelio revelata atque oblata, fide a nobis accipitur, veniaque peccatorum credentibus nobis in Filium Dei datur. Nam haec quidem iustitia in gratuita peccatorum remissione est posita, cum ea nobis non imputantur, nec in conspectum Dei proponuntur, sed eius misericordia obteguntur: quemadmodum Dauid pronuntiat beatos homines, quibus remissae sunt iniquitates, & quorum peccata tecta sunt. Itaque nos oportet, si salui esse volumus planeque beati, omnem propria operum iustitiam, eiusque fiduciam abijcere, solaque fidei iustitia niti vt gratiam apud Deum incamus, eámque hac summissione ac humilitate tueamur, vt nobis ipsis diffidamus, totam vero spe salutis nostrae ac fiduciam, in sola Dei misericordia fixam & locatam habeamus: neque Pharisaei illius sed Publicani potius imitemur, vt omnis nostrae iustitiae inopes, humiliter ad eius, qui misericordia dives est, gratia & iustitia confugiamus. neque vero sequamur exemplum Iudaeorum, qui cum studerent suam iustitiam stabilire, iustitiae Dei non fuerunt subiecti. Bap-tismum vero credo introitum esse nobis in Ecclesiam, quemadmodum Circuncisio Iudaeis erat, eiusque administrandi mandatum Apostolis datum fuisse, cum dictum est eis, vt irent ac docerent, baptizantes in nomine Patris & Filij & Spiritus sancti. Qui vero ad aquam à Deo in sacramentum institutam aliquid aliud adiungit, vt ignem, sputum, salem, aliásque huiusmodi quisquilias, is Ioannem Baptistam atque etiam ipsum Dominum Iesum non satis sapientem in eo instituendo suisse existimat. Neque vero salis & aquae benedictae, eius quâ isti vtuntur, vlla mentio in nouo Testamento facta est: sed quòd Ioan. Baptista ad flumē Iordanē baptizabat, & quòd Philipp° baptizauit Eunuchū reginae Candaces ad primam aquam quam nactus est. Hæ autem cum essent aquæ puræ, atque adeò vt creaturæ Dei bonæ ad vsum tam pium sanctificatæ, quid opus fuit alia addere quæ tantum corruptelam afferre possent? Quòd autem ita arbitrantur infantes, qui ante Baptismum moriuntur, damnatos esse, aut conspectu ipsius Dei priuari quæ grauis damnatio est: ego huiusmodi opinionem falsam atque impiam esse dixi. nam ita & potentia Dei minuitur, quasi non possit alio modo quam quem instituerit saluare: & salus eius symbolis atque elementis corruptioni obnoxiis alligetur: cum potius illa grauis solennisque promissio esset consideranda, qua Deus primum Abrahæ ac semini eius, deinde omnibus fidelibus, qui in locum eorum succederent, se Deum fore affirmauit. Itaque Paul. fidelium sanctâ esse sobolem dicit, etiam cum est adhuc in matris utero. vt de Hieremia & Ioanne Baptista legimus, qui etiam in utero, eius sanctificationis expertes nequaquam fuerunt. Quamuis igitur Deus hoc sacramentum instituerit, vt hoc modo infantes in Ecclesiam suam introduceret, atque ad salutem perduceret, in eo tamen non est tam acerbæ necessitatis lex, vt benignissimus Deus non possit aut nolit eis salutem dare, quibus beneficium huius lucis ac vitæ non impertierit vt sacramentum Baptismi capere possint.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit, speaking through the mouth of the apostle Peter, admonishes us always to be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks us for the reason of the hope that is in us, and to do so with all gentleness and reverence. Through the mouth of the divine Paul also he says that with the heart one believes unto righteousness, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. Therefore, since it has pleased God to cast me into these chains, not on account of murder, theft, fornication, or any other such crimes or wickedness committed by me, but because, when I was questioned about my faith, I was unwilling to assent to certain articles which are today in dispute, nor to confess that they are true, since they are contrary to the Word of God and to my conscience, I was unwilling, following that precept of the Spirit, to fail in my duty. And since, throughout the whole time during which I was questioned, I could not conveniently give you my confession in writing, as soon as the opportunity and the means were given to me, I wished to set it down in writing, so that you may understand that it is not an empty opinion or some obstinacy rashly taken up and fixed in my mind that has kept me from approving those articles of religion; rather, it is the highest certainty of truth and the persuasion of my mind, by which I know for certain that those articles plainly contradict the Word of God. I hope, with God's help, to demonstrate this to you point by point, leaving aside those things which I hold in common with all who are called Christians, such as the Apostles' Creed, in which I embrace and approve all the articles of faith contained in it. And first, concerning free will, which they attribute to man, that by his own motion he can of himself do good and evil: I say that man (since, as Paul testifies, after the fall of our first parent Adam he was cursed, and became a son of wrath and of death) by his nature can do nothing but offend God and damn himself. For Scripture testifies that the heart of man, from youth and from infancy, is depraved and prone to evil, and that nothing good can come from it; that among men there is not even one righteous, nor anyone who seeks God, but all are unprofitable, corrupt, and void of the fear of God, and therefore abounding in all malice and iniquity; that every thought and affection of men is hostile to God; that man is so abominable that, like a fish drinking water, he drinks in iniquity, and that he is more vain than vanity itself. Since all these things are true, what else can man produce from himself but sin, just as a bad tree bears bad and corrupt fruit? Therefore, since man is of such a kind, he cannot of himself do anything good, not even the least; rather, God must necessarily work it in him. Thus no glory for any of that whole good which God works in man is to be ascribed to us. For what have you, says Paul, that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you glory, as if you had not received it? Therefore all the glory of the good works that we do is to be ascribed solely to God, the author. Faith is indeed a noble thing, but it is a singular gift of God. For no one, says the Lord, can come to me unless the Father draws him, and again, no one can come to me unless it has been given to him by the Father. And the divine Paul clearly says that we are not even sufficient to think anything of ourselves, but that our sufficiency is from God; that it is God who works in us both to will and to perform, according to his good pleasure. Finally, that it is God alone who also brings to completion, even until the last day, what he has begun in us. Therefore the first, the middle, and the last things in our salvation are to be referred to God. For both the origin and the progress, and the outcome of our salvation, are to be referred to him. Moreover, Jeremiah says: I know, O Lord, that the way of man is not in himself, nor is it for man to direct his steps. And in another place: Turn me, O Lord, unto yourself, and I shall be turned. Ezekiel, however, as David also plainly testifies, teaches that it is the proper work of God to renew the heart and to soften its hardness, to write his law in our hearts and so to change them that from stony they become fleshly; finally, to make us walk in the way of his precepts and to fix the fear of his name so deeply in our minds that we never turn away from him. If therefore we believe in God and persevere in that faith and holiness of life, this does not arise in us, but proceeds from God, and is continued to the end. For before we believe, we can do nothing but sin, as the Apostle says: whatever is not of faith is sin. Likewise, faith is the gift of God; therefore also good works, and eternal life itself, since all these exist from faith as from their cause and origin. From this it can be sufficiently understood what the proper faculty of man is, and what power of free will there is in him, since by himself he can do nothing but act wickedly; and he cannot do anything at all unless God works it in him, even down to the will and the thought itself, which man, left to his own nature, cannot conceive as good; but, as was shown above, God stirs it up in him and conforms it to uprightness and truth. As to justification, I believe that man is justified by faith alone, which works through love, so that no part of that righteousness which ought to avail before God is owed to works. For just as a tree must be good before it can bear any good fruit, so a man must be righteous by faith before he can do any good work; for the person himself pleases God before he regards any of his works and accepts them as pleasing, as is well known from the example of Abel, to whom God had regard before he regarded his gifts. Therefore faith alone is what makes us righteous before God, not works; as Paul shows in all his epistles, and above all in those which he wrote to the Romans and the Galatians, in which he excludes all human glory from that righteousness and assigns the whole praise to the grace and mercy of God. For if righteousness, as the same Apostle says, is by the Law, then Christ died in vain. But all have sinned, and now are justified freely without the Law itself, freely by grace, through the redemption of Jesus Christ, whom God set forth as a propitiation through his blood. This righteousness is given to us: when it is revealed and offered in the Gospel, it is received by us through faith, and the forgiveness of sins is granted to us who believe in the Son of God. For this righteousness consists in the free remission of sins: our sins are not imputed to us, nor set before the sight of God, but are covered by his mercy, just as David pronounces blessed those men whose iniquities are forgiven and whose sins are covered. Therefore we ought, if we wish to be saved and truly blessed, to cast away all righteousness of our own works and all trust in it, and to rest only on the righteousness of faith, that we may gain grace before God; and we should maintain it with such humility and lowliness that we distrust ourselves, and that we place and fix our whole hope and confidence of salvation solely in the mercy of God. We should imitate not the Pharisee but rather the Publican, and, being poor in all our righteousness, humbly flee to the grace and righteousness of him who is rich in mercy. Nor should we follow the example of the Jews, who, while they strove to establish their own righteousness, were not subject to the righteousness of God. I believe that baptism is our entrance into the Church, just as circumcision was for the Jews, and that the command to administer it was given to the apostles when it was said to them: go and teach, baptizing in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. But whoever adds anything else to the water that God instituted as a sacrament, such as fire, spittle, salt, and other such trifles, thinks that John the Baptist and even the Lord Jesus himself were not wise enough in instituting it. Indeed, there is no mention in the New Testament of holy salt and blessed water, such as those men use; rather, there is mention that John the Baptist baptized at the river Jordan, and that Philip baptized the eunuch of Queen Candace at the first water he came upon. Since these were pure waters, and sanctified for so holy a use as good creatures of God, what need was there to add other things which could bring only corruption? As for the opinion that infants who die before baptism are damned, or deprived of the sight of God itself, which is a grievous damnation: I have said that this opinion is false and impious. For in this way the power of God is diminished, as if he could save only in the manner that he has instituted; and his salvation is bound to symbols and elements subject to corruption; whereas rather the grave and solemn promise should be considered, by which God affirmed first to Abraham and his seed, and then to all the faithful who should succeed them, that he would be their God. Thus the apostle Paul says that the offspring of believers is holy, even while it is still in the mother's womb; as we read of Jeremiah and John the Baptist, who, even in the womb, were by no means without that sanctification. Although, therefore, God has instituted this sacrament in order that in this way he might bring infants into his Church and lead them to salvation, nevertheless there is not in it so harsh a law of necessity that the most kind God cannot or will not give salvation to those to whom he has not granted the benefit of this light and life, so that they might receive the sacrament of baptism.

units.la: Cœna vero, est sacramentum à Domino in Ecclesia institutum, in quo ipse vult fungi erga nos domesticos suos officio optimi patrisfamilias, nutriens nō modò corpora nostra, sed etiam animas carne sua & sanguine: in quo vno saluberrimus animorum nostrorum pastus est. Eo autem tum vere pascimur, cum oculos mentis nostræ in cælum attollimus ad contemplandum Christum Iesum qui ad dexteram Dei Patris considet[?], atque in memoriam revocamus illud beneficium redemptionis, in quo se pro peccatis nostris in sacrificium obtulit. Itaque vere participamus corpori ac sanguini Domini, cum fide panem & vinum, vt signa monumentaque spiritualis refectionis ad animum pertinentis, sumimus: & credimus Christum Dominum, vt est pro nobis crucifixus ac mortuus, nō minus nobis impertiri & communicari, quàm cū panem qui à ministro fidelibus dispertitur. Quamobrem transsubstantionem illam, vt huic sanctæ Domini institutioni planè contrariam, atque à Sathana fallacibusque spiritibus inventam & in ecclesiam cum maxima pernicie introductam, prorsus repudio. neque enim panis ille corpus Christi vllo modo esse potest, quod (vt in symbolo fidei nostræ credimus, atque ab Spiritu sancto in Scriptura docentur) resuscitatum in cælumque receptum & ad dexteram Dei Patris summo cum honore collocatum, non amplius in terra corpore suo versatur, nec ante reversurus est, quàm ad iudicium omnes tum vivos tum mortuos vocaverit. Neque etiam huiusmodi transsubstantiationem aut præsentiam Christi corporalem in eo pane, aut corporis naturam, aut ipsius signi ac sacramenti pati potest. nam verum quidem corpus nō potest esse eodem tempore nisi vno in loco: corpus autem Christi quanuis gloria atque immortalitate sit ornatum, neque amplius obnoxium illi infirmitati carnis quàm nostra causa suscepit, in cæteris tamen naturam corporis retinet, vt pro magnitudine sua certo loci spatio sit circumscriptum non eodem tempore vagum, locisq; infinitus diffusum. Præterea cum corpus Christi sit gloriosum atque planè incorruptum, panis vero temporis progressu corrumpatur, quæ transmutatio ac transformatio huius in illud fieri poterit? Natura vero signi aliud ostendit esse quod significat, aliud quod eo significatur: illud esse aspectabile quod sub sensum cadit, rem autem ipsam natura & substantia plane diversam, quamvis aliquam consimilem[?] rationem cum signo suo habeat. Itaque quemadmodum aqua in Baptismo in sanguinem Christi, quo lavamur, non convertitur: ita panis in Coena in carnem converti non potest, cum eadem sit ratio utriusque Sacramenti, & natura omnium signorum atque symbolorum huiusmodi, ut ratione substantiae ab iis rebus distinguatur, ad quas significandas & repraesentandas adhibentur. Illam vero impiam consuetudinem & sacrilegam audaciam, qua Coenam Domini diminuerunt, & Laicos altera parte privauerunt, nullo modo probare possum. pugnat enim cum institutione Domini, qui omnes ex eodem calice bibere voluit: & cum Pauli testimonio, qui dicit rationem celebrandae Coenae Corinthijs se ita tradidisse, ut a Domino acceperat. Uoluit enim Dominus integram sui communionem proposito hoc utroque genere signorum demonstrari. Quare ut corporis ac sanguinis Christi simus participes, nihil est necesse ea in istis includi elementis. Quanvis enim corpus Christi in caelo sit, tamen fide quae res absentes percipit atque apprehendit, & virtute Spiritus qui coniungit ea quae longo intervallo sunt separata, eo plane participare possumus. Haec igitur verba, Hoc est corpus meum, figurate sunt intelligenda, quemadmodum, Agnus, Domini transitus appellatur: & Petra, Christus, cum tantummodo signa essent earum rerum, quarum aut praeteritarũ memoriam renovabant, aut futurarum spem aliqua insigni significatione praemonstrabat. De Missa, quam a Christo institutam esse dicunt, & sacrificium tum vivis tum mortuis utile: id falsum esse dico, & cum verbo Dei plane pugnare. nam ipsa Iesu Christi institutio aliud admonet ac iubet ut comedamus & bibamus, non ut ipsum Deo in sacrificium offeramus. Deinde hoc officium offerendi ad nullum hominem mortalem pertinet, sed unius Christi proprium est, quo ipse est persanctus, quum, ut ait Apostolus, seipsum semel obtulit, atque una oblatione suos in perpetuum sanctificavit: hac autem sanctificatione perfecta, nulla alia restat oblatio. Nam ob eam quidem causam constitutus fuit sacerdos secundum ordinem Melchisedec, ut nullum cius muneris atque honoris socium successoremque haberet. Itaque Christus Iesus summa sacerdotij dignitate spoliatur, quando ius sacrificandi in alios transfertur, vt eis illud sacrificium repetere ac renouare, aut confirmare, ad aliosque applicare liceat. Denique nemo, vt inquit Apostolus, debet honorem vsurpare, nisi a Deo vocatus suerit. At non legimus vllum alium praeter Christum ad eam dignitatem vocatum esse: praeterea cum promissio quae his verbis continetur, Hoc est corpus meum quod pro vobis traditur: iis solum offeratur qui sacramento communicant, eius vtilitas & vis non potest ad mortuos pertinere qui iam in ea communione non versantur. Adde etiam, quod fructus eius Missae, quem ad mortuos volunt peruenire, in Purgatorio, inanissimo hominum inuento figmentoque consistit, contra omne verbum Dei in quo nullam aliam purgationem quam sanguinis Iesu Christi legimus. Haec ego sentio & credo de iis fidei ac religionis capitibus, quae hodie sunt in controuersia, in quibus quidem vos facile perspicitis me nihil ex meo ingenio afferre ac dicere: sed pro ea gratia quam Deus in me contulit, omnia authoritate verbi eius approbare. Quod si his neglectis spretisque id agitis, vt me haereticum esse conuincatis, sicut a vobis antea sum declaratus: videte quam periculosum sit hoc modo progredi aduersus eum qui purum Dei verbum vobis proponit. Sed ego totam causam veritatis Deo authori vocationis meae commendo, cuiusque fidei committo, eum orans vt mihi patientiam & constantiam praestet, quo animo non solum aequo, sed etiam libenti id omne patiar quod me pro suo nomine perpeti voluerit: cui honor & gloria in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: The Supper is a sacrament instituted by the Lord in the Church, in which he himself wishes to act toward us, his household, as the office of the best of fathers, feeding not only our bodies but also our souls with his flesh and blood. In this one thing is the most wholesome food of our souls. We are truly fed when we lift the eyes of our mind to heaven to contemplate Christ Jesus, who sits at the right hand of God the Father, and when we call to mind that benefit of redemption, in which he offered himself as a sacrifice for our sins. Thus we truly partake of the body and blood of the Lord when, in faith, we take bread and wine as signs and memorials of the spiritual refreshment that belongs to the soul; and we believe that Christ the Lord, as he was crucified and died for us, is no less imparted and communicated to us than the bread which the minister distributes to the faithful. Therefore I utterly reject that transubstantiation, as completely contrary to this holy institution of the Lord, devised by Satan and deceiving spirits, and introduced into the Church with the greatest ruin. For that bread cannot in any way be the body of Christ, which (as we believe in the creed of our faith, and as the Holy Spirit teaches in Scripture) was raised again, received into heaven, and placed at the right hand of God the Father with the highest honour, and no longer dwells on earth in his body, nor will return before he has summoned all, both living and dead, to judgement. Nor can such a transubstantiation, or a bodily presence of Christ in that bread, or the nature of a body, be admitted in that bread, or in the sign and sacrament itself. For a true body cannot be in several places at the same time, but only in one place; and the body of Christ, although adorned with glory and immortality, and no longer subject to that weakness of the flesh which he took up for our sake, nevertheless retains the nature of a body, so that, according to its magnitude, it is circumscribed within a certain space of place, not wandering at the same time, nor spread infinitely through all places. Moreover, since the body of Christ is glorious and wholly incorruptible, but bread corrupts with the passing of time, what change or transformation of this into that could take place?
