Atque huiusmodi verba cum precibus addidit, Heu, ne mihi torquem ordinis tam excellentis insigne denegetis. Tum Suppræfectus, Siquidem ita vult, inquit, detur ei funis ut & cæteris. Id cum factum esset, ducti sunt ad locum supplicio constitutum, comitati quatuor Franciscanis & magno satellitum numero, qui omnes currum cingebant, ut impedirent illos tres martyres ne ad populum loquerentur. Eò igitur cum venissent, subitò accincti fuerunt atque ad postem alligati, fasceque lignorum aridorum circumcirca: atq; ita circumseptis hi tres, simul canticum Simeonis canere cœperunt, Nunc dimittis servum tuum Domine, &c. dum carnifex in circumitu ignem succenderet, qui paulò post eorum corpora consumpsit.
units.tr: A few days later, Marsacus himself and his companions, his cousin and Stephen the carpenter, who was born at Genabum on the Loire, a man of most ardent zeal and well instructed in the Word of God, were condemned together by the same sentence, pronounced from the tribunal, to be burned alive. After the judges had pronounced that sentence, they were greatly disturbed and astonished to see these three martyrs not only not dread their approaching death, but also praise God with every thanksgiving and praise, because they were counted worthy by him to suffer for his most holy name, so that as they came out of the court they began to sing a certain psalm. The Lieutenant could no longer bear to overlook this, nor to endure their holy joy and cheerfulness in God; but moved by great indignation, he ordered silence to be imposed on them, and as he went out from there he said, "Are these abject men to lift themselves up so against the great authority of the kingdom?" Then Marsacus withdrew into a small corner of the place where they were and began to pray to God. When one of the guards tried to stop him, Stephen said, "Is it right at this time that we be hindered from invoking and praying to our God?" Terrified by these words the guard fell silent and at once withdrew. Moreover, before they were led out of the prison to be taken to the final punishment, they placed a rope around the neck of each of the other two, Marsacus's cousin and Stephen. But Ludovicus Marsacus, when he expected the same mark and adornment and saw that it was not brought to him, because the judges took account of one who was of their equestrian order, those called the King's Ordinary, asked in a loud voice, in front of the Lieutenant and the other magistrates, whether the cause of his brethren and companions was other than his own. Adding such words with entreaties, he said, "Alas, do not deny me the collar, the emblem of so excellent an order." Then the Lieutenant said, "Since he wishes it so, let him be given a rope as well as the others." When this was done, they were led to the place appointed for execution, accompanied by four Franciscans and a large number of guards, who surrounded the cart so that they might prevent those three martyrs from speaking to the people. When they had come there, they were suddenly bound and fastened to the post, with dry bundles of wood piled all around; and so, surrounded, these three at once began to sing the canticle of Simeon, "Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart," etc., while the executioner went around kindling the fire, which a little later consumed their bodies.

units.la: MATTHAEUS DYMONETUS.
units.tr: MATTHAEUS DYMONETUS.

units.la: MAtthæus Dymonetus, mercator patria Lugdunensis, in sua ignoratione vitam in omnibus mundi cupiditatibus voluptatibusque dissolutam, & à modestia pietatéque Christiana alienam degerat. Nam in illis suis deliciis adeò abhorrebat à verbo Dei atque studio pietatis, ut eos qui Lugduni invocandi Dei causa coetus conventúsque haberent, insidiosè atque inimicè observaret. Postquam verò summa Dei misericordia ad cognitionem Euangelij vocatus est, statim fructus conversionis admirabilis ostendit. nam paulò post comprebefus[?] benfus[?] cùm domi suæ esset, ab his qui iurisdictionem Lugduni habent, primo aditu, quæ esset sua fides non dissimulanter & obscurè, sed ingenuè ac liberè declarauit: & postea in iudicio purissimam eius consessionem edidit: quam nos literis mandauimus, quemadmodum sequitur.
units.tr: Matthaeus Dymonetus, a merchant of Lyonnais birth, had lived in his ignorance a life dissolute in all the desires and pleasures of the world, and alien to Christian modesty and piety. For in those delights he so abhorred the Word of God and zeal for piety that he secretly and hostilely watched those who held meetings and assemblies in Lyon for the sake of calling upon God. But after, by the highest mercy of God, he was called to the knowledge of the Gospel, he at once showed the fruits of a wonderful conversion. For soon after, when he was at home, he was seized by those who have jurisdiction in Lyon; at the first hearing, when asked what his faith was, he declared it plainly, not evasively or obscurely, but frankly and freely; and afterwards in court he made a most pure confession, which we have committed to writing, as follows.

units.la: Die Lunæ qui fuit IX. Ianuarij M.D.LIII. cum essem domi nostræ coram Suppræfecto regio & Officiali Buatherio: cumq; illi perscrutati essent libros nostros, in quibus nihil plane repererunt quod damnarent, præter exiguum librum cantionum spiritualium: ego de mea fide ab Officiali fui interrogatus. qui iudex à me recusatus, rogauit Suppræfectum ut me interrogaret. Itaque ille monuit, me cum essem Christianus, debere rationem fidei meæ reddere. Id quod ego sine vlla dilatione feci, quemadmodum sequitur.
units.tr: On Monday, the 9th of January 1553, when I was at our house before the royal Lieutenant and the official Buatherius, they searched our books, and in them they found nothing at all that they could condemn, except a small book of spiritual songs. I was questioned about my faith by the official. I refused him as judge, and he asked the Lieutenant to question me. So the Lieutenant admonished me that, since I was a Christian, I ought to give an account of my faith. This I did without any delay, as follows.

units.la: Cùm igitur quæsiuissent ex me, ex qua parœcia essem, rogarunt deinde num crederem virginem Mariam ac Sanctos esse inuocandos, eósque nostros aduocatos esse. Quibus ego respondi, virginem Mariam omnium mulierum esse beatissimam, Sanctósque omnes beatos, eósque veram vitæ viam nobis commonstrasse. Itaque eos quidem nos debere imitari. aduocatos verò habere præter vnum Christum iustum, debere neminem. Interrogatus ab iisdem, num esset Purgatorium, vbi animæ eorum qui ex hac vita excesserunt, purgarentur. respondi, Iesum Christum per seipsum perfectam omnium vitiorum nostrorum purgationem fecisse, neque aliam esse requirendam. Interrogatus etiam, num omnia peccata nostra semel quidem in anno sacerdoti sint confitenda. respondi, non semel solum in anno, verumetiam quotidie coram Deo & hominibus testari nos esse peccatores oportere. Post autem haec responsa, Suppræfectus iussit me vsq; ad domum suam sequi. quò cum venissem, videremque eius mandato eundum mihi esse in carcerem, ab eo quæsiui, an haberet eius rei aliqua mandata aut querelas, criminaque aduersum me. Ad quod is respondit, se postridie mecum locuturum.
units.tr: When they had asked me which parish I belonged to, they next asked whether I believed that the Virgin Mary and the saints are to be invoked, and that they are our advocates. To this I replied that the Virgin Mary is the most blessed of all women, and that all the saints are blessed, and that they have shown us the true way of life; so indeed we ought to imitate them. But to have advocates, apart from the one righteous Christ, we ought to have none. Asked by the same men whether there is a Purgatory where the souls of those who have departed this life are purged, I replied that Jesus Christ, by himself, has made the perfect cleansing of all our sins, and that no other is to be sought. Asked also whether all our sins must be confessed to a priest once a year, I replied that we must testify before God and men that we are sinners not only once a year but every day. After these answers the Lieutenant ordered me to follow him as far as his house. When I came there and saw that by his order I was to be taken to prison, I asked him whether there were any orders, complaints or charges against me. To this he replied that he would speak with me the next day.

units.la: Die autem Lunæ, qui fuit XII. eiusdem mensis, M.D.LIII. venerunt in carcerem Officialis Primatius (vt vocant) & Officialis Buatherius, & Orrius inquisitor, & alij eiusdem farinæ homines, qui me interrogare voluerunt,in primisque Orrius,qui vt me authoritate officii sui magis premeret,dicebat se à Rege atque Pontifice inquisitore constitutum esse.Cui ego & caeteris respondi,eis nullum iudicium actionemque in me competere: & quanquam mihi poenam excommunicationis minarentur,nunquam tamen eos iudices agnoscere acciperéque volui,sed ad Suppraefectum Regium semper appellaui, paratus ei de mea fide respondere cum is me vellet interrogare. Itaque illi cum nihil aliud possent,me in obscurum,imò infimum carceris locum demittere volebant:sed ego custodem carceris monui vt videret quid ageret.
units.tr: On Monday, the 12th of the same month, 1553, there came to the prison the official Primatius (as they call him), the official Buatherius, Orrius the inquisitor, and other men of the same kind, who wished to question me. Above all Orrius, who, to press me more with the authority of his office, said that he had been appointed by the King and by the Pope as inquisitor. To him and to the others I replied that they had no jurisdiction or cause of action against me. Although they threatened me with the penalty of excommunication, I never wished to acknowledge them as judges or to accept them, but always appealed to the royal Lieutenant, ready to answer for my faith whenever he wished to question me. Since they could do nothing else, they wanted to thrust me into the dark, indeed the lowest, part of the prison; but I warned the jailer to see what he was doing.

units.la: Die veneris XX.eius mensis M.D.LIII. venit Suppraefectus cum Officiali Buatherio & inquisitore,aliisque qui me interrogare voluerunt. sed aduersus eos refutatione iudiciali vsus sum,conuersusque ad Suppraefectum,ea quae antea demonstraui,de mandatis regijs & querelis criminibusque in me collatis: praeterea quis aduersator mihi esset quaesiui: & quod captus fuissem atque in carcerem coniectus,appellaui:eorumque omnium acta cum ab eo postulassem,se curaturum mihi promisit. sed cum post multa verba facta,is dixisset se venisse vt testificaretur inquisitorem & caeteros à Rege esse constitutos,quibus mihi de mea fide respondendum esset:interrogatus iterum,dixi me credere ea omnia,quae Ecclesia sancta fide vera completeretur:Credere in Deum Patrem omnipotentem,creatorem caeli & terrae,& in Iesum Christum Filium eius vnicum Dominum nostrum,conceptum de Spiritu sancto,natum ex Maria virgine,&c. Credere etiam in Spiritum sanctum,sanctam Ecclesiam catholicam,communionē Sanctorum[?], &c.
units.tr: On Friday, the 20th of that month, 1553, the Lieutenant came with the official Buatherius, the inquisitor, and others who wished to question me. But against them I made a judicial objection, and turning to the Lieutenant I repeated what I had said before: about the royal orders, and the complaints and charges brought against me. Besides, I asked who my accuser was, and I appealed against my seizure and imprisonment; and when I had asked him for copies of all these records, he promised to see to it for me. But after much talk he said that he had come to testify that the inquisitor and the others had been appointed by the King, and that I must answer them about my faith. Asked again, I said that I believed all those things which the holy Church holds as true faith: that I believe in God the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth, and in Jesus Christ his only Son our Lord, conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, etc. I believe also in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church, the communion of saints, etc.

units.la: Tum vero illi instabant vt dicerem Ecclesiam Romanam. quibus ego Num,inquam,satis est dicere Ecclesiam catholicam vt nulla fiat mentio cuiusquam alterius,quam ego non agnoscam? Quaesiuerunt,quae ego intelligerem Sanctorum communionem,respondi,eam communitatem omnium fidelium,qui coniuncti fide,ita vnum corpus efficiunt vt Iesum Christum habeant:quemadmodum ait Paulus,Calix benedictionis,cui benedicimus,nonne corporis Iesu Christi communio est? nos quidem certè multi vnum corpus sumus,cùm vnius panis simus participes. Ex eo progressi sunt ad manducationem carnis & sanguinis Domini. de qua interrogatus,respondi eam spiritualem esse sicut ipse dicit se panem vitæ esse, qui de cælo descendit. qui ad eum venit, non esurire nec sitire. i. qui in eum credit. panem quem daturus esset, carnem suam esse, quam pro mundi vita traderet. Item, carnem suã vere esse cibum, & sanguinem vere esse potum. qui edit ipsius carnem ac sanguinem bibit, manere in eo, & ipsum in eo. Idem declarat etiam verba Christi quibus Cœnam instituit, quæ ab Euangelistis, atque à Paulo commemorata ostendunt verum Cœnæ usum spiritualem esse, eúmque ad salutarem animarum refectionem & gratiarum actionem esse referendum. Tum illi, Num credis, inquiunt, corpus & sanguinem Iesu Christi in pane esse, & postquam sacerdos eum consecrauit, verè ac certo ibi loco contineri? Panis, inquam, & vinum nobis vt signa & verba ad infirmitatem nostram adiuuandam data sunt, neque verò mentes nostræ defatigandæ sunt in his elementis quæ cernuntur, sed in cælum erigendæ, quò Christus ascendit, eóque corpus suum omni gloria ornatum extulit: neque inde ante ad nos est reuersurus, quàm ad iudicandum vivos & mortuos veniat.
units.tr: Then indeed they pressed me to say "the Roman Church." To them I said: "Is it not enough to say the catholic Church, without any mention of some other church which I do not acknowledge?" They asked what I understood by the communion of saints. I answered that it is the fellowship of all the faithful, who, joined together in faith, form one body so that they have Jesus Christ; as Paul says, "The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? For we being many are one bread, one body, for we are all partakers of that one bread." From there they moved on to the eating of the flesh and blood of the Lord. Asked about this, I replied that it is spiritual, just as he himself says that he is the bread of life which came down from heaven: he who comes to him will not hunger or thirst, that is, he who believes in him. The bread which he was to give was his flesh, which he would give for the life of the world. Likewise, his flesh is truly food and his blood truly drink; he who eats his flesh and drinks his blood abides in him, and he in him. The same is shown by the words of Christ by which he instituted the Supper, which are recorded by the Evangelists and by Paul: they show that the true use of the Supper is spiritual, and that it is to be referred to the salutary refreshment of souls and to thanksgiving. Then they said, "Do you believe that the body and blood of Jesus Christ are in the bread, and that after the priest has consecrated it, they are truly and certainly contained in that place?" I said, "Bread and wine have been given to us as signs and words to help our weakness. Our minds are not to be wearied with these elements which are seen, but raised up to heaven, where Christ ascended, and carried up his body adorned with all glory; and from there he will not return to us before he comes to judge the living and the dead."

units.la: Quid, inquiunt, de Missa credis? nego, inquam, à Iesu Christo institutam, aut aliud iam superesse nobis sacrificium cùm Christus suo perfunctus sit, quo vno cætera omnia sacrificia abolcuit. Neque etiam in Scriptura, vlla mentio Missæ fit: sed qui illam dicunt, iterum (quātū quidē in ipsis est) Filiū Dei crucifigunt. Quid, inquiunt, annon credis Papam caput esse ecclesiæ, qui indulgentias conferre possit? Ego inquam, Papam non agnosco, neque aliud in Ecclesia caput agnosco aut habeo præter Iesum Christum, cuius omnes fideles membra sunt. Postea cùm mecum multa alia loquuti essent, egerunt vt quæ ipsis responderam manu mea subsignarem. id quod feci, cùm ea mihi omnia interrogata & responsa recitassent, etsi non omnino ea scriberent quemadmodum ego dixeram.
units.tr: "What do you believe about the Mass?" they asked. I said that I deny it was instituted by Jesus Christ, and that no other sacrifice remains for us, since Christ has finished his own, by which single offering he abolished all other sacrifices. Nor is there any mention of the Mass in Scripture; those who call it a sacrifice crucify the Son of God again, so far as lies in them. "What then," they said, "do you not believe that the Pope is the head of the Church, who can grant indulgences?" I said that I do not acknowledge the Pope, nor do I acknowledge or have any head of the Church except Jesus Christ, of whom all the faithful are members. Afterwards, when they had said many other things to me, they urged me to sign with my hand what I had answered to them. I did so, after they had read out to me all the questions and my answers, although they did not write them down exactly as I had said them.

units.la: Die Sabbathi xxi. eius mensis redierunt ad me Suppræfectus, Officialis, atque Inquisitor, eo consilio & animo vt me interrogarent. A quibus postulau, vt mihi darent scripta ea capita, de quibus vellent fidè meã cognoscere, simúlque temporis spatium quo ad ea respondere posse. Id mihi nunquã concedere voluerũt. ego autè id ab illis propterea postulaui, quod cum vellem rationem fidei meae declarare, illi me in eo impediebant, dicebantque me officio concionatoris fungi velle: cum tamen illi quae a me dicta essent mendose scriberent. Haec Dymonetus.
units.tr: On Saturday the twenty-first of that month, the sub-prefect, the official and the inquisitor came back to me, with the intention and purpose of questioning me. I asked them to give me in writing the articles on which they wished to learn my faith, and at the same time a period of time in which I could answer them. They were never willing to grant me this. I asked for it for this reason: since I wished to set out the reasons for my faith, they hindered me in this, and said that I wished to take on the office of a preacher, although they themselves wrote down mistakenly what I had said. Thus Dymonetus.

units.la: Exemplum literarum, quas idem Dymonetus ad quendam amicum suum misit.
units.tr: A copy of the letter which the same Dymonetus sent to a certain friend of his.

units.la: Tsi amantissime frater & amice, ego saepe optaui dare ad te literas, quibus te & de meis rebus certiorem facerem & amater salutarem, nunquam tamen scribere potui duabus de causis impeditus, quarum altera fuit summa expectatio interrogationis atque responsionis meae, quam aduersarij non in longum tempus distulerunt. altera magna & varia tentatio, quam tum infirmitas carnis meae mihi attulit, tum etiam parentes mei & propinqui, qui nullam habent veritatis cognitionem: quorum quidem studio, opera, consilio diabolus magnopere est usus, ne regnum ipsius & Antichristi eius vicarij ulla in parte diminueretur: quod tamen nunc vehementer conquassatur ac labefactatur. Hoc autem ita habeto, eos nihil plane praetermisisse quod dici aut fieri posset ad auertendum miserum imbecillumque hominem, & impediendum quo minus sequeretur tam excellentem vocationem, atque tam praeclari operis functionem, ad quam Deus & Pater omnis misericordiae me delegit ac deduxit. Nam mihi una ex parte summa tormenta ipsamque mortem proponebant, ex altera parentum nostrorum ignominiam, dedecus, infamiam. His addebat maximam matris maestitiam, quam dicebant dolore moeroreque confectam mori: aliaque multa, quae longum esset scribere. quae quidem omnia mihi grauia & acerba ad tolerandum extitissent, nisi Dominus me Spiritu suo confirmasset, qui docet nobis matrem, uxorem, liberos, fratres, sorores, atque etiam vitam nostram relinquenda esse, ut sequamur optimum ducem nostrum Iesum Christum, atque pro eius causa dimicemus. Quamobrem ego vos saluto summa cum humilitate, & rogo ut Deum & Patrem Domini nostri Iesu Christi oretis ut mihi eam gratiam impertiat, ut ad extremum usque, constantiam fidei ac perseverantiam praestare possim, omnemque id in gloriam ipsius & in salutem nostram atque aedificationem Ecclesiae ita afflictae desolataeque redundet. Ego, charissime frater, mitto ad te exemplum eorum, quae ego interrogatus aduersariis respondi, ut vt extet apud te ea fidei meae confessio quam Dominus ad suam gloam à me ficri[?] voluit, pro ea exigua gratiae facultate quam ipse in me contulit: neque permisit, vt occultarem talentum quod mihi commisit & credidit vt illud multiplicem; quemadmodum tu quidè ex meis refponsis[?] videre poteris, in quibus exiguam doctrinam meam excusabis. neque enim diu est, ex quo Dominus me ad hanc sui cognitionem vocauit, atque ex densissimis tenebris & vmbra mortis eripuit, in qua maxima pars hominum depressa iacet. Dominus gratiam & pacem suam tibi impertiat. Frater noster Petrus Bergierus se etiam atque etiam vestris precibus commendat, sicut nos hoc in genere vos habemus commendatos, precésque pro vobis ad Deum cum benevolentia & charitate adhibemus. Matthaeus Dymonetus Evangelij nomine captiuus.
units.tr: Most loving brother and friend, I have often wished to send you a letter, to inform you of my affairs and to greet you lovingly, yet I could never write, being hindered for two reasons. The first was the great expectation of my questioning and answering, which my adversaries did not put off for long. The second was a great and varied temptation, brought on me partly by the weakness of my flesh, and partly by my parents and relatives, who have no knowledge of the truth. By their zeal, labour and counsel the devil has greatly used them, so that the kingdom of himself and of his vicar Antichrist might not be diminished in any part; yet now it is violently shaken and weakened. Know this, however: they have left nothing undone that could be said or done to turn away a wretched and weak man, and to prevent him from following so excellent a calling and so noble a work, to which God the Father of all mercy has chosen and led me. For on one side they set before me the greatest torments and death itself, and on the other the shame, disgrace and infamy of our parents. To these they added the greatest grief of my mother, whom they said would die worn out with sorrow and mourning, and many other things which would take long to write. All these would have been heavy and bitter for me to bear, had not the Lord strengthened me by his Spirit, who teaches us that mother, wife, children, brothers, sisters, and even our own life must be left behind, so that we may follow our best leader, Jesus Christ, and fight for his cause. Therefore I greet you with the greatest humility, and I ask you to pray to God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ that he would grant me the grace to show constancy and perseverance of faith to the very end, and that all this may redound to his glory, to the salvation of ourselves and the building up of the Church, so afflicted and desolate. I, most dear brother, am sending you a copy of the answers I gave to my adversaries when questioned, so that there may be with you that confession of my faith which the Lord willed to be made by me for his glory, according to the small measure of grace which he himself has bestowed on me. Nor has he allowed me to hide the talent which he entrusted to me and gave me that I might multiply it. You will be able to see this from my answers, in which you will excuse my meagre learning; for it is not long since the Lord called me to this knowledge of himself and snatched me from the thickest darkness and the shadow of death, in which the greater part of mankind lies oppressed. The Lord grant you his grace and peace. Our brother Peter Bergier commends himself again and again to your prayers, just as we too hold you commended in this way, and we offer prayers for you to God with goodwill and charity. Matthew Dymonetus, a prisoner for the sake of the Gospel.

units.la: Epistola Ioannis Caluini ad eundem missa.
units.tr: Letter of John Calvin sent to the same man.

units.la: ETsi charissime frater, mihi hoc quidem tempore id certamen suscipiendum non sit, in quo tu nunc versaris: spero tamen & confido te hanc meam exhortationem non minus libenter accepturum quàm si ego tecum captiuus essem. Neque studium ad te scribendi aliunde fuit profectum, aut re alia incitatum, quàm ea communione ac societate, quae nobis cum Christo, atque eius Euangelio, membrisque eiusdem omnibus ita constituta est vt omnes & consolationes & afflictiones communes habeamus & sentiamus. Magnopere autem te hortor & rogo, vt eam suscipias cogitationem, qua te in voluntatem optimi Patris caelestis totum permittas, qui vnumquemque nostrum ad eum ordinem ac locum, ad quem ei videtur, vocare solet. Interdum filijs suis paterne indulget, quoad illos ita tractatos, quasi longa manu ad id quod vult plane conformauerit. quemadmodum audimus Petro ore magni Magistri dictum esse, Cùm consenueris, te eô quô nolles ducet.
units.tr: Although, dearest brother, I am not now required to take up that contest in which you are engaged, I hope and trust that you will receive this exhortation of mine no less gladly than if I were a prisoner beside you. Nor has my eagerness to write to you arisen from any other source or been prompted by any other cause than that fellowship and union which has been established between us, Christ, his Gospel, and all his members, so that we all share and feel both consolations and afflictions in common. I urge and beg you especially to take up that thought by which you commit yourself wholly to the will of the best heavenly Father, who is accustomed to call each of us to that rank and place which seems good to him. Sometimes he indulges his sons as a father does, and yet, when he has so handled them, he has plainly shaped them to what he wills, as we hear it was said to Peter by the mouth of the great Master: "When you are old, you will be led where you do not wish to go." [John 21:18]

units.la: Interdum accidit vt tyrones rudésque accipiat, eos quidem certè qui in hoc certaminum genere non magnopere ac longo tempore exercitati fuerant. Vtcunque sit, hoc quidem inest boni, quòd is non minus potens est ad declarandam exhibendámq; virtutem in hominibus infirmis ac debilibus vt eos moneto[?] temporis inuictos reddat, quàm ad eandem continuandam in iis, qui iandiu ea senserunt. Neque enim tu, quemadmodū intelligo, ē numero eorū es, qui in primis ad agnitionem ipsius Dei vocati sunt: sed tamen Deus te in medium producat, ut testis ipsius sis. In prima autem hostilique aggressione Dominus huiusmodi virtutem & constantiam tibi dedit, ut inimici veritatis facile in te agnouerint eam Iesu Christi notam, quam ipsi ferre nullo modo possunt. Neque vero ignoro, sed pro mea singulari erga te beneuolentia ac [illegible, ~9 letters], quam tibi debeo, plane sentio eos nouos impetus quos inimicus satha in te facit: sed oportet confugere ad eum, qui iam tam praeclarè coepit, eumque orare ut opus in te suum perficiat. Si tu sustines multas & magnas tentationes, id non debes admirari, etiamsi tantam sentias in teipso fragilitatem, ut quodammodo vacillare videaris. Quin potius cognosce te hac ratione a Deo humiliari, ut eius auxilium in necessitate melius perspiciatur. deinde ut tu hoc modo ad inuocandum eius nomen magis magisque soliciteris, eoque adducaris, ut ad eius unius gratiam atque opem omne tuum perfugium abeas, quemadmodū necesse est ut vi quadam nos eò compellamur. Nec vero dubito quin extrinseci huiusmodi homines adhibeantur, qui ad accendendum ignem faces subiiciant, qui praetextu quidem amicitiae ac propinquitatis erunt tibi infestissimi omnium, & maximè capitales inimici. Ut enim corpus conferuent, id agent, quantum quidem in ipsis erit, ut animam in exitium coniciant. Accedit bis, quod in ingenio humano huiusmodi est officina salacium opinionum & cogitationum, quae nullam aliam vim habent quam ut perturbent eam quietem quam nos in sancta Dei nostri vocatione habere debemus. Is autem nobis praecipit, ut auersi a caeteris omnibus rebus, in ipsum unum, quemadmodum est aequum, oculos nostros coniiciamus, eumque solum respiciamus. Quare opus est ad omnem vim repellendam, ut tu omni ex parte armatus ac munitus sis. Neque vero vlla causa est cur consterneris, cum Deus promiserit se suos ita armaturum, ut eos Satan aggredi vercatur. Tantummodo te eius fidei virtutique committe, ac diffidens tibiipsi omnibusque tuis viribus, spera & confide eum ad te tuendū vim satis magnam habituru. Caeterum duo tibi imprimis sunt spectanda. primum, quae causa est ea quam tu defendis. deinde quae gloriae corona proposita est iis, qui in confessione Euangelij se constanter gesserint. Est enim tota ratio cultus Dei & gratia quã nobis in Christo declarauit, totáq; regni ipsius gloria, res adeò præclara ac pretiosa, vt mortalis homo nõ molestè gra uitérq; ferre debeat, si vitá impendat suã ad dimicandũ contra omnes corruptelas quæ in mũdum introductæ, ad ea quæ proposuimus abolenda summã vim habent. Deinde, nos scimus quis exitus omniũ certaminũ nostrorũ futurus est, & quòd is à quo sumus redempti, nunquã patietur vt tantũ pretium, quantũ est sanguinis ipsius pro nobis effusi, vnquã pereat: cũ nos eius signum in animis nostris vitáque impressũ habuerimus. Nos autem scimus, quos profuis recognoscat, ac testatur se in nouissimo die recogniturum, eos nimirum omnes qui eum in hoc mundo confessi fuerunt. Nondum quidẽ nobis notum est quid is de te constituerit: sed nihil omnino melius est, quàm vitam te ei tuam in sacrificium offerre, paratum eam linquere cum ipse voluerit: sperare tamen illum tandiu eam conseruaturum, quandiu ad salutem tuam pertinere iudicabit. Hoc autem quànuis sit carni difficile ac graue, est tamen eiusmodi vt in eo pij ac fideles homines possint conquiescere. Ac oranda est tibi optimus benignissimúsque Deus, vt id in corde tuo ira imprimat, vt nunquam ex eo deleri possit. Nos quidem pro nostro officio cum oramus, vt eam vim virtutis suæ in animo tuo efficiat, cúmque ira afficiat, vt plane persuasus esse possis, te sub tutela eius esse: idémque furorem inimicorum tuorum reprimat, séque omnibus in rebus Deum tuum ac Patrem ostendat. Quoniam autem intelligo Petrum Bergierum in eodem carcere tecum esse, te rogo, vt ei ex me plurimum salutis dicas, cum eóque has literas communices. pergamus semper, donec ad metam nobis constitutam peruenianus, atque in regnum æternum recolligamur.
units.tr: Sometimes it happens that he takes on novices and beginners, at least those who have not been trained for long in this kind of conflict. However that may be, this much good is present: he is no less able to show and display his power in weak and feeble men, so as to make them unconquered in time of ..., than he is to keep it going in those who have long experienced it. For, as I understand it, you are not, indeed, among those who were first called to the knowledge of God himself; but God nevertheless brings you forward into the midst so that you may be his witness. In the first hostile assault, the Lord gave you this kind of courage and steadfastness, so that the enemies of the truth readily recognised in you that mark of Jesus Christ which they can by no means bear. Nor indeed am I unaware, but out of my singular goodwill towards you and [illegible, about nine letters], which I owe you, I clearly feel those new assaults which the enemy Satan makes upon you. But we must flee to him who has so splendidly begun, and pray him to bring his work in you to completion. If you endure many and great temptations, you ought not to wonder at this, even if you feel in yourself such frailty that you seem in some measure to waver. Rather, recognise that by this means you are humbled by God, so that his help may be better seen in your need, and so that in this way you may be more and more anxious to call upon his name, and be brought to flee with all your refuge to the grace and help of him alone, just as we must be driven to it by a certain force. Nor do I doubt that men of this outward sort will be employed, who will heap on the fuel to kindle the fire; under the pretext of friendship and kinship they will be most hostile to you of all, and the chief enemies. For while they preserve the body, they will do what lies in their power to cast the soul into ruin. Besides this, there is in the human mind a workshop of such lewd opinions and thoughts, which have no other force than to disturb that quiet which we ought to have in the holy calling of our God. He, however, commands us, turning away from all other things, to fix our eyes upon him alone, as is right, and to look to him only. Therefore, to repel every force, it is necessary that you be armed and fortified on every side. Nor indeed is there any cause for you to be dismayed, since God has promised that he will so arm his own that Satan dares not attack them. Only commit yourself to his faithfulness and power, and, distrusting yourself and all your own strength, hope and trust that he will have force enough to defend you. Moreover, there are two things above all which you should keep in view: first, what the cause is that you defend; then, what crown of glory is set before those who have conducted themselves steadfastly in the confession of the Gospel. For the whole worship of God and the grace which he has declared to us in Christ, and all the glory of his kingdom, are a matter so excellent and precious that a mortal man ought not to bear it grudgingly or heavily if he lays down his life to fight against all the corruptions introduced into the world, which have the greatest power to hinder the abolition of those things we have put forward. Furthermore, we know what the outcome of all our struggles will be, and that he by whom we have been redeemed will never allow so great a price, as is the blood poured out for us, ever to perish, since we have borne his mark impressed upon our minds and lives. Yet we know that those whom he has acknowledged as his own, he will also acknowledge and bear witness to on the last day, namely all those who have confessed him in this world. It is not yet known to us what he has decided concerning you; but nothing at all is better than for you to offer your life to him as a sacrifice, ready to leave it whenever he wishes, yet to hope that he will keep it for as long as he judges it to pertain to your salvation. This, although it is hard and grievous to the flesh, is nevertheless of such a kind that pious and faithful men can rest in it. And you must pray to the best and most kind God that he will so impress this upon your heart that it can never be erased from it. For our part, as is our duty, we pray that he may work in your mind that power of his virtue, and so fill you with it that you may be fully persuaded that you are under his protection, and that he may restrain the rage of your enemies, and show himself to you as your God and Father in all things. Since I understand that Peter Bergier is in the same prison with you, I ask you to convey my warmest greetings to him, and to share this letter with him. Let us always press on until we reach the goal set before us, and are gathered into the eternal kingdom.

units.la: Vnũ ego oblitus eram te monere, vt inimicis pro ea fidei mensura, quã Dominus tibi dedit, modestè reuerétérq; respõdeas, hoc autè propterea dico, quòd facultas subtiliter accuratéq; disputandi nõ omnibus cõceßa & data est. Neq; etiã martyres magnopere eruditi ac subtiles extiterúnt, vt in aliquas difficiles obscuráq; disputationes quæstionesq; ingrederetur. Ita tu modeste te subnuttes [?] gubernationi Spiritus Dei, cum omni sobrietate ac moderatione respónde, consciuans eã Scripturæ regulam, Credidi, propterea loquar. Neque tamen impediat, quo minus tu libere atque integre loquaris, hoc plane statuens, cum qui promisit se nobis daturum os & huiusmodi sapientia, cui aduersarij resistere non potuerunt, tibi nunquam defuturum.
units.tr: There is one thing I forgot to remind you of: that you answer your enemies modestly and reverently, in proportion to the measure of faith which the Lord has given you. I say this because the ability to dispute subtly and precisely has not been granted and given to everyone. Nor indeed were the martyrs very learned and subtle, so as to enter into difficult and obscure disputations and questions. So, submitting yourself with humility to the guidance of the Spirit of God, answer with all sobriety and moderation, keeping before you that rule of Scripture: "I believed, and therefore I have spoken." [2 Cor. 4:13, from Ps. 116:10] Yet let nothing hinder you from speaking freely and completely, clearly settling this in your mind: that he who has promised to give us a mouth and such wisdom that our adversaries cannot resist will never fail you.

units.la: Altera epistola Ioan. Cal. missa ad eos captiuos pro verbo Dei, quorum mentio paulo ante facta est.
units.tr: The second letter of John Calvin, sent to those prisoners for the word of God whom he mentioned a little earlier.

units.la: Harissimi fratres, nos cum intellexissemus quid inimici veritatis de causa vestra concluserint, atque statuerint: in maiore animi dolore, cura ac solicitudine, quàm unquam antea, versatisumus[?]. Cùm autem is dominus, quem vos non ignoratis, hàc transiret, dum prauderet, ne eius discessum retardarem, confeci celeriter eam literarum formam, quae mihi ad scribendum accommodata & utilis esse videbatur. Deus autem tam nobis quàm caeteris suis omnibus dedit aliquod spatium respirandi. Nos quidem eum exitum expectamus[?], quem ipse dare voluerit, eumq; semper oramus ut vos manu valida prehensos tueatur, neque permittat ut unquam deficiatis, denique vos in sua tutela custodiaque perpetuo habeat. Equidem mihi plane persuasi nullam vim tantam futuram, quae eam virtutem, quam ille in vos cõtulit, commoveat aut labefactet. Vos quidem iandiu ante praemeditati estis illud postrenum certamen, quod subituri estis, si optimus Deus vos eo deducere voluerit. quin etiam hactenus pro sancto eius nomine ita dimicastis, ut longus iam usus obfirmare potuerit, ut quod restat, omni animi studio persequamini. Qua in re fieri non potest quin aliquos fragilitatis vestros aculeos sentiatis. Sed cõfidite cū cui seruitis, ita in cordibus vestris per Spiritum sanctum suum dominaturū, ut eius gratia fit omnes tentationes superatura. Etenim si is promisit se eos in patientia cōfirmaturū, qui pro suis peccatis aliquas castigationes patiũtur, quomodo ijs unquam deerit qui pro sua causa affligũtur, quorumq; opera & vita in re tam sancta ac praeclara utitur ut testes veritatis ipsius cōstituantur? Itaq; memoria tenete, quod is qui habitat in vobis, mũdo fortior ac potentior est. Nos officium nostrum praestabimus, eum orando ut nomen eius vestra constantia fiat illustrius ac gloriosius, consolationeq; eius Spiritus mitigetur atq; amabile reddatur quicquid carni amarū est: itaque sensus ad se vestros rapiat, ut intuentes coronā illā caelestē, sitis parati quicquid est nudi abijcere. Ego accepi quandam chartam, in qua subtilia argumenta continentur illius miserrimi ac stolidissimi hominis Orrii, quibus probare vult, licere idola ac simulachra facere. Atqui nescio, an vos eam mihi miseritis et an me ci respondere vultis, quae fuit causa ut nihil in eo attingere voluerim, cum de voluntate vestra mihi plane non constaret. Illud quidem ego existimo vos non magnopere ea responsione indigere. Sed si eam desideraveritis, mittam vobis per eum qui primus ad vos proficiscetur. Ego fratres, Deum nostrum benignissimum oro ut vos in sua protectione perpetuo retineat, omnibus in rebus adiuuet, efficiatque ut ipsum reipsa atque experientia patrem vestrum esse sentiatis, ac plane cognoscatis quam pretiosam et charam salutem suorum habeat. Me autem vestris precibus etiam atq; etiam commendo. VII. Mart. M.D.LIII.
units.tr: Most dear brothers, when we learned what the enemies of the truth have concluded and decided concerning your cause, we were in greater grief of mind, care and anxiety than ever before. But since that gentleman, whom you know, was passing through here and was about to leave, I did not want to delay his departure, so I quickly drew up this form of letter, which seemed to me suitable and useful for writing. God has given us, as he has given all his people, some space to breathe. We indeed await the outcome which he himself wishes to give, and we always pray that he will protect you, holding you with a strong hand, will never allow you to fail, and will keep you in his care and custody forever. I am fully persuaded that no force will be great enough to shake or weaken the courage which he has bestowed upon you. You have long since considered that final struggle which you are to undergo, if the best God wishes to lead you to it. Indeed, so far you have fought for his holy name in such a way that long practice may have strengthened you, so that you should pursue what remains with all your zeal. In this matter it cannot be that you do not feel some stings of your frailty. But trust in him whom you serve: he will so reign in your hearts through his Holy Spirit that by his grace he will overcome all temptations. For if he has promised to strengthen in patience those who suffer some chastisement for their sins, how will he ever be wanting to those who suffer for his cause, and whose work and life are used in so holy and noble a matter that they are set up as witnesses of his truth? Therefore keep in memory that he who dwells in you is stronger and mightier than the world. We will do our part, praying that his name may become more illustrious and glorious through your steadfastness, and that his consolation may soften and make sweet whatever is bitter to the flesh; so may he draw your senses to himself, so that, gazing upon that heavenly crown, you may be ready to cast off whatever is worldly. I have received a certain paper, containing subtle arguments of that most wretched and foolish man Orrius, by which he wishes to prove that it is lawful to make idols and images. But I do not know whether you have sent it to me, or whether you wish me to answer it; this was the reason I chose to touch on nothing in it, since I was not clearly sure of your wish. Indeed I think you have no great need of such a reply. But if you desire it, I will send it to you by the one who sets out first to you. I pray, brothers, to our most kind God, that he keep you forever in his protection, help you in all things, and bring it about that you feel him in very deed and experience to be your Father, and clearly know how precious and dear a salvation he holds for his own. I commend myself to your prayers again and again. 7 March 1553.

units.la: Sed ad Dymonetum redeamus: in quo quidem facile perspici potest, quemadmodum Deus electos suos ad se exiguo temporis spatio et momento attrahat. Ille enim qui paulo ante ad cognitionem Evangelij adductus fuerat, cuiusque nomine in carcerem coniectus, cum ibi acerrimos impetus parentū ac iudicū, qui incolumitate proposita eum a fidei proposito volebat abducere, constanter repulisset, ad ultimum supplicium ductus est, die Sabbathi, XV. Iul. M.D.LIII. Ibi autem cum esset, multa populo demonstrauit, imprimisque impium Missae Purgatoriiq; abusum: ita ut placide et summo cum silentio ab omnibus auditus fuerit. Deinde laetus invocans semper Domini nomen, genus mortis vsitatum summa animi aequitate et patientia perpessus est.
units.tr: But let us return to Dymonetus, in whom it can easily be seen how God draws his elect to himself in a short space of time and in a moment. For he who had a little before been brought to the knowledge of the Gospel, and on whose account he had been cast into prison, when there constantly repelled the fiercest assaults of his parents and the judges, who, holding out his safety, wished to lead him away from his purpose of faith, was led to the final punishment on the Sabbath day, 15 July 1553. While he was there, he showed much to the people, and above all the impious abuse of the Mass and of Purgatory, so that he was heard calmly and in the greatest silence by everyone. Then, joyfully calling always upon the name of the Lord, he underwent the usual kind of death with the greatest equanimity and patience.

units.la: Liber septimus Actionū MARTYRVM.
units.tr: The Seventh Book of the Acts and Monuments of the Martyrs.

units.la: GVLIELMVS NEEL.
units.tr: WILLIAM NEEL.

units.la: PRAETER caeteros praestantes pietate viros, qui fidelibus Northmaniae cum doctrinae syncerit-tate tum vitae integritate praeluxerunt, egregie[?] extitit Dei seruus Gulielmus Neelus: qui sectae an-tea Augustinianae monachus, postea quam cognitione veritatis donatus fuisset, non destitit omnibus quibuscunque fieri possct, modis docere atque promulgare Euangelium Filij Dei. Quodā itaque die Rothomago, cuius urbis civis erat, discedens, trāsiit per oppidum Aurincense, quúmque venisset ad pagum quendam cui nomen erat Nonancurtum, in diversorium se recepit ut vires cibo atque potu reficeret, ibi reperiens plures sacrificos qui se vino ingurgitabant, multáque indecorè effœminatéq; fecerant: hos benevolè reprehendit atque instituit, quemadmodum passim per hospitia ipsum fecisse cōstat.
units.tr: Among the other men of outstanding piety who shone among the faithful of Normandy, both for the purity of their doctrine and the integrity of their lives, the servant of God William Neel stood out eminently. Once a monk of the Augustinian order, he was granted the knowledge of the truth, and from then on he did not cease to teach and proclaim the Gospel of the Son of God by every means he could. On a certain day he was leaving Rouen, the city of which he was a citizen, and passed through the town of Aurinc. When he came to a village called Nonancourt, he lodged at an inn to refresh his strength with food and drink. There he found several priests who were drinking themselves full of wine and had done many shameful and effeminate things. He rebuked them kindly and instructed them, as it is well known he did in inns everywhere.

units.la: Quum autem videret istos sacerdotes adeo impunè metas honestatis transfilire, non solum mores eorum impuros, sed etiam doctrinam infectatus est. Quod ægreferēs Decanus Ilerensis qui aderat, dictus vulgò Legoux, huc mox coprehendi iussit, Aurincúq; deduci: quo in loco in carcere Episcopi coniectus fuit, atq; de fide primum interrogatus per Pœnitentiarium Aurincensem M. Simonem Vigorem, hominem eruditū: qui libros eorum qui purè de religione Christiana scripserūt legit, sed variis tum honorum tum pecuniæ studijs distrahitur: nec tamē veritatis hostis aut persecutor haberi nec dici vult.
units.tr: When he saw that these priests so easily overstepped the bounds of decency, he attacked not only their impure morals but also their doctrine. The dean of Ilyers, who was present and was commonly called Legoux, took this badly and at once ordered him to be seized and taken to Aurinc. There he was thrown into the bishop's prison, and was first questioned about his faith by the penitentiary of Aurinc, Master Simon Vigor, a learned man. He had read the books of those who had written purely about the Christian religion, but he was distracted by various pursuits of honours and money. Yet he did not wish to be regarded or called an enemy or persecutor of the truth.

units.la: Neelus coram hoc pœnitentiario veritatem confessus est non modò in omnibus articulis qui proponebantur: verumetiam eos quos Papistæ mordicus defendunt, authoritate Scripturæ confutaut. Idque toto Quadragesimæ tempore singulis ferè diebus fecit, quo quidem tempore Pœnitentiarius ille, animum Neeli variis disputationibus labefactare studuit: sed frustra tamen: nam iste constanter usque in finem veritatis partes tuitus est.
units.tr: Neel confessed the truth before this penitentiary, not only on all the articles that were put to him, but also confuted with the authority of Scripture those which the Papists stubbornly defend. He did this on nearly every day of the whole of Lent. In that time the penitentiary tried by various disputations to shake Neel's resolve, but in vain; for Neel held constantly to the side of the truth until the end.

units.la: Sæpenumerò Pœnitentiarius eum monebat, & blandè admodum hortabatur ut se revocaret, vitæ incolumitatem illi promittens. Cùm disquisitioni interesset aliquando Episcopus Aurincensis, nec apud Neelum proficeret quicquam Pœnitentiarius: Mi amice, aiebat hic, caue verbo ullo tuam conscientiam læseris.
units.tr: The penitentiary often warned him, and urged him very kindly to recant, promising him safety of life. Once when the bishop of Aurinc was present at the examination, and the penitentiary had made no progress with Neel, the bishop said: "My friend, take care not to wound your conscience with any word."

units.la: Tandem post multas percontationes (ut tergiversationis & fuci quo Pœnitentiarius veritatem occultare conabatur, ansam tolleret) Neelus postulauit sibi dari potestatem mandandi chartæ quicquid de religione sentiret. Pœnitentiarius non recusauit, sed illi certos dies præscribi optauit quibus suam sententiam de religione describeret. Neelus itaque hanc nactus opportunitatem, diligenter præcipuos articulos de quibus antea disputatum erat, papyro commisit. Ac primùm de Sacramento altaris, quod vocat, interterrogatus scripsit in hanc rationem.
units.tr: At last, after many questionings (so as to remove the occasion of the evasion and deceit by which the penitentiary tried to hide the truth), Neel asked that he be given permission to commit to paper whatever he thought about religion. The penitentiary did not refuse, but wished certain days to be set for him in which to write down his opinion of religion. Neel, therefore, seizing this opportunity, carefully committed to paper the main articles about which he had been disputing earlier. And first, questioned about the sacrament of the altar, as they call it, he wrote as follows.

units.la: Vera Cænæ institutio est eiusmodi: Iesus Christus accepit panem, undéque fregit, & postquam gratias egisset, dixit, Accipite, hoc est corpus meum quod pro vobis tradetur. facite hoc in mei memoriam. Idem de calice dixit, Prehedite[?], sumite omnes: hic est sanguis meº qui pro multis effundetur in remissionem peccatorum. Horum nos verborum expendere oportet vim atque dignitatem. nam quo maior & præstantior res est, eo curandum est diligentius ut integra & syncera conserentur[?] néue quo modo corrumpatur. Iesus autem instituit & dedit Ecclesiæ conseruandum sacramentum, ut meminerit sese redemptam à morte peccati per sacrificium corporis illius: quemadmodum ait Apostolus quòd seipsum obtulerit semel, nec amplius morietur. Consideremus igitur hæc attentius, ut in memoria habeamus, eum effudisse suum sanguinem, quem obtulit Deo Patri in remissionem peccatorum Ecclesiæ suæ semel, ut in perpetuum eam saluam faceret. In hac sacra Cœna Christus se magistrum, Ecclesia verò ancillam exhibet: nimirum ut palàm fiat ei deberi obedientiam, & quicquid præceperit præstetur. ut par est magistrum imperare, seruum parere & facere quod ille præceperit. Deinde idem Christus se sponsum Ecclesiæ declarat, quam singulari ductus amore sponsam sibi ascisçit legitimam: officium autem fidelis sponsæ est consentire, & quod sponso placuerit præstare ipsa debet: alioqui non rectè fidelis, humilis ac docilis, sed contrà fœdifraga, superba & contumax iure dicetur. Præterea Christus hac in Cœna patris officio fungitur, quod est alere suos filios: dum scilicet corpus & sanguinem (quorum symbola sunt panis & vinum) præbet, qui cibus est incorruptus atque æternus. Dictum est quòd acceperit panem ac vinum, dicendo, Hoc est corpus meum & sanguis meus, cõedite & bibite omnes: quibus verbis instruere voluit suos discipulos quorum ignorantiam & tarditatem ingenij probè callebat. quos quum ea quæ carnis sunt saperet magis quàm quæ Spiritus, cùm sæpè aliàs reprehendit, tum etiam quum loqueretur de cibis: ea nempe quæ per os intrant non inquinare animam. præterea quum similitudinem serentis & alia ipsis ob oculos poneret, quæ capere non poterant. nec reuera fieri potest ut qui sumus animales, spiritualia intelligamus, nisi Deº qui Spiritus est, mentis oculos nobis aperiat ut ea quæ spiritus sunt dignoscamus. quod satis liquet exemplo Nicodemi qui licet insignis nomodidascalus esset, tamen verba Christi percipere nequiuit, Quod qui regnum cælorum ingredi vellet, eum iterum nasci oporteret. Dominus itaque imbecillitatis nostræ rationem habens, in Cœna sua proponit ea quæ & oculis videri & manibus tangi queant, ut nobis detur notitiam rei quæ visu minime percipitur, quæque in animis nostris habitat, animásque nostras nutrit, corporis scilicet & sanguinis sui, quæ nullis externis sensibus, sed spiritualiter tantum percipi possunt. Proinde omnino viva fide opus est: alioqui non vita sed altera mors est. Nunc autem videamus quomodo Christus se Magistrum, Sponsum & Patrem exhibeat his verbis, Accipite & comedite: hoc est corpus meum. Quicunque Christi servus obsequens & discipulus, filius aut uxor esse vult, necesse est sumat, comedat corpus eius, & sanguine eius bibat. non quidem ex opinione Scribarum & Pharisæorum ut dentibus conterant, atque in stomachum trajiciant, quo modo caro edi & vinum bibi solent: de quo postea latius. nunc autem studiose dictum & præceptum Iesu Christi inspiciamus, ne forte quis hallucinetur: Christus exhibens panem, demonstrabat corpus suum panem esse cælestem qui solus animas pascit, ut panis materialis corpus tantummodo nutrire potest: præbens deinde vinum, significabat sanguinem suum esse potum animæ laborantis sití quam ex æstu peccatorum contrahit. Sanguis enim Christi reficit nos & recreat, dum peccatum pellit, animam accendit bono zelo & affectu, haud secius quàm vinum sitim restinguit, corpusque totum calefacit, oblectat atq; firmius reddit. Hæc autem nobis in animo cogitanda sunt, quando panem & vinum in Cœna nostris oculis cernimus: quibus indigne vescimur, nisi erigamus mentem ad ea quæ nobis offert Christus, corpus videlicet & sanguinem suum in pastum spiritualem. neq; enim anima eo quo corpus nostrum pane materiali sustentatur, quoniam ipsa spiritus est. Itaq; dixi Christo parendum ob causas suprà dictas, qui ait, Accipite, comedite: non autem, Prehendite corpus meum & ex eo sacrificium facite ad remissionem peccatorum, ac deinde ipsum comedite: id profectò veteres Legis ceremonias referret, quum Presbyteri & Sacrificatores oblatas Deo victimas quasdam edebant ipsi, alias adolebat, nonnullas dimittebat: in quo figura extabat sacrificij quod Christus corpore suo fecit ad plenam atque perfectam omnium fidelium salutem. & quia sacrificium, quod Christus semel fecit, aeternum est, quo servat electos non in hoc seculo tantum, sed in vitam aeternam restituit: Christianorum est accipere, comedere, non autem offerre: siquidem Christus seipsum obtulit, qui non corpus nostrum & vētrem sed animam pascit. proinde talem ipsum comprehendamus qualem se nobis praestat, & ne fraudemus spiritum suo pabulo quod fide sumit. Commendemus autem animam cum corpore Patri per dilectum eius Filium qui suo sacrificio semel plenè ei satisfecit pro omnibus peccatis nostris, quorum non recordabitur in aeternum. nam accepto hoc sacrificio, nos simul pro iustis in gratiam recepit, adeo ut Christus cum corpus suum & sanguinem dedit quo nos reficeret, sua & se totum nobis tradiderit qui peccatorum nostrorum reatum subijt. Itaque ipse qui iustus est, ac gratus Deo Patri suo, nos quoque iustos & acceptos Deo Patri suo & per eundem nostro, effecit: cui gloria & honor in secula, Amen.
units.tr: The true institution of the Lord's Supper is of this kind: Jesus Christ took bread, broke it, and after giving thanks said: Take, eat; this is my body, which will be given for you; do this in remembrance of me. He said the same about the cup: Drink, all of you; this is my blood, which will be poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. We ought to weigh the force and dignity of these words. For the greater and more excellent the thing is, the more diligently we must take care that it is handed on whole and pure and is not corrupted in any way. Jesus, moreover, instituted and gave to the Church the sacrament to be kept, so that she might remember that she was redeemed from the death of sin through the sacrifice of that body; as the Apostle says, that he offered himself once, and dies no more. Let us therefore consider these things more attentively, so that we may keep in mind that he shed his blood, which he offered once to God the Father for the forgiveness of sins, so that he might keep his Church safe forever. In this holy Supper Christ presents himself as Master, and the Church as handmaid: plainly so that it is evident that obedience is owed to him, and whatever he has commanded is to be performed; as it is right that the master commands, and the servant obeys and does what he has ordered. Then the same Christ declares himself the Bridegroom of the Church, whom, moved by singular love, he has taken as his lawful bride; but the duty of a faithful bride is to consent and to perform what pleases her bridegroom, otherwise she will rightly be called not faithful, humble and teachable, but on the contrary faithless to her vow, proud and obstinate. Besides, Christ in this Supper performs the office of a Father, which is to feed his sons, while he gives his body and blood (of which bread and wine are the signs), which is incorruptible and eternal food. It has been said that he took bread and wine, saying: "This is my body and my blood; eat and drink, all of you." With these words he wished to instruct his disciples, whose ignorance and dullness of mind he knew well. Since they savoured the things of the flesh more than the things of the Spirit, he rebuked them often at other times, and also when he spoke about foods, namely that the things which enter through the mouth do not defile the soul. Moreover, when he set before their eyes the likeness of the sower and other things which they could not grasp. Indeed, it cannot happen that we, who are natural men, understand spiritual things, unless he who is Spirit opens the eyes of our mind, so that we may discern the things that are of the Spirit. This is clear enough from the example of Nicodemus, who, although he was a distinguished teacher of the law [νομοδιδάσκαλος], could not grasp the words of Christ, that one who wished to enter the kingdom of heaven must be born again. The Lord, therefore, mindful of our weakness, in his Supper sets before us things that can be seen with the eyes and touched with the hands, so that knowledge of a thing that is not perceived by sight is given to us: that is, of his body and blood, which dwell in our souls and nourish them, and which can be perceived by no outward senses, but only spiritually. Therefore a truly living faith is altogether necessary; otherwise it is not life but another death. Now let us see how Christ presents himself as Master, Bridegroom and Father in these words: Take and eat; this is my body. Whoever wishes to be an obedient servant and disciple of Christ, a son or a bride, must take and eat his body and drink his blood. Not indeed in the opinion of the scribes and Pharisees, that they should grind it with their teeth and send it down into the stomach, as flesh is usually eaten and wine drunk; of which more later. But for now let us carefully consider the saying and command of Jesus Christ, lest anyone go astray. Christ, in offering the bread, showed that his body is the heavenly bread, which alone feeds souls, as material bread can nourish only the body; then, in giving the wine, he signified that his blood is the drink of a soul labouring with thirst, which it contracts from the heat of sins. For the blood of Christ restores and refreshes us, while it drives out sin, kindles the soul with good zeal and affection, just as wine quenches thirst, warms the whole body, delights and makes it stronger. These things, moreover, are to be thought of in our minds when we see the bread and wine in the Supper with our eyes; we would eat them unworthily unless we lift up our minds to what Christ offers us, namely his body and blood as spiritual food. For the soul is not sustained by material bread as our body is, since it is itself spirit. Therefore I have said that we must obey Christ for the reasons stated above, who says: Take, eat; not: "Seize my body, and from it make a sacrifice for the forgiveness of sins, and then eat it yourselves." That would indeed bring back the ceremonies of the old Law, when the priests and sacrificers ate some of the victims offered to God, burned others, and let some go; in which there was a figure of the sacrifice that Christ made by his body for the full and perfect salvation of all the faithful. And because the sacrifice which Christ made once is eternal, by which he keeps the elect not only in this age but restores them to eternal life, it is for Christians to receive and eat, not to offer; since Christ offered himself, who feeds not our body and belly but our soul. Therefore let us grasp him as he presents himself to us, and let us not cheat the spirit of its food, which it takes by faith. Let us commend our soul with our body to the Father through his beloved Son, who by his one sacrifice has fully satisfied him for all our sins, which he will remember no more forever. For, once this sacrifice is accepted, he receives us at the same time as just men into his favour, so much so that when Christ gave his body and blood to refresh us, he handed over to us his own self, wholly, he who bore the guilt of our sins. Therefore he himself, who is just and pleasing to God his Father, has also made us just and acceptable to God his Father, and through the same Son to ours; to whom be glory and honour for ever and ever. Amen.

units.la: Rogatus fuit annon crederet corpus Iesu Christi esse in sacramento altaris realiter & vere quemadmodum prodijt ex vtero Virginis Mariae, & postea in orbe concionatus est, idem qui comedit & bibit in Cœna, denique qui in cruce pependit: anne eo modo diceret in sacramento sumendum. Ad hoc ille respondit se nulla ratione induci posse ut ita crederet. id enim plane Scripturae ac fidei repugnare, in qua habemus Christum natum de Virgine, ubera matris suxisse: atque dum cōcionaretur, passum esse famem, sitim, calorem, frigus. tum etiam maledictioni crucis fuisse obnoxium, quia mortalis erat, nec adhuc resurrexerat. In hoc statu dum adhuc esset, nos etiam in morte manebamus: quandoquidem ut nos e faucibus mortis eriperet vitaeque restitueret, mori ipsum atque superata morte in vitam excitari oportuit. horrenda igitur haeresis est, quòd ita corpus Christi comedendum asseritis. Atqui si verum praedicaretis, error esset manifestus, quia eum mortuum & resusçitatum credimus corpore nunc immortali & glorioso frui. Confiteor quidem, inquit, ipsum in cœlis ad dexteram Dei Patris idem habere corpus quod e Virginis vtero extulit, immutatis tamen corporis qualitatibus, nec enim corpus comedimus quale sumpsit in utero Virginis, sed quale nunc residet ad dexteram Dei Patris: alioqui nullum esset in Ecclesia Sacramentum. nec enim Cœna nec Baptismus sacramenta censerentur, quorum vis omnis & efficacia in sanguine, morte & resurrectione Christi sita est. Proinde ipsorum opinionem dicebat merum esse Sathanæ commentum, eique se, quia pater est mendacij & omnis maledictionis, nullo pacto fidem adhibiturum.
units.tr: He was asked whether he believed that the body of Jesus Christ is in the sacrament of the altar really and truly, just as it came forth from the womb of the Virgin Mary, and afterwards preached in the world, the same body that ate and drank at the Supper and finally hung on the cross, and whether he would say that it is to be received in the sacrament in that way. To this he replied that he could not be brought by any reasoning to believe it so. For this plainly contradicts Scripture and the faith, in which we have Christ born of the Virgin, sucking his mother's breasts, and, while he preached, suffering hunger, thirst, heat and cold; and further, that he was subject to the curse of the cross because he was mortal and had not yet risen. While he was still in that state, we also remained in death, since, if he was to snatch us from the jaws of death and restore us to life, he had to die and, having overcome death, be raised to life. It is therefore a horrible heresy that you assert the body of Christ is to be eaten in this way. Indeed, if you preached the truth, the error would be manifest, because we believe that he, having died and been raised, now enjoys a body that is immortal and glorious. "I do confess," he said, "that in heaven, at the right hand of God the Father, he has the same body that he brought forth from the womb of the Virgin, but with its qualities changed; for we do not eat the body as he took it in the womb of the Virgin, but as it now sits at the right hand of God the Father. Otherwise there would be no sacrament in the Church, for neither the Supper nor Baptism would be counted sacraments, since all their power and efficacy lies in the blood, death and resurrection of Christ." Therefore he said that their opinion was a mere invention of Satan, and that he would by no means give it credence, since Satan is the father of lies and of every curse.

units.la: De purgatorio autem sic respondit, se ad extremum usque Spiritū confiteri ac tueri velle sanguinem Christi pro nobis effusum, solum & perfectum esse purgatorium, qui purgat filios Dei ab omnibus iniquitatibus. Idque probabat locis Scripturæ ad Hebr.i.v.vi. & Canonica Iacobi, ostendens Christianum simulac ex hac vita migraret, omnibus iam purgatum ac liberatum cruciatibus recta ingredi requiem quam primum anima ex corpore discesset. Scriptum est apud Ezechielem, Quo loco arbor ceciderit, in eo etiam manebit, id est, Si homo in gratia Domini nō moritur, manebit in loco omnis gratiæ expers, inferno videlicet. nam gratia Dei, inquit Divus Paulus, salvi estis per fidem: donum Dei est. non operibus ne quis glorietur. atque idem ad Titum, Secundum misericordiam suam ipse nos salvos fecit. Deus autem nunquam misericordia sua respicit peccatorem, quin animam puriore reddat. Quisquis ergo moritur gratia & misericordia Dei donatus, quum purus ac vacuus sit a peccatis, nonne salutem conse-quetur? nihil profecto certius. Recitantur apud Ioannem ipsa Christi verba: Ego sum resurrectio & vita. qui credit in me, etiamsi mortuus fuerit, vivet: & qui vivit & credit in me, non morietur unquam. Iesus Christus hoc loco se profitetur esse resurrectionem & vitam, deinde proponit duo genera mortis, unam corporalem alteram æternam. Ac quum se resurrectionem esse fatetur, nō de generali loquitur qua omnes ad extremum iudicium resurgent: non quidem ad vitam universi, quia reprobis qui morte perierunt æterna nulla vitæ spes est reliqua. Sequitur ergo, verba Iesu Christi referenda esse ad eum qui in viva fide moritur, quem ipse post hanc mortem corporis traducit in vitam æternam. quod quidem ipse declarat, quum dicit, Qui credit in me etiamsi mortuus fuerit viuet, adeo vt mortuo corpore, spiritus vitae initium faciat. quae vita haud dubie aeterna est, in qua Purgatorij nullus metus erit. nam id ipse post testatur, Qui viuit & in me credit, non morietur vnquam mortem alteram, quae est inferno. In eodem Euangelio recitatur, quod quisquis credit in Filium Dei non venturus sit in iudicium, sed a morte in vitam transibit. Constat his locis, credenti post mortem nullum vsquam restare Purgatorium. nam si, etiam dum hac luce fruitur, vita donatur aeterna: plena sane fruitione doni sibi a Christo in hac terra promissi potitur, postquam anima ex hoc corpore euolauit. piis enim, vt patet ex hac Christi oratione, mors corporis tantummodo transitus est ad vitam. Huc spectat illud Apocalypseos, Beatos esse qui in Domino moriuntur, de fidelibus nimirum loquens, quos solos vita manet aeterna. quotquot ergo priuari ea beatitudine alio concedunt, miseros atque infelices esse oportet.
units.tr: Concerning purgatory, he replied in this way: that he wished to maintain and defend to his last breath that the blood of Christ shed for us is the only and perfect purgatory, which cleanses the sons of God from all iniquities. He proved this from passages of Scripture, Hebrews 1 and 6 and the canonical Epistle of James, showing that the Christian, as soon as he departs from this life, having already been cleansed and freed from all torments, enters straightway into rest, as soon as his soul has left the body. It is written in Ezekiel: "Where the tree has fallen, there it will also remain"; that is, if a man dies outside the grace of the Lord, he will remain in a place devoid of all grace, namely in hell. For, says the divine Paul, "by grace you are saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God; not of works, lest anyone should boast." And the same in his letter to Titus: "According to his mercy he saved us." But God never looks upon a sinner with mercy without rendering the soul purer. Whoever therefore dies endowed with the grace and mercy of God, since he is pure and free from sins, will surely attain salvation? Nothing is more certain. In John are recited the very words of Christ: "I am the resurrection and the life; he who believes in me, though he die, shall live; and whoever lives and believes in me shall never die." Jesus Christ here declares that he is the resurrection and the life, and then sets out two kinds of death, one bodily and the other eternal. And when he says that he is the resurrection, he does not speak of the general resurrection by which all will rise at the last judgment, not indeed to life for all, since for the reprobate who perish by death there is no remaining hope of eternal life. It follows, then, that the words of Jesus Christ must be referred to the one who dies in living faith, whom he himself, after this bodily death, brings over into eternal life. He himself makes this clear when he says, "He who believes in me, though he die, shall live," so that, with the body dead, the spirit makes a beginning of life. That life is undoubtedly eternal, and in it there will be no fear of purgatory. For he himself testifies afterwards: "Whoever lives and believes in me shall never die the second death, which is hell." In the same Gospel it is recited that whoever believes in the Son of God will not come into judgment, but will pass from death into life. From these passages it is evident that for the one who believes there remains no purgatory anywhere after death. For if, even while he enjoys this life, eternal life is given him, then surely, once the soul has flown out of this body, he fully possesses in fullness the gift promised him by Christ on this earth. For to the godly, as is plain from this prayer of Christ, the death of the body is only a passage into life. To this point looks that saying of the Apocalypse, "Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord," speaking of the faithful, of course, to whom alone eternal life remains. Therefore all who assign to another place those who are deprived of that blessedness must be wretched and unhappy.

units.la: Caeterum quum nos a peccatis solo Christi sanguine purgari affirmo, non eximo plane Christianos aerumnis in hoc mundo ferendis. Iustus est enim Dominus simul & misericors. Si iustitiam ipsius spectemus, omnes merito peccatorum nostrorum, deuoti sumus exitio, sed misericordia qua libere cuius vult miseretur, mutat aeternas poenas leuioribus in hoc mundo plagis. idque exemplo docemur Dauidis, qui commisso adulterio se morti aeternae obnoxium reddiderat. iuxta illud, quod nec adulteri nec fornicatores vnquam regni caelestis haereditatem accipient: attamen Dauid haudquaquam damnatus est, sed misericordia Dei absolutus atque seruatus, qui illum poenis temporarijs affecit, vt aeternis liberaret: Hinc dolores & angustiae graues quas tulit mortuo infante: Et aliâs ob delictum suum ingens populi ipsius multitudo peste interijt. Idem in aliis seruis Dei perspici poterit, quos variis miseriis exercet prout ei visum fuerit. Ig-ne afflictionum eos velut in fornace refingit, deque iis sic experimentum facit. Atque Dei nostri & Patris amor erga nos singularis in eo spectatur. castigat enim (vt scriptum est) quos amat: nimirum vt sentientes ferulas, contrito atque humili corde ad ipsum redeant & misericordiam ipsius implorent. Itaque quum eos videt tristes & dolentes ob delicta, protinus omnium iniquitatum ipsorum obliuiscitur: imo in memoriam deinceps non reuocat, quemadmodum ipsemet per Prophetam testatur.
units.tr: Moreover, although I affirm that we are cleansed from sins by the blood of Christ alone, I by no means exempt Christians from the hardships to be borne in this world. For the Lord is just and at the same time merciful. If we look at his justice, we are, by reason of the merit of our sins, doomed to destruction; but by his mercy, by which he freely shows mercy to whom he wills, he changes eternal punishments into lighter afflictions in this world. We are taught this by the example of David, who, having committed adultery, had made himself liable to eternal death, according to that saying that neither adulterers nor fornicators will ever receive the inheritance of the kingdom of heaven. Yet David was by no means condemned, but was absolved and preserved by the mercy of God, who afflicted him with temporal punishments so as to free him from eternal ones. Hence the grave sorrows and anguish he suffered when the infant died; and elsewhere, on account of his sin, a huge multitude of his people perished by pestilence. The same can be seen in other servants of God, whom he exercises with various miseries as it seems good to him. He refashions them as in a furnace by the fire of afflictions, and makes trial of them in this way. And the singular love of our God and Father towards us is seen in this: for he chastises, as it is written, those whom he loves; that is, so that, feeling the rod, they may return to him with contrite and humble heart and implore his mercy. Thus, when he sees them sad and grieving over their offences, he straightway forgets all their iniquities; indeed, he does not thereafter recall them to memory, as he himself testifies through the Prophet.

units.la: Quod ad filios Dei attinet abiectos & contritos, certum est eos moriendo vitam aeternam possidere. quare bono iure David omnes beatos praedicat quorum remissa sunt peccata: & alibi quoque merito beatum censet cum cui Dominus non imputauit peccatum.
units.tr: As for the sons of God, cast down and crushed, it is certain that by dying they possess eternal life. Therefore David rightly pronounces blessed all those whose sins are forgiven, and elsewhere also rightly counts blessed the one to whom the Lord does not impute sin.

units.la: David his locis de beatitudine loquitur non quae a leui spe & promissione fallaci pendet: sed eam effert felicitatem, quam homo contritus atque humilis adipiscitur mox ut ex hoc corpore discesserit: quippe qui merito Iesu Christi omnibus poenis quae post hanc vitam impios manent, exemptus est. Christus enim, ut inquit Paulus, iustitia nostra est quae nos iustos facit, nostra sanctificatio & redemptio. adhæc ut Propheta ait, Iustus ex fide sua viuet. proinde cum iustus fit & in hoc mundo viuat, nonne relicto mundo vitam victurus est longe perfectiorem? Id sane nemo negare potest quin se professu[?] veritatis hostes[?] declaret.
units.tr: David in these passages speaks of a blessedness that does not depend on a light hope and a deceitful promise, but he sets forth that happiness which the contrite and humble man attains as soon as he has departed from this body, since by the merit of Jesus Christ he is freed from all the punishments that await the wicked after this life. For Christ, as Paul says, is our righteousness that makes us righteous, our sanctification and redemption. Moreover, as the Prophet says, "The just shall live by his faith." Therefore, since he is made righteous and lives in this world, will he not, when he leaves the world, live a life far more perfect? No one can deny this without declaring himself an enemy of the truth.

units.la: Postremo huc sermo rediit, ut dicerem me tantum in sanguine Iesu Christi purgationem quaerere, quia id mihi profecto maxime idoneum censerem purgatorium: eo qui uti nolet, valeat. hic mihi obiecerunt aduersarij ut suum astruerent purgatorium, locum ad Philippenses: Omne genu flectitur, caelestium, terrestrium, & infernorum. atque ibi infernum accipi pro ipsorum purgatorio volebant: verum id nequaquam ipsis concessi. nam ibi Paulus non de illo purgatorio sermonem habet: sed egregiam Christi gloriam diuinis laudibus prosequitur, & triumphum canit quo ille potitus est per mortem crucis: adeo ut omnis creatura Angeli simul & homines, atque etiam inferi, qui sunt ipsi diaboli, cogantur confiteri Iesum Christum propria victoria ad coelos ascendisse, atque nunc regnum gloriae Dei Patris sui possidere nostro nomine, quia carnem nostram quam assumpsit, eo extulit. Quocirca neutiquam dubitare debemus quin salui futuri simus, modo viuam fide retineamus: siquidem ille conscientias nostras ab omni peccato purgauit: cui honor & gloria sit in perpetuum, Amen.
units.tr: Lastly, the discussion has come round to the point where I said that I seek purgation only in the blood of Jesus Christ, because I certainly judge that this is the most suitable purgatory for me; whoever is unwilling to use it may farewell. Here my opponents objected, to establish their own purgatory, the passage in Philippians: "That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, things on earth, and things under the earth." And they wanted "things under the earth" to be taken as their purgatory; but I by no means granted this to them. For Paul is not there speaking of that purgatory at all, but pursues the remarkable glory of Christ with divine praises and sings the triumph which he gained through the death of the cross: so that every creature, angels as well as men, and also the infernal powers, that is the devils themselves, are compelled to confess that Jesus Christ, by his own victory, has ascended to the heavens and now possesses the kingdom of the glory of God his Father in our name, because he has raised up the flesh he assumed. Wherefore we ought in no way to doubt that we shall be saved, provided we hold fast in living faith; for he has cleansed our consciences from every sin, to whom be honour and glory for ever, Amen.

units.la: Dictum illud Augustini, quod scilicet non crederetur Euangelio, nisi Ecclesia illud pro Euangelio recepisset: inter alias quaestiones ei propositum fuit, ut quid de eo sentiret intelligere possent adversarij. Ipse vero in hanc rationem respondit, Ea est Euangelij virtus & dignitas ut omnium creaturarum caelestium aeque atque terrestrium adminiculis facile carere possit: idque propter admirabilem potentiam qua repletum est. in eo namque reconditi sunt thesauri atque divitiae Dei: ut sunt promissiones de remissione peccatorum, & de quiete aeterna per eiusdem misericordiam nobis factae. Quòd si fide non ficta Euangelium istud sanctum pro Euangelio salutis, ut re ipsa est, amplectamur, non reperietur alibi euangelium quod servet animas, quae est potentia huius Euangelij, ut testati sunt S. Iacobus, S. Paulus, & S.
