Adhæc minimè nunc agi de conuocando uniuersali Concilio nostra causa: sed satis ac super fore, modò Furbit{9} Episcopi uices gerès, qui pro sua liberalitate ultrò pollicebatur se effecturũ, ut simplici puróq; Dei verbo in rectà viam nos reduceret, in hanc rem incuberet ipse, vel alij quos designare placuisset.
units.tr: Then, although by God's grace we were certain of our faith, yet if we were taught from Scripture that we had fallen into error, or were defending some false doctrine, we were ready to render obedience to our God, since he had from long ago implanted in our minds this holy zeal by which we are carried towards his worship, even while, still groping in darkness, we rashly worshipped him according to our own will. And so we said we had been moved by him to investigate a little more carefully on which side the truth lay, especially at this time when turbulent disputes and contentions about religion are raging everywhere; and that at last, by the judgement of the church of Geneva, which defends the truth with true piety, we had assented to it. We asked for nothing except that the holy Bibles be brought forward, by which the whole controversy might be settled. And since the book of the Christian Institution, which had been snatched from us, was there to hand, we said that whatever they objected, we would show in it the most certain solutions. And although they proclaimed that this book had been condemned, and that the Council of Trent had provided that it must in no way be read, but that it was allowed to teachers, especially when the question is of recalling to the right way wretched heretics, which is the title they gave us, we replied as follows. As for their claim that it has been condemned, and that for each and every heretic there would be need of a new council: if this method had more weight in bending us than all the contrary arguments set out in that book for confirming and keeping us in our faith, it could not be but that we would be judged hypocrites and pretenders, and indeed worthy to be hated by God and by all creatures, even if our tongue confessed that what they affirm is true, while our conscience, convicted and forced to resist by those arguments, would not allow us to measure ourselves so shamelessly. Besides, we said that there was no question at all of summoning a universal council for our cause; but that it would be quite enough, provided Furbitus, acting in the bishop's place, who of his own generosity offered of his own accord to bring it about that he would lead us back into the right way by the simple and pure word of God, would take this matter in hand himself, or entrust it to others whom it might please him to appoint.

units.la: Quod attinet ad negotium nostrum, quod idem est ipsius Domini, siue causam, quâ nos miseri homunciones ac terræ vermiculi tuemur, sciatis velim nos vi. Idus Iulij deductos fuisse ad eũ qui Proprætoris locũ tenebat, iudice à suprema Curia delectum, & stipatum duobus vicarijs, uno quidé episcopi Tarentesiaci, altero autem episcopi Gratianopolitani: præterea Inquisitore fidei, itémque aliis monachis tũ Dominicanis tum Franciscanis, episcopo Furbito, & aliis patronis qui nostræ causæ iudices constituti fuerant unà cum Procuratore regio. Quum perlecta effet à Præfecto fidei nostræ confessio apud ipsum prius edita, rogarunt an verũ contineret, ac vellemúsne in ea perseuerare. quibus omnino ita esse Spiritus sancti virtute & gratia freti respondimus, atqs adeò velle nos quicquid illa coplectitur propugnare ad ultimũ vitæ spiritũ, & profusam ultimâ sanguinis nostri guttâ, ut quæ nitatur puro Dei verbo, quod extat tũ in veteri, tũ nouo Testamento. Verum quidem est, nos quia Bernates obtulerant curiæ Parlamenti libellũ supplicem, ac nuntium miserant unà cum scholastico quodam Lausannesi, quò statim liberaremur, postulauisse ut hoc sequuti ius nobis dicerent, nec pro legitimis iudicibus nostris agnoscere istos vicarios & fidei inquisitorem, quos palàm constat esse professos Euangelij & puriorum ecclesiarum hostes: denique coram ipsis nos minime respondsuros. quod certè profitebamur, non ut subterfugijs elaberemur,aut vllo modo declinaremus certamen, sed ne tanquam veros iudices admittere videremur.nam si Curia nobis alios designet ac statuat,nos esse paratos ad edendam fidei nostrae & religionis Christia-nae confessionem longè ampliorem,eámque ex Scripturis comprobaturos pro gratia quam Deus nobis largitus fuerit. Tunc Propraetor ille bis ac ter silentium imperauit,& nobis ferociter minatus est. Sed in provocatione nostra perstitimus: atque ita in carcerem reducti sumus,excepto fratre nostro,& commilitone ac socio in opere Domini Ioanne Vernutio, qui contra monachos disputauit horas plus minus quinque tum mane,tum post meridiem. Ex eo autem quum idem Proprætor senatui nostra responsa & provocationem significasset, proximo die Dominico, qui erat xiiii. eiusdem mensis,in quoddam curiae coenaculum conuenerunt Senatores cum illis quorum iam mentio facta fuit, & causidicorum turba ad numerum circiter triginta. Eò quum singuli vnus post alium venissemus, nobis pronuntiatum est senatusconsultum,quo iubebatur ut delecti illi de causa nostra omnino cognoscerent intra triduum, alioqui deiectu iri suo munere ad annum integrum:ac eodem ipso decreto praecipitur ut quicquid quaeratur à nobis, aperte respondeamus, idque posteaquam manibus sublatis de more,& interposito iurciurando nos vera dicturos recepimus:ea tamen lege iurauimus,ut provocationi nostrae nihil hoc derogaret, vel causae nocceret.Interim verò quod ad supplicem illum libellum spectat, postulauimus ut aliquid ex iure decerneretur. Quum ergo recitata mihi essent quae professus fueram,& breuiter prius respondærem de Missa,& praeceptis sanctae matris ecclesiae(sicuti vocabant)& de sacramentis quae ipsa probat & tuetur, perspicuè illis respondi ut antea: nempe Missam in locum sacrosanctae coenae Domini inuecta suisse,cui non magis conuenit cum illa,quàm luci cum tenebris:& tantum abesse ut eadem illa sit corporis Christi sacramentum,ut potius mera sit & turpis ciusdem abnegatio:atq; adeo Missam esse execrandum nefandūq;, sacrilegiū quo sanguis Christi pedibus calcatur,neque in ecclesia Romana vlla esse coena Domini. Caeterum rogatus an credere corpus & sanguinem Christi esse in pane & vino Coenæ. minime vero, inquâ. sed quum celebratur sacra Coena & administratur in ecclesiis ex Euangelio repurgatis, vbi Dei verbum pure annuntiatur, & Coena distribuitur ex vera & simplici institutione Christi, quemadmodum diserte scribitur Matthaei 26.Lucæ 22. Marci 14, & Actorum 2. & prioris ad Corinth.11. Dum fideles hoc modo illi communicant, & panem ac vinum accipiunt fide praediti, & vera poenitentia tacti: iunctâ simul charitate, vt tamen panis substantia & qualitate maneat panis, vinum etiam vinum: tunc eos signa accipere, veritatemque ipsam & rem significatam, corpus scilicet & sanguinem Christi, idque spiritualiter ore fidei: qui verus est animarum nostrarum cibus ac potus, & perfectum integrumque illarum alimentum. Quod autem attinet ad haec verba, Hoc est corpus meum, dixi tropum esse Scripturae satis vsitatum, quem Synecdochen vel Metonymiam vocant, vbi nomen rei significatae signo tribuitur: sicuti quum petra dicitur Christus, & columba Spiritus sanctus. atqui certum esse petram non fuisse Christum, neque columbam Spiritum sanctum: ac mihi persuasum esse, quam fingunt ipsi transsubstantiationem panis & vini in carnem & sanguinem, vt substantiae & qualitates panis & vini commutentur, commentum esse adeo crassum & ridiculum, vt quiuis mediocri sensu praeditus merito ridere possit. Sed quia mundus veritatem Dei & Iesu Christi postposuit Sathanae mendacijs & antichristi fraudibus & imposturis, permisit vt spiritus malignus in illis operatus sit cum efficacia erroris, & eo amentiae traxerit, vt quum Coenam Domini accipere deberent, panis buccellam prostrati adorauerint, & pro Deo suo agnouerint. Deinde Spiritu Dei propulsus exposui breuiter, ex quo in Ecclesia Domini collectus sum, me nouos quosdam motus interiores sensisse, tum ex verbi praedicatione, tum ex administratione Sacramentorum. quae quidem accepi velut ab ore Dei, qui ministrorum suorum lingua vtitur tanquam instrumento: atque si res istae, vt mihi, compertae ipsis essent, longe aliter iudicaturos. Tunc ex monachis vnus aliquis rogauit, qui scirem vetus ac nouum Testamentum Dei verbum esse: neque hoc credi debere, nisi quatenus Ecclesia admittit ac probat. Quod ad me spectat, non credo, inquam, verbum Dei sacris Scripturis comprehensum ob eam causam esse Dei verbum: sed quia Stylus Scripturarum sermo Dei est, quem Spiritus sanctus Prophetis, Apostolis & Euangelistis dictauit. Nam Petrus quum palam esset professus Christum esse Filium Dei viuentis, eumque habere verba vitæ æternæ: Iesus statim respondit beatum illum esse, neque ista carnem & sanguinem illi reuelasse, sed Patrem cælestem: eum ex Deo natum, qui credit Iesum esse Christum, & eius verba recipit: quisquis Filium audit, ipsum quoque Patrem audire, & qui videt Filium, Patrem etiam videre: edoctos esse à Deo, & Spiritum sanctum in se habere, qui testatur eorum spiritui ipsos à Deo esse, & omnes à Deo edoctos. Ex capite 54. Isaiæ, & Ieremiæ 31. Ioannis 6, & à 14, usque ad 18, Ioannis satis constat esse verbum Dei. Prophetæ qui aduentum Filij Dei prædixerunt, nihil præter Dei verbum memoriæ mandarunt. Paulus 8. capite ad Rom. docet Spiritum Dei habitantem in nobis testificari nostro, Christi nos esse, ac per ipsum fieri ut clamemus, Abba, Pater. Atque tum veluti canes mihi adlatrare coeperunt, quod dixissem me Spiritum Dei habitantem in me habere, qui mihi confirmabat suo testimonio esse Dei verbum, & cordi meo insculpebat ac faciebat promissiones salutis, gratiæ, fauoris & amoris Dei erga me singularis: denique certò me persuasum esse de mea in Christo adoptione, & de mea per ipsum salute. Tunc Inquisitor Latinè obiecit quod Paulus de se fatetur, nempe, Nihil mihi conscius sum, sed in hoc non sum iustificatus. quem locum perperam detorsit, sicuti quidam etiam causidici Nicodemitæ qui aderant, coacti sunt eum monere, atque ita ludibrio se ipse exposuit. Ex altera autem parte Franciscanus quidã suo latratu aures obtudebat, & mihi obiectabat præsumptionem esse diabolicam, ita certò persuasum esse de Spiritu sancto ac Dei gratia, neque aliud licere quàm ex coniectura aliquid suspicari. Huic bellua respondi, fidem nostram nimium frigidam fore, si coniecturis humanis innitatur: sed necesse omnino esse ut fulciatur Dei promissionibus eius verbo comprehensis: & quisquis hac certitudine & fiducia præditus non est, neque sentit certum testimonium animo suo reddi à Spiritu, eum nescire quidnam sit fides & Christiana religio, & quicquid de ea loquatur vel garriat, id totum ab ignaro prodire. Quod attinet ad Papæ potestatem eiusque traditiones, ad Conciliorum authoritatem: quod etiam maior numerus traditiones ecclesiæ Romanæ tuetur, non autem religionis Christianæ doctrinâ amplectitur: quod grex Domini perexiguus est, & porta angusta quæ ducit ad vitam æternam, paucíque per eam ingrediuntur, sed ampla quæ trahit in exitium: subiicci exemplum paucorum, qui cum Noah servati sunt: itémque filiorum Israel qui numero perpauci erant, si comparetur reliquo mundo, qui idololatræ, sine Deo, & vera religione vacui erant. Hic acrius exceperunt: Annon vides quot homines contra insurgant? Video, inquam, Simeonis vaticinium impleri, Lucæ 2. Christum scilicet signum esse cui contradicetur: & Act. vltimo, vbi Paulo responderunt Iudæi, sibi esse notum, vbique contradici verae religioni Christianæ. Quidam vero ex causidicorum turba quum surrexisset, clamavit, Nescis quidnam permultis aliis tui similibus factum sit? & eos vltimo supplicio affectos tanquam hæreticos ignoras? Prima, inquam, est hæc lectio, quam à Christo summo doctore ac magistro meo didici, nempe, quisquis vult esse eius discipulus, illi suam crucem esse ferendam vt ipsum sequatur: eam autem describit posthac ac depingit, iubens vt abneget semetipsum, & vitam suam sponte pro ipso exponat, quam seruabit ipse: qui vero seruauerit, eam perdet. Legite caput decimum Matthæi, quo prædicatur qui nos persecuuti fuerint, putaturos se Deo obsequium præstare ac sacrificium offerre, sicuti etiam Christus, Ioannis 6, confirmat. Atque vera est hæc piorum omnium conditio, vt non modo credant in eum, sed pro ipso quoque patiantur, Philippensium primo circa finem. Adductum fuit etiam quod Scriptura tum veteris tum noui Testamenti nobis testatur de persecutionibus in veros Dei seruos ad mortem vsque paratis, vt exemplum illud trium iuuenum qui in fornacem ardentem coniecti[?] sunt, quia religionem suam abnegare noluerant, & erectum idolum prostrati adorare. itémque Danielis factum memorabile: mors etiam Iacobi, & Stephani, Actorum septima. capite circa finem, & initio duodecimi.
units.tr: As for our case, which is the Lord's own cause, or the cause for which we poor little men and worms of the earth stand, you should know that on the 6th day before the Ides of July we were brought before the man who held the office of propraetor. He had been chosen as judge by the supreme Court, and he was flanked by two vicars, one from the bishop of Tarentaise and the other from the bishop of Grenoble. Also present were the inquisitor of the faith, other monks both Dominican and Franciscan, the bishop Furbity, and other patrons who had been appointed as judges of our cause, together with the royal procurator. When our confession, which I had earlier published before him, had been read aloud by the prefect of our faith, they asked whether it contained the truth and whether we were willing to persist in it. We replied that it did, relying on the power and grace of the Holy Spirit, and that we were prepared to defend to our last breath and to pour out our last drop of blood everything it contains, since it rests on the pure Word of God, which is found in both the Old and the New Testament. It is true that we, because the people of Berne had presented a supplication to the Parliament court and had sent a messenger, together with a certain schoolmaster from Lausanne, so that we might be released at once, had asked that the court, following this course, should give us justice, and should not acknowledge as our lawful judges these vicars and the inquisitor of the faith, who are clearly known to be enemies of the Gospel and of the purer churches. In short, we said we would not answer before them. We professed this indeed not to escape by evasions or in any way to shun the contest, but so that we would not appear to admit them as true judges. For if the court would appoint and designate others for us, we were ready to set out a far fuller confession of our faith and of the Christian religion, and to prove it from the Scriptures, according to the grace God has given us. Then the propraetor twice and three times ordered silence and threatened us fiercely. But we persisted in our appeal, and so we were led back into prison, except for our brother and fellow soldier and companion in the work of the Lord, John Vernut, who disputed against the monks for about five hours, in the morning and after noon. Afterwards, when the same propraetor had reported our answers and our appeal to the senate, on the following Sunday, which was the fourteenth day of the same month, the senators gathered in a certain upper room of the court together with those already mentioned, and a crowd of about thirty advocates. When we were brought there one after another, the senatorial decree was announced to us, by which those chosen judges were ordered to examine our cause fully within three days, or otherwise they would be removed from office for a whole year. And by the same decree it was commanded that whatever was asked of us we should answer openly, and this after we had, with hands raised as is customary and an oath interposed, promised to speak the truth. We swore, however, on the condition that this should in no way detract from our appeal or harm our cause. Meanwhile, as far as that supplication is concerned, we asked that something be decided in accordance with law. Since, therefore, what I had professed was read out to me, and I first briefly replied about the Mass and the precepts of the holy mother Church (as they called them) and about the sacraments which she approves and maintains, I answered clearly as before: namely, that the Mass has been introduced in place of the most sacred Lord's Supper, with which it agrees no more than light with darkness; and that it is so far from being the sacrament of Christ's body that it is rather a mere and shameful denial of it; and therefore the Mass is an accursed and abominable sacrilege, by which the blood of Christ is trampled underfoot, and there is no Lord's Supper at all in the Roman Church. Moreover, when I was asked whether I believed that the body and blood of Christ are in the bread and wine of the Supper, I said: by no means. But when the holy Supper is celebrated and administered in churches cleansed according to the Gospel, where God's Word is purely proclaimed and the Supper is distributed according to the true and simple institution of Christ, as is plainly written in Matthew 26, Luke 22, Mark 14, Acts 2, and 1 Corinthians 11, then, while the faithful communicate in this way and receive the bread and wine endowed with faith and touched by true repentance, joined at the same time with love, the bread remains bread in substance and quality, and the wine remains wine, yet they receive the signs, and the truth itself and the thing signified, namely the body and blood of Christ, and this spiritually, by the mouth of faith. He is the true food and drink of our souls, and the perfect and complete nourishment of them. As for these words, This is my body, I said that it is a trope fairly common in Scripture, which they call synecdoche or metonymy, where the name of the thing signified is given to the sign: just as when Christ is called a rock, and the Holy Spirit a dove. Yet it is certain that Christ was not a rock, nor the Holy Spirit a dove. And I am persuaded that the transubstantiation of bread and wine into flesh and blood, which they invent, so that the substances and qualities of bread and wine are changed, is such a gross and ridiculous fiction that anyone of ordinary sense may rightly laugh at it. But because the world has preferred the lies of Satan and the frauds and impostures of Antichrist to the truth of God and of Jesus Christ, God has allowed the evil spirit to work in them with the efficacy of error, and has drawn them into such madness that, when they ought to receive the Lord's Supper, they prostrate themselves and worship a morsel of bread and acknowledge it as their God. Then, driven by the Spirit of God, I briefly explained that, since I had been gathered into the Church of the Lord, I had felt certain new inward motions, both from the preaching of the Word and from the administration of the sacraments. These I received as if from the mouth of God, who uses the tongue of his ministers as an instrument; and if these things were known to them as they are to me, they would judge far differently. Then one of the monks asked me what I knew the Old and New Testament to be, the Word of God, and said that this should not be believed unless insofar as the Church admits and approves it. As far as I am concerned, I said, I do not believe that the Word of God contained in the holy Scriptures is the Word of God for that reason, but because the style and speech of the Scriptures is the speech of God, which the Holy Spirit dictated to the prophets, apostles and evangelists. For when Peter had openly professed that Christ is the Son of the living God, and that he has the words of eternal life, Jesus at once replied that he was blessed, and that flesh and blood had not revealed this to him, but the heavenly Father; he is born of God who believes that Jesus is the Christ and receives his words; whoever hears the Son hears the Father also, and whoever sees the Son sees the Father too; they are taught by God, and have the Holy Spirit in them, who bears witness to their spirit that they are of God, and that all are taught by God. From Isaiah chapter 54, Jeremiah 31, John 6, and from John 14 to 18, it is sufficiently clear that this is the Word of God. The prophets who foretold the coming of the Son of God committed to memory nothing but the Word of God. Paul, in Romans chapter 8, teaches that the Spirit of God dwelling in us bears witness to our spirit that we are Christ's, and that through him we are enabled to cry, Abba, Father. Then, as if they were dogs, they began to bark at me, because I had said that I had the Spirit of God dwelling in me, who by his testimony confirmed to me that this is the Word of God, and who engraved on my heart and made real the promises of salvation, grace, favour and the singular love of God toward me; in short, that I was certainly persuaded of my adoption in Christ and of my salvation through him. Then the inquisitor objected in Latin what Paul says of himself, namely, I am conscious of nothing against myself, but I am not thereby justified. He twisted this passage wrongly, and some of the advocates present, who were Nicodemites, were forced to warn him, and so he exposed himself to ridicule. On the other side, a certain Franciscan deafened our ears with his barking, and objected to me that it was a diabolical presumption to be so certainly persuaded of the Holy Spirit and of the grace of God, and that one may do no more than suspect something by conjecture. To this beast I replied that our faith would be far too cold if it rested on human conjectures, but that it must necessarily be supported by the promises of God contained in his Word; and whoever does not possess this certainty and confidence, and does not feel that the Spirit gives sure testimony to his soul, does not know what faith and the Christian religion are, and whatever he says or babbles about them, all of it comes from one who is ignorant.

units.la: Quod autem attinet ad Conciliorum quam ipsi vsque adeò iactant authoritatem respondimus, nobis probari quod decretum fuerat ac statutum de capitibus religionis Christianae, modo ex Dei verbo, quod intelligatur pro fidei analogia, sicuti Roman. xii, docet Paulus. Illos vero tantum ea tueri, quae ad stabiliendam Papae tyrannidem faciunt, qui verus est Antichristus, posterioris ad Thessalonicenses secundo capite coloribus suis depictus a Spiritu Dei, qui nobis illum per os Pauli descripsit, ut eum deuitemus, ne cum ipso trahamur in exitiū. Quòd si in hoc mundo ex vestris decretis & concilijs tanquam haeretica a vobis damnamur, scitote in altero vobis fore negotium cum Iudice, qui nos fideles & catholicos agnoscens sua sententia absoluet: vos autem ex aeternis suis statutis iudicabit, & morti perpetuae addicet, nisi resipiscatis, ac vijs vestris peruersis omnino valere iussis in quibus Papa vos detinet fascinatos suis mendacijs, puram Filij Dei veritatem sequamini. Tandem ira perciti, me tanquam obstinatum remiserunt.
units.tr: As for the authority of the Councils, which they so greatly boast of, we answer that we approve whatever has been decreed and established concerning the articles of the Christian religion, provided it is drawn from the Word of God, which is to be understood as the analogy of faith, as Paul teaches in Rom. xii. But they defend only those things which serve to establish the tyranny of the Pope, who is the true Antichrist, painted in his own colours in the second chapter of the later Epistle to the Thessalonians by the Spirit of God, who described him to us through the mouth of Paul, so that we may avoid him and not be dragged with him to destruction. But if in this world you condemn us as heretics by your decrees and councils, know that in the next world you will have to deal with a Judge, who, acknowledging us as faithful and catholic, will absolve us by his sentence, but will judge you by his eternal statutes and consign you to everlasting death, unless you repent and, utterly renouncing your perverse ways in which the Pope keeps you bewitched by his lies, follow the pure truth of the Son of God. At last, roused to anger, they dismissed me as obstinate.

units.la: Heri qui x vii. dies erat, monachi nos supremo suo decreto pronuntiarunt haereticos, & ab ecclesia Romana velut membra putrida exduxerunt. Nos vero laetis animis professi sumus certum nobis hoc esse testimonium, quo satis constabat nos esse ex Ecclesia Christiana, qui Christum caput nostrum agnoscimus, quū praesertim Antichristus nos a sua reijceret: nosq; via qua itur in paradisum feliciter ingressos, quum Sathanae membra ex suorum numero exclusos testarentur. Laudetur perpetuo Dominus ob singularem suam erga nos gratiam, quae nos eripuit ab horrenda impietate istorum sceleratorum, qui diabolos carne indutos plane referunt. Nos in dies expectamus quaenam feratur contra nos sententia, & quem exitum nobis daturus sit Dominus noster Iesus Christus, qui siue viuamus, siue morti tradamur, nobis est lucrum: ac felices erimus si Domino moriamur, sicuti Ioannes in Apocalypsi docet. Literas nostras legite, quas scripsimus ad dominos & fratres nostros verbi Ministros, & reliquos etiam fratres, qui nobis scripserunt. Egimus quoque gratias magnificis, nobisque multum obseruandis dominis nostris Syndicis ac Senatui Geneuensi, pro tot beneficijs in nos collatis, atque supplices rogauimus eos, ut infinita Dei donafemper agnoscant, & meminerint sibi victoriam ab ipso dari contra improbos, atque inter ultima nostra suspiria nobis summae voluptati & laetitiae fuit, dum tam sanctas leges ab illis latas fuisse, & eas typis excusas,promulgatas voce praeconis & publice affixas intelleximus. Det vobis Dominus ac reliquis fratribus & sororibus, ut ad regulam legis Divinae mores ac vita vestra formetis, & statutis illis sponte & ex animo pareatis. x v. Calend. Augusti. M. D. LV. Vobis postremam salutem dico, & omnium benevolentiae ac piis precibus me commendo: ultimum vale, inquam, & summum vobis dico ex hac vita discedens, ut in caelestem illam gloriam admittar, & accipiam coronam quae nobis reposita est ac parata per Iesum Christum Regem & Dominum nostrum.
units.tr: Yesterday, which was the seventeenth day, the monks pronounced us heretics by their final decree and cast us out of the Roman Church like rotten members. We, however, declared with glad hearts that we have this as a sure testimony that we belong to the Christian Church, since we acknowledge Christ as our head, especially as Antichrist rejects us from his own. We have entered happily by the way that leads into paradise, while they bear witness that we have been excluded from the number of Satan's members. May the Lord be praised forever for his singular grace towards us, which has rescued us from the horrible impiety of those wicked men, who plainly resemble devils clothed in flesh. Each day we await what sentence will be pronounced against us, and what outcome the Lord Jesus Christ our Lord will give us. Whether we live or are handed over to death, it is gain to us, and we shall be happy if we die in the Lord, as John teaches in the Apocalypse. Read the letter we wrote to our lords and brothers, the ministers of the Word, and to the other brothers who wrote to us. We also gave thanks to the magnificent and much-honoured lords, our Syndics and the Senate of Geneva, for the many benefits bestowed upon us, and we humbly asked them always to acknowledge God's infinite gifts and to remember that victory against the wicked is given to them by him. Among our last sighs it was a supreme pleasure and joy to us, when we learned that such holy laws had been passed by them, printed, proclaimed by the voice of a herald, and publicly posted. May the Lord grant you, and the other brothers and sisters, to shape your morals and life by the rule of the divine law, and to obey those statutes willingly and from the heart. Written on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of August, 1555. I bid you a last farewell and commend myself to your goodwill and pious prayers. A final farewell, I say, and my highest greeting to you as I depart from this life, that I may be admitted into that heavenly glory and receive the crown laid up and prepared for us through Jesus Christ, our King and Lord.

units.la: Epistola à Ioanne Vernutio scripta omnium nomine, qua confirmantur Acta quae iam breviter exposita sunt.
units.tr: Letter written by John Vernutius on behalf of all, confirming the Acts which have already been briefly set out.

units.la: die Veneris duodecimo scilicet huius mensis, Fratres charissimi & obseruandi domini, ad eum deducti sumus qui praetoris locum tenet: aderant vicarij Episcopi Tarentesiaci & Gratianopolitani, Inquisitor fidei: aliquot monachi & causidici circiter triginta. hoc porro factum fuit proximo die Dominico. Iussit Praetor ille quatuor coram se sisti, nempe Laborierium, Trigaletium, Batallium & Tauranum. nam Vernutius frater, non ita mordicus institerat provocationi nostrae, quam literis Bernatium suffultã tuebamur[?]: sed potius cum illis differens de religione, multo plura dixerat quam vellent. Deinde recitatum nobis fuit Senatusconsultu, quo iubebatur Praetor intra triduum de causa nostra cognoscere, alioqui suo munere abdicatum iri ad annum integrum: nec provocationem nostram ullo modo obstare. Tandem lecta fuit confessio fidei a nobis iam edita: atque rogati, an propositum nobis esset in ea perseuerare, statim respondimus nos ad id paratos esse, vel ad ultimam sanguinis nostri guttam profundendam, quum illa puro Dei verbo nitatur. Hic conatus est fidei Inquisitor nos a Dei veritate suis imposturis abducere. sed Domini virtute Spiritus sui, & verbo nos ita instruxerat, ut constanter perstiterimus, ac laetis animis redierimus gloriam illi tribuentes, & gratias illi egerimus quod nobis eam opem tulisset. Quid porro tunc dictum fuerit,& à quibus & quorsum,difficile esset omnia sigillatim perscribere,quum & otij minimum sit,& eò servitutis fimus redacti, adeoq; in totius actionis progressu tanta fuerit perturbatio: quanquam fusius rem ut gesta est ab initio, explicari cupimus literis communibus ad fratres omnes perscriptis. Monachi,& eiusdem farinae homines varias quaestiones excitabant, sed quid responderetur ad singulas, minime expectabant: licet hoc vehementius urgeretur,& expeteretur acrius in speciem. Inter alia quaesitum fuit de sacramento (quod vocant) matrimonij,& extremae Unctionis, atque etiam de Missa,& Papa. quisque pro mensura fidei suae respondit ad quaesita,& ut audientia ipsis facta fuit: nonnulli privatim ex Scriptura, alij in genere rogarunt quaestionarios istos & spinosos ut de rebus quaerent praestantioribus quam de Missa & eiusmodi nugis,& eas valere iuberent: quod si cuperent de his disputare, Genevam concederent, aliásq; repurgatas ecclesias: ubi reperiret quibuscum disceptare liceat sine ullo periculo, quanvis discedant victi. Qua in re satis ostendunt egregia illa sua charitate, quae quidem vera est Christianorum nota: quin pede movere non dignentur, ut eos in viam reducant, à quibus placidè audirentur,& qui fasciculis & ignibus minimè cum illis disputarent, ut solet ipsi pro suo more. Monachi isti quiritabantur nos minus severe tractari,ac proinde reddi audaciores: atque addebant, Genevae omnes esse latrones. sed exceptum fuit, eos ipsos esse, qui ex alieno saginantur[?]: & unumquemque Genevae laboris intentum esse, ut ex sudore vultus sui vivat. Quod ad Papam attinet, ita responsum fuit, si ex Scriptura probetur esse caput verae Ecclesiae, nos ex animo amplexaturos omnia eius decreta, & quos ipse fabricavit fidei articulos. sed nunquam hoc caput obtineri potuit. His rebus ita gestis, eo ipso die sepositi fuimus alij ab alijs usque ad horam quintam serotinā. Die Lunae sequenti iusserunt etiam à nobis summoneri Batallium & Tauranum, ut hac ratione illos terrerent,& à sententia dimoverent. Verum quae Dei optimi nostri est gratia, tam constantes perstiterunt, ut iudicum mandato ad nos reducti fuerint. Itaque nunc omnes simul agimus, nos mutuò solantes, laeti, ac precibus & Psalmis confirmantes, quos Domino canimus: atq; damus operam, ut freti eius promissis expectemus quem ipsi dare exitu libucrit,siue viuamus,siue moriamur.
units.tr: On Friday, the twelfth of this month, dear brothers and esteemed lords, we were brought before the one who holds the office of praetor. Present were the vicars of the Bishops of Tarentaise and Grenoble, the Inquisitor of the faith, some monks, and about thirty lawyers. This took place on the following Sunday. The praetor ordered four of us to be brought before him, namely Laborierius, Trigaletius, Batallius and Tauranus. For brother Vernutius had not insisted so stubbornly on our appeal, which we were defending with support from letters of Bernatius [?]; rather, in disputing with them about religion, he had said much more than they wished. Then a decree of the Senate was read to us, by which the praetor was ordered to examine our case within three days, otherwise he would be removed from his office for a full year; and our appeal was in no way to stand in the way of this. Finally the confession of faith, already published by us, was read out, and we were asked whether we intended to persevere in it. We at once replied that we were ready to do so, even to shed the last drop of our blood, since it rests on the pure Word of God. Here the Inquisitor of the faith tried to lead us away from God's truth by his deceits. But by the power of his Spirit and by his word the Lord had so strengthened us that we stood firm, and we returned with joyful hearts, giving glory to him and thanking him that he had brought us this help. What was said at that time, and by whom and to what purpose, would be difficult to set out item by item, since there is scarcely any leisure, we have been reduced to such servitude, and the confusion throughout the whole proceeding was so great. Yet we wish to explain the matter more fully, as it was done from the beginning, in a common letter written to all the brothers. The monks and men of the same kind raised various questions, but they did not at all expect what answer would be given to each, although they pressed this more vehemently and sought it more eagerly in appearance. Among other things it was asked about the sacrament (as they call it) of marriage and of extreme unction, and also about the Mass and the Pope. Each answered the questions according to the measure of his faith, and as far as a hearing was granted to him: some privately from Scripture, others in general terms. They asked these questioners, who were captious and thorny, to inquire into matters of greater importance than the Mass and such trifles, and to bid them farewell. If they wished to dispute about these things, they should go to Geneva and to the other reformed churches, where they would find people with whom they could contend without any danger, even though they depart defeated. In this matter they show well enough, by that outstanding charity of theirs, which is indeed the true mark of Christians, that they do not deign to move a foot to bring back those from whom they would be heard calmly, and who would not dispute with them by means of faggots and fires, as they are wont to do according to their custom. Those monks complained that we were treated too leniently and were therefore made more bold, and they added that everyone in Geneva was a robber. But it was retorted that they were the ones who are fattened on what belongs to others, and that everyone in Geneva is busy at his labour, so that he lives by the sweat of his brow. As for the Pope, the answer was given that if it were proved from Scripture that he is the head of the true Church, we would from our hearts embrace all his decrees and the articles of faith which he has devised. But this headship could never be established. With these things thus done, on that same day we were separated from one another until five o'clock in the evening. On the following Monday they also ordered Batallius and Tauranus to be summoned by us, so that in this way they might terrify them and turn them from their opinion. But by the grace of our best God they stood so firm that, by the order of the judges, they were brought back to us. And so now we all live together, comforting one another, glad, and strengthening one another with prayers and the Psalms which we sing to the Lord. We take care that, relying on his promises, we may await whatever outcome he shall please to give, whether we live or die.

units.la: Antonius Laborierius Ministris ecclesiae Genevensis, & omnibus suis fratribus atque amicis, qui Genevae agunt. S.D.
units.tr: Antonius Laborierius to the ministers of the church of Geneva, and to all his brothers and friends who live at Geneva. Greetings.

units.la: Obseruandi domini, ac patres mihi unice dilecti, & fratres in Christo charissimi, satis superque iam reuera sum expertus, Dei beneficio, quanti nos faciatis, ex ea diligentia qua adhibuistis, ut nobis vinctis opem ferretis sine ulla exceptione, quum nihil prorsus a vobis ad hoc fit praetermissum. In quo quidem certe satis etiam testati estis vestram erga nos charitatem singularem minime fictam esse, nec similem multorum benevolentiae, qui praeferentes bona & commoda huius mundi, auxilio quod filiis Dei ferre possent, taciti malunt oculis suis videre innoxium sanguinem profundi, ut quos pudet opprobrij Christi: & tamen plenis buccis iactant se insignes esse Christianos, & eximiae supra alios charitatis. Verum, Deo meo gratias ago, qui mihi patefecit eo toto tempore quo versatus sum apud vos, ac deinde magis etiam ex quo vinculis constringor, idque in summam meam aedificationem, vos esse veros ministros, fideles servos ac Dei filios, fide & charitate praestanti. quod quidem omnibus ex testimonio vocationis vestrae, & Dei nostri gloria notum est. Qui in nobis opus suum suum coepit, ille det ut in finem usq; perseveremus. Duo illi fratres nostri, qui proximis diebus a vobis missi huc venerunt, literis significarunt a vobis desiderari quam singuli fidei confessionem ediderimus. Lubenter quidem voluntati vestrae satisfecissemus: sed ex quo frater noster I.G. nuper hinc discessit, neque charta, neque libri, neque alia quibus nos solaremur ad manum fuerunt. Itaque, nullo modo id praestare licuit. Atque nunc charta nobis conceditur ea quam videtis mensura, vel potius parsimonia. Vos igitur rogo ut me excusatum habeatis, atque etiam colligere velitis confessionem meam, aut saltem eius praecipua capita ex superioribus meis literis, & simul ea omnia completi quae gesta sunt usque ad eam Iudicum sententiam qua miserorum remigum violentae & horrendae servituti sumus mancipati.
units.tr: Honoured sirs, my fathers whom I love above all, and dearest brothers in Christ: by God's goodness I have already learned, more than enough, how highly you value us, from the care you have taken to bring help to us in our chains without any exception, since nothing at all has been left undone by you for this purpose. In this you have certainly shown that your love for us is singular and not feigned, and unlike the goodwill of many who, preferring the goods and conveniences of this world, would rather silently watch innocent blood being poured out than give the help they could bring to the sons of God, since they are ashamed of the reproach of Christ, and yet boast with full mouths that they are outstanding Christians and possess a charity beyond all others. But I give thanks to my God, who has shown me, throughout the whole time I lived among you, and even more since I have been bound in chains, to my great edification, that you are true ministers, faithful servants and sons of God, outstanding in faith and charity. This is known to all from the testimony of your calling and from the glory of our God. May he who has begun his work in us grant that we persevere to the end. Those two brothers of ours who were sent by you and came here in recent days have informed us in writing that you want each of us to publish a confession of faith. We would gladly have satisfied your wish, but since our brother I.G. left here recently, neither paper, nor books, nor anything else with which we might comfort ourselves has been at hand. So it has not been possible for us to do this in any way. Now paper is granted to us only in the measure you see, or rather in a sparing amount. I therefore ask you to hold me excused, and also to be willing to gather my confession, or at least its principal heads, from my earlier letters, and at the same time all the events that have taken place up to that sentence of the judges by which we were handed over to the violent and dreadful servitude of the wretched galley slaves.

units.la: Interim fatis fit, nunc vobis a me exponi quidquid actum est in Senatu, ex quo ita fuit contra nos pronuntiatum. Die igitur Mercurij, qui scilicet xxi est Augusti, in carcerem ad nos venit sub horam quartquartam pomeridianam Iudex ille, cuius partes erant nobis sententiā proferre, qua ex Senatusconsulto remigijs illis coactis nos addixit. Cui respondimus, gratias Deo nostro immortales nos agere, quod dignos reddceret homines, qui ꝓ[?] sancto ipsi° nomine paterentur. quia vero Procurator regius huic sententiae intercessit, Vernutius frater Statim a Senatu accersitur, qui diu apud iudices constitit. Et quoniam temporis angustiae premebant, in diem sequentem remittitur: atque eo vespere sepositus a nobis fuit, idque non sine magno animi nostri anxietate & molestia. itaque eius nomine nostroque ad preces confugimus. Postridie rursum ad iudices reducitur, vbi totum tempus matutinum absumitur: & quae singularis est Dei gratia, tam strenuè in eorum conspectu se gessit, atque ita illis restitit, vt nihil ex eius constantia imminuerunt, neque de gradu exturbauerint. Interea autem nesciebamus ecquid valeret, nec quid contra eū ageretur. A meridie Senatus minimè coactus est.
units.tr: Meanwhile, it is enough that I now set out for you whatever has been done in the Senate since sentence was passed against us in that way. So, on Wednesday, which is the 21st of August, at about four o'clock in the afternoon, that judge came to us in prison, whose task it was to pronounce the sentence by which, in accordance with the decree of the Senate, we were condemned to those galleys. To him we replied that we gave immortal thanks to our God, who had made us worthy to suffer for his holy name. But because the royal Procurator interposed an objection to this sentence, Brother Vernutius was summoned at once from the Senate, and he remained a long time before the judges. And since the shortness of the time pressed, the matter was deferred to the following day; that evening he was separated from us, and not without great anxiety and distress of our minds. Therefore we took refuge in prayers, both for him and for ourselves. The next day he was again brought back before the judges, where the whole morning was spent; and by the singular grace of God he conducted himself so bravely in their presence and so resisted them that they could diminish nothing of his constancy, nor drive him from his position. Meanwhile, however, we did not know what was prevailing, nor what was being done against him. From the afternoon the Senate was not at all convened.

units.la: Die Veneris autem mane sub horam septimam ipse accersor, & in cubiculum quod vocant Iudiciorum deducor, illic sedebant duo Præsides, nouem consiliarij, aduocatus regius, & actuarius. Simul atque sum ingressus, alter ex præcipuis actuario iußit vt tabulā mihi offerret in qua depicta erat cruci affixi imago, ac mihi præcepit, vt genibus flexis procumberem. Hic ego, Absit, inquam, vt me coram idolo & creatura prosternam. Næ tu nimium mordax es, aiunt, an putas senatui ac nobis etiam esse in animo vt imaginem adores? nihil minus, inquiunt. sed iubet Senatus vt Deum adores, & magistratui honorem deferas: quod vt facias in genua prouoluaris, vt coram Deo tuo promittas iurciurando interposito te vera dicturum, & summa cum reuerentia nobis responsurum. Istud ipsum, inquam, viri obseruandi, vehementer expecto, vt Deum adorem, & honorem magistratui deferam, adeoque illi obsequar. Itaque vestro mandato me obsequuturum recipio, modo hinc faceßat & tollatur idolum, alioqui nunquam præstabo, quum id prorsus in Dei probrum & dedecus cedat. Tunc ergo actuario iußit, vt imaginem auferret.
units.tr: On Friday morning, however, at about seven o'clock, I myself was summoned and led into the room which they call the chamber of judgment. There sat two presidents, nine councillors, the royal advocate and the clerk. As soon as I entered, one of the chief men ordered the clerk to bring me a tablet on which the image of the crucified One was painted, and he commanded me to bow down on my knees. Here I said: "Far be it from me to prostrate myself before an idol and a creature." "Why, you are too biting," they said. "Do you think the Senate and we ourselves intend that you should worship a picture? Nothing of the kind," they said. "But the Senate orders you to worship God and to pay honour to the magistrate; and so that you may do this, fall on your knees, so that, before your God, with an oath interposed, you may promise that you will speak the truth and answer us with the greatest reverence." "That very thing, I said, honoured sirs, I greatly desire: that I should worship God, pay honour to the magistrate, and so obey him. Therefore I accept that I shall obey your command, provided that this idol is taken away and removed from here; otherwise I shall never do it, since it would turn entirely to the reproach and dishonour of God." Then he ordered the clerk to take away the image.

units.la: Atque, quum ea ratione ac via non succederet, mihi iterum præcepit ut in genua prociderem, præfatus minimè Senatum intelligere, ut alium præter unicū Deum adorarem, in cuius conspectu velA lent me vera respondere, ac solum ipsis parere, ut quæ Magistratui debetur, obedientiam publicè profiterer. Ego igitur præfatus, & palam testatus me nihil aliud velle ac mori potius malle, in genua procidi. Statim iussit ut afferretur idolum, ad quod iurarem: id quum viderem me in pedes erigere conatus sum & professus me nunquam facturum quod volebant. Itaque præcepit iterum, ut è medio tolleretur: & Biblia mihi afferrentur, ad quæ iuraui me vera dicturum. hinc autè accidit, ut prius quæstio de idololatria quàm de meo nomine satis diu agitata fuerit. Postea rogauit qui vocarer, unde ortus essem, & quæ vocationis meæ species. quibus ego plane respondi ut res habet. Deinde, qui captus fuisse, quid contra me actum ab aliis iudicibus, & quænam esset sententia in nos lata, monens ab ea Procuratorem regium prouocasse. Ego igitur totum actionis progressum exposui, & quod attinet ad sententiam, à me impediri nõ posse Procuratoris regij prouocationem: sed quod ad me attinet, paratum esse placidè ad subeundum quidquid Deo placuerit, siue solutis vinculis abeam, siue morti addicar, siue remigum miserrimæ seruituti mancipor: quum eius nomine alterutrum mihi sit ferendum. Hic me rogauit, cur relicta patria, Geneuâ me recepissem. Ego verò causam sine fuco adduxi. Tunc iussit ut surgerem: atque quum in eius conspectu starem, vsus est oratione admodum eleganti, venusta, & varys lenocinijs ad me permouendum referta, denique sic elaborata, ut nunquam magis appositam nec ita concinnam auduerim: qua docere conatus est potuisse me nõ minus pie sanctèque domi meæ viuere & illic Deum colere, quàm Genuæ: & grauem etiam ipsi Deo iniuriâ facere, quòd non sine scandalo à meis discessissem. Neque verò à Scripturæ testimonijs abstinuit, ut hoc suaderet. Denique sub finem orationis suæ argumenta sumpsit, quibus probaret, operibus nos iustificari: nobis liberum esse Arbitrium: Papam, vtcunque sceleratè fit vita (ut libenter verbis suis fassus est) habendum esse pro Episcopo: & iniquè ac perperam facere quisquis illum Antichristum appellat: Missam esse Cœnam, & sacrificium gratiarum actionis: Cæremonias quæ in in Baptismo observantur, licet sint superuacanea, tamen esse tolerabiles, quum Paulus Timotheum circumciderit, & caput suum abraserit: atque multa eiusmodi proposuit, quibus me rogabant omnes, ut ad suam ecclesiam redire non grauarer. Hic quanuis in carne mea pungerer acrius, mihi tamen suppeditauit Dominus quod illis respondercm[?]. Ac primum quibus de causis mihi non licebat fana conscientia diutius in Papatu morari, quū illic & Euangelij praedicatione & vsu Sacramentorum priuarer. Deinde argumentis respondi, quae ad probandum liberum Arbitrium & operum merita adduxerat: & rationes prorsus contrarias adiunxi. sed ille sermonem meum statim abrupit, ut coactus fuerim conqueri & petere annon[?] Senatui placeret audientiam mihi fieri. Tunc igitur moderatior habitus fuit sermo, atque ita de singulis illis capitibus ad horam usque decimam differumus. Ego quidem minutius ex parte possem referre quidquid ordine tractatum fuit: sed veritus ne mihi defit charta, & quia etiam vobiscū reputare melius potestis, tantum ascribam nostrarum disputationum clausulam, quae fuit eiusmodi (ficto necne animo, an ferio id fecerit nescio) ut consenserit nō esse liberum arbitrium: nos fide iustificari, & nō operibus: Missam nulle nugis, adeoque impijs superstitionibus referta esse: neque eam posse censeri sacrificium pro expiandis peccatis, sed tantum actionis gratiarum: corpus Christi minimè tanquam in loco includi in pane, neque sanguinem in vino, & qui illic adorant, idololatras esse. quod ad Papam spectat, non esse episcoporum episcopum: sed solum esse episcopum Romanum, ac illum quidem & alios episcopos & sacrificos ecclesie[?] viuere, neque vlla in parte officio suo defungi: atque vera & sanctam emendationē vel censuram esse expectandam. Denique nihil non prope mihi assentiebatur, ut in haec verba prorumpere coactus fuerim, Utinā, vir ornatissime, quotquot sunt in Gallia monachi tantum Theologiae ac tu didicissent! nam statim facilis esset inter nos consensus. Et si quid ego iudico, non est quod metuam ne tuis calculis damner, nisi reluctante conscientia feceris. Nam si re vera sum hereticus (quod falsum est) tu quoque sis necesse est. Hic quotquot aderant consiliarij subscripserunt, & ex ipsis vnus nomine C R. cui mandatum erat ut causam nostram inspiceret & postea coram Senatu exponerct, mihi dixit, Hæreticus, vt ille est, fis oportet: non autem vt tu, fit ipse. Huic homini breuiter respondi, me illi nolle esse simile. forte enim effem hæreticus ficta quadam ratione, sed optarim, inquam, vt ille, ac vos omnes, quemadmodū ego, hæretici effetis: nempe sola hominum opinione & falso mundi iudicio. Tum idem ille ex præcipuis alter, vultu rubore consperso, iterū more suo me cœpit hortari vt Christum abnegarem. quum vero se nihil consequi videret, iusserunt vt reducerer, quòd hora prandij illorum instaret ac vrgeret. Ergo in angustum quoddam cubiculum abducor, sepositus à meis fratribus, quod mihi valdè acerbum & graue fuit: quum vehementer optarem illos monere quibus astutiis & artibus illi Iudices agerent. Verum statim me ipse consolatus sum, & maxime illo solatio, quòd Dominus tam mirabiliter mihi adfuisset. Itaque illi gratias egi & precatus sum fratrum meorum nomine quos nondum accersitos sciebam. Et quoniā ille alter qui primas tenebat, ea mihi concesserat quæ iam retuli, cum illis colloqui magis optabam, vt Dei iudicium ob oculos ponerem. Eum igitur rogaui qui mihi prandium attulit, si redirent à prandio Iudices, vt ipsis ex me diceret, supplicitèr me precari vt mihi liceat iterum eos alloqui: quod se factūrum recepit. Statim ergo votis ardentioribus à Deo petij, vt illos rursum alloquerer, ac mihi daret vt eos officij sui & muneris probè monerem, deinde innocentiam nostram probarem, & diuinum iudicium proponerem. Ita in precibus ac meditatione perstiti ad horam secundam pomeridianam, qua minister ille renuntiat se Iudicibus exposuisse quod postulaueram, atque etiam vt ad illos veniā dicturus quæ vellem. Hoc igitur nuntio lætus, statim locum illum ingredior vbi sedebant, quemadmodum matutina actione fecerant. Cùm in eorū conspectu starem, ille quem dixi consessus moderator, Quid est, inquit, quod nobis dictū cupis magister Antoni? Tum erecto ad Deum animo, vt opem & auxilium ab eo peterem, cōmemorare cœpi quōdnam esset illorum munus & officium: & quorsum Deus eos præfeceerit excubijs agendis pro populi sui salute: adeóque suum ipsius nomen illis communicauerit. atque ita sum hortatus vt suis partibus probè difungeretur ex Dei præscripto & voluntate. Deinde fratrum meorum innocentiam, & meam simul comprobaui, quam ignorare nō poterant, terat, quùm illam manè confessi essent ipsi, neqʒ possent eorũ numero cẽferi, qui ex ignoratione sententias ferunt de hæresibus, vt vocant, pro iudicio & opinione monachorum, quia Deus eos singulari cognitione ad reẽte iudicandum instruxerit. ac proinde Christi causæ rationem haberet, de qua in nobis, qui sumus eius membra, iudicaturi erant: atque hîc Dei iudicium serìò proposui: denique palàm feci quàtam suorũ curâ Dominus gerat. In summa circiter vnâ horâ, Dei beneficio, ita sum collocutus, vt sermo abruptus mihi nõ fuerit, & dixerim quæcunqʒ Dominus suppeditauit, & testimonia ex Scripturis accommodauerim ad institutum, vt Deo tribuenda sit gloria ob eam quam tulit mihi opem, & auxilium singulare. Omnes quandiu ita disserui coniectos in me oculos habuerũt, & ego vicissim in eos: ac quosdam ex iunioribus vidi, quibus lachrymæ ex oculis fluebant. Vbi verò dicendi finem feci, alter ex duobus præcipuis vera quidem esse professus est quæcunque de ipsorũ munere disseruerâ: sed mihi satis esse notum, diserte Deum iussisse per Mosen, vt hæretici maximè puniantur: nec me posse vnquam negare, quanuis nonnulla verè dixissem, quin proximos meos grauiter offendissem, quùm Papam Antichristum & filium perditionis appellarem, & Missam diaboli commentum, gesticulationem histrionicam, adeóque omnis impietatis caput execrandum: itaque sanguinem meum non posse innocentem haberi, ac multa eiusmodi adiunxit. Hæreticos certè puniendos facilè concessi, & in exemplum proposui impurum illum canem Servetum, qui Geneuæ vltimo supplicio affectus fuit: verùm sedulò cauerent, ne in Christianos & Dei filios velut hæreticos animaduertâ: sicuti vniuersus Senatus certò sciebat, imò conscientiæ suæ testimonio conuictus erat nos esse Dei filios: ac proinde etiam atque etiam viderent, ne Pilati iudicio communicarent, vt fauorem Principum huius mundi & sacrificorum Belial sibi concilient ac demereantur. Tandem sæpius me rogauit propositis in medium varijs lenocinijs, vt in ipsorum conspectu palinodiam simpliciter canerem, & me ita dimissum iri, quum magnum fructũ proferre possem: & eã palinodiâ minimè periculosam fore: ac tum demũ mihi nouã Missam fabricauit, & larvatũ quoqʒ Papa induxit varijs coloribus depictũ: obsecràs vt hæc probarem. Excepi ad Missæ emendationem omnino requiri, vt prorsus e medio tollatur: & Pauli exemplo, ad primam Domini institutionem veniendum, vt Cœna restituatur pristinæ suæ integritati, quam lubens admitto & agnosco. Quod ad Papam attinet, si moribus & doctrina Petri, & Apostolos referat, me pro episcopo habiturum. Postea in angustum illud cubiculum remissus sum. Sub horam quartam Trigaletus frater ad eos productus est, qui vt ipse vobis scribit, Dei beneficio idem illis respondit. Postridie autem Batallius & Tauranus fratres adducti sunt, & toto eo mane certarunt, quibus ita Dominus auxilio fuit, vt mirum in modum cohibuerint Sathanà, & fraudulētas eius artes discusserint. Tādem Senatus mandato, læti in eundem locum simul omnes conclusi sumus. die Lunæ proximo (qui 26. erat Augusti) simul etiam omnes in Senatum deducimur, atque satis prolixè nos hortati sunt qui illic sedebat, vt in viam rediremus. Vermutius frater, Dei gratia, copiosè respondit omnium nomine, vt gloria tribuerimus Deo nostro, quòd victoria potiti discesserimus. Cæterum, ab eo tempore damnati sumus nos omnes eorum calculis, & igni, vt fertur, adiudicati. Gratias Deo agimus, & horâ expectamus, ac nos commendamus vestris omnium precibus.
units.tr: Since this method did not succeed, he again ordered me to kneel. He prefaced it by saying that the Senate did not intend that I should worship any god but the one God, before whose sight I was to speak the truth, and that I should give only to them the obedience owed to the magistrate, and publicly profess it. Therefore I, having said this beforehand and openly declared that I wished nothing but rather to die, knelt down. At once he ordered an idol to be brought, by which I was to swear. When I saw it, I tried to rise to my feet and declared that I would never do what they wanted. So he ordered again that it be removed from the room, and Bibles were brought to me, on which I swore that I would speak the truth. From this it happened that the question about idolatry was debated for quite a long time before the question about my name. Afterwards he asked what I was called, where I was born, and what kind of calling I had. To these I answered plainly, as the matter stood. Then he asked how I had been taken, what had been done against me by the other judges, and what sentence had been pronounced against us, warning me that the royal procurator had appealed from it. I therefore set out the whole course of the proceedings. As for the sentence, I said that I could not prevent the royal procurator's appeal, but that for my part I was ready calmly to bear whatever God should please: whether I should go free with my chains loosed, or be condemned to death, or be consigned to the most wretched slavery of the galleys, since whichever of these it was, I had to bear it for his name. Here he asked me why, having left my homeland, I had gone to live in Geneva. I gave the reason plainly, without pretence. Then he ordered me to stand up, and while I stood before him he used a speech that was very elegant, graceful and full of various enticements to win me over, and so carefully worked out that I have never heard anything more apt or more polished. In it he tried to show that I could live as piously and holily in my own home, and worship God there, as in Geneva, and that by leaving my people I had done a grave injury to God himself, since I had left them not without scandal. Nor did he refrain from the testimonies of Scripture to persuade me of this. Finally, towards the end of his speech, he brought forward arguments to prove that we are justified by works, that the will is free, that the Pope, however wickedly he lives (as he willingly confessed in his own words), is to be regarded as a bishop, and that whoever calls him Antichrist does so unjustly and wrongly; that the Mass is the Lord's Supper and a sacrifice of thanksgiving; and that the ceremonies observed in Baptism, although superfluous, are nevertheless tolerable, since Paul circumcised Timothy and shaved his head. He put forward many things of this kind, and all of them urged me to return to their church without reluctance. Although I was pricked more sharply in my flesh, the Lord nevertheless supplied me with what to answer them. First, I explained for what reasons I could not, with a good conscience, remain any longer in Papacy, since there I was deprived both of the preaching of the Gospel and of the use of the sacraments. Then I answered with arguments to the points he had brought forward to prove free will and the merits of works, and I added reasons wholly contrary to them. But he at once cut off my speech, so that I was compelled to complain and to ask whether it would please the Senate that I be given a hearing. Then the discussion was conducted more calmly, and so we disputed about each of those heads until the tenth hour. I could indeed report in some detail everything that was treated in order, but, fearing that paper might run short for me, and because you can also reflect on it better among yourselves, I shall add only the conclusion of our disputations, which was of this kind (whether he did it with a feigned or a serious mind I do not know): he agreed that the will is not free; that we are justified by faith and not by works; that the Mass is full of trifles and of such impious superstitions, and cannot be counted a sacrifice for the expiation of sins, but only a thanksgiving; that the body of Christ is by no means included as if in a place in the bread, nor the blood in the wine, and that those who adore there are idolaters. As for the Pope, he said that he is not the bishop of bishops, but only the bishop of Rome, and that he and the other bishops and priests of the church live (and fail in no part of their duty), and that a true and holy correction or censure is to be expected. In short, he agreed with almost everything I said, so that I was compelled to break out into these words: "I wish, most distinguished sir, that all the monks in France had learned as much theology as you! For then agreement between us would be easy at once. And if I judge anything rightly, there is no reason for me to fear that you would condemn me by your votes unless your conscience struggled against it. For if I am truly a heretic (which is false), you too must be one." Here all the councillors who were present signed, and one of them, with the initials C. R., to whom it had been entrusted to examine our case and afterwards set it out before the Senate, said to me: "You must be a heretic, as he is; but he is not so, as you are." To this man I answered briefly that I did not want to be like him. For perhaps I would be a heretic on some pretext, but I wished, I said, that he and all of you, just as I am, might be heretics: that is, by the sole opinion of men and the false judgement of the world. Then that same man, one of the chief men, his face sprinkled with blushing, again began, in his usual manner, to exhort me to deny Christ. But when he saw that he gained nothing, they ordered me to be taken back, because the hour of their lunch was at hand and pressing. So I was led off into a narrow little room, set apart from my brothers, which was very bitter and grievous to me, since I greatly wished to warn them by what tricks and arts those judges were acting. Yet I at once consoled myself, and most of all with that comfort, that the Lord had been so wonderfully present to me. So I gave him thanks and prayed on behalf of my brothers, whom I knew had not yet been summoned. And since that other man who held the first place had granted me what I have now related, I desired more to talk with them, so as to set the judgement of God before their eyes. So I asked the man who brought me my meal, if the judges returned from lunch, to tell them from me that I earnestly begged that I might be allowed to speak to them again; which he undertook to do. Therefore I at once asked God with ardent prayers that I might speak to them again, and that he would give me to admonish them properly of the duty and office of their station, then to prove our innocence, and to set forth the divine judgement. So I persisted in prayer and meditation until the second hour after noon, when that minister announced that he had reported to the judges what I had asked, and that I was to come to them and say what I wished. Glad at this message, I at once entered the place where they were sitting, just as they had done in the morning session. When I stood in their sight, the one I mentioned, who presided over the assembly, said: "What is it that you wish to say to us, Master Antoine?" Then, with my mind raised to God, that I might seek help and aid from him, I began to recall what their duty and office was, and for what purpose God had set them over his people, to keep watch for the safety of his people, and so had shared his own name with them. And so I exhorted them to discharge their own part properly according to God's prescription and will. Then I showed the innocence of my brothers and of myself alike, which they could not be unaware of, since they had themselves confessed it that morning, and since they could not be counted among those who pass judgement on heresies, as they are called, out of ignorance and by the opinion of monks; for God had equipped them with singular knowledge to judge rightly. And therefore they ought to have regard to the cause of Christ, concerning which they were to judge in us, who are his members. And here I earnestly set before them the judgement of God; lastly, I made plain how greatly the Lord cares for his own. In all, for about one hour, by God's benefit, I so talked that my speech was not broken off, and I may say that I set forth whatever the Lord supplied, and fitted testimonies from the Scriptures to my purpose, so that glory might be given to God for the singular help and aid that he brought me. All of them, for as long as I thus spoke, kept their eyes fixed on me, and I in turn on them; and I saw some of the younger ones, from whose eyes tears were flowing. When I had made an end of speaking, one of the two chief men professed indeed that everything I had said about their office was true, but that it was well enough known to him that God had plainly commanded through Moses that heretics be punished most severely; and that I could never deny that, although I had said some true things, I had nevertheless gravely offended my neighbours when I called the Pope Antichrist and the son of perdition, and the Mass a devilish invention, a theatrical gesticulation, and indeed a detestable head of all impiety; therefore my blood could not be held innocent; and he added many things of this kind. I readily conceded that heretics are to be punished, and I set forth as an example that impure dog Servetus, who was put to death at Geneva by the last punishment. But they should take great care not to punish Christians and sons of God as if they were heretics: since the whole Senate knew for certain, indeed was convicted by the testimony of its own conscience, that we are sons of God; and therefore they should see again and again that they do not share in the judgement of Pilate, so as to win and merit for themselves the favour of the princes of this world and of the priests of Belial. At last he repeatedly asked me, with various enticements put forward, that I should simply sing a palinode before their eyes, and that I would be dismissed when I could bring forward great fruit, and that such a palinode would be by no means dangerous. Then at last he fashioned for me a new Mass, and brought in a masked Pope, painted in various colours, begging me to approve these things. I replied that for the amendment of the Mass it was altogether necessary that it be entirely removed, and that, after Paul's example, we must return to the first institution of the Lord, so that the Supper may be restored to its original integrity, which I gladly admit and acknowledge. As for the Pope, if he should follow the morals and teaching of Peter and the Apostles, I would hold him as a bishop. Afterwards I was sent back into that narrow room. About the fourth hour Brother Trigalet was brought before them, and, as he himself writes to you, by God's benefit he answered them in the same way. On the following day Brothers Batallius and Tauranus were brought in, and they contended all that morning; the Lord so aided them that they wonderfully restrained Satan and broke up his deceitful arts. At last, by order of the Senate, we were all shut up together, glad, in the same place. On Monday next (which was the 26th of August) we were all led together before the Senate as well, and he who sat there urged us at some length to return to the road. Brother Vermutius, by the grace of God, answered fully in the name of us all, that we had given glory to our God because we had departed having gained the victory. Otherwise, from that time we have all been condemned by their votes, and, as is reported, adjudged to the fire. We give thanks to God and await the hour, and we commend ourselves to the prayers of you all.

units.la: Dilectio Dei nostri optimi, & Patris: gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi per communicationem Spiritus sancti sit vobiscum perpetuò, Amen.
units.tr: May the love of our best God and Father, and the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, through the communion of the Holy Spirit, be with you always. Amen.

units.la: Harissimi atque vnicè dilecti fratres, quandò minimè videtur Deo nostro, vt nobis liceat commodè quàm singeli edidimus fidei nostræ confessione & quidquid contra nos ab aduersarijs nostris actum est vobis copiosius perscribere, sicuti nonnulli vestrum expetunt, & literis quas nobis scribere placuit, etiam flagitant: nos omnes æquis animis id ferre conuenit, & satis nobis esse debet, quòd tantum boni adhuc largitur, vt possimꝰ vobis nuntiare velut per laceras partes quænam sit summa totiꝰ rei, pro ea quæ nobis datur chartæ & atramenti mensura vel portione. nam alioqui nihil est quod magis optemus, quàm dare operam omnem, quantisper à Deo vita hæc nobis conceditur, vt grati testemur quàtum vobis debeamus pro innumeris illis solatijs, & exhortationibus plane Diuinis, quas ex vestris literis accepimus postquam in vincula coiecti sumus: ex quibus quidem possumus vere testari nos longè plꝰdoctrinæ, fortitudinis, & constantiæ consecutos, i.lq;[?] vestris precibus assiduis, quarum experti sumꝰ admirabiles fructus, & quotidie experimur:quàm toto eo tēpore quo Dominus veritatē nobis patefecit:unde magnā ex animo gratiā vobis habemus: & simul sériò obtestamur ut tū in precibus vestris tū etiā in scribendo pergatis, donec tandē ad Dominū colligamur. Reddita nobis fuerūt postremæ vestræ literæ die Sabbathi, sed in tempore nec opportunius adferri poterat. nā eo toto die mirā cōsolatione ex earū lectione percepimus. Cur autē frater noster Ioannes Vernutius die Dominico ad Iudices non fuerit adductus, hæc ratio fuit, quòd iam die Mercurij sine vlla provocatione responderat. & dū responderet, moniti sumus ut provocaremus, quia Senatus causam nostram cognoverat ante literas Bernatium acceptas. itaque provocavimus. cupiebamus enim coram toto senatu sisti[?], hac ut ratione facilius monachorum proteruiam compescerémus, non quòd respondissemus illo ipso die: sed monachis illis respondebamus, & in provocatione nostra perstabamus. Hac igitur de causa accersiti fuimus die Dominico. Postridie vnus post alium omnes euocamur excepto fratre Vernutio, qui accersitus non fuit: atque sic eorsum producti sumus ad Iudices nostros, qui in eum locum coierant ubi rerum capitalium iudicia exercentur in palatio. Illic Proprætor primus sedebat, aderant etiam qui Regis partes sustinent. item consiliarij, & causidici circiter viginti. praeterea Inquisitor fidei cum Officialibus (quos vocant) huius urbis, & Tarentesiacæ ditionis: denique monachi quatuor aut quinque partim Franciscani, partim Dominicani. quia verò dies erat Dominicus aderant quoque alij permulti, qui cum nihil aliud haberent quod agerent, illuc conuenerant. Cæterum, ex Proprætoris mandato nobis recitatum fuit senatusconsultum, quo diserte illi & eius collegis præcipitur, ut intra triduum causæ nostræ finem imponant: alioqui suo munere abdicatum iri ad annum integrum. Ex eodem etiam senatusconsulto iussit Proprætor ille ut audiremus, atque etiam responderemus his monitionibus, quas Inquisitor nobis erat propositurus, nisi convicti hæreticos, seditiosi factiosíque homines, & obstinati ac pervicaces haberi vellemus: atque ita statim damnari omnium sententijs. Hic invocato prius nomine Dei, excepimus nos iam satis ac super respondisse illis monitionibus atque etiam nolle nos quicquam Dominorum nostrorum Bernatium & Geneuensium priuilegijs derogare. Iterum utgemur eodem mandato: itaque respondemus (postquam clare quod dicitur Esa. 38. protulimus, Domine vim patior, respondè pro me) nos ea lege obsequuturos, vt nihil ex eo priuilegio, & libertate illorum dominorum nostrorum imminuatur, vel derogetur: & modo etiam nihil obstet, quo minus tum apud Senatum ipsum, tum apud Regem queratur, & iniuriam sibi factam persequantur: quum praesertim ad hoc violenter cogeremur. Statim ergo actuarius quod a nobis responsum fuerat tum coram Praetore, tum aliis etiam ex scripto recitauit. quum perlegisset, interposito iureiurando ex nobis quaesitum fuit, an persistere in nostris responsis vellemus. nos vero excepimus, quum illa puro Dei verbo nitantur, neque ex illo vnico veritatis fonte, quidquam nobis adhuc contra fit offensum vel probatum, nos nullo modo posse aliter pronuntiare. vt autem aperte constaret, nos minime haereticos esse, nec obstinatos, recepimus si ignorantia labimur, aut erramus vlla in parte, & ex verbo Dei hoc doceamur nos sententiam statim mutaturos. Neque enim aliud nobis esse consilium, vel animum, quam credere & sequi Iesum Christum, eumque crucifixum, in illa quam ipse verbo suo indicauit via. Itaque si probetur ab ea nos aberrare, eos precari, vt nos ad illam dirigerent, ac veritatem nobis patefacerent quam sequamur, nosque libenter & ex animo obsecuturos. Hic fidei Inquisitor sermonem concinnum orditur, vt antea saepe, atque ita contexit, vt solius Papae, nullam autem Christi mentionem faceret. Et quoniam sua exhortatione affirmabat quaedam in responsis nostris capita esse plane haeretica, rogauimus vt ea nobis comonstraret. Nunc vobis singula non referemus, sed tantum quae sunt praecipua. Tu Inquisitor ille obiicit, duo tantum sacramenta a nobis recipi, alia vero quinque repudiari, quae semper in Ecclesia locum obtinuerat. Respondimus, si ex Dei verbo palam faceret alia esse, nos facile assensuros & ita polliceri. Quintum igitur caput ad Ephesios citauit: Quid? an non, inquit, de matrimonio scribitur, hoc sacramentum magnum est? excepimus, Itane vero magister Scripturas intelligis, vt hoc ad matrimonium detorqueas? Atqui Paulus ipse, pronuntiat, se de Christo & Ecclesia accipere. itaque genuinum Apostoli sensum prorsus euertis. Verum si de matrimonio etiam loqueretur, modo literis graecis tinctus esses, statim deprehenderes vocabulum illud perperam fuisse redditum. Imò, inquit, ego nonnihil ex ea lingua teneo. Dic ergo nobis, si placet, ecquid Græcè scriptum sit. Tum ille attonitus obmutuit. Addidimus igitur, Domine, satis videmus te pudore suffusum non audere vocabulum illud enuntiare. Nos ergo quale sit dicemus: Vox Græca tantùdem valet atque secretum vel arcanum, non autem Sacramentum. Tum Inquisitor, Iam nimis disputatum est, inquit, quia hæretici estis: Quid de extrema unctione sentitis? Excepimus, Sed domine, prius de matrimonio disceptemus, & ordine progrediamur, vel saltem victum te fatearis. Hic derepente omnes & Officiales, monachi, & causidici conclamarunt, plus satis verborum iam profusum esse, nec amplius disputandum. Seuere igitur præceperunt, ut responderemus. Nos autem mirati tantam eorum festinationem, diximus nimiùm præcipites ipsos ferri ad damnandos quinque innoxios, & mortis adiudicandos, ut qui nollent iusta illorum causam propius expendere, nec videre qualis esset aduersariorum calumnia. Hæc ergo paucis subiecimus, vos satis superque intelligitis istos homines qui nobis aduersantur, nihil eorum quæ dicunt posse ullo modo probare: & quia vobis hoc molestum est, bilem vestram in nos effunditis. Verùm, si nos hic audire pro vestro officio recusetis, iudicum omnium Iudicem supremum habemus Deum nostrum, qui nos placidè audiet, ac nobis omnibus ius reddet, & in cuius conspectu vobis tandem vel inuitis reddenda erit ratio iniuriæ, quam nunc Christo unico eius Filio inferre non dubitatis, dum nos qui sumus eius membra, tam miserè tractatis. Iusserunt nihilominus ut responderemus de illa extrema unctione. Ea Iacobus, inquiunt, præcepit: neque hoc cludere vel subterfugere potestis. Excepimus nos certè profiteri[?], quia initiò publicatum fuit Euangelium ab Apostolis, quia necesse erat ut miraculis editis confirmaretur doctrina, tunc fuisse signa, vel sacramenta quæ miracula illa referebant, quorum veritas subsequebatur: cuiusmodi erat manuum impositio, quæ donum Spiritus sancti significabat, ac simul ipsa veritas sequebatur, ut satis constat ex Actorum historia. Sic etiam illa olei inunxio adeò erat salutaris, ut eam sanitas mirabiliter consequeretur. Ubi autem Euangelij publicatio excepta fuit à mundo, tunc visibile Spiritus sancti donum, atque etiam miracula cessarunt: ac proinde illa signa, quæ citra veritatem omnino vana sunt. Deinde qui convenit unctioni illi, & vestrae quam iactatis? an non palam est quaecunque à vobis fiunt, blasphemijs referta esse? quaenam inde sanitas sequitur? nunquam illam circunfertis, nisi quum deplorata sunt omnia. Rogarunt iterum, annon illa unctio peccatorum remissionem conferret: Excepimus, in contextu remissionem peccatorum unctioni minimè tribui, sed diserte precibus ex fide conceptis. remissionem enim peccatorum nostrorum non alibi quàm in Christi sanguine sitam esse. Obiecerunt haec omnia prorsus à Concilijs damnata: nos igitur esse haereticos. Sed quanta in hoc toto sermone fuerit perturbatio, & quàm confusus strepitus, dici non potest. Nam semper septem vel o-cto simul obstrepebant: & interim eorum stultitiam ac ineptias obiter perstringebamus, ut qui aderant tantam istorum vesaniam ridere etiam cogerentur. Praeterea quaesitum à nobis fuit, an non vellemus fidem habere Concilijs. respondimus nobis semper probari Concilia & statuta quae verbo Dei consentiunt, & quae illo nituntur: alioqui minimè à nobis admitti: quin potius ea nos execrari tanquam humanas traditiones, & commenta plane diabolica, & quae Dei veritati repugnat: sicuti Paulus Gal. praecipiebat, ut hoc facerent: etiamsi Angelus nobis afferret è caelo aliam doctrinam, quam quae Euangelio comprehenditur.
units.tr: Most beloved and singularly dear brothers, since it does not seem good to our God that we should be allowed to set out at length, as conveniently as we would like, the confession of our faith that each of us has published, and everything that our adversaries have done against us, as some of you desire and as your letters also urge us to do, we ought all to bear this with an even mind. It should be enough for us that God still grants us so much good that we can report to you, as through torn fragments, the sum of the whole matter, in whatever measure of paper and ink is given to us. For otherwise there is nothing we desire more than to devote all our effort, for as long as God grants us this life, to bear grateful witness how much we owe you for the countless comforts and exhortations, truly divine, which we have received from your letters since we were thrown into chains. From these we can truly testify that we have gained far more in learning, courage and constancy, through your constant prayers, whose remarkable fruits we have experienced and still experience every day, than in all the time in which the Lord has revealed the truth to us. For this we hold a great thankfulness to you in our hearts. At the same time we earnestly beg you to persevere, both in your prayers and in writing, until at last we are gathered to the Lord. Your last letters were delivered to us on the day of the Sabbath, and they could not have been brought at a more opportune time, for we received wonderful consolation from reading them throughout that whole day. As for why our brother John Vernutius was not brought before the judges on the Lord's day, the reason was this: he had already answered on Wednesday without any appeal. While he was answering, we were warned to appeal, because the Senate had heard our case before the letters from Berne were received. So we appealed. For we wished to be brought before the whole Senate, so that we might more easily check the insolence of the monks. This was not because we had answered on that very day; rather, we were answering those monks and persisted in our appeal. For this reason we were summoned on the Lord's day.
