Ex quo quidē fauore singulari ad nos incredibilis fructus redit, cum scilicet conatus, turbas, & perturbationes cernimus quibus Sathan cum suis flabellis distringitur, iure possumus illum cum suis ridere, qui nobis bene conscii, tranquilla mente & pacata fruimur, certo persuasi de prouidentia Dei Patris nostri, qui non sinet vel pilum unum e capite nostro praeter voluntatem suam defluere: & quod maius est, hac confidentia praediti, ut permissurus non sit quidquam nobis accidere, nisi quod in bonum nostrum & salutem cedat, in Ecclesiae suae æ-dificationē, & regni sui progressum, deinde ubi gratiam quamDeus nobis confert serio agnouimus, iam parati sumus ad obsequium eius voluntati praestandum, sive moriendum, sive nobis viuendum sit. Sathan ergo moliatur quidquid libuerit, & eius flabella furore crepent, ac insaniant si velint. postquam sibi Christus nos acquisiuit & sibi coniunxit ac Patri suo: neque Sathan ipse, neque eius carnifices unquam poterunt nos ab illo diuellere, ac multo minus ex ipsius manu rapere. Nam quantumuis debiles sumus, in Christo tamen omnia possumus, qui ut nobis dedit virtutem, qua nomen suum intrepidē palam confiteamur, ita etiam vires suppeditabit, quibus pro ipso patiamur, idque pro ea quam voluerit mensura. Nihil est prorsus in mundo, quod nobis propositum hac lectionem ex memoria, Dei beneficio, deleat vel obliteret. Te igitur vehementer rogo, ut haec tibi sint solatio, & vicissim bono etiam sis animo & forti, confisa promissionibus capitis, ac ducis nostri, ut eius gaudio fruaris mecum, & lætitia nostra in ipso compleatur. Gratias ago Deo nostro optimo qui me literis tuis plurimum consolatus est, atque etiam magis postquam mihi ab hominibus huius ciuitatis, qui te ibi viderunt, renuntiatum est de ea quam tibi largitur Deus, constantia. Peto abs te ut agnoscas summum hoc beneficium ex singulari Dei dono proficisci & fluere, ideoque, magis te ex animo deiicias, & totam addicas in eius obsequium: quo scilicet amorem erga te suum, & gratias prosequatur. Vere enim testari possum, etiam si nullum alium fructū mors mea proferret vt Deo fauente prolaturam (spero) nisi quod te velut dormitatem excitauerit, sicuti ad me perlatum est, ad maiorem gratiarum Dei agnitionem: hoc solum satis superque esse, quo pergam alacriter ad mortem subeundam. Oro autem Deum optimum, vt rectum hoc & sanctum initium inte perficiat, & ad se magis ac magis te deducat virtute Spiritus sui. Iam non dubito, quin memoriae mandaueris quod superioribus meis literis ad te scripsi: ac praesertim vt syncerū Dei timorem ob oculos semper tibi proponas, & reuerenter, atque etiā summo ardore sacrosanctū eius verbum amplectaris: & iterum Dei nomine hoc ipsum abs te peto.
units.tr: On the Sunday just past, my most dearly loved sister, I wrote to you at length, that God in his goodness might guide and govern our affairs; but I suspect my letters were never delivered to you. This good brother who carries this letter to you has promised me that he will find out whether they are still in the city and will see to it that they are handed on to you. So I will not now repeat what I have been gathering there, especially since you will understand from him what has happened so far much better than I can write it. Satan does not cease to try by his own cunning to hinder the work of God, and now he attacks us more fiercely than ever. But God makes us all the stronger so that we may resist him vigorously, though there are many weaknesses by which we are surrounded and besieged, and we experience the dreadful corruption of our flesh, since we offend our Lord God more than we would wish. Yet the mercy and goodness of our God surpass our wickedness, so that he never ceases to work in us by the power of his Spirit, and always more and more he kindles our hearts to lay down our lives willingly for the defence of his most holy name. From this singular favour there comes to us an incredible fruit: when we see the attempts, the uproar and the disturbances with which Satan and his followers are stirred up, we may rightly laugh at him and them, while we, conscious of our innocence, enjoy a calm and peaceful mind, firmly persuaded of the providence of God our Father, who will not allow so much as one hair to fall from our head apart from his will. And what is greater still, endowed with this confidence, we are sure that he will permit nothing to happen to us except what turns to our good and salvation, to the building up of his Church and the advance of his kingdom. Then, when we sincerely recognise the grace that God bestows on us, we are ready to render obedience to his will, whether it be that we must die or that we must live. Let Satan therefore attempt whatever he pleases, and let his fans crackle with fury and rage if they will; since Christ has acquired us for himself and joined us to himself and to his Father, neither Satan himself nor his executioners will ever be able to tear us away from him, much less snatch us out of his hand. For however weak we are, in Christ we can do all things, for he who has given us the strength to confess his name boldly and openly will also supply the strength by which we may suffer for him, and that in whatever measure he wishes. There is nothing at all in the world that can, by God's benefit, blot out or erase from my memory what I have proposed here. I therefore earnestly beg you that these words may be a comfort to you, and in turn that you may also be of good cheer and courage, trusting in the promises of our head and leader, so that you may share his joy with me and our gladness may be made complete in him. I give thanks to our best God, who has greatly comforted me by your letter, and even more so after the men of this city who saw you there reported to me the steadfastness that God bestows on you. I ask you to acknowledge that this greatest benefit proceeds and flows from the singular gift of God, and therefore to cast off all discouragement and to devote yourself wholly to his service, so that he may continue his love and his favours towards you. For I can truly testify that even if my death brought forth no other fruit, which by God's favour I hope it will bring forth, except that it has roused you, as one drowsing, to a greater acknowledgement of the grace of God (as has been reported to me), this alone would be enough and more than enough for me to go on cheerfully to meet death. I pray moreover that our best God will bring to completion this right and holy beginning in you, and will draw you more and more to himself by the power of his Spirit. I do not doubt that you have committed to memory what I wrote to you in my earlier letters, especially that you should always keep before your eyes the sincere fear of God, and embrace his most holy word reverently and even with the greatest ardour; and again in the name of God I ask this of you.

units.la: Primis meis literis, quas ad te, soror & coniunx mihi charissima & fidelissima, dedi, quū adhuc domi Praetoris essemus, vbi vincti primum stetimus, tibi scripsi me daturum operam, si Deus commoditatem vllam mihi concederet, vt quid factum velim de his quae in patria reliquimus bona, copiose intelligeres. Deus autem, quae est singularis eius gratia, voluit vt exiguum hoc chartae folium in manus meas inciderit, quo scilicet id nunc efficere. Vnde gratias ago Deo optimo, & vt idem praestes, abs te peto vehementer. Quid huc vsque contra nos actum fuerit iam intellexisti. Nunc vero scias nos die Mercurij proximo ad Iudices nostros iterum deductos fuisse. Et interim sic Deus nobis semper adfuit, vt in nominis sui confessione perstemus. Hoc tempore in horas expectamus, dum ad supplicium trahamur. Alium enim causae nostrae exitum minime sperāmus, quidquid rationum vel opis homines excogitent vel inquirent. Te igitur rogo, vt assiduis precibus nos Deo commendes, quo nobis inuicta constantiam largiatur, vt scilicet quod in nobis coepit, opus absoluat.
units.tr: In my first letter, which I wrote to you, my sister and wife most dear and most faithful, while we were still at the house of the magistrate, where we were first held in chains, I told you that I would take care, if God gave me any opportunity, to make you fully understand what I wish done concerning the goods we left behind in our homeland. But God, in his singular grace, has willed that this small sheet of paper should fall into my hands, by which I can now accomplish this. For this I give thanks to our best God, and I earnestly ask you to do the same. You have already understood what has been done against us until now. But know now that on Wednesday last we were led again before our judges. Meanwhile God has always so stood by us that we persevere in confessing his name. At this time we are waiting hour by hour to be dragged to punishment, for we do not hope for any other outcome of our cause, whatever reasons or help men may devise or seek. I therefore ask you to commend us to God with constant prayers, that he may grant us unconquered constancy, so that he who has begun the work in us may complete it.

units.la: Quod ad me attinet, tibi quidem possum affirmare, nunquam me quidquam inmūdo [?] magis expetiuisse, quam pro tuenda hac causa mortem oppetere desiderem, si mihi Deus tantum hoc beneficiū contulerit, & ego iam Dei gratia ad id paratus sum, & credo neminē esse ex fratribus meis, & strenuis consultationibus [?] qui tantundem profiteri non possit: haec ad te scribo, vt agnoscas & serio sententias quantum in nos gratiarum Deus conferat. Et peto abs te quam possum maxime, vt toto vitae tempore cognoscendis his beneficijs, & saepius memoria repetendis operam tuam impendas, & re ipsa demonstres tibi fuisse maritum qui in numerum filiorum Dei cooptatus est. diligenter autem caveas, ne Christi sententia in te competat, nēpe duos in eodem lecto dormituros, unum vero incolume & salvum fore, altero praetermisso. Sed ex animo des opera discendae & amplectendae[?] unicae Dei voluntati, ut illi tota vita obsequaris: te tota exerceas in eius timore & reverentia, & agnoscas tot beneficia, quae ex mera ipsius gratia accepisti, quo scilicet eius filia maneas, & censearis, sicuti semper eo velut sigillo agnovi te obsignatā: & aliquando tandē mutuo aspectu frui possim in illa gloria, ad quam nos Christus invitat. Scis porro te adhuc esse iuvenem, ideoque privata societate[?] mea (si Deus ita voluerit maximo nostro bono) te ipsam in eo solare, & Christum loco patris tui, & mariti suscipe, donec alium tibi dederit: & certo persuasus sum te ab illo minime defertum iri, sed rebus tuis longe melius prospecturum, quam tu ipsa possis optare. Assiduē igitur eum ores, diligas, metuas & ore & facto: adsis sacris concionibus, improba consortia devites, & cum piis omnibus Dei cultoribus liberter versaris, vide ne quid pro tuo arbitrio geras, sed omnia de sententia, & consilio amicorum nostrorum suscipias, quos eodem in te animo esse atque in me semper experta es: ac praesertim D. Calvini, qui non sinet ut rebus tuis male consulatur, si eius monitis pareas: quod certe debes, & ut facias rogo. nam illum hominem Dei Spiritu regi non ignoras. Iam quum alteri viro nubes (quod quidem consulo) velim ut ab eo consilium petas, nec quidquam eo imprudente aggrediaris. maritum porro tibi deligas, qui Deum ex animo timeat: vel matrimonium ne contrahas. Sed spero Deum sicuti expediet tibi prospecturum. Primum igitur ac summum est, ut eum preceris, & in eius bonitate recubas. illum rogavi tuo nomine, & assiduē etiam rogo. Satis vero meministi quantus fuerit mutuus inter nos amor toto tempore, quo visum est Deo optimo ut una degeremus. pax eius semper in medio nostri resedit: ac mihi in rebus omnibus valde obsecuta es. Rogo te ut eandem semper, vel etiam meliorem te praestes erga eum, cui ductu & auspiciis Domini coniungeris: Deus tibi aderit, tuaeque soboli. In memoriam saepius revoces quae ex me didicisti principia (quanquam hic non ita ut poteram, officio meo erga te defunctus sum) & super ea aedificare non desinas, ut propius ad Deum accedas. Si pater tuus de morte mea certior fuerit factus, non dubito quin isthuc accurrat, vt te in Papatum retrahat: sed te supplex oro Dei nomine, & quatenus saluti tuae consultum cupis, ne illum audias: eum potius repelle, & quae Deus in te contulit beneficia praeferas, dum te in domum suam deduxit: annon plusquam misera esses, si relicta Dei domo, ad diabolum deficeres? Quam horrendum exitium te manerét? potius te in profundam abyssum demersam cupere. verum mihi persuadeo mortem tibi potiorem esse, sicuti etiam expediret & magis tibi esset salutare. Deum tamen ora, vt te Spiritus sui virtute fortiorem reddat. Parentes quoque mei conabuntur filiolam nostram ad se pertrahere: sed rogo te atque etiam Dei nomine tibi praecipio, ne tantum hoc scelus patrari sinas, quidquid tibi contingat. Testor enim me coram Deo exacturũ eius sanguinem ex manibus tuis, & si culpa tua perierit, in caput tuum illius interitum redundaturum. Peto igitur abs te per illud quod Deo patri nostro debes obsequium, & per maternum tuum ossicium ac munus: denique per illum amorem, quo me vt maritum tuum, & filiolae patrem prosequeris, vt eam rite ac sedulo in Dei timore erudiendam cures, simulatque ad aetatem pietati discendae matura peruenerit. Libenter quidem patri tuo, & vtrique parenti meo scripsisse: sed neque chartam, neque atramentum praeter id quod vides ad manum habeo, nec habere possum. Ad eos ergo velim perscribas quidquid Dei gratia mihi accidit, & illos etiam consoleris, & narres incredibilia & maxima quae Deus in me contulit dona. Sic Deus sua gratia eorum animos morte mea excitet ac tangat, vt melius ipsum agnoscant, quam me vivo fecerint meis monitis & exhortationibus. Deus illorum misertus ignoscat.
units.tr: As for myself, I can assure you that I have never desired anything more than to die in defence of this cause, if God grants me this favour, and by God's grace I am already prepared for it. I believe there is no one among my brethren, and no one of the steadfast, who could not profess as much. I write this to you so that you may recognise, and seriously consider, how many blessings God bestows upon us. I ask you as earnestly as I can to devote your efforts through the whole of your life to recognising these benefits and to recalling them often in memory, and to show by your deeds that you were the wife of a husband who was numbered among the children of God. Take care, however, that the saying of Christ does not apply to you: that of two people in one bed, one will be taken and the other left. Rather, with a sincere heart, give yourself to learning and embracing the one will of God, so that you may obey him all your life. Exercise yourself wholly in his fear and reverence, and acknowledge the many blessings you have received from his pure grace, so that you may remain his daughter and be counted as such, as I have always known you to be sealed with that seal; and at last we may enjoy one another's sight in that glory to which Christ invites us. Moreover, you know that you are still young. Therefore, since my fellowship with you is now private (if God so wills, for our greatest good), console yourself in it, and take Christ in place of your father and husband, until he gives you another. I am firmly persuaded that he will never forsake you, but will provide for your affairs far better than you yourself could wish. So pray to him constantly, love him, and fear him in word and deed. Attend the holy sermons, avoid wicked company, and gladly associate with all the worshippers of God. Take care not to do anything by your own judgement, but undertake everything on the advice and counsel of our friends, who you have always found to be as kindly disposed towards you as they were towards me; and especially that of Master Calvin, who will not allow your affairs to be ill managed if you follow his admonitions. This you certainly ought to do, and I ask you to do it, for you know that this man is ruled by the Spirit of God. Now, when you marry another husband (which indeed I advise), I wish you to seek his counsel, and not to undertake anything without his knowledge. Choose for yourself a husband who fears God from the heart, or do not marry at all. But I hope God will provide for you as will be expedient. The first and highest duty is therefore to pray to him and to rest in his goodness. I have asked him on your behalf, and I continue to ask him constantly. Indeed you remember well how great was our mutual love throughout the time it pleased the best of God that we should live together. His peace has always dwelt in the midst of us, and you have been most obedient to me in all things. I ask you to show the same, or even greater, devotion towards him to whom you are joined under the guidance and auspices of the Lord. God will be with you, and with your offspring. Recall often the first principles you learned from me (although here I have not been able to discharge my duty to you as I would have wished), and do not cease to build upon them, so that you may draw nearer to God. If your father is informed of my death, I do not doubt that he will hasten there to draw you back into Popery. But I earnestly beg you in God's name, and as far as you desire your own salvation, do not listen to him; rather repel him, and put before him the blessings God has bestowed upon you in bringing you into his house. Would you not be more than wretched if, having left the house of God, you fell away to the devil? What dreadful ruin would await you? Rather, you would wish to be plunged into the deepest abyss. Yet I am persuaded that death is preferable for you, as it would also be more expedient and more salutary for you. Nevertheless, pray to God that he may make you stronger by the power of his Spirit. My parents also will try to draw our little daughter to themselves; but I ask you, and also command you in God's name, not to allow such a wicked deed to be carried out, whatever may happen to you. For I testify before God that I shall demand her blood at your hands, and if she perishes through your fault, her destruction will fall back upon your own head. I therefore ask of you, by the duty you owe to God our Father, by your maternal office and charge, and finally by that love with which you regard me as your husband and the father of your little daughter, that you see to it that she is duly and diligently brought up in the fear of God as soon as she reaches an age ready to learn piety. I would gladly have written to your father and to each of my parents, but I have neither paper nor ink beyond what you see at hand, nor can I obtain any. Therefore I would like you to write to them everything that has happened to me by God's grace, and to console them too, and to tell them of the incredible and very great gifts God has bestowed upon me. May God, by his grace, stir and touch their hearts through my death, so that they may come to know him better than they did through my counsel and exhortations while I was alive. May God, having pity on them, forgive them.

units.la: Alia eiusdem ad uxorem epistola:
units.tr: Another letter of the same to his wife:

units.la: Literis[?] meis, quas ad te, Anna soror mihi chariss. die Veneris proximo dedi (qui duodecimus erat huius mensis Iulij) ita scripsi quod volebam, vt vix sperarem me amplius quidquam scripturum: Dominus tamen qui suos nunquam solatio destituit, pro sua bonitate voluit, vt ante obitum meum scribendis ad te his literis me possem adhuc oblectare, quibus tibi communicem tot consolationes, quas Deus optimus mihi confert in ipsa cruce beatissima, qua quidem me pro sua gratia exercere in gloriam suam, aedificatione Ecclesiae & salutem meã dignatur, ut mecum Dei beneficia reputes & agnoscas, atque ob id gratias illi agas in precibus assiduis, sicuti ego facio tui semper in illis memor. Interim rogo te ut innumera Dei erga nos dona sedulo & accurate expendas. Illis enim Dei promissiones impletas esse cernimus, pollicetur se propinquum afflictis fore, & ita adfuturum ut personam nostram suscipiat, quo scilicet in nobis affligatur. Quod ad me spectat, hoc certe Dei gratia, luculenter sum expertus. nam singularem Dei bonitatem ita probe nunquam percepi, atque ubi coniectus sum in vincula. Et credo te posse tantundem affirmare, quemadmodum intelligere mihi videor ex literis tuis, quae maximo solatio mihi fuerunt, quum videam Deum optimum tibi mirum in modum adesse, non modò quod attinet ad animum, quem (Dei gratia) video erectum in solatium admirabile, sed quod etiam ad corpus ipsum spectat. Nam quo tempore tecum agebam, minime tibi licuit tot amicos experiri quos Deus ex quo vinculis constringor, in tuum auxilium excitavit, qui de te magis sunt soliciti, vel saltem non minus quam ego esse possim: atque ut ex multorum literis & promissis extellexi, nunquam tibi defuturos spero, quamdiu facultas ipsis a Domino suppetet. Quapropter gratias ago quam possum maximas Deo meo. Sed unde id, quaeso, proficiscitur? annon Deus ipse tibi conciliat & offert mille amicos, patres & fratres loco unius mariti, quem ex hac vita eripit ut ad se deducat? an tibi cum ipso expostulandi locus relinquitur, quia[?] centuplo maius largiatur, quam abs te auferat? Agnosce, quaeso, summam hanc & immensam Dei nostri bonitatem, & simul vide quato[?] praestantior sit afflictio carnis quiete, res adversae prosperis, & opibus egestas. Haec exercitia non immerito vocatur in Scripturis fidei nostrae documenta & probationes. Nam certe non ita serio absque fide sentiuntur, nisi fiat examen velut in fornace. Ego igitur & tu laudemus Deum, & illi uno ore laudes concinamus, qui nos beatorum numero censere dignatus est: Felices, inquit, sunt illi qui pro nomine meo persecutionem patiuntur. Atqui, Dei gratia, certo nobis constat utrumque nostrum pro eius nomine pati: te (inquam) etiam, quia mihi dubium non est quin multo acerbius quam ego persecutione afficiaris. Quo te beatiorem agnoscas necesse est, ac soleris in Domino, & totam fiduciam tuam in eo colloces. Nimiū experta es quū in patria degeremus, & primorum cōsuetudine vterer satis familiariter, & apud eos gratia & authoritate valerem, quàm procul à Deo optimo tunc abessem. Atque etiam ex quo Geneuæ egimus, quum plus ciborum aliquando suppetebat, eò minus tum memores Dei & eius donorum eramus. contrà vero quum in patria non succedebat ex voto nec pro mundi libidine, ad Deum confugiebamus. Geneuæ quum imminceret nobis egestas, oculos erigebamus ad Deum, ardētioribus votis eum precabamur, oblectabamus nos assidua lectione & mutuò nos consolabamur: tunc denique toti ab eo pendebamus. Discas igitur, quaeso, potius te oblectare penuria rerum quàm diuitijs, otio & delitijs, contenta scilicet opibus quas nobis Christus offert, ac praecipit ut in cruce sua quaeramus, & nostram ipsum sequentes feramus. Caeterum spero Dominum facturum ut quod nunc patior in tuam salutem cedat, idq; magis quàm quicquid unquam tibi contigit, si modò perpendas & contempleris quam Deus nobis monstrat bonitatem, & percipiendam inter afflìctiones proponit. Sic autem velim eam tecum reputes, ut nunquam tibi obrepat illius obliuio. Poteris in mentem reuocare quod antehac scripsi, cuius nullam tibi nunc mentionem facio. Copiosius ad te scribere, sicuti maximè cupio, non esset mihi taediosum nec molestum: sed minimè licet. nam nec charta, nec atramentum nec otium mihi est, quia multi saepe nos invisunt, & clanculum vel furtim tantum scribimus.
units.tr: My letter, which I sent to you, dearest sister Anna, on Friday last (the twelfth of this month of July), I wrote as I wished, so that I hardly expected to write again. Yet the Lord, who never leaves his own without comfort, in his goodness has allowed me, before my death, to delight myself by writing to you once more, and to share with you the many consolations that the best of Gods gives me in this most blessed cross. By his grace he deigns to exercise me in it for his glory, for the edification of the Church and for my salvation, so that you may consider and acknowledge with me the benefits of God, and on that account give him thanks in your constant prayers, as I do, remembering you always in them. Meanwhile I ask you to weigh carefully and diligently the countless gifts of God towards us. For we see that his promises to the afflicted are fulfilled: he promised to be near them and to be so present that he would take up our cause, and so be afflicted in us. As for myself, by the grace of God I have clearly found this to be true. I have never so thoroughly perceived God's singular goodness as since I was cast into chains. I believe you can say as much, as I seem to gather from your letter, which was a very great comfort to me, when I see that the best God is present with you in a wonderful way, not only as regards your spirit, which I see (by God's grace) raised up to a remarkable consolation, but also as regards your body. For at the time when I was with you, you could hardly experience as many friends as God has raised up to help you since I was bound in chains. They are more anxious about you, or at least no less than I could be. And as I have learned from the letters and promises of many, I hope they will never fail you, for as long as the Lord gives them the means. Therefore I give my God the greatest thanks I can. But whence, I ask, does this come? Does not God himself win you a thousand friends and offer them to you, fathers and brothers in place of one husband, whom he snatches from this life to lead him to himself? Or is there room left for you to complain to him, because he gives back a hundredfold more than he takes from you? Acknowledge, I beg you, this supreme and immeasurable goodness of our God, and at the same time see how much more excellent affliction of the flesh is than quiet, adversity than prosperity, and poverty than wealth. These trials are rightly called in Scripture the proofs and tests of our faith. For they are not felt in earnest without faith, unless the examination is made as if in a furnace. Therefore let you and I praise God, and let us sing his praises with one voice, he who has deigned to count us among the blessed: "Blessed," he says, "are those who suffer persecution for my name." Indeed, by God's grace, we are certain that both of us suffer for his name: you too (I say), since I have no doubt that you are being persecuted far more bitterly than I. You must recognise yourself the more blessed for it, and be accustomed to rest in the Lord and place all your trust in him. You have experienced too much, when we lived in our homeland, and I made fairly free use of the company of the chief men, and had influence and authority among them, how far I was then from the best God. Moreover, since we lived at Geneva, when at times more food was available, we were then the less mindful of God and his gifts. On the other hand, in our homeland, when things did not go as we wished, and not according to the world's pleasure, we fled to God. At Geneva, when poverty threatened us, we raised our eyes to God, begged him with more fervent prayers, comforted ourselves by constant reading and consoled one another; then at last we depended wholly upon him. Learn therefore, I beg you, to take your delight rather in lack of things than in riches, in ease and pleasures, being content with the riches that Christ offers us, which he bids us seek in his cross, and following him, bear our own. Moreover, I hope the Lord will so act that what I now suffer will turn to your salvation, and to a greater degree than anything that has ever happened to you, if only you weigh and contemplate the goodness that God shows us, and sets before us to be grasped amid afflictions. I would have you so consider it that its forgetting may never creep upon you. You may call to mind what I wrote before, though I make no mention of it to you now. I would gladly write to you at greater length, as I most earnestly desire, and it would be no weariness or trouble to me; but it is by no means permitted. For I have neither paper, nor ink, nor leisure, because many often visit us, and we write only secretly and by stealth.

units.la: Literas tuas, Anna soror mihi unicè dilecta, xv. Septemb. scriptas accepi una cum tela & caligis, quas per fratrem O. ad me misisti. Tibi gratiam habeo, & mihi pergratum est quòd mei non oblita fueris, praesertim hoc frigido tempore quo nunc valde infestamur. Verùm multo adhuc iucundius fuit quòd ex literis tuis quae beneficia in te confert Deus, perspicuè intellexi. Sic enim percipio fructum orationum quas pro te fundo: unde ad agendas illi gratias impellor, sicuti etiam facio assiduè. Scribis iisdem tuis literis, quum tibi renuntiatum est de morte mea cui adiudicatus sum, hoc acerbum & graue statim initio fuisse, & potionem valde amaram: quod quidè facilè mihi persuadeo, qui probè noui tuam debilitatem: cui ut fortiter resistas, abs te peto, quum iam à longo tempore fatis exercitata meis vinculis esse debeas, & de exitu (hoc vero est, de morte, quae mihi impendebat) certior facta, simulatque captus fui, ne mei amplius memineris tanquam mariti tui, nisi forte oculis tuis me iam exustum, adeoque in cineres redactum subijcias & intueris[?]: & hac ratione nō amplius mihi coniuncta, nisi vinculo fraternae charitatis, quam pro me precari debes ex ossicio, quantisper Deus in hoc misero corpore quasi in ergastulo me volet inclusum manere. Confugias ad Deum nostrum custodem viduarum, & vindicem unicum. Nam praeterquam quod contingeret, si hinc exire detur, etiamsi Dominus nostri misertus libertati nunc restituat: tamen ita spero de singulari eius bonitate, ut me tandem aliquando ad mortem pro tuenda salutis doctrina vocare dignetur. Ergo si assuefacas, & animum velut obfirmes ad me tanquam mortuum intuendum, tibi grave non erit audire, quum de obitu meo nuntium accipies, si Deo optimo ita visum fuerit: atque etiam multum confirmaberis in posterum ad ferenda quaecunque Dominus immittet. Ut autem facilius hoc consequaris, velim tecum reputes ac perpendas exemplum probae illius viduae Ruth, quod nisi intelligas, frater noster, V. aut alius quispiam tibi exponere non grauabitur. In ea historia sancta perspicies probam illam mulierem Ruth, quae marito suo esset orbata, postquam natali solo renuntiauerat & cognatis omnibus idololatris, ut se reciperet in terram ubi Dominus pure colebatur: quum illuc socrum suam Noemy esset secuta, probâ[?], inquam, Ruth penuria coacta fuisse egredi ad spicilegium faciendum in agris, ut se & socrum suam tenuiter aleret: atque ita se placidè Domino commisisse, quem sui custodem elegerat. Deus vero illam non deseruit, sed tam liberaliter prospexit, ut eam marito Booz in uxorem dederit, & ex eorum sobole progenitus sit & propheta & rex Dauid, ac tandem Christus Dominus noster exortus inde fuerit. Ex quo vides, ut Dominus eos tractet, qui in eum toti recumbunt. Ego quidem minime dubito quin egestate vel penuria terrearis: sed expende potius, quanto sit locupletior universo mundo is qui te in fidem suam recipit. An passurum existimas ut quidquam tibi desit. nunquam certè id sinet, modo illi confidas:quin potius efficiet, ut in tua necessitate nihil desideres, sed omnia tibi copiosius affluant, quam possis animo complecti. Nam quòd huc usque, Dei gratia, nobis satis superq; semper fuit, cùm nulla re indiguerimus, hoc à me qui tibi eripior, non est profectum, sed à Deo ipso, cuius ope & praesidio tuta manes. Satis ergo tibi sit, quòd ille, à quo nobis omne bonum manat, profluxit & affluet, tecum manebit, nec unquam te deseret, ac iam ipse facit ut bonitatem suam experiaris, antequam penuria labores. Priusquam enim ad spicilegium cogaris sicuti proba Ruth, excitauit tibi non unum Booz, sed ingentem eorum numerum, quorum nomina postremis meis literis recensui, ut tibi probarem Deum veracem, & fidum esse in suis promissis, quae magis efficaciter senties quum opus erit. in necessitate enim maximè Dei subsidium agnoscitur.
units.tr: I have received your letter, Anna, my sister most dearly loved, written on the fifteenth of September, together with the cloth and the stockings which you sent me through brother O. I give you thanks, and it is most pleasing to me that you have not forgotten me, especially in this cold time, when we are now much troubled. But it was far more delightful still that from your letter I clearly understood what benefits God bestows on you. For thus I perceive the fruit of the prayers that I pour out for you, and I am moved to give thanks to him for them, as indeed I constantly do. You write in the same letter that when you were told of my death, to which I had been condemned, it was at first a bitter and grievous thing, and a very bitter draught. This I easily believe, for I know well your weakness. I ask you to resist it bravely, since you ought by now to be well trained by my long chains, and once you were informed of the outcome (that is, of the death which hung over me), as soon as I was taken, do not remember me any longer as your husband, unless perhaps you picture me already burned before your eyes and reduced to ashes. In that way I am no longer joined to you except by the bond of brotherly love, which you ought to pray for me out of duty, for as long as God wishes me to remain shut up in this wretched body, as if in a prison. Flee to our God, the guardian of widows and their only defender. For apart from what might happen if it is granted that I leave here, even if the Lord, having mercy on us, now restores us to liberty, yet I so trust in his singular goodness that he may at last deign to call me to death for the defence of the doctrine of salvation. So if you accustom yourself, and steel your mind to look upon me as dead, it will not be grievous to you to hear, when you receive news of my death, if it seems good to the best God; and you will be greatly strengthened hereafter to bear whatever the Lord sends. So that you may more easily attain this, I would have you consider and weigh the example of the godly widow Ruth, which, unless you understand it, our brother V. or someone else will not hesitate to explain to you. In that holy history you will see that good woman Ruth, who was bereaved of her husband, after she had renounced her native soil and all her idolatrous kin, in order to betake herself to the land where the Lord was purely worshipped. When she had followed her mother-in-law Naomi thither, the good Ruth, I say, being pressed by want, went out to glean in the fields, so as to feed herself and her mother-in-law meagrely; and so she calmly committed herself to the Lord, whom she had chosen as her guardian. God did not forsake her, but provided for her so generously that he gave her in marriage to Boaz her husband, and from their offspring came the prophet and king David, and at last our Lord Christ Jesus arose from that line. From this you see how the Lord deals with those who lean wholly upon him. I certainly do not doubt that you are frightened by poverty and want; but rather consider how much richer than all the world is he who takes you into his faith. Do you think he will allow you to lack anything? He will certainly never permit that, provided you trust in him. Rather he will bring it about that you desire nothing in your need, but that everything flows to you more abundantly than you can take in. For the fact that until now, by God's grace, we have always had enough and more, when we lacked nothing, did not come from me, who am being taken from you, but from God himself, by whose help and protection you remain safe. It is enough for you, then, that he from whom all good flows to us has flowed and will continue to flow; he will remain with you and never forsake you, and even now he makes you experience his goodness before you labour under want. For before you are compelled to glean, like the good Ruth, he has raised up for you not one Boaz but a great number of them, whose names I listed in my last letter, so as to prove to you that God is true and faithful in his promises, which you will feel more effectually when need arises. For it is in necessity above all that God's help is recognised. I ask you

units.la: Quòd ad filiam tuam attinet, pupillarum ille & viduarum custos non minorem eius quàm tui curam gerit. Nam divina sua providentia satis ostēdit se patrem eorum esse qui parentibus orbati sunt. huic quidem rei confirmandae vel unicum Mosis exemplum debet tibi sufficere. Quonam pacto deseritur? Ille non solùm parentibus caret, sed à patre & matre destitutus, aquis exponitur, ac si de eius salute actum esset. Interim paterna Dei nostri bonitas pro eo excubias agit, à quo ipse non cognoscitur: inde per Pharaonis regis filiam extrahendum curat, & ita euchit[?], ut in redemptione AEgyptiaca dux Israelitarum constituatur. Ergo in Dei nostri providentiam oculos conijce, & agnosce eius potentiam non imminutam esse, ac multò minus bonitatem erga suos. Tibi satis sit, quòd te in filiam adoptauerit, & me filiorum suorum numero ascripserit. Alterius haud dubiè quàm ipsius non erit filiola nostra, quum sit noster & liberorum nostrorum Deus, noster, inquam, Deus æternus. Confidas itaque & speres illum erga te, & filiam tuam fore eundem, quem & Ruth, & Mosi, & suis omnibus se præbuit. Ego sanè mihi persuadeo, te & filiam tuam, ubi vita defunctus fuero, multò ditiores fore, quàm nunc sitis. Nam bonorum quae mihi largitus est Deus, mihi, inquam, ut uni tertio, vos hæredes critis, & ea vobis restituet, ac longè plura etiam dabit post mortem meam. est enim verax & fidelis. Ac rogo te ut animo diligenter hoc insculpas, ne si tibi moriendum sit, in desperationem incidas ob filiam tuam, quæ à nobis seiuncta[?] multo erit locupletior quàm si cum ea versaremur, modò succedat tot Dei beneficijs, quæ pro sua liberalitate in nos contulit. Tantùm coram Deo sincerè ambules, & filiam tuam in eius timore erudias, & in illum reijcias cætera omnia. Ego igitur persuasus te mandaturam memoriæ quicquid ad te scripsi, te & filiam tuam illi commendabo, qui maiorem vestri curam gerit, quàm ipse possim.
units.tr: As for your daughter, that guardian of orphans and widows cares for her no less than for you. By his divine providence he shows plainly that he is the father of those who have been bereaved of parents. For confirmation of this, the single example of Moses ought to be enough for you. How was he abandoned? He not only lacked parents, but, forsaken by his father and mother, he was exposed on the waters, as if his safety were already at an end. Yet the fatherly goodness of our God kept watch over him, though he did not know it. Through Pharaoh's daughter he arranged for Moses to be drawn out, and so raised him up that he was made leader of the Israelites in the Egyptian deliverance. Therefore fix your eyes on the providence of our God, and acknowledge that his power is not diminished, much less his goodness towards his own. Let it be enough for you that he has adopted you as his daughter and counted me among his sons. Beyond all doubt she will not be our little daughter only, since God is ours and our children's, ours, I say, the eternal God. Trust and hope, then, that he will be towards you and your daughter what he showed himself to Ruth, to Moses, and to all his people. For my part I am quite persuaded that you and your daughter, when I have died, will be much richer than you are now. For you will be heirs of the goods which God has bestowed on me, on me, I say, as on one third party, and he will restore them to you, and will give you far more even after my death. For he is true and faithful. I ask you to engrave this carefully on your mind, so that, should you have to die, you do not fall into despair on account of your daughter, who, separated from us, will be much richer than if we were still living together, provided that she succeeds to the many blessings of God which, in his generosity, he has bestowed upon us. Only walk sincerely before God, bring up your daughter in his fear, and cast all other cares upon him. Therefore, being confident that you will commit to memory whatever I have written to you, I commend you and your daughter to him, who cares for you more than I am able to.

units.la: Alia eiusdem Laborierii epistola ad quendam amicum.
units.tr: Another letter of the same Laborierius to a certain friend.

units.la: Deus noster opt. & Pater pro immensa sua gratia participé te semper faciat bonorum, quæ semel nobis cōmunicauit per manum unigeniti Filii sui Domini nostri, idque Spiritus sui virtute.
units.tr: May our best and greatest God and Father, by his immense grace, always make you a partaker of the good things which he once communicated to us through the hand of his only-begotten Son, our Lord, and that by the power of his Spirit.

units.la: DE rerum mearum statu, frater integerrime, & de singularibus Dei in me donis, sicuti alias tibi dixi, & scripsi, possum adhuc in præsentia certò cōfirmare, Deum optimum ita mihi adesse magis ac magis, ut nunquam ingenuerim ob vincula quibus cōstringor, neque ob carcerem quo inclusus detineor, neque ob mortem quæ mihi impendet, neque ob ullos cruciatus quicunque mihi acciderint: sed Dei gratia, in illis oblector, & longè maiori lætitia perfundor quàm ego unquam senserim: & nonnunquam tristitia quadam afficior quòd strictius non distincar, & grauius aliquid patiar pro tuenda Dei nostri optimi causa, ut ad eum laudandum magis inciter, & in illum prorsus recumbam atque confugiam ad eius auxilium. Non quòd affirmare velim nullos à carne mea insultus, & quidem grauissimos mihi esse: sed quicquid tentet illa vel moliatur, spiritus (Dei beneficio) promptus est, ac victor sine magna repugnantia euadit: ut coniectis in Dominum negotijs meis omnibus omnino paratus sim ad excipiendum quicquid mittere visum fuerit: & siue ad mortem, siue ad vitam me vocet, certò scio eam mihi suppeditaturum virtutem, ut me voluntati ipsius placidè summittam, quum in me expertus iam fuerim promissionem, quam Patriarchæ Iacob facit, Genef. 38. vbi inquit, Ecce, tecum sum, & quocunque proficiscaris te seruabo. deinde subiungit, Nam te non deseram, donec perfecero quæ tibi dixi. Peto igitur abs te & aliis omnibus meis fratribus optimis, ne vlla anxietate vel cura meo nomine laboretis: tantùm vos oro, ut pro me gratias Deo nostro optimo agatis, & eum precemini, ut eadem semper fide mecum agat usque in finem, sicuti pro vobis omnibus cum assiduè rogo. Verum quidem est, & hoc vobis familiariter etiam referre libet, me duabus de causis graviter laborasse ex quo in carcerem coniectus sum: quarum altera Deus pro sua bonitate sustulit, ut iam tranquillo & quieto sim animo: in altera verò me velut defixum adhuc maximo meo bono retinet, nempe quum video me circundatum, & quasi obrutum summis Dei nostri beneficijs, hic in me perspicio tantum ignaviæ & torporis esse in illis agnoscendis, ut merito me pudeat: & præterquam quòd ita sum stupidus, video me refertum esse tot infirmitatibus & corruptelis, ut nesciam quid in mundo utilitatis afferre possim mea opera: quò fit ut Dei gratia, mortem libentius expetam, dum agnosco quàm feliciter mihi sit cessurum, si Deus optimus ab hoc misero corpore dignetur me liberare. Nam si Helias à Domino postulavit, ut se assumeret, dicens se minimè præstare maioribus suis: quid ego dicam miserrimus homuncio refertus omni iniquitate & ignorantia? Hei mihi, fratres, à vobis omnibus supplex peto, ut Deum meo nomine rogetis, ut hoc penitius animo meo infigat, quò scilicet fructū inde percipiam, qui mihi offertur: & ita me excitet ac erigat à stupore meo, ut eius beneficia mecum reputans, illi gratias agam, ut decet. Hoc enim est caput in quo multum adhuc laboro. Quod ad alterum spectat, certè ad tempus aliquod magna tristitia affectus sum, quum viderem tot bonos ac pios viros se totos impedire ad me servandum & eripiendum: deinde etiam meo nomine sumptus maximos facere: meo, inquam, nomine qui postquam exiero, quemadmodum iam dixi, nulli usui sim futurus, nisi Deus pro sua bonitate prouiderit. Ac præsertim dum propius expendo, si Dominus non sinat rationes iam excogitatas eum exitum sortiri quem vos omnes speratis, impensas omnino perituras, & summum dolorem ac cruciatum vobis inflictum iri. Atque in hoc ita sum distractus, ut optarem vos nunquam mihi notos fuisse, nam de meis vinculis nihil anxij vel solicitì fuissetis. Sed Deus optimus, qui suos diutius animi angore distringi non patitur, oculos meos ad se erexit, & ita facilè perspexi hoc minimè fieri à vobis tantùm, neque mea causa: non à vobis, inquam, quia opera vestra sic utitur, ut palàm constet ipsum exeruisse & admouisse manum suam, ac Domini esse opus. Dico etiam non mea causa tantum, quod sive Dominus me vocet ad se, sive vobis restituat, charitas illa in qua mihi opem tulistis, in maximam Dei nostri optimi gloriam cedet: ac praesertim quum vos ipsi causa fueritis ut non solum fidei nostrae confessio, sed etiam charitas vestra perferatur ad Regis ipsius aures, & aliorum multorum, idque in exitium quibusdam, aliis vero in salutem: sed hoc totum in Dei nostri laudem. Ex quo etiam nebulones illi scelerati, qui conantur ecclesiam Genevensem probris lacerare & ignominiae exponere, dum falso eam charitate vacuam spargunt, impudentiae convicti longe magis pudefient, quum intelligent tam admirandam charitatem quam in nos usi e-stis: quae procul dubio non minorem fructum proferet, quam fidei nostrae confessio. & gratias ago Deo optimo, qui mihi concedit ut iam fructum utriusque cernam oculis meis antequam ex hac vita migrem. Deinde vobis hoc maxime prodest: quia certo inde statuitis Spiritum Dei in vobis operari, & proferre fructus adoptionis vestrae, quum sine fuco testari positis vos esse ex eorum numero, quos Apostolus ultimo capite ad Hebraeos alloquitur, quum inquit, Memores estote vinctorum, tanquam unà cum illis vincti: & eorum qui affliguntur, ac si ipsi quoque afflicti corpore essetis. Laudetur itaque Deus noster optimus, quod satis luculenter comprobastis hoc modo vos esse vera Christi membra. Id porrò quum in media tristitiae ac doloris mei acerbitate viderem, ex praeclaro illo vestro facto summam laetitiae voluptatem cepi, non tam certe ob illud quod accepi beneficium, & eam quam sensi levationem (unde gratias Deo & vobis omnibus ago maximas) quam ob eas quas iā exposui rationes. Vos ergo Dei nomine obtestor & rogo, quum Deus vobis dederit ut probe teneatis quid charitatis vinculum & eius exercitium valeat, ne unquam fatigemini, sed continuo cursu pergatis, non quidem erga nos (nam, Dei gratia, satis superque defuncti estis) sed erga quoscunque alios, non ignari nos omnes unum esse corpus in Christo, & alios mutuo aliorum esse membra. neque enim ex vobis opes & divitias habetis, sed a Deo qui eas vobis largitus est. Atqui minime vobis eas contulit ut illic subsidatis, & velut affixi haereatis. Nam pro sua bonitate & gratia vos altius erigit, & sedere facit in locis cælestibus, idque in Christo Iesu. An ergo vultis rursum descendere? nequaquam fratres charissimi, sed oculis semper altius erectis, date operâ ut bonis quæ dedit vobis Deus, ut ac frui possitis pro eius voluntate, sicuti decet. Ac efficiate ut quemadmodum ecclesia vestra, Dei beneficio, ea est hodie quæ in mundo præ aliis splendidius relucet ob synceram verbi Dei prædicationem, & purum Sacramentorum usum, quæ in ea rite administrantur: sic etiam operibus vestris in omni charitate ita resplendeat, ut eius claritas & splendor non tantum perstringat, sed prorsus configat oculos perditissimo illi Antichristo Romano: & omnibus eius membris, & ita regnum illius cuertat ac pessundet, ut unicum caput nostrum, & dux noster Iesus Christus ubique regnum solus obtineat, & imperet. Dominus Deus id vobis concedat, & quæcunque in me confertis beneficia cumulatè rependat. Is enim est qui mercedem eiusmodi bonis refert, non pari quidem mensura, sed centuplo maiore. Nunc frater integerrime, abs te peto vehementer, ut amicos omnes meos, fratres ac sorores plurimum salutes meis verbis, quos osculo facto deosculor: eosq; rogo ne molestè ferant, si quemadmodum cuperem singulis non scribo: atque etiam ab illis postulo, ut hanc epistolam, quam tecum velim ipsis esse communem, sibi scriptam putent. nam te compellas, omnes alloquor. Eos autè valdè precor Dei nomine, ut ad me scribant, quòd scilicet me parè ad obitū quem imminere sentio: hoc verò est, ut ad mortè oppetendā cohortentur, neque amplius meminerint liberationis, de qua nullo modo cogitare libet, nec gratum est. Nam si Dominus de morte cogitantem me veluti deprehendat & liberet, tanto amplior[?] eius laudandi materia suppeditabitur, quòd ex numero dormientium excitauerit, cum quibus animo quiescere iucundum est, quantisper Domini reuelationem expecto. Etsi enim Dei gratia, mortem hactenus ob oculos mihi proposui, ut eam sponte & alacriter oppetam, nihil tamen in futurum mihi polliceri audeo, quum tanta infirmitate circundatum & implicitum me videam. Quòd si Paulus testatur Philipp.3.cap.se nondum illam apprehendisse, nec assecutum esse ut iam perfectus sit: sed omissis quæ sunt à tergo, se ad ea quæ à fronte sunt eniti, iuxtaque præfixum signum insequi palmam supernæ vocationis per Christum Iesum: ego longè maiorem debilitatem in me debeo agnoscere: atque ita nullo respectu habito ad ea quae huc usque feci (nisi ut singularem Dei bonitatem serio agnoscam) mihi colligendus magis ac magis est animus ut stadium percurram, & vitae cursum emetiar. Literae autem vestrae, cohortationes & sanctae preces ad hoc mihi summopere conducent, sicuti hactenus (Dei gratia) profuerunt. Vos igitur supplex rogo, ut iterum particeps sim illarum, si qua fieri possit. Tibi laetus gratulor, mi frater, eam Dei benedictionem, quam tu & uxor tua (cui me commendatum eiusque precibus valde cupio) experti estis, dum vobis filium dedit: atque etiam magis laetor, quod Abraham vocetur. det illi Dominus ut vere sit Abrahae filius, quod scilicet eius fidem & obedientiam imitetur, & ita baculi & solatio tibi sit quum ad senectutem perveneris.
units.tr: Concerning the state of my affairs, my most upright brother, and the particular gifts of God to me, as I have told and written to you before, I can still confirm with certainty at present that God the best is so present with me, more and more, that I have never been dismayed by the chains that bind me, nor by the prison where I am held shut in, nor by the death that hangs over me, nor by any torments that may come upon me. By the grace of God I am delighted in them, and I am filled with a far greater joy than I have ever felt. Sometimes, however, I am troubled by a certain sadness that I am not more tightly bound and do not suffer something more grievous for the defence of the cause of our best God, so that I might be stirred up the more to praise him, and lie down entirely upon him and flee to his help. I do not mean to affirm that I am free from the assaults of my flesh, and those very grievous ones; but whatever it attempts or undertakes, the spirit (by God's benefit) is ready and comes off the victor without great resistance. So, with all my affairs committed wholly to the Lord, I am entirely prepared to receive whatever he thinks fit to send, and whether he calls me to death or to life, I know for certain that he will supply me with the strength to submit myself calmly to his will, since I have already experienced in myself the promise that he made to the patriarch Jacob, Gen. 38., where he says: "Behold, I am with you, and wherever you go I will keep you." Then he adds: "For I will not leave you until I have done what I have told you." I therefore ask you, and all my other excellent brothers, not to be troubled or anxious on my account; I only beg you to give thanks to our best God for me, and to pray him that he would always deal with me in the same faith to the end, as I constantly ask for you all. It is true, and I am pleased to tell you this as a friend, that I have been grievously troubled for two reasons since I was thrown into prison: God has, in his goodness, removed one of them, so that now my mind is calm and quiet; but the other still holds me fixed, to my greatest good. Namely, when I see myself surrounded and, as it were, overwhelmed by the greatest benefits of our God, I perceive in myself so much sloth and lethargy in acknowledging them that I am rightly ashamed. Besides which, I am so dull, and I see myself so filled with so many weaknesses and corruptions, that I do not know what use my work could be to the world. Hence, by the grace of God, I desire death all the more willingly, since I recognise how happily it will turn out for me if God the best deigns to free me from this wretched body. For if Elijah asked the Lord to take him up, saying that he was in no way better than his forefathers, what shall I say, I, a most wretched little man filled with all iniquity and ignorance? Alas, brothers, I humbly beg all of you to pray to God on my behalf, that he would fix this more deeply in my mind, so that I may indeed receive the fruit that is offered to me, and so that he may rouse and raise me from my stupor, so that, reckoning up his benefits with me, I may give thanks to him as is fitting. For this is the chief point with which I still struggle much. As for the other, I was for some time struck with great sadness when I saw so many good and pious men devoting themselves entirely to saving and rescuing me, and also incurring very great expense on my account, on my account, I say, who, once I have got out, as I have already said, will be of no use to anyone unless God in his goodness provides for it. And especially when I consider more closely whether, if the Lord does not allow the plans already devised to turn out as you all hope, the expenses will be utterly wasted, and the greatest grief and torment will be inflicted on you. And in this I am so distracted that I wish you had never known me, for then you would have been neither anxious nor troubled about my chains. But God the best, who does not suffer his own to be long distressed by anguish of mind, has raised my eyes to himself, and so I readily perceived that this has happened not only through you, nor for my sake alone: not through you, I say, because he uses your work in such a way that it is plain he has stretched out and put forth his hand, and it is the Lord's work. I say also that it is not for my sake only, since whether the Lord calls me to himself or restores me to you, that love with which you have brought me aid will turn to the greatest glory of our best God: and especially since you yourselves have been the cause that not only the confession of our faith, but also your love, is carried to the ears of the King himself and of many others, and this to the ruin of some, but to the salvation of others: but all this is to the praise of our God. From this too, those wicked scoundrels who try to tear the Genevan Church with reproaches and expose it to disgrace, while they falsely spread that it is empty of love, will be far more put to shame, convicted of impudence, when they understand how admirable is the love you have shown towards us; which without doubt will bring forth no less fruit than the confession of our faith. And I give thanks to God the best, who grants me to see with my own eyes the fruit of both before I depart from this life. Moreover, this helps you most, because you can be certain from it that the Spirit of God is working in you and bringing forth the fruits of your adoption, since you plainly show that you are of the number of those whom the Apostle addresses in the last chapter of the Hebrews, when he says: "Remember those in bonds, as if bound with them; and those who are afflicted, as if you yourselves were afflicted in body." Let our best God then be praised, that you have in this way proved sufficiently clearly that you are true members of Christ. Now when I saw this in the midst of the bitterness of my sadness and pain, I took the greatest joy and pleasure from that splendid deed of yours, not so much for the benefit I have received, and the relief I have felt (for which I give the greatest thanks to God and to you all), as for those reasons I have now set out. Therefore I entreat and beg you in the name of God, that since God has given you to hold firmly what the bond of love is and what its exercise is worth, you never grow weary, but keep on running your course without ceasing; not indeed towards us (for, by the grace of God, you have done more than enough), but towards any others whatever, knowing that we are all one body in Christ, and that we are members of one another. For you do not have your wealth and riches from yourselves, but from God, who has given them to you. Yet he has by no means given them to you so that you should settle down there and cling as if fastened. For in his goodness and grace he raises you higher and makes you sit in the heavenly places, and that in Christ Jesus. Do you then wish to come down again? By no means, dearest brothers, but with your eyes always lifted higher, take care to use the good things God has given you, so that you may enjoy them according to his will, as is fitting. And see to it that, just as your Church is today, by God's benefit, the one that shines more brightly than others in the world on account of the pure preaching of God's Word and the sound use of the Sacraments, which are rightly administered in it, so also your works, in all love, may shine so that their brightness and splendour not only dazzle but utterly pierce the eyes of that most wicked Roman Antichrist and all his members, and so overturn and ruin his kingdom, that our only Head and leader Jesus Christ may alone hold and rule the kingdom everywhere. May the Lord God grant this to you, and repay abundantly whatever benefits you have bestowed on me. For he is the one who returns such rewards for good deeds, not in equal measure indeed, but a hundredfold greater. Now, my most upright brother, I earnestly ask you to greet all my friends, brothers and sisters, very warmly in my words, and I kiss them with a kiss; and I ask them not to take it amiss if I do not write to each one separately, as I would wish; and I ask them also to think of this letter, which I would like to be shared with them through you, as written to themselves. For I address you, but I speak to them all. I earnestly pray them, in the name of God, to write to me, so that I may know that they are ready for the death that I feel is close at hand. What I mean is that they should exhort me to meet death, and no longer think of deliverance, which I do not at all wish to think about, nor is it welcome to me. For if the Lord finds me thinking of death and sets me free, as it were, there will be a greater matter for praising him, in that he has raised me from among the sleepers, with whom it is pleasant to rest in mind, while I wait for the Lord's revelation. For although by the grace of God I have so far set death before my eyes, so that I may face it willingly and eagerly, I still dare promise nothing for the future, since I see myself surrounded and entangled by such great weakness. But if Paul testifies, Philipp. 3. chap., that he has not yet grasped it, nor attained to the point of already being perfect, but, leaving behind what is behind, strives towards what is before, and presses on towards the mark for the prize of the heavenly calling through Christ Jesus, then I ought to acknowledge a far greater feebleness in myself; and so, with no regard to what I have done so far (except to acknowledge God's singular goodness with earnestness), my mind must be gathered more and more so that I may run the course and measure out the race of my life. Your letters, exhortations and holy prayers will contribute greatly to this, as they have hitherto profited me (by the grace of God). I therefore humbly ask you to let me share in them again, if that can be done. I congratulate you gladly, my brother, on the blessing of God which you and your wife (to whom I commend myself, and whose prayers I greatly desire) have experienced, in that he has given you a son; and I rejoice all the more that he is called Abraham. May the Lord grant that he be truly a son of Abraham, that is, that he imitate his faith and obedience, and so be a staff and comfort to you when you come to old age.

units.la: Ioannis Trigaleti epistolae aliquot ad socerum suum.
units.tr: The letters of John Trigaletus to his father-in-law.

units.la: Dilectio Dei Patris nostri, & gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi, vnà cum Spiritus sancti communicatione in te semper maneat, Amen.
units.tr: May the love of God our Father, and the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, together with the fellowship of the Holy Spirit, remain with you always. Amen.

units.la: Accepi[?] litteras tuas, mi pater & frater in Domino nostro Iesu Christo, scriptas xiiii. Calend. Iulij: quibus scribis te miratum fuisse quod ad te non scripserim, sicuti commutationes mei ad amicos suos scripserunt: & metum tibi iniectum ne quid gravius patiar quam reliqui. Haec non fuit causa, sed quia tum exscribebam libellum supplicem quem Isthuc misimus. nos enim tres eadem catena vincti eramus. Quod autem attinet ad mœrorem quem dicis te concepisse graviorem quam ex re alia quae tibi unquam acciderit in tuis afflictionibus, idque profensu carnis, hoc mihi facile persuadeo. Et certe benevolentiam tuam in me paternam semper ego sum expertus, unde tibi gratias ago quammaximas. Quantū ad lætitiā spectat qua animo te cepisse confirmas, ubi tecum expendisti quantum honoris Deus optimus nobis detulerit, quum nos vocavit ad confessionem Filii sui unigeniti: in eo sane perspexi syncerum amorem tuum & affectum vere Christianum: unde etiam me tibi deuinctum esse sentio: ac te rogo, & Christi nomine hortor ut in hac tam pia sententia & sancto animi proposito constanter perseueres. Dominum pro nobis ora, vt quemadmodum vires ac robur suppeditauit ad bonum certamen incipiendum, nobis quoque virtutem & gratiam largiatur, qua perseueremus donec solidam victoriam consequuti, triumphum deinde agamus, & accipiamus coronam gloriæ quam nobis Christus caput nostrum & dux noster in cælis præparauit. quò proculdubio magis ac magis aspiramus, & in dies votum nostrum & desiderium perueniendi augetur, idque Christi Seruatoris & Redemptoris optimi beneficio. Verè hoc dico & affirmo Dei Spiritum (qui certissimus est conscientiarum nostrarum magister, & qui etiam intus eas docet) ita nobis certò testari de electione nostra, vocatione & adoptione: itémque de remissione peccatorum nostrorum, de nostra reconciliatione & iustificatione, quæ nobis morte & resurrectione Iesu Christi Domini nostri parta est, vt nunquam de salute mea sic edoctus fuerim, neque ita persuasus tot ac tam varijs lectionibus & infinitis prope concionibus, quibus adsui dum in eius schola versarer, vt nunc re ipsa sentio, & animo etiam experior in hoc afflictionis & crucis examine: adeo vt egredi ex hoc peccati corpore, & indui corpore glorioso quàm citissime cupiam. Quod tamen non fit sine magno carnis certamine aduersus spiritum qui strenuè reluctatur: vt verissimum sit, corpus hoc vinctum quo se redimat expetere: contrà vero spiritum velle tanquam fœdum carcerem deserere: illud mundum cupere, hunc autem refugere: vt horrenda inter vtrumque contentio exoriatur: Siccine, inquit corpus, moriendum est? Itáne vero, inquit spiritus, hic clanguere cogar? Tandem corpus addit se longè meliora desiderare. Sed ego & tu excipit Spiritus, longè fallimur: Solius Dei optimi voluntas fiat. Hæc est victoria quam Dominus virtute Spiritus sui nobis confert post diuturnum certamen: vt nos totos in Patris nostri obsequium tradamus, omnia in eius manum committentes: & hac spe freti non dubitemus, quin sicuti in hac vita caduca se fidum custodem corporum & animorum nostrorum comprobauit, ita etiam in vita cælesti futurus sit. Eum autem supplex oro nomine Iesu Christi Filij sui, vt nos in hac fide & spe tueatur vsque ad vltimum vitæ nostræ spiritum.
units.tr: I have received your letter, my father and brother in our Lord Jesus Christ, written on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of July. In it you write that you were surprised I had not written to you, as other prisoners have written to their friends, and that you were afraid I would suffer something more grievous than the others. That was not the reason. I was then copying out the supplication that we sent to you there, for the three of us were bound in the same chain. As for the sorrow you say you have felt, greater than any you have ever suffered in your afflictions, and that it comes from the feelings of the flesh, I can easily believe this. Indeed, I have always known your fatherly affection toward me, and for it I give you the greatest thanks. As for the joy you say you felt in your mind when you considered how great an honour the good God has conferred on us in calling us to confess his only-begotten Son, I have clearly seen in this your sincere love and truly Christian affection. For this I feel myself bound to you. I beg you, and exhort you in Christ's name, to persevere steadfastly in this so pious purpose and holy resolve. Pray the Lord for us, that as he has supplied strength and power for us to begin the good fight, so he may also grant us virtue and grace to persevere until we have won a complete victory, and then celebrate our triumph and receive the crown of glory that Christ, our head and our leader, has prepared for us in heaven. Without doubt we aspire to this more and more, and day by day our desire and longing to attain it grows, by the goodness of Christ our Saviour and Redeemer. I say and affirm truly that the Spirit of God, who is the most certain teacher of our consciences and who also teaches them inwardly, bears such certain witness to us concerning our election, calling and adoption, and likewise concerning the forgiveness of our sins, our reconciliation and our justification, which were won for us by the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ our Lord, that I was never so taught about my salvation, nor so persuaded, by so many and such varied lessons and by almost countless sermons, which I attended while I was at school in his teaching, as I now know in fact and experience in my soul in this trial of affliction and the cross. So much so that I long to leave this body of sin as quickly as possible and to be clothed with a glorious body. Yet this does not happen without a great struggle of the flesh against the spirit, which resists strenuously. So it is most true that this bound body seeks to free itself, while the spirit, on the other hand, wishes to leave it as a foul prison; the one desires the world, the other flees from it; and a dreadful contest arises between the two. "Must I then die?" says the body. "Must I then," says the spirit, "be forced to cling here?" At last the body adds that it desires far better things. "But you and I are far mistaken," the spirit replies: "let only the will of the most good God be done." This is the victory that the Lord, by the power of his Spirit, gives us after a long struggle: that we surrender ourselves wholly to the obedience of our Father, committing everything into his hand. Relying on this hope, we do not doubt that, just as in this frail life he has proved himself a faithful keeper of our bodies and souls, so he will be such in the life to come. I pray to him earnestly, in the name of Jesus Christ his Son, that he will keep us in this faith and hope to the last breath of our life.

units.la: De Massiliensi professione iam vobis scripsimus: ac nisi literas illas perferat qui istas reddet, forte non multo post accipietis. Quidquid fit, Deus & Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, cuius nomine vincti & captiui tenemur, gratiam hanc nobis conferet, vt sanctum nomen suum extollamus, & Ecclesiam ædificemus, siue per ignem, aut aquam ex hoc misero & calamitoso mundo commigremus: siue nobis vita prorogetur, in eo viuemus: siue mors sit oppetenda, pro illo & eius nomine moriemur: atque vt scribitur in Apocalypsi, Beati sunt illi, qui moriuntur in Domino. O mortem felicem, laborum omnium quietem, & transitum ex vita mortali ad immortalem vitam! qua quidem morte ingredimur in solidam & perfectam possessionem immortalis gloriæ, quæ nobis ab æterno parta est, & parata per Iesum Christum caput & ducem nostrum. Ille nos tanquam membra sua deduxit in via qua ipse ad hanc gloriam conscendit. Quamobrem lætamur in nostris afflictionibus momentaneis, quæ magnum pondus futuræ gloriæ, quasi secum vehunt: quo fit vt à mundo stulti & amentes iudicemur: sed satis est nobis, si Deus pronuntiet nos esse prædictos Spiritus sui sapientia, quam prophani homines, excæcati à Sathana, & imposturis vel artibus Antichristi eius filij dementati, carentes oculis fidei, nullo modo perspicere, nec animo complecti possunt. Nos igitur, mi pater, simul dicamus ambo cum piis omnibus, Tibi Domine sit omnis honor, sit gloria: nobis hoc concedas, vt beneficiorum tuorum semper simus memores, tum in rebus aduersis, tum etiam prosperis. hanc vero precationem in animo & ore semper habeamus, ne scilicet ingrati & immemores tot bonorum & gratiarum quas Deus in nos conferre dignatur, ipsum quasi violenter ad eas nobis cripiendas cogamus. Clamemus ergo cum sanctis martyribus, Sancte, sancte, sancte sanctorum, tibi vni sit laus, honor & gloria, & imperium perpetuo, Amen. Certe, mi pater, ea quidè est animi mei vehementia & ardor, vt mihi temperare, & calamum cohibere non possim, quin adhuc pauca hæc verba nunc addam, nempe vincula seu carcerem, Iesu Christi Domini nostri scholam esse, in qua plus vno die proficitur, & melius discitur [?]ecquis re-uera sit fructus & vis fidei, & quænam sit syncera pietas, idque vsu & experimento, quàm integro animo quisquam discat ex sola cognitione & scientia, quæ partim lectione, partim ex concionibus comparatur. Faxit Dominus vt fructum qui ad nos redit tum ex cognitione tum ex vsu, verè percipiamus & absque fuco & hypocrisi: ac scrio nos intus afficiat, & permoueat sensu & pia cogitatione bonorum, quæ nobis innumera illic proponuntur, ne vnquam simus eorum immemores: sed vt toto vitæ nostræ cursu agnoscamus, & accepta illi feramus ex animo, ore & factis, vt illi soli gloria tribuatur, & proximi nostri ædificentur, Amen.
units.tr: We have already written to you about the Marseilles confession. Unless the one who delivers this letter also carries that one, you will perhaps receive it not long after. Whatever happens, God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, in whose name we are held bound and captive, will grant us this grace: that we may exalt his holy name and build up the Church, whether we depart from this wretched and calamitous world by fire or by water; whether life is prolonged for us, and we live in him; or whether death is to be faced, and we die for him and for his name. And as it is written in the Apocalypse: "Blessed are they who die in the Lord." O happy death, rest from all labours, and passage from mortal life to immortal life! By this death we enter into the solid and perfect possession of immortal glory, which was won for us from eternity and prepared through Jesus Christ, our head and leader. He has led us, as his members, along the same way by which he himself ascended to this glory. Therefore we rejoice in our momentary afflictions, which, as it were, carry with them a great weight of future glory; and so we are judged foolish and mad by the world. But it is enough for us if God pronounces us wise by the wisdom of his Spirit, a wisdom that profane men, blinded by Satan and driven mad by the impostures and arts of Antichrist, his son, lacking the eyes of faith, can in no way perceive or embrace. Therefore, my father, let us both say together with all the godly: "To you, Lord, be all honour and glory." Grant us this, that we may always be mindful of your benefits, both in adversity and also in prosperity. Let us always hold this prayer in mind and on our lips, lest we, being ungrateful and forgetful of the many good things and graces that God deigns to bestow on us, should by force, as it were, compel him to take them away from us. Let us therefore cry out with the holy martyrs: "Holy, holy, holy, the Holy of Holies: to you alone be praise, honour and glory, and dominion for ever. Amen." Truly, my father, my zeal and ardour are so great that I cannot restrain myself or hold back my pen from adding a few more words now: that chains or prison are the school of Jesus Christ our Lord, in which more progress is made in one day, and what the real fruit and power of faith is, and what sincere godliness is, is learned more by use and experience than any man learns with a whole heart from knowledge and learning alone, which is gained partly from reading and partly from sermons. May the Lord grant that we truly perceive the fruit that comes back to us both from knowledge and from practice, and that without deceit and hypocrisy; and may he move and stir us inwardly, in feeling and in pious thought, by the good things set before us there in countless ways, so that we never forget them; but that throughout the whole course of our life we may acknowledge them, and receive them from him with our whole heart, mouth and deeds, so that glory may be given to him alone, and our neighbours may be built up. Amen.

units.la: QVIA iam intellexisti, charissime pater & frater in Christo Iesu Domino nostro, ex postremis nostris literis (in quibus descripta erat fidei nostræ confessio, quam Dei optimi gratia & virtute simul omnes edidimus coram Senatoribus supremæ huius curiæ) statum causæ nostræ, nimirum nos igni adiudicatos esse, fusius ea de re tecum non agam. Verè quidem hoc vnum tibi confirmare possum ex testimonio, quod Spiritus sanctus conscientiæ meæ certò reddit, nempe sicuti nihil melius pio Dei cultori potest accidere, quàm hac via commigrare in vitam æternam: ita nihil ardentius à nobis expeti, nec alacrius expectari, quàm felicem illum diem, quo abripiemur ad suauissimum illud sacrificium. Nam præterquàm quòd honor & gloria Dei nostri maximi, & Domini ac Seruatoris Iesu Christi, ædificatio Ecclesiæ eius, confirmatio, lætitia & consolatio fratrum nostrorum: deinde certum exitium, & interitus Sathanæ, Antichristi & omnium eius membrorum, & hostium veritatis illi mancipatorum, quasi concluditur & continetur publico hoc & solenni testimonio quod ore nostro edimus, & proprio sanguine obsignamus: qui certè præcipuus est fructus, quem mors nostra felicissima producit: accedit etiam, si quis priuatim nos spectet, tantum boni & lucri quod ad nos inde manat, vt animo comprehendi non possit: ac multò minus verbis, aut scriptis explicari. An, quæso, parui momenti res est, liberari ex quatuor carceribus, quibus nos concludimur, quemadmodum vos tribus, ut in libertatem perpetuam vindicemur, & afferamur? quorum quidem unus est mundus iste totmiseriis refertus, qui nobis vana sua figura, imposturis & praestigiis oculos praestringit & illudit. Secundus vero est, corpus nostrum tot sordibus inquinatum, & fœto-re plenum. Tertius est, anima nostra cum omnibus suis partibus, mete, memoria, ratione, voluntate & cupiditatibus nostris atq; perturbationibus, quae nos huc & illuc abstrahunt, & omnino avertunt ab his quae Deus nobis praecipit. Annon illa est velut gurges quidam, & abyssus omnium vitiorum, ac scelerum, quae sua gravitate horrore incutiant? Fecit Deus optimus, ut illis serio tangamur, quo ingemiscamus, condoleamus, eorum nos pudeat, ac nobis ex animo in illis displiceamus: contra vero nos totos addicamus virtuti, iustitiae, & sanctitati: crucifigamus veterem nostrum hominem, & carnem nostram subigamus, ne perversae cupiditates amplius in nobis dominentur, sed in vitam novam resurgamus, ut obsequium Deo nostro optimo praestemus, & fructus iustitiae & integritatis quos habeat gratos, proferamus, quo palam constet nos esse membra Christi eius Filii, ac vere regenitos & renovatos a Spiritu sancto in gloriam illius, & proximorum nostrorum aedificationem. Haec sunt commoda & fructus quos ex morte & resurrectione magni illius Seruatoris[?] & Redemptoris Iesu Christi inter alios percipimus. Eo nos Spiritus sanctus hortatur per os Apostolorum, Pauli scilicet 6.7.8, ad Rom. cap. & in epist. ad Ephes. & Colossenses. Petri etiam duabus epist. in quarum assidua lectione te exerceas & frequenti meditatione ac lectione omnium Psalmorum: neque unquam fatigeris, sed instar Catechismi semper habeas, nepe ubi semel perlegeris, ad initium redeas: atque ita Deo iuvante fructum inde singularem colliges. Quartus denique & ultimus carcer ad nos proprie nunc spectat, idque Dei nostri optimi beneficio, qui nos Filii sui Iesu Christi vinctos & captivos dedit in castellum hoc Cameriacum, in quo pro bonitate sua maiore copia in nos effudit dona & benedictiones tum animi tum corporis, quam alio quovis loco, ubicunque versatisimus. Et hoc quidem de prima quae inde ad nos redit utilitate. Caeterum si expenditur vita, quam omnes tanto pere naturaliter expetunt, annon felici morte ad veram vitam ingredimur? An laetitia & oblectatione[?]
units.tr: Since you have already learned, most dear father and brother in Christ Jesus our Lord, from our last letters (in which was set out the confession of our faith, which we all together made public before the senators of this supreme court by the grace and power of the best God) the state of our cause, namely that we have been condemned to the fire, I will not go into that matter at greater length with you. Indeed, I can assure you of this one thing from the testimony which the Holy Spirit certainly gives to my conscience: just as nothing better can befall a pious worshipper of God than to pass over into eternal life by this way, so nothing is desired by us more ardently, or awaited more eagerly, than that happy day on which we shall be snatched away to that most sweet sacrifice. For, besides the fact that the honour and glory of our greatest God and Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, the building up of his Church, the strengthening, joy and consolation of our brothers, and then the certain destruction and ruin of Satan, of Antichrist and of all his members and the enemies of the truth who are bound to him, are, as it were, contained and enclosed in this public and solemn testimony which we give with our mouths and seal with our own blood (which is certainly the chief fruit that our most happy death produces), there is also, if anyone regards us privately, so much good and gain flowing to us from it that it cannot be grasped in the mind, much less explained in words or writing. Is it, I ask, a matter of little moment to be freed from the four prisons by which we are shut in, just as it is for you three that we should be claimed and brought into perpetual liberty? Of these, the first is this world, full of so many miseries, which with its empty show, its impostures and tricks dazzles and deceives our eyes. The second is our body, defiled with so much filth and full of stench. The third is our soul with all its parts: mind, memory, reason, will, and our desires and disturbances, which draw us here and there and turn us altogether away from what God commands us. Is not that like a kind of whirlpool and abyss of all vices and crimes, which by their weight strike horror?
